**[gd.games](https://gd.games/) gets a fresh new look!** Discover a revamped community page, a bigger focus on multiplayer, new categories like Trending, and exclusive badges to reward the most active players.


## 💝 Improvements

* Report errors of store extensions in the 3D editor as crash reports
* Add an action to change the body type of 3D physics objects
* Add the ability to generate an invoice for purchase or subscription payments, from the GDevelop Profile
* Catch 3D editor not starting with a warning message and prevent crashes in 2D editor

## 🐛 Bug fixes

* Fix unfocused variable fields displaying autocompletion
* Fix missing stencil buffer for the shared 3D renderer (Thanks snowyukitty!)
* Fix tile map instances leaking their geometries in the scene editor
* Fix tile map objects leaking their geometries and buffers when destroyed (Thanks @kenny-ish!)
* Fix "for each child variable" loops not displaying autocompletion
* Fix potential leak of GDevelop cloud session cookie to arbitrary hosts when opening a rogue project on desktop app (Thanks @carfeii!)
* Fix wrong spacing in the new effect dialog
* Fix CRT and Old film effects showing their noise on the whole screen
* Fix collision masks of Tiled image collection tiles being offset and partially ignored

AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome:
It’s not always the big issues: sometimes what you need is a few fixes and tweaks to pump up the overall stability 🔩

## Full changelog

See also the [v0.107.79 GitHub milestone][ms-v0.107.79].

### Security

- Go version has been updated to prevent the possibility of exploiting the Go vulnerabilities fixed in [1.26.6][go-1.26.6].

- AdGuard Home is now more resistant to resource exhaustion attacks when using DNS-over-QUIC.

    This is GHSA-w6v6-f44j-3rj2.  We thank @ATinyShoe for reporting this security issue.

### Added

- Bootstrap servers configuration now supports comments.

- New property `"language"` in `POST /control/install/check_config` and `POST /control/install/configure` HTTP APIs.

- The user is able to remove the static lease's hostname via the HTTP API.

### Changed

- The `edge` channel has been switched to the new UI and versioning scheme.

### Deprecated

- `strict_sni_check` is now deprecated.

### Fixed

- DNS64 treating unresolved `CNAME`/`DNAME` answers as the end of resolution chain (#7514).

- Blocked requests without an EDNS(0) OPT record (#8183).

[go-1.26.6]: https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI

[ms-v0.107.79]: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome/milestone/114?closed=1

AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy:
### 🚀 v0.14.11

#### New Features

- **Relative-date comparisons** — Added Today, Yesterday, and Tomorrow to date comparisons such as before, after, on or before, and on or after, so filters followed the calendar without selecting a new date each day.
- **YouTube captions** — Added direct import of available timestamped captions into AI transcript blocks without downloading audio or using transcription minutes. Retained audio transcription and file upload as alternatives when captions were unavailable.
- **Missing row pages** — Added a "Create empty page" action when a supporting server reported an unavailable row document, with a warning and explicit confirmation. Kept readable and locally cached content ahead of recreation.

#### Improvements

- **Gallery views** — Added grouped card layouts, configurable previews and card sizes, image fitting, and cover repositioning.
- **Feed views** — Refreshed card previews, quick actions, reactions, and comment discussions, with a full-page action for longer content.
- **Plans and connections** — Routed hosted upgrade prompts through the Plan settings, kept Cloud billing unavailable in local and self-hosted sessions, and added clearer connection-loading errors with retry actions.

#### Bug Fixes

- Fixed linking databases with incomplete sync data, refreshing embedded database tabs after sync, and loading repaired rows after an explicit retry.
- Made formula properties easier to find in filter and sort pickers, paused incompatible filters when formula result types changed, and corrected rollups that read other rollups.
- Preserved center peek when navigating between rows and prevented canceled row-page opens from leaving later opens stuck.
- Corrected page-reference states for trashed, missing, and temporarily unavailable pages, and stopped slow permission lookups from holding up the Share menu's people list.
- Kept reconnect feedback visible until the connection was confirmed, with another retry available if it did not connect.

#### ⚠️ Action Required

- Self-hosted workspaces still require **AppFlowy Cloud v0.19.10 or later**. Before enabling missing-row-page recovery, deploy its server support to every node handling live edits.

## [4.29.3] - 2026-10-24

Life is like a box of chocolates.

### 新增

- 消息追踪：进一步完善消息追踪能力，支持记录和观测所有入站消息事件，以及事件对应的插件调用和 Agent 调用。（需要先在 WebUI 左下角设置中开启） (#10614)
- 诊断导出：支持从控制台和系统设置导出支持脱敏的系统诊断包，包含日志、追踪、配置、插件状态和环境等信息。 (#10418, #10659)
- 安装脚本：新增多语言安装流程和中国大陆镜像支持。 (#10629)

### 修复

- 备份：补全定时任务、持久化文件和相关数据目录的备份与恢复，避免数据遗漏。 (#10644, #10661)
- Gemini：支持模型自定义生成参数，保留显式设置的零值；修复非字符串枚举导致工具 Schema 不兼容的问题。 (#10719, #10635)
- NVIDIA Rerank：保留模型专属 API 端点路径，避免请求错误的通用地址。 (#10732)
- 电脑使用：修复 Shipyard Bay 执行结果的解析，以及 Windows Shell 超时或取消时的子进程清理。 (#10671, #10729)
- WebUI：修复配置刷新后模型元数据丢失、默认聊天模型选择、插件侧栏名称本地化、桌面更新通知和配置模板字段默认值。 (#10522, #10663, #10576, #10622, #10517)
- WebUI：优化配置说明与条件选项显示，修复全屏日志中的 Pip 安装弹窗、日志流连接等待和页面切换后的重复日志，并明确插件筛选范围。 (#10647, #10608, #10666, #10694, #10691)
- 数据库：使用跨数据库兼容的 JSON 查询表达式。 (#10664)

### Added

- Message tracing: Improved tracing to record and inspect all incoming message events and their associated plugin and Agent calls. Enable it first in Settings in the lower-left corner of the WebUI. (#10614)
- Diagnostics: Export system diagnostic bundles with redaction support from the console and system settings, including logs, traces, configuration, plugin status, and environment information. (#10418, #10659)
- Installer: Added multilingual setup and mainland China mirrors. (#10629)

### Fixed

- Backups: Include scheduled tasks, persistent files, and related data directories in backup and restore operations. (#10644, #10661)
- Gemini: Honor model-specific generation parameters and explicit zero values, and handle non-string enums in tool schemas. (#10719, #10635)
- NVIDIA Rerank: Preserve model-specific endpoint paths instead of substituting a generic endpoint. (#10732)
- Computer use: Parse Shipyard Bay execution envelopes correctly and clean up Windows shell child processes on timeout or cancellation. (#10671, #10729)
- WebUI: Preserve fetched model metadata after configuration refresh; restore default chat model selection; localize plugin sidebar names; fix desktop update notices and template field defaults. (#10522, #10663, #10576, #10622, #10517)
- WebUI: Clarify configuration hints and conditional settings; keep the Pip dialog visible in fullscreen logs; flush log stream headers promptly; prevent duplicate logs after navigation; clarify plugin filter scope. (#10647, #10608, #10666, #10694, #10691)
- Database: Use portable JSON query expressions. (#10664)

BigPizzaV3/CodexPlusPlus:
本次为问题修复版：适配 Codex 26.1027，修复原生 Fast 按钮消失；修复网关在单供应商时因熔断 / 429 冷却比直连更容易失败；修复 Codex++ 以管理员身份运行时 Windows 商店版 Codex 启动后立即退出、主 Codex 用官方登录时 API 供应商多开仍走官方账号、插件市场搜不到插件等问题；供应商池可配置 new-api 访问令牌显示余额，DeepSeek 等厂商余额也显示在供应商卡片上。

### 新增

- **new-api 中转站显示余额**：识别为 new-api 的供应商，详情里多一行「访问令牌」，填上 new-api「个人设置 → 安全设置」里生成的访问令牌（新版分权限令牌需勾选「个人资料 · 查看」）后，卡片显示账户余额；不填时照旧（#2793）。
- **DeepSeek 等厂商的余额显示在供应商池卡片上**，与「用量」页同一来源（#2793）。
- **Agent 协作同一 Agent 可并发执行任务**：每个 Agent 可设「同时执行任务数」（1–4，默认 1，与之前一致）；未达上限时新任务直接开始，达到上限再排队，多个会话共用同一上限。并发任务请使用不同的工作目录，同一目录时会提示（#2800）。
- **多开页可直接编辑、删除供应商**：卡片悬停出现编辑和删除，删除前检查是否在用并二次确认；接入网关后「从第三方导入」（含 cc-switch）也不再被隐藏（#2801）。

### 修复

- Codex 26.1027 上原生 Fast 按钮消失：新版 Codex 改了入口模块的加载链路，Codex++ 找不到要改写的模块（#2788、#2792）。
- Windows：Codex++ 以管理员身份运行时，商店版 Codex 启动后会降权重启、脱离商店包环境而立即退出；现在以管理员运行时会让 Codex 跳过降权。Windows 激活 Codex 的调用加了超时，不再一直卡在「启动 Codex」（#2789、#2795、#2764）。
- 网关比直连更容易因限流失败：上游偶发几次 5xx 后，网关的熔断会把唯一的供应商整体挡 60 秒、全部本地回 429（`gateway_keys_cooling`），Codex 重试几次就报 exceeded retry limit。现在只有在有别家可换时才熔断；没给恢复时间的 429 首次只冷却 5 秒、并按上游给的恢复时间；Key 很快能恢复时网关稍等再发；「请求避震」不再对 429 反复重发同一个 Key（#2802、#2761）。
- 主 Codex 用官方登录时，用 API 供应商启动的多开实例仍以官方账号登录、消耗官方额度（#2794）。
- 经网关或本地代理转发到 Chat Completions / Anthropic 协议上游的流式请求，用量统计和请求日志里的 token 一直是 0（#2803）。
- 插件市场开启后，在 Codex 插件页搜索搜不到插件市场里的插件（新版 Codex 的插件搜索改走服务端）（#2790）。
- 侧栏折叠再展开时，已删除的会话会先闪出再消失（#2791）。
- 会话页的项目路径在 Windows 上显示 `//?/` 前缀，同一目录被分成两组（#2791）。
- 「修复与维护 → 同步目标」里出现点不了的内部别名 `codex_plus_managed`（#2791）。
- 旧版 Codex（例如 Intel Mac 上的 Codex）上用量状态栏不显示（#2753）。
- 从旧版本自动更新到新版本后，macOS「应用程序」文件夹里的 `.codex-plus-update-…` 残留目录没有被清理（#2774）。
- 供应商池卡片不再显示中转站类型（sub2api / new-api），只显示倍率和余额，类型放在悬停提示里。

This release fixes a number of bugs related to gitignore matching as well as
some performance improvements in directory tree traversal.

> In case you haven't heard of it before, ripgrep is a line-oriented search
> tool that recursively searches the current directory for a regex pattern.
> By default, ripgrep will respect gitignore rules and automatically skip
> hidden files/directories and binary files.

Platform support:

  ripgrep.

Performance improvements:

* [PERF #3293](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/3293):
  Improves directory traversal time on very large corpora.

Feature enhancements:

* [FEATURE #3275](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/3275):
  ripgrep now respects `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`.

Cherry Studio 2.1.8 - Editing, Voice, and Integration Updates

✨ New Features
- [File Editing] Isolate drafts across notes, skills and artifacts, retain failed edits for retry, and support up to 8 MiB text editing and previews.
- [Language] Add Italian (it-IT) UI support with full translations and emoji picker.
- [Voice] Hold the mouse button in a text input to start dictation, release to transcribe.
- [Voice] Streaming speech synthesis with real-time audio playback.
- [Web Search] Add Tencent Yuanbao Search as a built-in provider.
- [Scheduled Tasks] Create and manage scheduled tasks through an agent chat with an interactive task card.
- [Screenshot] Copy the capture to clipboard while keeping the overlay open.
- [Selection] Select text anywhere to automatically copy it and show a quick-quote toolbar.
- [Composer] File and link tokens align with the text line, show per-type file icons, and load favicons while editing.
- [RTF] Preview Rich Text Format files as formatted documents.
- [Feishu] Configure whether the bot only replies to @mentions in group chats.
- [Remote Access] Set a custom hostname, IP or port for pairing invitations.
- [Assistant] Remember the “Also archive related topics” choice for future archives.

🐛 Bug Fixes
- [Notes] Fix note content being overwritten when switching between cached notes.
- [Skills] Show localized error messages when a ZIP or folder is missing SKILL.md, without leaking temporary paths.
- [Chat] Expand long user messages by default; keep follow-up queues independent of read receipts.
- [Proxy] Match short wildcard IP bypass rules like 192.168.* on Windows.
- [Claude Code] Keep the 1M context budget when routing through the internal gateway.
- [Tab Bar] Closing the last tab opens the Launchpad instead of quitting the app.
- [File Preview] Preserve reading state when refreshing files; fix line spacing for Word documents.
- [Sidebar] Selected entries use neutral filled icons in both light and dark themes.
- [Chat Layout] Isolate list-group expansion state per window.
- [Paintings] Cap loading grid density to prevent performance issues.
- [MCP] Keep literal # characters in saved headers and environment values.
- [Knowledge] Ship a baseline sqlite-vec build for Linux x64.
- [Voice] Add diagnostics for operation failures and stream timeouts.
- [Agent Session] Continue the target workspace when creating across agents; surface compaction failures.
- [Messages] Drop historical tool parts with incompatible replay inputs.
- [Virtual List] Hand sticky headers over at the pinned stack bottom.
- [Notes] Fixed an issue where dismissing the "note changed on disk" conflict dialog left the editor session stuck, failing all later note renames, deletions, and moves with misleading errors.

🔒 Security
- [Electron] Upgrade to 44.9.3 for certificate security fixes.

AdminLTE 4.10.1 refreshes the build toolchain and demo integrations, fixes responsive and accessibility issues, and adds broader regression coverage. Public AdminLTE component APIs and the published package's Node.js requirement remain unchanged.

### Changes

- Update compatible stable dependencies, including Astro 7.3.7, Rollup 4.64.2, Playwright 1.64.0, Vitest 5.0.3, Sass 1.105.1, and ESLint 10.12.0. Replace npm-run-all with its maintained npm-run-all2 successor.
- Update demo/integration CDN libraries, migrate FullCalendar to 7.1.1, correct jsVectorMap asset paths, and refresh existing integrity hashes.
- Fix tablet header overflow, fullscreen icon synchronization and isolation from card-maximize controls, local calendar dates, calendar accessible names, table filter labels/grid semantics, and light/dark contrast.
- Repair Astro source checking, the ESM Prettier configuration, and the Unicorn preset. Add Chromium/Firefox/WebKit and Node.js 22/24/26 CI, light/dark accessibility checks, and local gzip budget enforcement.

### Verification

- Clean npm installation and complete production build, lint, TypeScript declarations, and all 15 bundle-size budgets.
- 80 unit tests on Node.js 22, 24, and 26; 378 browser scenarios across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; accessibility checks on 24 representative pages in both themes.
- The exact publishing tarball installs successfully on Node.js 20/npm 10 with strict engine checks. Production dependencies audit clean.

### Compatibility and security

Source builds require Node.js 22.22.3+, 24.16.0+, or 26.3.0+ and npm 10+. These contributor requirements use devEngines; compiled-package consumers retain Node.js >=20 support.

TypeScript remains on 6.0.3 because the latest Astro checker and TypeScript ESLint versions do not support TypeScript 7. Development tooling retains twenty propagated high-severity npm audit findings from the unpatched [braces advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm). This dependency is not included in the published runtime dependency tree.

Npm publication is handled separately by the maintainer. The attached npm tarball is the validated publishing artifact.

DarkFlippers/unleashed-firmware:
## Main changes
- Current API: 88.19
- iButton: **Choose which blanks a write may target** - new Settings -> Write Blanks list in the iButton app, where RW1990.1, RW1990.2, TM2004 and TM01x can each be switched on or off; a write then only tries the enabled ones instead of every blank type in turn, and the write screen names the type it is currently attempting rather than showing an unlabelled "Writing ID" throughout. Each attempt that is not the blank in front of you costs real time (RW1990.1/.2 about 900 ms each, TM01x about 335 ms), so narrowing the list is the difference between a write that lands right away and one that walks the whole sequence first. Writing with nothing enabled, or with nothing enabled that the loaded key can actually be written to, says so instead of blinking forever. The choice is saved and is honoured by the ibutton CLI as well (by @mishamyte | PR #1153 | Closes #1152)
- RFID: **Add Manually by facility code and card number** - picking a format under Add Manually now asks whether to enter the card as FC/ID or as hex. FC/ID takes the numbers printed on the card, one number input per field, and builds the data itself: EM4100 (all clocks), HID H10301 and the HID formats below, ioProx XSF (with its version), AWID and Pyramid 26-bit, and Gallagher (with region code and issue level). Formats without such a layout go straight to hex as before (by @matthewb-worthe | PR #1149)
- RFID: **HID H10302, H10304, H10306, AMAG S10401 and Corporate 1000 35-bit now read** - a Generic HIDProx card of one of these lengths whose parity checks out shows its FC and card number on the read and saved-card screens, one line per format the frame fits (a 37-bit card can fit more than one). The formats are listed under Add Manually too, entered by FC/ID and saved as HIDProx. The "Data:" line of HIDProx cards is gone: it repeated the hex shown above it and lost bits after the first digit on 37-, 35- and 26-bit frames (by @matthewb-worthe | PR #1149)
- RFID: **Casi-Rusco C10106 badges now read** - the badges are EM4100 frames, so an EM4100 read whose 40 bits fit the badge layout gets an "or C10106: credential card" line under the EM4100 text, the twelve-digit badge id split as the access system prints it. There is no parity to check, so it is one possible reading; it is only shown for credentials beginning with 15, as the badges are numbered, which keeps it off almost all other EM4100 cards. Add Manually gets a Casi-Rusco C10106 entry that takes the two numbers and saves an EM4100 card at RF/32, the clock the badges use (by @matthewb-worthe | PR #1149)
- GUI: **Number input starts on a value it accepts** - a number input whose range excludes 0, such as 1-26, opened on an empty field that the Save key refused, so there was no way to confirm anything until a digit was typed. It now starts on the nearest value the range allows, and an empty field reads as 0 and is accepted or refused like any other value. Applies to every app using the widget, including JS apps (by @matthewb-worthe | PR #1149)
- RFID: **Choose which chips a write may target** - new Settings -> Write Chips list in the 125 kHz RFID app, where T5577, EM4305 and each Hitag micro / ID82xx variant (8265, 8210, H5.5) can be switched on or off; a write then only tries the enabled ones instead of every chip in turn, which cuts the wait when the blank in front of you is not the first one on the list (each attempt that is not the chip present costs a verify read of up to 2 s). Writing with nothing enabled, or with nothing enabled that the protocol can actually be written to, says so instead of retrying forever. The choice is saved and is honoured by the rfid CLI as well (by @mishamyte | PR #1146 | Closes #1145)
- RFID: **Write an EM4100 id onto a Hitag S / ID8268 clone** - the ID82xx "china clone" Hitag S chips (F8268, 8211 and relatives) join T5577, EM4305 and the Hitag micro variants as a write target, so a saved EM4100 key can be cloned onto one from the 125 kHz RFID app and the rfid CLI. **This chip is switched OFF by default - turn "8268" on in Settings -> Write Chips to use it.** That is deliberate: pages 4 and 5 hold application data on a genuine Hitag S, nothing the Flipper can read tells a genuine tag from a clone, and unlike the blind writers this one selects whatever tag answers - so cloning a key with a real Hitag S in range must not silently overwrite it. It is also the only target that checks before it writes: SELECT needs the tag's own UID, so the Flipper reads and confirms that first, and skips the attempt when no such chip is in range instead of waiting out a verify read. EM4100 at RF/64 only, the rate the chip's factory config emits (by @mishamyte | PR #1148 | Closes #1147)
- SubGHz: **Genius remotes now work** - Genius uses the same frame as Faac SLH but its own key, so a Genius remote used to show the wrong counter and could not be resent. Add a `Manufacture: Genius` line to the .sub file next to its `Seed:` and it reads and sends properly, with the signal screen saying Genius instead of Faac SLH. **Genius 433MHz** and **Genius 868MHz** are new in Add Manually
- SubGHz: **Monarch and KEY remotes are read and resent properly now** - both used to come up as Unknown. Monarch covers the Dorcas 22366CLN, and KEY is new in Add Manually as **KL: KEY 433MHz**. Monarch remotes differ from each other in one value, so Advanced Add Manually asks for it (Enter DISC.) and a received signal keeps whatever its remote used
- SubGHz: **New protocol KeyFinder2** - the colour-button key finder fobs the existing KeyFinder decoder could not read. Shows the button colour next to the code, **unverified**: the colour names come from a single four button fob, so another fob may name them differently
- SubGHz: **Nord ICE remotes send the full pair, and their other buttons** - a press puts two frames on air that differ in one bit, and only one of them was ever resent; both are rebuilt from a single key, so files saved by an earlier build transmit the pair unchanged, and the bit and gap timings now match the remote. The arrows on the send screen reach the remote's other three buttons, the button editor works, and saving keeps whichever button was sent. **Nord ICE 433MHz** is in Add Manually too, generated on button 4
- SubGHz: **HomeGate remotes now work** - new KeeLoq manufacturer key, so these remotes read and send properly. **HomeGate 433MHz** is in Add Manually too
- SubGHz: **Prastel 433MHz** is new in Add Manually, generated on button 1. The arrows on the send screen now reach the remote's other three buttons and the button editor works - **the button map is unverified**, it follows the other four button remotes
- SubGHz: **Nice O-Code 433MHz** is new in Add Manually - Advanced asks for the installer code (Enter IC) so a remote can be made for a gate you already have. The `Nice O-Code` app, which recovers that code from a remote, now has **New** next to Save: it writes a second remote with the same code and button but its own serial and a fresh counter, so it works alongside your original instead of fighting it
- SubGHz: **New app - Seed Capturer** - collects the Fix + Hop pairs an offline seed recovery needs from a FAAC SLH, Genius or Erreka remote, under Apps -> Sub-GHz. Pick the manufacturer and 433.92 or 868.35 MHz AM650, then press the remote's button over and over: it locks onto the first Fix it hears and keeps every distinct Hop under it, up to 10. Two hops are enough to save, more narrow the search. Captures go to /ext/apps_data/subghz_seed_captures for the qUnleashed app to recover the seed from
- Main menu: **Two new menu styles - Macintosh and 3D** - pick them in Settings -> Desktop -> Menu Style. Macintosh is a classic Mac OS desktop - title bar with the Flipper's name, icon grid, paged with arrows; 3D is a carousel that flies the icons along a path with the selected one zoomed in front. Both are reimplementations of MIT-licensed Arduboy/Arduino originals: Ardutosh by [@jhhoward](https://github.com/jhhoward/Ardutosh) and the 3D OLED menu by [@upiir](https://github.com/upiir/arduino_3d_menu_oled) (by @apfxtech | PR #1155)
- SubGHz: **New protocol Doorbell32** - unbranded 433MHz doorbells. KeyFinder, KeyFinder2 and Doorbell32 are all in the Sensors ignore group
- SubGHz: **KeeLoq Erreka programming mode** - the 0xF button now sends the seed in the clear like the original remote, same as BFT, and the seed is saved with the signal so the hops can be rebuilt. **Erreka 868MHz** joins **Erreka 433MHz** in Add Manually, for the IRIS IR02/868 and IR04/868 remotes
- NFC: **Texkom (Техком) keys now read and emulate** - the 13.56 MHz intercom fobs, in TK13, TK15, TK17 and MMBIT flavours. Read one and you get its UID, which variant it is and whether its checksum is valid; save it and it emulates. TK13, TK17 and MMBIT can also be made up in Add Manually. Writing to a blank is not supported (by @mishamyte)
- SubGHz: Longer 112bit Nice O-Code frames are read by the `Nice O-Code` app now. O-Code is shown in Read as a raw key with a note to use that app, instead of a Nice One with a random serial, and Save and Send are hidden for it since without the installer code there is nothing to rebuild it from
- SubGHz: Nice Flor-S, Nice One, Came Atomo and Beninca ARC remotes show one entry per press in Read instead of one per frame, and Nice O-Code is told apart from Flor-S and Nice One properly now
- SubGHz: The `Nice O-Code` and `Security+ PIN` apps support external radio modules now
- Apps: Build tag (**14oct2026**) - **Check out more Apps updates and fixes by following** [this link](https://github.com/xMasterX/all-the-plugins/commits/dev)
## Other changes
- OFW: NFC: FeliCa emulation and reading are more robust - an emulated card no longer goes quiet for the rest of a reader's session after it turns one command down, a Standard card answers Polling only for the System Codes its own dump holds and can switch System by IDm, a bad read or write gets the proper error status instead of no answer, writes refuse read-only services and either land in full or not at all, blocks above 255 are addressed properly, and reader timeouts follow what the card declares in its PMm (OFW PR 4465 | by @kormax)
- OFW: NFC: A FeliCa Standard card's system key version is the system's own now, not the root area's - it was filled in from area 0000, a different node with a different key, so the Key version shown for a system was wrong on every card where the two differ. The system node 0xFFFF is queried directly, in the same Request Service batch as the areas and services, and an emulated card answers that node from the stored system key version. The FeliCa file format is at version 4 because of it: a file saved by an earlier build holds the root area's key version on its system line, so that value is no longer read back as the system's and the field shows as unknown until the card is read again (OFW PR 4462 | by @kormax)
- NFC: **The nfc CLI no longer reboots the Flipper on an EMV card** - the CLI keeps its own table of protocol names and EMV was never added to it, so scanning, dumping or emulating one printed a null string and hard-faulted. A protocol missing from that table now fails loudly where it is looked up instead of taking the device down (by @mishamyte)
- NFC: **Add Manually no longer reboots the Flipper on a card that is not NFC-A** - the generated-card screen assumed every generator produced an ISO14443-3A descendant and read that data unconditionally; the check that was meant to catch otherwise is compiled out of a release build. It reads the UID through the generic accessor now (by @mishamyte)
- RPC: **Storage read can ask for a range** - a read request takes an offset and size, so a companion app can fetch part of a file instead of all of it (by @apfxtech | PR #1174)
- Docs: [SubGHzRemoteProg.md](/documentation/SubGHzRemoteProg.md) rewritten - 27 systems in alphabetical order with a jump table, 17 of them new, a table of which key sends each protocol's programming button, and how to use the Seed Capturer app with FAAC SLH, Genius or Erreka and recover the seed in qUnleashed afterwards
- Build: An app that embeds plugins builds a second time instead of failing - the plugin staging dir is a VariantDir of the app's source dir, so globbing it named source paths that never exist; each plugin's staged .fal is a direct dependency now (original implementation by @RogueMaster)
- Build: Adding or removing a file asset rebuilds the .fap that embeds it - assets are enumerated the way they are bundled, so the dependencies match what ends up in the binary (original implementation by @RogueMaster)
- Build: A recursive source glob walks each app tree once instead of once per source pattern (original implementation by @RogueMaster)
- Build: macOS leaves `.DS_Store` and `._*` sidecars in any folder it touches, and they are skipped now instead of being embedded in a .fap, listed in the resources Manifest, packed into the update tarball or compiled in as an icon - an `._*.png` next to a real icon used to fail the build outright
- NFC: **MIFARE DESFire Light is recognised instead of coming up as ISO14443-4A (Unknown)** - the card takes only ISO 7816-wrapped commands and answers a plain native frame with SW 6700 ("wrong length"), so every DESFire command the firmware sent was refused and nothing in the ISO14443-4A family claimed the card. DESFire now settles on whichever command mode the card answers, keeping the plain frames the EV series expects and falling back to wrapping only when the card refuses the frame itself. Its own hardware type (0x08) is accepted too, so it reads as **Mifare DESFire Light**. Light has no PICC-level free memory, key settings or key versions - it answers 0x1C to all three - so the read now carries on without the fields a card refuses rather than failing, and the info screen says the card has a single fixed application instead of blaming authentication. A status code the firmware does not model is reported as a refusal by the card rather than as a broken exchange, so a card leaving the field mid-read can no longer be saved as a thin successful one. Detection relies on GetVersion alone, whose 28-byte layout and hardware type already tell DESFire apart from MIFARE Plus and NTAG 4xx. Reading the Light's file contents is not part of this (by @mishamyte)
- GUI: **Loading screen can show a label next to the spinner** (by @mishamyte | PR #1169 | Closes #1168)
- NFC: **Show progress while a large per-UID (CUID) dictionary loads on Read** (by @mishamyte | PR #1167 | Closes #1166)
- LF RFID: A Write Chips settings file saved by a newer firmware no longer confuses the write screen - a build that knows fewer chips still accepts the file, and used to keep the bits for chips it does not have; they are dropped as the file is read now. With every chip this build knows switched off but a newer-only one still set, a write said "No enabled chip can write this protocol" instead of "No write chips enabled. Enable one in Settings". Apps reading the setting through the API now only see chips their firmware has (by @mishamyte | PR #1164 | Fixes #1154)
- NFC: What a reader writes to an emulated FeliCa card is kept again - the check that decides whether emulation changed the card passed an element count where a byte count was wanted, so only the first byte of the system list was ever compared; blocks a reader wrote into an emulated FeliCa Standard card read back as unchanged and were dropped instead of being kept in the shadow file. That length is element-aware now, and the FeliCa system and DESFire application lists - whose entries own nested arrays, so comparing their bytes only compares pointers - are compared entry by entry (by @MNeroba | PR #1107)
- NFC: The MIFARE Classic dictionary attack ends as soon as the card is fully read - a card that reuses the same keys across its sectors is often solved by the key reuse pass while the attack is still on sector 0, but it used to walk every remaining sector with the counters already full, and then start the next dictionary phase on a card with nothing left to find, which looked stuck. With a per-UID dictionary those leftover sectors also cost a scan of that dictionary for every key index (by @mishamyte | PR #1151 | Fixes #1150)
- SubGHz: Better checks on ext module init in CLI
- SubGHz: Sending a receive-only signal from the mobile app or qFlipper no longer crashes the Flipper - the Send button on the device is hidden for a protocol the firmware can decode but not encode, while the RPC path has no such check, so asking the Flipper to transmit a saved iDo 117/111 file reached the transmit path, found no encoder to allocate, and then handed that NULL to a free that requires a real instance. It is reported as an error now, and the transmitter pointer is cleared after every teardown instead of being left dangling (by @MNeroba | PR #1104)
- SubGHz: An unknown radio preset is an error instead of a crash now - the preset lookup in lib/subghz reports a miss rather than taking the device down, and loading a key or starting TX/RX fails with the unknown-preset error those paths already had; Add Manually -> Security+ 2.0 also stopped leaking a transmitter on every generated key (Closes #1159 | Closes #1161)
- LF RFID: Keri tags now read correctly - the PSK slicer reports one level ~135us long on a frame as unbalanced as Keri's, so every run of ones decoded a bit too long and no genuine Keri card read at all, not even one the Flipper had just written; the skew is corrected both ways round now, and the two frames in the register must agree before a read is accepted, since Keri carries no parity or checksum (OFW PR 4449 | by @mfcarroll)
- LF RFID: Capture durations are now exact - the counter had no hardware zero, so the origin was written by software inside the capture ISR, one interrupt latency after the edge the hardware had already latched, and every duration handed to a decoder read ~1.7us short; the counter free-runs now and consecutive captures are differenced. Every decoder quantises each duration and rounded the bias away, so no read changes - it is margin for anything measuring absolute time (OFW PR 4442 | by @mfcarroll)
- NFC: Emulating a card straight from Favorites awards Dolphin XP, like emulating it from NFC -> Saved already did (OFW PR 4448 | by @peakji)
- HID: Mouse Jiggler and Mouse Jiggler (Stealth) stop when you press Stop - the timer was left firing into an empty callback until you closed the screen. Leaving the screen now clears the running state too, so re-opening it no longer shows a highlighted "Stop" for a jiggler that is not running, where the first press only put the label back. Over Bluetooth the jiggler waits for the link instead of sending into nothing, and a connection completing while the app is still starting is no longer missed; Stealth movement is never zero on an axis, so a scheduled jiggle always moves (by @MNeroba | PR #1112)
- OFW: RPC: An app can no longer be handed a forged RPC context - an app started in RPC mode is given its session as an address inside the launch argument string, so a crafted `RPC <hex>` argument could hand an app any pointer and have it write through it. Live sessions are tracked now, an argument that looks like a context but names no live session is refused, and the callback setter checks the session under the same lock that stops it being freed mid-call
- OFW: NFC: An NDEF SmartPoster that nests itself no longer overflows the stack - a SmartPoster holds a nested NDEF message, parsed by recursing into it, and nothing stopped a card from nesting them as deep as it liked. The depth is capped at 8 now, and a record below that says "Nesting too deep" instead of taking the parser down with it
- OFW: NFC: A saved DESFire file whose access rights are longer than the field that holds them is refused instead of being read past the end of it
- OFW: iButton: A saved key naming a protocol this build does not have is refused on load, instead of being looked up by an invalid protocol id
- OFW: Storage: A read error part way through unpacking a .tar is treated as a failure - the negative error code the read returns was handed to the write as a length
- LF RFID: `LFRFIDProtocolIndala224` moved to the end of the protocol enum - it had been inserted after Indala26, which shifted the id of every protocol after it, so an app built against a different SDK version acted on the wrong protocol. Saved cards are unaffected: the files name their protocol, they do not store its id
- API: `mf_desfire_send_chunks` is an exported function again - the deprecated name became a macro alias when the poller function was renamed, which took it out of the API table and left apps calling it unable to link. It is a wrapper around `mf_desfire_poller_send_chunks` now, so both names work
- OFW: Build: `fap_dist` no longer races the dist commands - a dist command wipes `dist/<flavor>` when it starts, so installing the faps is ordered after the dist commands the build is running

## What's New in v0.5.0

The first release since May. The web UI is rebuilt around the canvas, draw.io is bundled with the app, the settings dialog is redone, and the MCP server reaches feature parity with the web app. Desktop users get every fix that landed on `main` over the last five months.

### New Features

- **Canvas-first UI with a bundled draw.io**: the canvas fills the window and the chat floats on its right. draw.io v32.0.2 is served from the app's own origin (no separate draw.io container, works offline), so the app drives the editor directly: every AI change is a version card with a thumbnail that can be compared, restored or undone; an AI change is one Ctrl+Z step; changed shapes are highlighted; selected shapes are sent to the model; draw.io's own toolbar, menus (auto layout, Mermaid, CSV import) and page tabs are available. New start screen, session rename and switcher, and opening `.drawio` files (#957, #962)
- **Settings dialog rebuilt**: tabs for Models, General, Drawing and About. Adding a provider is three numbered steps (connection, models, test), with a searchable provider picker, one status line per provider, Bedrock sign-in by API key or access keys with a session token, and a model picker that lists every model as working, untested or failed (#958)
- **MCP server 0.3.0, feature parity with the web app**: the drawing guide and 30 icon libraries over MCP, `screenshot_diagram` for visual checks, all-or-nothing `edit_diagram`, sessions auto-saved to `.drawio` files (`DRAWIO_DATA_DIR`), preview themes and dark mode, editable SVG export. The web app now reuses the MCP server's diagram code (#951)
- **Multi-page documents in the MCP server**: `add_page`, edit a page by id, name or index, export specific pages (#862)
- **`load_diagram` MCP tool**: load a `.drawio` file from disk into the session, including draw.io's compressed format (#893)
- **Admin panel at `/admin`**: manage server settings in a web UI instead of environment variables, enabled by setting `ADMIN_PASSWORD`; secrets are masked, serverless hosts get a read-only view (#866). Its copy is rewritten in plain words in all four languages (#963)
- **Model lists and catalog**: 18 providers can fetch their model list into a searchable picker; a models.dev snapshot flags models without tool calls, which cannot draw; the Test button checks all models at once and shows response times (#951)
- **New providers**: AIHubMix (#865), Atlas Cloud (#896) and MiMo by Xiaomi (#887); MiniMax default model upgraded to M3 (#857)
- **Comma-separated `AI_MODEL`**: `AI_MODEL=a,b,c` is enough for a quick multi-model server setup (#870)
- **Quota by the CDN's client IP**: `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` and `ORIGIN_SECRET` stop quota bypass through a faked `X-Forwarded-For` header (#956)

### Improvements

- **Claude 4.7 and later, GPT 6**: requests retry without sampling settings and with adaptive thinking on models that reject `temperature`; GPT 6 models show their reasoning; suggested models updated to Claude 5 and GPT 6; Bedrock model ids fixed to use inference profiles (#951)
- **Provider error hints**: provider errors are classified into 12 kinds, each with a hint the user can act on and an "Open model settings" button (#951). When the server's own key is refused, the chat shows a quota hint instead of two unhelpful lines (#953)
- **Output token budget**: `maxOutputTokens` is always sent (#915) and the default is raised to 64000 with a retry at the provider's limit, so reasoning models reach the tool call instead of ending without a diagram (#927)
- **Self-hosted deployments**: the MCP server card is hidden when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SELFHOSTED` is true (#711); `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is accepted as an alternative to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (#853); suggested models refreshed for all providers (#863); `env.example` lists every provider (#881)
- **Accessibility**: the viewport no longer blocks pinch zoom on phones (#881)

### Security

- **SSRF in `/api/parse-url`**: private and internal URLs are blocked (#845), including private IPv6 (#858), DNS rebinding and redirects (#878). Advisory GHSA-wqcv-5qvx-vx75
- **MCP preview page XSS**: the session id is validated and the history panel no longer uses `innerHTML` (#951). Advisories GHSA-jx8r-j32j-q3mq and GHSA-rv7m-56x2-7q2c
- **Chat route hardening**: file parts only accept `data:` URLs, server credentials only run server models, a client base URL for Vertex only works with the client's own key; helper routes share the access code check and have body size limits (#951)
- **Admin settings**: the settings file target is validated before it is reported writable (#894)
- **Dependencies**: vulnerable packages updated (#804), esbuild security update (#867)

### Bug Fixes

- **Image input**: the name-based "model does not support images" check is removed, so vision-capable models such as Qwen and Kimi are no longer blocked (#326, #877); DeepSeek V4 Vision receives images after the SDK update (#934, #951)
- **MCP exports**: export replies are tagged by request, so an autosave SVG is never saved as the PNG export and parallel page exports no longer write the wrong image (#795, #951)
- **Model test**: validation uses the same client as chat, including Azure OpenAI's `createAzure`, and its output budget is raised from 20 to 1024 tokens so models that think before answering pass the test (#820, #884, #951)
- **Ollama**: chat requests go to Ollama's `/api` path again (#954); the desktop server bypasses the system proxy for localhost (#951)
- **Multi-page diagrams**: autosave, history and `.drawio` download keep every page after an export (#895)
- **Stop button**: a stop or a closed tab reaches the provider even after a garbage collection pause (#965)
- **Streaming edits**: cut-off cell XML is refused in `edit_diagram` operations, so the canvas no longer jumps out of view while an edit streams (#960)
- **MCP `edit_diagram` freshness**: the 30 second time gate is replaced by a content comparison (#890)
- **Sessions and canvas**: restoring a session no longer replays the last drawing over the saved diagram, a failed or stopped edit restores the canvas, XML repair no longer corrupts valid diagrams, storage errors are reported and chats are never deleted silently (#951)
- **Chat input**: template dialogs no longer send the message, sending waits for file extraction, an IME Enter no longer sends (#951)
- **Desktop app**: API keys are decrypted after `ready` so Windows and Linux get them, config writes are atomic with a backup of a corrupt file, navigation away from the app is blocked (#951)
- **Bedrock**: tool streaming works under Zod v4 (#860)
- **Model selector**: long labels no longer overflow (#910)
- **Validation retry**: the retry counter is cleaned up when the visual check throws (#881)

### Developer Experience

- E2E tests run in six shards (#959); the MCP server is published to npm through OIDC trusted publishing (#891); the Docker image carries provenance and SBOM attestations (#902)
- Biome pinned and `public/` excluded from formatting (#869, #912); the MCP package check reads npm 12's pack output (#952)

# v0.12.1

**Every install path works again, and Helm charts join the graph.**

v0.12.1 fixes v0.12.0's package installs and the other install paths we found broken while checking every channel. It also links Helm charts to what they deploy, and stops the graph from inventing a registry for container images.

> **Upgrading?** The first index of each existing project after the upgrade is a full rebuild, once (image identities changed; see below).

## Fixed: installs

- **npm, PyPI and Go installs.** `npm i`, `pnpm add`, `pip install` and the Go wrapper could not install v0.12.0 on any platform. Each wrapper refused an archive member above 256 MiB, and every v0.12.0 binary is 331-335 MB. The size limits are gone from all three wrappers. The archive is still verified against the release's `checksums.txt` before it is unpacked, its contents must be exactly the expected files, and the binary must answer `--version`. Thank you, @hydroplexus, for the precise report (#2657).
- **Homebrew.** The formula was still at 0.10.3, and on Linux it installed the dynamically linked build, which needs glibc 2.38 (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and RHEL 9 do not have it). It now installs the current release, and on Linux the static `-portable` build that runs on any distribution.
- **`go install`.** A pinned `go install .../pkg/go/cmd/codebase-memory-mcp@vX.Y.Z` never worked, and `@latest` installed a stale version. Releases now carry `pkg/go/vX.Y.Z` tags, and the wrapper installs the release matching its own version.
- **npm `next`.** The `next` dist-tag no longer points to an old release candidate; a stable release moves it.
- **Docs.** winget and Chocolatey were listed as install channels but are not published; they are removed until they are. Windows arm64 builds ship and are now listed.

**Install-path smoke tests.** Every pull request and every release now installs the npm, PyPI and Go wrappers, the way a user's package manager does, against the real release archives, and runs the binary each one installed. A release is published only after these installs pass, so an installer that cannot install what we ship can no longer reach you.

## Helm charts in the graph

A Helm chart used to be an isolated node. Now it links to what it deploys (#2663):

- **Chart → objects** (`DEPLOYS`, `via: chart`): every Kubernetes object rendered from the chart's `templates/` (a subchart's objects belong to the subchart).
- **values file → Chart** (`CONFIGURES`): `values.yaml` and `values-<x>.yaml` beside `Chart.yaml`.
- **Chart → images** (`DEPLOYS`, `ref: image`): every image its objects name literally (a templated image names none).

`HelmRelease → Chart → Deployment → Image` is now one traversable path. On 20 infrastructure repositories, charts with no outgoing edge dropped from 238 of 260 to 109, and 2,511 chart-to-object links appeared; every other edge stayed identical.

## Images keep the registry the code names

An image without a registry host used to be stored under an invented `docker.io/library/...` (#2654). Docker Hub is only Docker's default: Podman and CRI-O resolve short names through a search list, mirrors rewrite them, and a local build tag may exist on no registry at all. An image now keeps its name as written, with `registry: unknown` when no host is stated; a stated host is kept (Docker Hub's spellings become `docker.io`). `FROM nginx` and `image: docker.io/library/nginx` are now two Image nodes. This changes image identities, which is why each project is rebuilt once after the upgrade.

## Upgrade notes

- The first index of each existing project after the upgrade is a full rebuild, once.
- Image nodes without a stated registry now carry `registry: unknown` and the name as written, instead of `docker.io/library/...`.

# Devolutions UniGetUI 2026.3.3

This release lets you add your own installers to the Software Catalog, adds Extensions starting with Git Repositories, lets you choose package list columns by right-clicking the header, and asks for confirmation before uninstalling or ignoring several packages. It also fixes many WinGet, PowerShell and Scoop update bugs.

### New Features
* The Software Catalog can now offer installers: .exe and .msi on Windows, and .pkg, .dmg and .zip on macOS. They are served from a shared folder or a web folder and can be installed, updated and uninstalled like any other package
* The Catalog Editor is now hidden behind its own setting, under Settings > Experimental
* Added Extensions in Settings, starting with Git Repositories. It keeps your local Git clones up to date on their default branch and shows their worktrees and branches. Extensions are off by default.
* You can now choose which columns a package list shows by right-clicking its header. Changes apply right away.
* Added an optional Release date column to package lists.
* You can update an ignored package once from **Manage ignored updates**, and it stays ignored afterwards.
* Scoop can now install a specific version.
* Added a Release notes item to the right-click menu on Software Updates.
* `unigetui://package` links now open a package's details.
* You can now hide the tray icon while UniGetUI keeps running in the background.
* Added an option to quit UniGetUI once automatic updates have finished.

### Improvements
* UniGetUI now asks for confirmation before uninstalling packages, and before ignoring updates for several packages at once.
* On first launch, package managers whose tool isn't installed are now turned off, and pages say when no package manager is available instead of reporting that everything is up to date.
* Cargo no longer needs `cargo-binstall` or `cargo-update`.
* `update-all` and `update-manager` commands now work in headless mode.
* In-app dialogs now close when you click the dimmed area around them.
* Toolbar buttons are disabled when they have nothing to act on.
* The operations panel now counts failed operations separately.
* The search settings in the filter pane are grouped into one collapsed **Search options** section.
* On macOS, the menu bar icon now matches the menu bar's color, and the window buttons sit inside the glass sidebar.
* Improved Tab and Shift+Tab navigation in tabbed pages.

### Bug Fixes
* Fixed Bun packages not being listed when Bun uses a custom install folder.
* Fixed logging out or shutting down on Linux being blocked by UniGetUI.
* Fixed long translated labels being cut off on the package details action button.
* Fixed npm not being found on macOS when it is installed through nvm.
* Fixed operations that need administrator rights failing in headless mode.
* Fixed Store and MSIX apps showing names like `ms-resource:AppStoreName`.
* Fixed the Close button stopping short of the window's right edge.
* Fixed the swapped package counts in the page subtitle.
* Fixed updates not appearing for packages with very large version numbers, such as Scoop nightly builds.
* Fixed updates running even when an app listed under "Close apps before installing" couldn't be closed.

Thank you to everyone who reported issues and contributed improvements to the project.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/Devolutions/UniGetUI/compare/v2026.3.2...v2026.3.3

# v2.7.3 插件发布

本次发布 DSH 插件，基于当前主线并包含 #709 的真实工具集兼容修复。桌面应用版本及官方桌面安装包保持原状。

## 免费车道兼容

- 官方 OpenCode 推理路径接入原生 Bun 传输，补全缺失的环境信息，并一次性迁移旧的哈希派生会话映射；同一会话继续稳定复用 ID。
- 针对已复现的真实 DSH 工具集拒绝，为 `subagent_fork`、`working_directory` 使用可逆出站别名。工具描述、参数及宿主实际执行能力保留；响应恢复原名，别名碰撞会自动避让。
- 修复 Chat 历史消息同时带有 `content: []` 和 `tool_calls` 时漏改工具名的问题。
- 取消 HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 代理握手或关闭中继时立即清理出口连接，避免继续等待独立握手超时。

## 账号渠道与连接稳定性

- EAC router 对各渠道可明确识别的排队响应提供同渠道、同模型的账号轮换，保留已启用账号、余额及模型限制策略。
- 修复排队与额度换号后的实际账号归属、认证续期预算，以及 OpenCode 匿名槽与账号槽的轮换；已经向下游输出后不重放请求。
- 客户端断开或取消时及时关闭上游响应并释放并发槽，减少残留连接及无效占用。

## 安全升级与维护

- 宿主无法安全热重载时，验证并安装新版本后明确提示重启生效；待重启期间阻止再次安装，保留回滚备份。
- 识别由包管理器管理的安装，继续通过宿主的安装与更新流程维护程序。
- 渠道包构建增加功能标记检查，避免重新构建时退回旧能力。
- 中英文 README 同步交流群12、群号 `1130235133` 及新二维码。

## 安装前提

**默认 OpenCode 免费推理需要自行安装原生 Bun。插件不会自动下载或安装 Bun。** 可以用 `OUR_FREE_MODEL_BUN` 指定可执行文件；查找路径和传输设置见 [免费车道传输说明](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model/blob/v2.7.3/docs/oc-free-transport.md)。

`OUR_FREE_MODEL_FREE_TRANSPORT=node` 可切回此前的 Node 传输用于诊断，但不保证上游接受。上述兼容修复不解除真实额度、地区或账号限制，也不承诺所有 429 均可恢复。

自行安装的旧版用户可在插件升级页检查更新；宿主管理的安装请通过原安装方式更新可信 tarball。手工安装使用本次完整插件包，保留原有用户数据目录，不要仅替换入口文件。

## 回退

升级器继续执行原有签名、文件大小、SHA-256、备份与回滚校验。手工回退使用上一版可信插件包，并保留配置、账号及统计数据。


## 本次发布验证

- 完整 `npm test` 108/108 套件通过，包含生产签名发布检查、原版 1.3.1 与 2.5.9 升级回归；根目录及独立端类型检查、生成产物一致性检查通过。
- 发布 PR 四项 CI 全部通过，合并后的 main 检查与签名工作流通过。
- tarball 从固定提交的 LF 字节构建，全部 80 个运行时文件逐字节匹配正式签名清单，解包后入口加载通过。
- 使用原版 2.5.9 升级器从公开固定提交地址完成下载、生产验签和安装，80 个运行时文件摘要一致，测试用户数据保留；新入口在全新进程中加载成功。此项不代表真实 DSH 宿主中的热重载已验收。
- raw、jsDelivr、gcore jsDelivr、gh-proxy 四个默认更新源均完成全部文件的 SHA-256 与回读校验。CDN 已整树刷新。
- 本机没有原生 Bun 或 darwin-arm64 工作台引擎，相关原生进程测试跳过；未调用真实模型上游，未执行桌面端工具调用验收。

## Highlights

### New analysis mode: `/understand-figma` (#559) — by @gruming

Point the tool at a Figma file and get the same navigable knowledge graph you get for code: pages → screens → components/variants/instances, plus a light design-system model (design tokens and `uses_token` edges). Deterministic parsing via the Figma REST API, LLM enrichment via a new `design-analyzer` agent, screen thumbnails in the dashboard sidebar, incremental `UP_TO_DATE` re-runs, and `FIGMA_TOKEN` kept strictly in the request header. Schema additions are backward compatible (6 node types, 3 edge types, `kind:"design"`). Follow-up fixes landed for real-API style-key bridging, published component keys, kind-scoped alias normalization, and dashboard edge-category filters.

### Data directory renamed to `.ua/` — fully backward compatible

Analysis artifacts now live in `.ua/` instead of `.understand-anything/`. Projects analyzed by older versions need **no migration**: when a legacy `.understand-anything/` directory exists it keeps being used for both reads and writes. The resolution rule is implemented once in core (`resolveUaDir`) and honored by every bundled script, skill, agent definition, hook, and the dashboard dev server.

### New language support

- **Dart** (#435) and **C++ test/benchmark ignore patterns** (#480, #466) — by @thejesh23
- **Scala** (#553, from #493) and **Swift** (#537) — by @KumamuKuma
- **Kotlin** (#347) — by @tirth8205
- Modern TS type-declaration extraction fixes (#532) — by @jiang4wqy

### New platform support

- **Kiro** (#364) — by @smjeong84
- **Nanobot** (#419) — by @chengyongru
- **Trae** (#235) — by @ZebangCheng
- Windows `install.ps1` vibe support (#550) and Windows test portability (#531, #538, #551) — by @KumamuKuma

### Merge-pipeline reliability

- Structural subdomain edges (`contains_flow`/`flow_step`/`cross_domain`) are no longer silently dropped: loud warnings, a persisted `merge-report.json`, and automatic retry on the next run (#529).
- Batch files that load but contribute zero nodes/edges are flagged in the phase report instead of vanishing into a partial merge (#484).
- Karpathy wiki parser handles title-case `Index.md`/`Log.md` and article-root-prefixed `[[wiki/...]]` links (#342).
- Cross-layer container layout cache fix (#541) — by @computersniper; UTF-8 domain context on Windows (#524) — by @multimail-dev; Phase 7 cleanup and scan-result preservation fixes (#387, #332) — by @tirth8205 and @ZebangCheng.

### Security hardening

- Skill-injection ReDoS hardening (#557) — by @jiang4wqy
- Recursive subagent dispatch prevention (#560) — by @crow-1412

### Pipeline performance & DX

- Semantic batching and output chunking (#204), `/understand` pipeline perf (#346) — by @tirth8205
- Conversation-language auto-detection on first run (#378) — by @BozhengLong
- Config schema validation tests (#471) — by @yiziff; CI on Node 24 runtimes.

## What's New in v1.15.0

You can now install OpenSpec without Node.js, using one command, and `openspec update` can now show what it would change before changing anything.

### New

- **Standalone install** - Install OpenSpec with one command and no Node.js: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/main/scripts/binary/install.sh | sh` on macOS and Linux, or `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/main/scripts/binary/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows. Every release now ships binaries for macOS, Linux (glibc and musl) and Windows on x64 and arm64, with `SHA256SUMS`. npm and the other package managers keep working as before.
- **`openspec update --dry-run`** - Reports the files an update would add, change or delete without writing anything; add `--json` for machine-readable output.

### Improved

- **Faster `--json` commands** - `status`, `instructions`, `new change`, `templates`, `validate` and `schema` no longer load the spinner package when run with `--json`, so they start a little faster. Output is unchanged.
- **`openspec feedback`** - Filed issues now match the bug form, and the manual-submission link opens the bug form with your message, version and environment filled in.

### Fixed

- **`openspec new change`** - The progress line now names the schema the change is actually created with, instead of always saying `spec-driven`.
- **`/opsx:verify`** - A REMOVED requirement is matched to its baseline by its exact name, so a similarly named replacement is no longer mistaken for it.

Graphify-Labs/graphify:
## 0.9.97 (2026-10-27)

- Security: **rationale redaction** credential redaction for rationale labels moves to a single pre-cache choke point (`_redact_rationale_labels` inside `_safe_extract`), so no extractor can skip it, and it now covers more leak shapes: URL userinfo with an empty user or with `/`/`@` in the password, PEM private-key bodies, tokens glued to surrounding text by `_` (for example `ghp_...`), Slack `xoxe-` refresh tokens, short JWTs, and Common Lisp docstrings that previously built labels without redacting. Benign strings (hashes, `sk-` prose, URLs without userinfo) are left alone (#4647, thanks @0xkaushik-ai).
- Security: **deps** anyio is floored to `>=4.14.2` in the `mcp` extra, above CVE-2026-63374 (an IDNA 2003 vs 2008 hostname-validation bypass that let a MITM on a non-ASCII domain present a cert for a different ASCII host, CVSS 9.3). anyio is only a transitive dependency and the lockfile already resolves 4.15.1, so this is a floor to stop a future re-resolution from regressing.
- Fix: **markdown** ATX headings parse per CommonMark: a trailing run of `#` is not part of the heading text (`## Setup ##` is "Setup"), up to three spaces of indent are allowed (four is an indented code block), and a hash-only line like `## ##` mints no node (#4790, #4791, thanks @jaimemartinez).
- Fix: **markdown** fenced code blocks are tracked by CommonMark rules (backtick and tilde fences, info strings, matching close length), so a line that looks like a heading inside a fence no longer leaks as structure, and a heading after a `~~~` block that contains a ` ``` ` line is no longer lost (#4787, #4788, thanks @jaimemartinez).
- Fix: **yaml** structural extraction reads the composed node tree, so keys carry their written spelling and their own source line instead of all landing on line 1, and YAML 1.1 bare keys like `on`/`off`/`yes`/`no` are no longer folded to booleans (a workflow `on:` block is extracted, not turned into a `True` node) (#4784, #4785, thanks @jaimemartinez).
- Fix: **razor** a component's `@implements` interfaces are extracted as `implements` edges instead of being silently dropped (#4820, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **terraform** an aliased provider block gets its own alias-qualified node (so two `provider "aws"` blocks no longer collapse into one and lose attributes), and a `provider = aws.west` reference resolves to it instead of dangling; a `local` literally named `provider` is no longer misread (#4819, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **cobol** paragraphs that follow a nested `END PROGRAM` reattach to the enclosing program instead of sticking to the nested one, via a program stack (#4824, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **blade** a `wire:click` directive binds the bare method name: dotted modifiers (`wire:click.prevent="submit"`) are matched, call arguments are trimmed from the name (`deleteItem(5)` binds `deleteItem`), and a `$`-prefixed magic action mints no fabricated edge (#4823, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **pascal** a `record` is recognised as a type with its own methods in the regex fallback (the default path without the optional `pascal` extra), matching the tree-sitter path; `operator` members are extracted too (#4825, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **vbnet** an `Operator` declaration is extracted as an `operator`-kind member of its class and its body is walked for calls, so a helper call inside an operator no longer vanishes (#4821, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **fortran** a `call` resolves to the subroutine it actually names instead of a target salted with the calling file's name (which never resolved), using the extractor's own cross-file stub idiom (#4795, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **cli** `graphify query --help`/`-h` (and now `graphify explain --help`/`-h`) with nothing else prints usage instead of running a literal query for the text "--help"; a longer question that merely contains "--help" as a substring still runs as a query (#4830, thanks @curl-man).
- Fix: **js** a nested (inner) function no longer leaks into the file-wide name map, so a call elsewhere in the file binds to the top-level function of that name rather than an inner one it cannot see; recursion, shadowing and sibling scopes resolve correctly (ports the Python scope scheme to JS/TS) (#4767, thanks @smngvlkz).
- Fix: **ocaml** every binding in an `and`-chained `module ... and ...` or `class ... and ...` is extracted, not just the first, so later bindings are no longer silently dropped; each carries its own source line (#4822, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **verilog** a SystemVerilog class `task` method is modeled like a `function` one (its own node, `method` edge and parameter-type references), and a task-local variable no longer leaks as a false field reference on the class (#4774, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **build** an edge with no `relation` is dropped instead of persisted, on both the build and the raw `--no-cluster` write paths, and alias folding (`relationship` to `relation`) runs before the check (#4810, thanks @legendteddy; reproducer also filed as #4826 by @sunhouy).
- Fix: **build** the shrink guard counts a saved document-mention node that folds into its AST file twin on reload as present, not lost, so a cluster-only write is no longer refused when nothing was actually lost (#4778, #4779, thanks @AndresDiagoM).
- Fix: **detect** a linked git worktree whose main checkout resolves inside the scan root is pruned, so a sibling worktree no longer gets indexed as a second full copy of the repo (#4683, #4833, thanks @barlowa124; duplicate work in #4685 by @AndresDiagoM).
- Fix: **resolution** an inline comment in a pnpm-workspace glob is stripped per YAML rules, and a glob that `Path.glob` rejects (a `**` component or an absolute pattern) is skipped with a warning instead of crashing the whole `extract` run (#4681, #4687, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **report** a community hub `[[wikilink]]` is slugged through the same `export._obsidian_safe_stem` the export uses, so the link matches the file the export actually writes instead of dangling (#4696, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **wiki** a community relabelled only by letter case keeps its article instead of having the sweep delete the file the run just wrote; on a case-sensitive filesystem the stale lower-case twin is unlinked rather than renamed over the fresh file (which would silently restore the old body) (#4508, #4798, thanks @dupeisen).
- Fix: **query** filler verbs `get`/`gets`/`got`/`getting` are dropped from query terms (like the existing `work`/`works`), so a framework hub labelled "Get" is not pulled in as a BFS seed by an exact-match bonus; node lookups for a literal `Get` still resolve (#4686, thanks @AndresDiagoM).

HKUDS/nanobot:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.4.0`** makes everyday work easier to continue — with durable conversation history, a more capable workbench, and a clearer path to the next update.

**Keep moving.** The gateway now stores model history and browser transcripts in SQLite, imports existing conversations, and coordinates updates around saved state. Stable and opt-in Preview releases share one update flow, with explicit confirmation before installation and restart.

The browser workbench is easier to navigate and connect: complete prompt-history navigation, remote instances, clearer delegated-task details, richer attachments, and more consistent mobile controls. The terminal gains Mermaid diagram viewing and target-specific native bundles. Both clients continue to use the same Python gateway.

This release also makes installation ownership explicit. Supported managed installations can update and recover the program through the app; other installations receive instructions for their original package manager or deployment. Recovery does not mean restoring an old copy of your chats. Please read the upgrade notes before replacing an existing installation.

## Highlights

- **One update flow, with your confirmation** — Check releases in Settings → About, choose whether to receive Preview updates, review the exact version, and confirm installation and restart. Supported official-installer and POSIX uv environments can use the in-app flow once the public release has verified approval proof.
- **Recovery that protects current data** — Installer-managed updates can attempt repair and, when safe, restore the original program and service. Configuration and conversations are not automatically replaced with an older backup. Installation owners outside that flow keep their own repair route.
- **Durable conversation history** — SQLite brings model history and WebUI display history under gateway ownership. Existing JSONL history is imported with source backups retained. Paging, live-output reconciliation, queued follow-ups and goal continuation receive reliability fixes.
- **A clearer browser workbench** — Navigate the full prompt history with bounded loading, search loaded messages and session handles, rename topics inline, and archive topics in batches. Delegated tasks have clearer run state and detail views.
- **Your workbench, on the right host** — Connect to existing remote instances with explicit host identity, pairing and reconnect feedback. Update instructions identify the gateway computer, rather than assuming it is the device displaying the page.
- **Richer files and a better small-screen experience** — Local-file and video attachments, image thumbnails, file cards, Markdown source views, reading-size controls, and touch and theme improvements. External websites open in the browser instead of an arbitrary embedded preview.
- **Diagrams in the terminal** — View, zoom, pan and copy Mermaid diagrams without leaving the conversation. Platform wheels contain the matching native TUI and built WebUI; supported wheel installations need neither Bun nor a first-launch TUI download.
- **More control over models and integrations** — Searchable providers, explicit API choices, per-preset request overrides, shared proxy choices, Linear and WhatsApp Agent Platform channels, QQ QR setup, and DeepSeek Search. Scheduled jobs can be edited, enabled and disabled in place, with recent runs available for inspection.
- **A fix for Windows idle memory growth** — Process-status polling now reuses native type and API bindings on Python versions before 3.14, while keeping live process checks and handle cleanup.

## Upgrade Notes

- **Distribution availability.** The verified v0.4.0 packages are available in this GitHub Release and on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/nanobot-ai/0.4.0/). In-app automatic installation is not enabled for this release yet: it requires verified release approval proof and the applicable public release sources. Publishing these files does not enroll users in Preview or start an update.
- **Upgrade v0.3.5 through its original installation method first.** That release does not contain this new in-app updater. Run the installer, package manager or container replacement on the gateway computer under its original OS account. Existing installations are not silently converted into official-installer environments. Follow the [installation-owner instructions](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/updating.md#installation-owners), including recorded extras, constraints and custom options.
- **Stop shared writers and back up the complete instance.** Finish active work, stop all nanobot processes using the environment or data, and back up the selected configuration directory and workspace together. Include authentication, sessions and WebUI state. Do not copy only a live SQLite database file. After upgrading, use the original launcher, check the running version, open older conversations, write a new message and verify another restart.
- **SQLite changes the downgrade procedure.** JSONL import remains available throughout 0.4.x; older JSONL-only installations must pass through an import-capable release before 0.5.0. Keep imported source backups and the old WebUI directory. Older versions cannot read new SQLite display history. A downgrade requires a stopped-writer backup-restoration procedure that accounts for messages created since the backup; it is not an automatic data rollback. See [Session Storage](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/cli-reference.md#session-storage).
- **An update can restart the gateway.** Confirming installation can interrupt running tasks. Turning Preview off saves the subscription but does not downgrade an installed Preview. Recovery cannot guarantee service restoration after permanent storage damage, incompatible data writes, or loss of both recovery processes. Missing or unverifiable public assets must not be treated as a successful install. See [Updating nanobot](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/updating.md).
- **Fresh official-installer instances stay in the background.** Their normal WebUI launcher starts a persistent instance. Closing the terminal or browser does not stop it; use `nanobot gateway stop` with the same configuration and workspace selectors. Existing unrecorded installations retain their original lifecycle. Local macOS WebUI sessions can show a Dock icon; `--no-dock` suppresses it.
- **Review migrated configuration before saving.** Legacy proxy conversion remains supported in 0.4.x. The old OpenAI `apiType` / `api_type` selector is converted to `api` in 0.4.0 and the immediately following release; save the current format during that window. See [Configuration](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/configuration.md).
- **Platform requirements remain explicit.** Python 3.11+ is required. Native wheels target macOS 13+ arm64/x64, glibc 2.17+ Linux arm64/x64, and Windows x64; x64 requires SSE4.2. Windows ARM64 and musl Linux do not have native wheels. Chinese terminal diagrams require suitable installed fonts: Heiti SC on macOS, Noto Sans CJK on Linux, or Microsoft YaHei on Windows. Diagram source remains accessible if rendering is unavailable.
- **Keep container data volumes and reconnect clients.** Replace the container through its deployment owner; do not upgrade packages inside a running container. Reconnect or reload WebUI/TUI clients after upgrading the intended gateway, and follow any client/host compatibility guidance shown.

## Community

Thank you to everyone who contributed code, reviewed changes, reported problems, supplied reproductions and tested nanobot in everyday use. Clear bug reports and useful use cases remain important contributions. We want the agent to stay small and inspectable while becoming easier to rely on for daily work.

## Upgrade Notice

Before updating HandBrake, please make sure there are no pending encodes in the queue, and be sure to make a backup of any custom presets and app preferences you have, as they may not be compatible with newer versions.

Windows users, please make sure to install [Microsoft .NET Desktop Runtime version 10.0](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0/runtime)
Download available from Microsoft:
- [For x64 (AMD or Intel CPUs)](https://aka.ms/dotnet/10.0/windowsdesktop-runtime-win-x64.exe)
- [For Arm64 (Qualcomm or other)](https://aka.ms/dotnet/10.0/windowsdesktop-runtime-win-arm64.exe)


## HandBrake 1.11.2

### All platforms

#### Video

- Fixed a crash that happened when doing a 2-pass lossless x265 encode
- Fixed a memory leak that happened when doing a 2-pass MPEG-4/MPEG-2/VP9/FFV1 encode

#### Audio

- Updated the list of supported dithers and encoders combinations
- Fixed the Core Audio AAC encoder 7.1 channel layout

#### Subtitles

- Fixed the VobSub palette creation in the MP4 container

#### Build system

- Improved build system compatibility with older build tools

#### Third-party libraries

- Updated libraries
  - FFmpeg 8.0.2 (decoding and filters)
  - SVT-AV1 4.1.0 (AV1 video encoding)

### Linux

- Added WebM MIME type to the list of the supported formats

### Mac

- Improved handling of unsupported presets
- Updated Sparkle automatic update library

### Windows

- Improved handling of unsupported presets
- Improved queue low space pause behaviour
- Fixed the automatic audio track name generation
- Fixed the summary description of HDR video

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

  - **pip installs: rotate your `SECRET_KEY` if other users on the machine can read your data directory.** Older versions saved the generated `SECRET_KEY` in `<data_dir>/.env` (`~/.local/share/label-studio/.env` on Linux) with permissions that let any local user read it. This release makes the file readable only by its owner, but a key that may already have been read stays valid until you change it. To rotate it, delete the `SECRET_KEY` line from `.env` (or set a new `SECRET_KEY` environment variable) and restart. Everyone will need to log in again, and existing access tokens stop working.
  - **Image exports skip media on private networks.** When `SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED=true` (the default), `COCO_WITH_IMAGES`, `YOLO_WITH_IMAGES` and `YOLO_OBB_WITH_IMAGES` exports no longer download media from private or local network addresses. The export still completes, but those images are left out of the archive. If your task media is hosted on an internal server, set `USE_DEFAULT_BANNED_SUBNETS=false` and list only the ranges you want blocked in `USER_ADDITIONAL_BANNED_SUBNETS`, or set `SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED=false`.
  - **Set `LABEL_STUDIO_HOST` so image exports can include uploaded files.** Exports now download files from Label Studio itself only when its address can be trusted: when `LABEL_STUDIO_HOST` is set, or when `ALLOWED_HOSTS` is restricted. On a default install with neither, uploaded files that aren't on the local disk (for example, when the default storage is S3, GCS or Azure) are left out of image exports.
  - **Uploaded HTML, SVG and XML files open in a sandbox.** When these files are opened from `/storage-data/uploaded/`, they are served with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, so scripts inside them don't run. Images, PDFs, audio and video aren't affected. If you run your own reverse proxy instead of the bundled nginx config, add the same header for these content types. See the `$uploaded_file_csp` map in `deploy/default.conf`.

  ## Security

  - The generated `SECRET_KEY` file (`<data_dir>/.env`) is now created readable only by its owner, and an existing file is restricted on startup. The data directory is also created readable only by its owner.
  - S3-compatible storage endpoints are now checked for private or local addresses every time a connection is opened, not only when the storage is saved. This blocks DNS rebinding. Storages saved before this check existed are also re-checked.
  - Image exports now block media URLs that point at private or local network addresses.
  - Image exports no longer send the organization owner's API token to a host taken from the request's `Host` header.
  - Uploaded HTML, SVG and XML files served from `/storage-data/uploaded/` are sandboxed, both when Django serves them directly and when they are served through the bundled nginx.
