JuliusBrussee/caveman:
Caveman 4.0.1 fixes what turned up in the first hours of 4.0.0: a Windows uninstall bug, a sync that could never catch up, and problems on OpenCode 2 and Pi.

### Windows

- `caveman off --all` left the Caveman Blocks hook in Claude Code's settings, and every `caveman setup` added another copy. Blocks v0.1.0-rc.5 installs its binary as `.exe`, recognises the entries rc.4 wrote, and replaces them on the next `caveman setup`.
- An npm `.cmd` shim that forwards to a native `.exe` launches again.
- Hook child processes no longer flash a console window.

### Sync

- `caveman sync` uploads a large backlog of local spans in batches. Before, a store over the 16 MiB import cap failed with "Request body exceeds configured limit" on every retry.
- The `ExperimentalWarning: SQLite` line is gone.
- Known issue: the practice-findings part of `caveman sync` still reports "Request rejected". That is a Caveman Cloud bug and needs no CLI update once Cloud is fixed.

### OpenCode

- On OpenCode 2, a subagent spawn reset the mode for every session, undoing "stop caveman" and `/ultracave`. Subagent sessions no longer touch the mode.
- The "provider is not routed" warning reads where a provider actually sends requests.

### Pi

- `caveman wrap pi` after `caveman enable pi` loaded the extension twice and Pi exited 1.
- Routing a model no longer resets the thinking level (`--thinking high` stayed only until session start).
- Works with Pi 1.1+ custom-message turns.
- `@caveman-ai/pi` 0.3.1: the npm package now reads Caveman 4's config and port.

### Claude Code and Codex

- The prompt hook gives up after 2 seconds when the host sends no complete payload, like the other hooks.
- Blocks honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME`; it used to write the hook into `~/.claude` regardless.
- `caveman status` no longer says "account refresh offline" after signing in to a different account.

### Smaller fixes

- Proxy: one key sent in both auth headers keeps its bearer; a Termux-built proxy is recognised as Caveman's own.
- Memory: longer retry on SQLite contention.
- `/caveman-compress` asks for a file path instead of improvising on pasted text, and says that the file goes to your model provider.
- Tested agent pins moved to current Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Kilo and Qwen releases.

### Versions

- `@caveman-ai/cli` 4.0.0 → 4.0.1, binaries `bin-v4.0.0` → `bin-v4.0.1`, `@caveman-ai/pi` 0.3.0 → 0.3.1, Blocks v0.1.0-rc.4 → v0.1.0-rc.5.

### Companion releases

- [Signed binaries, module index and container: `bin-v4.0.1`](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/releases/tag/bin-v4.0.1)
- [npm CLI: `@caveman-ai/cli@4.0.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@caveman-ai/cli/v/4.0.1)
- [npm Pi extension: `@caveman-ai/pi@0.3.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@caveman-ai/pi/v/0.3.1)
JustVugg/colibri:
169 pull requests since v1.12.1, 88 of them from contributors. Every MoE
engine now runs on any GPU a Vulkan driver can see: the routed experts on a
shared device tier, the dense layers on a device chain (all of them, or the
first N that fit), and a second GPU for more experts. Three model families
arrive (MiMo-V2.6, Qwen3-Coder, Qwen-Image-2.1) and one dense checkpoint
(Qwen3.8-27B). Qwen3.8 Flash Next gets int4 experts and speculative decoding
that is on by default. Every text engine serves up to 16 conversations at once.
The release archives carry the GPU backends. Setup is one step, and there is one
decision API (System One).

### Several conversations at once

- **#1955**: every text engine serves several conversations at once (`coli serve
  --kv-slots N`, up to 16), as GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 Flash did: qwen36 (Qwen3.6,
  Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3.8-27B), qwen38, OLMoE, Inkling, Kimi K3, MiMo-V2.6,
  DeepSeek V4 and V4.1. Each slot keeps its own conversation's state, and every
  decode step takes the next token of each active request as one batch, so the
  weights and experts a step reads serve all of them. A request gets the tokens
  it gets alone, checked frame for frame on every engine, on the CPU and with
  the expert tier. With more than one slot nothing drafts and the dense chain
  stays off.

### Vulkan on every engine

- **#1830**: every engine's resident matrices run on any Vulkan GPU (fmt 10, 11
  and 12 added), each configuration checked against the engine's own CPU run on
  Lavapipe (`tests/vulkan_engines.sh`).
- **#1834**: tiled GEMMs for prefill in every weight format, and a
  cooperative-matrix GEMM where the device has one.
- **#1840**, **#1843**: a shared routed-expert tier (`vk_tier.c`). It holds a
  cache of experts in device memory, filled from the expert history and adapting
  while you chat, and computes the resident experts of each step as one async
  batch while the CPU computes the rest. First on qwen38 and qwen36, then on
  every MoE engine: GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 Flash, Inkling, OLMoE, Kimi K3, MiMo-V2.6,
  DeepSeek V4 and V4.1.
- **#1844**, **#1848**, **#1849**, **#1851**, **#1857**: the dense chain
  (`vk_chain.c`), a layer's dense part in one submission, on qwen36, qwen38,
  MiMo-V2.6 (sliding window and sinks on the device), OLMoE, Inkling (and
  OLMoE's PILOT race fixed), GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 Flash (shared MLA, DSA, KDA and
  mHC ops), Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4.1 and DeepSeek V4.
- **#1871**: staged device-local uploads for cards without Resizable BAR, where
  the mapped path failed or spilled to system RAM.
- **#1901**: expert streaming for big prompt steps, memory budgets and
  speculative verification on the device.
- **#1909**, **#1913**, **#1916**, **#1918**: a partial dense chain. The first N
  layers that fit go to the device, the CPU runs the rest, and nothing is
  uploaded that the chain will not use, so an 8 GB card with a larger trunk keeps
  the chain and its expert tier instead of losing both. `COLI_VK_CHAIN_LAYERS`
  forces N, `coli plan` predicts it. DeepSeek V4, qwen36 and olmoe, qwen38,
  GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 Flash.
- **#1920**: a second GPU for the expert tier (`COLI_VK_DEV2=auto|<index>`) on
  every MoE engine: the experts after the primary device's, each step one batch
  per device, both in flight at once. A failing second device gives its experts
  back to the CPU and the tier goes on with the first.
- **#1942**: the dense chain's layers on two GPUs. With `COLI_VK_DEV2`, the
  layers a partial chain leaves go to the second device instead of the CPU, on
  every chain engine (qwen36, qwen38, OLMoE, MiMo-V2.6, Inkling, GLM-5.2,
  GLM-5.3 Flash, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4.1 and V4). `COLI_VK_CHAIN_LAYERS2` forces
  how many, `COLI_VK_CHAIN_DEV2=0` keeps them off. A lost second device leaves
  the CPU to run its layers, the recurrent state rebuilt where it was held.
  Checked on Lavapipe opened twice; two real GPUs not measured yet.
- **#1933**: `COLI_VK_KV_COLD=device` (opt-in): with the KV cache split past the
  device's budget, the host's part of the attention runs on the device too, from
  host memory it reads in place, so a step runs in one frame. The prompt gains
  4-6% on a Radeon 780M, decode is slower there (hence off by default); a
  dedicated GPU has not been measured.
- **#1948**: several conversations at once on the dense chain. colibri's
  multiplexed decode (`KV_SLOTS`, one row from each active conversation) runs on
  the device: the batch's matrices as one, each row's attention over its own
  conversation's KV mirror (up to `COLI_VK_CHAIN_MUX`, default 16, beside the
  chain's own) with its own DSA list; two devices and the partial chain too.
  Every frame checked against the CPU's on Lavapipe; not measured with a real
  checkpoint yet.
- **#1934**, **#1935**, **#1936**, **#1937**, **#1938**, **#1939** (@huppiflupp):
  the matrix units for prompt attention and int8/int4 prompt GEMMs on the
  chain, a step's experts as one grouped GEMM (decode: one grouped GEMV per
  phase), qwen36's routing in parallel, and int8 decode GEMVs sized by the
  matrix. On a Radeon 780M with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B the first token of a
  1000-token prompt comes in 9.3 s instead of 12.6, decode 6.1 tok/s instead
  of 5.7, perplexity unchanged.
- **#1954**: on an Intel GPU the dense chain decoded garbage (Qwen3.6 on an Iris
  Xe, the default there). Its pipelines now run at the subgroup size the device
  reports; the device compiles at 8 to 32 lanes, and the chain's GEMVs had run
  at another width than the one they read. On Windows the chain also finds its
  optional shaders (MLA, KDA, mHC, DeepSeek V4, the split KV cache), and the
  split cache frees its host memory with the matching call.
- **#1911**: `COLI_VK_DEV=<index>` picks the device on a machine with two GPUs of
  the same kind; the cooperative GEMM's epilogue stride is aligned to 16 bytes, a
  validation error on some drivers (#1908).
- **#1846** (@crichalchemist): correct expert-batch results under MoltenVK's
  default mode.
- **#1762**, **#1763** (@Kenneth-Javier): the Vulkan loader linked on Windows
  under `-static`, and the Vulkan objects linked into every engine-including
  test rule.

### Models

- **#1813**, **#1819**, **#1820**, **#1827**, **#1835**: MiMo-V2.6 (Flash and
  Pro): the engine, the vision tower, tool calling and Brio mode with logprobs,

- **#1777**, **#1779**: dense checkpoints of the Qwen3.6 family on the qwen36

- **#1780**: Qwen-Image-2.1, text to image: a C engine, pictures in the
  terminal, the web app and the OpenAI images API.
- **#1951**: Qwen-Image on the GPU and a faster start. The weights load in
  7.5 s instead of 34 (four layers at once, quantized straight from bf16, the

- **#1831**: Qwen3.8 Flash Next's routed experts as int4-g64: 1.4 to 1.56x

- **#1832**, **#1917**: speculative decoding with the checkpoint's MTP head,
  lossless, +12-14% on the release; with #1917 it is on by default with prompt
  lookup on every engine that has it (`Q38_MTP=0`, `COLI_LOOKUP=0` turn them
  off), and `coli plan` counts the MTP head's memory.
- **#1814**: Inkling reads the embedding norm under the name transformers 5.18
  writes.

### System One: one decision API

- **#1856**: `POST /v1/systemone`, one decision API, and the Laya decision
  engine; `/v1/brio` is removed.
- **#1868**: GLiNER2.5-Decide as a native decision engine (DeBERTa-v3 and
  GLiNER2's head).
- **#1872**: Clef as a native decision model on qwen36, a joint head over

- **#1743**: the brio serve gates run in CI against the converted fixture.
- **#1753** (@tarazum): brio normalizes to sum by default and warns when a mean
  mixes option token counts.

### Setup and the CLI

- **#1953**: the release archives carry the GPU backends: every Linux and
  Windows engine built with Vulkan and its shaders, the macOS engines with
  Metal, and a Windows CUDA package (`coli_cuda.dll` for compute 8.0 and newer,

- **#1842**: one-step install and start (`start-here`, `coli setup`), the

- **#1850**, **#1896**: setup picks the backend that works on the machine: on an

- **#1903**: an engine already built is brought up to date with `make` before it

- **#1817**: in `coli chat`, a line that starts with a picture's path is a

### The serve contract

- **#1353** (@monotophic): `logprobs`, `top_logprobs` and `echo` on the OpenAI

  `preserve_thinking` rendered so standard clients get KV prefix reuse.
- **#1802** (@bherald): opt-in strict GLM tool-call parsing.
- **#1765** (@SulimanAbdulrazzaq): GLM-5.3's reasoning stays out of the
  `/v1/messages` answer.
- **#1791**, **#1793** (@Avicennasis): Anthropic image blocks are served and a
  tool result's picture is not dropped; the modalities a model card claims are
  the ones the engine loaded.
- **#1787**, **#1804** (@benmaster82): unsupported OpenAI result shaping is
  refused; the completions keepalive streams as a text chunk.
- **#1782**, **#1783**, **#1785**, **#1786** (@kevin9327): malformed tool calls,
  text parts, tools, messages and image URLs answer 400 instead of 500.
- **#1809** (@Stamina9): non-string brio message text is refused.
- **#1749**, **#1751**, **#1789**, **#1803** (@enitimeago): glm53 reports REUSE
  in detail and logs CANCEL, does not restore a pin over rows another branch
  rewrote, handles cancellation during prompt processing, and continues from the
  cache instead of prefilling again.

### Correctness and security

- **#1930**: hardening of three input paths. The files the engines keep beside a
  model (`.coli_kv`, `.coli_usage.tmp`, `hot_pinned.bin`, `.coli_ckpt/`) are
  opened without following a symlink and only as regular files, so a link
  planted in a downloaded model directory no longer redirects the engine's
  writes. Request grammars are limited to 32767 alternates and symbols per rule
  (past that the walker's index wrapped) and are refused with a message.
  colibri, kimi_k3 and deepseek_v41 check the indexer's and RoPE's head
  dimensions in the config.
- **#1739**, **#1740**, **#1754**, **#1755**, **#1854**, **#1855**
  (@namespaceMarcello): the published advisory fixes carried to glm53, qwen36 and
  deepseek_v41; glm53 refuses f32 tensors shorter than the config reads and
  matrices whose shape differs from it; deepseek_v41 keeps engram lookups inside
  their table; qwen36 gives the same logits at every expert-cache capacity on FMA
  builds and never evicts an expert a MoE run is still reading.
- **#1775**: the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 pre-tokenizer in `tok.h`, so Turkish
  tokenizes as HF does.
- **#1799** (@RayanR000): the DeepSeek V4.1 reference sends top-k ties to the
  lowest index and its indexer never keeps -inf.
- **#1812** (@ZacharyZcR): the shared-expert bindings of DeepSeek V4's fused MoE.
- **#1611** (@Cometbuster4969): OLMoE uses the shared RAM probe, with a
  plausibility floor.
- **#1744**, **#1745** (@kevin9327): a numeric `node_id` no longer kills the
  cluster's topology and health requests, and a manifest that is not a JSON
  object no longer crashes the experiments validator.
- **#1356** (@monotophic): the ablation scoring mode replaced by a checked,
  digest-bound one.
- **#1904**: DeepSeek V4's `PROF` measures the expert wait instead of printing 0
  and folding it into `attention_s` (#1852).
- **#1902**: Windows expert prefetch is asynchronous and its queued work bounded.

### Speed on the CPU

- **#1837**: every engine's per-token projections run per block of rows in
  prefill.
- **#1761** (@mfethe1): a NEON arm for batched `matmul_fp8`, bit-exact, 6 to 10x
  at prefill shapes.
- **#1790**, **#1798** (@RayanR000): the f32 matmul runs eight `fmaf` chains at
  once with the same bits on every FMA build, and one vectorized f32 matmul
  serves quant.h, olmoe, inkling and qwen36 (#442).
- **#1773** (@JackKnifeAI): glm53's dense prefill batched, bit-identical per
  token.
- **#1784** (@kreuzzelg): qwen36's DeltaNet layer on the card
  (`Q36_DN_GPU=1`), expert homes per layer range (`QT_HOME=layer`), the shared
  expert offered on request.
- **#1323**, **#1343** (@Avicennasis): qwen36 reads routed experts from a qpack
  container through bounded Metal slots, and MLX-affine dense weights and norms.
- **#1261** (@Kenneth-Javier): an optional explicit AMD XDNA2 lane for the GLM
  shared expert.

### Build, tests and CI

- **#1758** (@Kenneth-Javier): header prerequisites generated with `-MMD -MP`
  (#1741).
- **#1845**, **#1912**: the sanitizer runs and the bf16 gates hold on AVX-512
  runners, whose CPUs keep bf16 on the CPU.
- **#1914**: the Windows UCRT64 job's limit from 35 to 60 minutes.
- **#1795**, **#1821**, **#1836**, **#1839**: four flaky tests made
  deterministic.

### Docs

- **#1897**, **#1833**: the README rewritten for the release (one-step setup,
  models per machine, GPUs, System One) in five languages, with the site.
- **#1768**, **#1776**: every engine in the environment reference, DeepSeek V4.1
  in its own section, and the weights-from-disk options.
- **#1788** (@jamshaid120): duplicate entries removed from the DeepSeek V4 docs.
- **#1801** (@benmaster82): the web app's image alt count and German image
  labels.
- **#1738**: the 1.12.1 entry's pull request count corrected.

## 获取方式

### Docker（多架构 linux/amd64 / linux/arm64）

```bash
docker pull docker.io/bestzwei/libretv:2.21.1
docker pull ghcr.io/librespark/libretv:2.21.1
```

两个 registry 的镜像内容一致（同一组 digest），`latest` 也指向本版本。

### 免 Docker（下方附件，Node 18+）

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
tar -xzf libretv-2.21.1-standalone.tar.gz -C libretv
cd libretv && PASSWORD=your-password PORT=8080 node server.js
```

预构建包与 CPU 架构无关（x86_64 / arm64 / armv7），环境变量与 Docker 部署一致。

> 镜像由 docker-publish 工作流在同一 tag 上构建，刚发布时可能还要 5–10 分钟才可拉取。

LizardByte/Sunshine: ## ‼️ Attention This release contains a high-severity security update for Linux hosts. For more information, see: - [GHSA-fp6g-27w5-489j](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/security/advisories/GHSA-fp6g-27w5-489j) Linux users should update as soon as possible! ## ⚠️ Breaking changes and migration notes - Windows hosts using Virtual HID Driver must update to version `2026.914.1218.10` or newer. Earlier driver versions are not supported by this Sunshine release. ## ✨ Highlights - **Clearer Windows virtual-input choices.** A new `gamepad_driver` setting lets users choose all available drivers, only Virtual HID Driver, or only ViGEmBus. Selecting ViGEmBus also suppresses Virtual HID Driver notifications. ([#5653](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5653)) - **More reliable Linux capture and encoding.** This release fixes multi-plane DMA-BUF handling for wlroots capture, corrects variable-rate behavior across KWin versions, and allows Portal capture with VA-API to use high-priority EGL contexts. ([#5699](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5699), [#5705](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5705), [#5709](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5709)) - **Improved encoder compatibility.** Updated to FFmpeg 9. Fixes include accurate AV1 and HEVC capability detection, FFmpeg 9 Vulkan queue support, NVENC support in Linux builds without CUDA, and ARM64 NVENC DLL loading on NVIDIA RTX Spark. ([#5554](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5554), [#5675](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5675), [#5698](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5698), [#5682](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5682)) - **Correct network-interface binding.** Sunshine now consistently respects the configured `bind_address`, including IPv4 addresses in dual-stack mode, and Web UI links use the configured address correctly. ([#5700](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5700)) - **Easier XDG Portal recovery.** Linux and FreeBSD users can clear a stale Portal restore token directly from the Troubleshooting page and select their display again. ([#5701](https://github.com/LizardByte/Sunshine/pull/5701)) - **Broader Linux availability.** Release coverage now includes Alpine Linux 3.24 packages, openSUSE Leap 16.0 and Tumbleweed builds, and Ubuntu 26.10 packages. ## 🚀 Xray-core v26.10.21, Kernel AmneziaWG, Per-Client Hosts & a Rebuilt Telegram Bot

- 🔐 **Security hardening** — Fresh databases get a random first user, generated WireGuard/AmneziaWG configs are checked line by line, and client IPs behind a proxy can no longer be spoofed.
- ⚙️ **Xray-core v26.10.21** — The panel follows the new core's XDRIVE and Lua-script rules and adds the finalmask source-IP filter, Lua noise scripts and XDNS over DoH.
- 🚄 **Kernel AmneziaWG** — An opt-in Linux kernel datapath per inbound, plus much faster uploads on the embedded datapath.
- 🎯 **Smarter hosts** — Bind host rules to individual clients, give a host a pool of SNIs, expand CIDR ranges into random IPs, and order hosts across inbounds.
- 🤖 **Telegram bot rebuilt** — One live screen per chat edited in place, inline search for long lists, and admin notifications routed to a forum topic.
- 🔗 **Cipher suites in share links** — Links carry `cs` and pin the fingerprint so it takes effect, with presets in the editor.
- 📈 **Large-install performance** — Cached subscription bodies, indexed token and Telegram lookups, a pooled gRPC connection and far fewer redundant database writes.
- 🐳 **Docker on ARM and 386** — The `linux/386`, `arm/v6` and `arm/v7` images now ship the right Xray and MTProto binaries.

---

### 🔐 Security
- A new database's first panel user gets a random username and password printed to the server log, not a fixed default pair ([`1df8ab29`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/1df8ab29))
- WireGuard and AmneziaWG `.conf` files from the subscription service, clients page, inbound modal and subscription page are built line by line and render nothing when a value holds a control character. Imported `vpn://` profiles that carry wg-quick hook directives are refused, and client `allowedIPs` are validated on every save ([`0faad4f4`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/0faad4f4))
- The client address behind a trusted proxy comes from the proxy end of `X-Forwarded-For`, and a client-supplied `X-Real-IP` is no longer believed. The documented Caddyfile and the docs reverse-proxy generator now overwrite it ([`d50c419e`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/d50c419e))

### 🆕 New
- AmneziaWG inbounds can run on an opt-in Linux kernel datapath. It runs NAT-only, with host preflight checks, a bundled installer pinned to verified module commits, and accounting that survives restarts. It never goes through awg-quick, and the master refuses to push kernel mode to nodes that predate it ([#6877](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6877)) @YoungReckless4
- AmneziaWG clients accept a randomised persistent-keepalive range such as `15-25` in `.conf` and `vpn://` profiles ([#6881](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6881)) @YoungReckless4
- The Telegram bot keeps one live screen per chat and edits it in place. The menu is grouped into Server, Clients, Traffic and Maintenance, long lists open through inline search, QR codes arrive as one sheet, and repeated notices collapse into one ([#6760](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6760)) @DIMFLIX
- Admin notifications can go to a forum topic with `chatId:topicId` ([#6879](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6879)) @gr219
- A client can be bound to specific host rules, so its raw, JSON and Clash subscriptions render only those hosts ([#6620](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6620)) @NethminaYasas
- A host can hold a pool of SNIs, picked at random per config or once per subscription fetch for the whole host group ([#6923](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6923)) @Pejman-Yousefi-Official
- A host address can be a CIDR range, expanded into up to 100 unique random IPs per subscription fetch and in panel previews and tunnel exports ([#6784](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6784)) @Pejman-Yousefi-Official
- Hosts can be reordered by drag-and-drop, and an opt-in setting makes every subscription format follow the Hosts page order across inbounds ([#6895](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6895)) @HamedSanaei
- Share links carry TLS cipher suites as the `cs` parameter, and both link importers read it back ([#6825](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6825)) @rqzbeh
- The cipher suite picker offers client cipher presets and warns when suites are set under a uTLS fingerprint that ignores them. The mask editors offer two chained tlshello fragment presets ([`f9926947`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/f9926947), [`7f82daa4`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/7f82daa4))
- A helper builds the dynamic `echConfigList` form (domain + DoH resolver) and warns that locally generated ECH keys do not work behind a CDN ([#6869](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6869)) @55575455
- The host "Mihomo X25519" switch now drops ML-KEM from REALITY proxies for networks whose DPI blackholes ML-KEM handshakes ([#6803](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6803)) @Toximiner
- Shadowsocks inbounds with a TCP HTTP header now appear in Clash/Mihomo subscriptions through the `obfs` plugin ([#6838](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6838)) @EmmaHermione
- A new opt-in switch also takes the `dns` and `sniffer` blocks from remote Clash rule templates ([#6868](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6868)) @yelloduxx
- A failed-check threshold for `node.down` alerts stops flaky nodes from flooding Telegram, email and Discord with down/up pairs ([#6768](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6768)) @STRENCH0
- A new `node-admin` API token scope lets a master update a node's panel without handing out a full admin token ([#6666](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6666)) @libmur-dev
- `GET /panel/api/clients/get/subId/:subId` returns the full client records for an exact subscription ID ([`0516a1f8`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/0516a1f8))
- The mask editors gain the finalmask source-IP filter, a Lua script field for noise masks, and the full XDNS DoH resolver options ([`61b129d5`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/61b129d5))
- Slovak (sk-SK) panel and bot locale ([#6889](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6889)) @Vaso73

### ⚡ Improved
- Xray-core updated to v26.10.21; the pulled v26.10.10 binary pins are replaced ([`61b129d5`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/61b129d5))
- Go 1.27.3 with current Go, frontend and docs dependencies ([`775b2b0b`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/775b2b0b), [`57fd6179`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/57fd6179))

- Fewer redundant database reads and writes for client IPs, global traffic totals and inbound stats enrichment on every cycle ([#6929](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6929), [#6930](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6930), [#6931](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6931)) @HamedSanaei

- The router, sidebar, page titles and command palette read the panel's pages from one manifest, so no page can go missing from one of them ([#6922](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6922)) @muditagrawal2007

### 🐞 Fixed

**Xray & inbounds**
- Enabling PROXY protocol on a fallback target behind a VLESS/Trojan TLS inbound no longer breaks the fallback; the master now sends the header the child expects ([#6880](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6880)) @mvanhorn
- A private DoH server is reachable again: the DNS allow rule now opens the port Xray actually dials ([#6918](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6918)) @jayhemnani9910
- User routing rules now match TUIC traffic, and adding or removing a TUIC client no longer restarts Xray ([#6875](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6875)) @poise52
- The inbound Advanced JSON editor keeps your formatting and caret instead of reformatting on every keystroke ([#6857](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6857)) @HamedSanaei
- AmneziaWG's fallback egress port can no longer land on the Xray API or a relay port ([`d103c0c0`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/d103c0c0))

**Traffic & limits**
- Periodic resets and Reset All Client Traffic now switch quota-disabled clients and inbounds back on, instead of leaving them at zero usage but offline ([#6833](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6833), [#6834](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6834)) @jayhemnani9910
- Client IPs are recorded and shown again with fail2ban disabled; only enforcement needs it ([#6830](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6830)) @yudongyouqing
- Deleting an inbound or purging depleted clients no longer deadlocks the traffic poll on PostgreSQL, and a delete can no longer be undone by a concurrent edit ([#6912](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6912)) @muditagrawal2007

**Nodes**
- A client is no longer stuck disabled on a node, flipping on every master tick, when the master's own limits still allow it ([#6876](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6876)) @muditagrawal2007
- A client re-created on a node inbound right after deletion is no longer hard-deleted 15 minutes later as a sync orphan ([`47be0635`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/47be0635))

**Subscriptions & hosts**
- Links that carry cipher suites with a blank fingerprint now pin `fp=unsafe`, so the suites actually take effect ([`c3d4a153`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/c3d4a153))
- Editing an inbound's external proxy now updates its imported hosts, so subscriptions stop handing out the old address ([#6831](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6831)) @FZ1010
- Every subscription route sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, so caches in front of the sub server cannot serve stale traffic or routing data ([#6862](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6862)) @yukh975
- The XHTTP XMUX counts, such as the default `maxConnections: 3`, now reach Clash/Mihomo subscriptions ([#6843](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6843)) @PosvdM

**Monitoring**
- Overview refreshes the server's public IPv4/IPv6 every five minutes instead of keeping the first lookup, or N/A, until a restart ([#6933](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6933)) @Vaso73
- In LXC containers, CPU, swap and uptime come from the container instead of the host, and a value that cannot be measured shows as a dash instead of 0 ([#6920](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6920)) @Vaso73

**Bots**
- Bot usage commands and the hourly report look up a Telegram account's clients through the indexed client table, ending high PostgreSQL CPU on large installs ([#6887](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6887)) @HamedSanaei

**Panel & API**
- Link and Telegram requests that arrive during start-up no longer fail with "sub link provider not registered" ([#6914](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6914)) @muditagrawal2007
- Clean systemd stops and restarts no longer log false shutdown errors ([#6884](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6884)) @rqzbeh
- Requests rejected for a missing or wrong CSRF token are now logged with the method, path and trusted client address ([#6692](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6692)) @ericanannn-blip
- Outbound TCP probes dial unbracketed IPv6 servers correctly instead of reporting them unreachable ([#6850](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6850)) @HamedSanaei
- The panel works with screen readers, including tab names on phone-width screens ([#6907](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6907)) @alireza0
- The Russian dashboard download label reads as a noun instead of a button ([#6890](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/pull/6890)) @almirus

**Docker**
- The `linux/386`, `linux/arm/v6` and `linux/arm/v7` images ship the matching Xray and MTProto binaries under the names the panel looks for. An unknown architecture now fails the build instead of packaging amd64 ([`4d6db99b`](https://github.com/MHSanaei/3x-ui/commit/4d6db99b))

MemPalace/mempalace:
A palace can now be audited and repaired in guided steps, and EmbeddingGemma 2 arrives as an opt-in embedder with native image, audio and video search. Every palace records the embedding model that built it and refuses to open with a different one. Conversation mining stops discarding text, status, search, wake-up and hub mines stay responsive on large palaces, and a round of correctness fixes from the 3.11 review hardens metadata updates, recovery and HTTP validation.

### Upgrade notes

- **The first conversation mine after upgrading re-mines each conversation file it covers, once.** The exchange chunker no longer discards text (#2591), so conversation drawers filed before 3.11 count as stale and are re-chunked and re-embedded from transcripts still on disk; transcripts no longer on disk keep their drawers. Project files are not re-mined. Expect roughly 40 minutes to 3 hours per million drawers, depending on hardware. On a large palace, back up first and run it in batches at a quiet time, for example `mempalace mine <dir> --mode convos --limit 200`; an interrupted run resumes where it stopped.
- **A palace refuses to open with a different embedding model than the one that built it.** Search, mining and MCP writes stop with a message that names the fix: set `embedding_model` (`config.json` or `MEMPALACE_EMBEDDING_MODEL`) back to the model the palace was built with, or re-embed with `mempalace repair rebuild-index`. A palace with no recorded model opens with the configured one and a warning that names `mempalace palace set-embedder`. (#2694, #2717)
- **`EntityRegistry.research()` and `confirm_research()` are removed.** They were an opt-in, off-by-default Wikipedia lookup that nothing in the CLI, MCP server, miners or hooks called. Existing `wiki_cache` entries in `entities.json` are still read by `lookup()`. (GHSA-mrj5)

### EmbeddingGemma 2 and embedder identity

- **EmbeddingGemma 2 is available as an opt-in embedder.** Set `embedding_model: embeddinggemma2` and install `mempalace[embeddinggemma2]`, or `mempalace[multimodal]` for media (Python 3.10+, PyTorch). It runs on CUDA when present, on Apple MPS, or on CPU, and supports 768/512/256/128 dimensions. A CUDA out-of-memory error halves the batch and retries. (#2694, #2717)
- **Native image, audio and video retrieval.** A built-in `media` source adapter embeds original files into a separate `mempalace_assets` collection, and opt-in CLI/MCP media search returns typed local asset references alongside matching drawers. File-level retrieval is experimental. (#2694)
- **Existing palaces are untouched unless you opt in.** The default MiniLM path is unchanged and nothing is re-embedded. An unknown `embedding_model` keeps the MiniLM fallback, while near misses of a known name are refused instead of silently falling back. (#2717)
- **Every palace records which embedder built it, and every write path fails closed on a mismatch.** CLI, MCP, mine and `repair` check the recorded identity; `repair rebuild-index` and `--mode from-sqlite` record it again after a verified rebuild; new Qdrant and pgvector palaces record it; and MCP refuses rather than falling back to Chroma's default embedder. (#2717; fixes #2709)

### Palace audit and guided repair

- **`mempalace audit` scores how well a palace is organized,** across five layers (rooms, wings, tunnels, hallways and knowledge graph), with concrete findings, `--json` output and `--fail-under` for cron or CI. It is read-only and runs against a palace an MCP server is serving. (#2576)
- **Guided repair tooling:** `mempalace instructions audit` walks an agent and user through the findings; `rooms propose` / `apply` give a wing a closed room set; `wings split` turns a machine-level transcript wing into one wing per project; `tunnels propose` / `prune` and `hallways --rebuild` / `--prune-spellings` clean up noisy links; and `kg normalize` maps one-off predicates onto a closed vocabulary. Everything is a dry run until `--yes`, and interrupted runs finish on retry. LLM-backed steps default to a local endpoint and need `--accept-external-llm` for anything else. (#2576, #2655, #2656, #2657, #2664, #2668, #2669)
- **Metadata-only updates on the SQLite backends are ~6000x faster,** so wing and room moves on large palaces finish in seconds. (#2576)

### Correctness fixes from the 3.11 review

- **Metadata-aware updates and upserts guard the inputs used for embedding.** Concurrent document or metadata changes are refused before publication, and removed fields are omitted from embedding metadata. (#2734)
- **Drawer listings keep metadata and page previews in one recovered snapshot,** and fall back to Chroma while recovery is pending. (#2734)
- **Room recovery rejects damaged journals before applying changes,** and approved tunnel proposals keep their full spelling context. (#2734)
- **Malformed HTTP tool names return normal JSON-RPC validation errors** instead of failing during dispatch. (#2734)

### Performance and large palaces

- **Status, search and wake-up stay responsive on large palaces.** Count caches no longer expire before they are used (8–12 s down to about 1 ms on a 360k-drawer palace), the MCP server stops reloading the vector index on almost every call, wake-up reads recent drawers from SQLite, and mining no longer rescans the palace with quadratic paging. (#2593)
- **Mines on very large palaces do far less redundant work,** and a mine on the HTTP hub yields to queued requests between files. (#2567, #2593, #2688, #2689, #2690, #2691)
- **Diary reads and single-drawer lookups read from SQLite** when it already has the rows. (#2650)

### Bug fixes

- **Conversation mining no longer discards text** after a `---` markdown rule, before the first user turn, or in short exchanges. (#2591)
- **`mempalace_reconnect` no longer runs under a running mine;** it waits up to 10 s and then returns `MineInProgress`, and a mine that failed some files raises `MineFileErrors` and exits 1. (#2701, #2705)
- **In-process SQLite reads keep Chroma's locks,** so status, taxonomy, BM25 and integrity checks no longer risk torn reads. (#2506, #2573, #2652, #2658)
- **`event_list` and `event_wait` no longer hide another agent's request** because the caller passed its own `from_agent`. (#2616)
- **Hub and daemon routes keep `--include-ignored` and `--include-subagents`,** and relative `sweep` / `sync` paths resolve against the caller's directory. (#2582, #2583, #2584, #2733)
- **`sync --apply` no longer removes drawers of files that are still on disk** behind mounts and bind mounts. (#2368, #2564)
- **The stdio MCP servers stay up and answer** on unparseable lines and when their hub is gone. (#2534, #2555, #2557)
- Also: `mempalace.yml` is accepted and updated by `init` (#2699, #2704); `.al` and `.ps1` sources are mined (#2702, #2706); case-only wing/room renames apply (#2426); KG writes no longer need the peer-writer lease (#2423); the legacy `repair` holds the palace lock (#2569); EmbeddingGemma's q8 memory blow-up is fixed (#2693); DirectML sessions run serially (#2687); and more — see the full list below.

### Security and dependencies

- **ChromaDB telemetry is disabled explicitly,** not just silenced. Nothing was transmitted on the supported 1.x line. (GHSA-8h77, #2524)
- **The unused Wikipedia lookup is removed,** so local-first is a property of the code rather than a default argument. (GHSA-mrj5, #2526, #2527)
- **Pillow 12.3.0, chromadb 1.5.9 and routine lock bumps.** Pillow 12.3.0 needs Python 3.10+, so Python 3.9 installs stay on Pillow 11.3.0, which is affected by the Pillow advisories fixed in 12.3.0. `SECURITY.md` now warns against exposing a Chroma HTTP server. (#2719)
- **Read-only MCP tools advertise `annotations.readOnlyHint`,** so plan modes and read-only subagents can use memory search without a host-side allowlist. (#2610, #2640)

---

**Install / upgrade**

```bash
pip install --upgrade mempalace        # or: uv tool upgrade mempalace / pipx upgrade mempalace
```

Optional EmbeddingGemma 2 and media search (Python 3.10+): `pip install -U "mempalace[embeddinggemma2]"` or `"mempalace[multimodal]"`, then set `embedding_model: embeddinggemma2` for a new palace. See `docs/embeddinggemma2.md`.

Optional native exact-vector search: the `mempalace_native_core` wheels and standalone `mempalace-native` executables are attached to this release (see `crates/README.md`).

A big thank-you to everyone who contributed. This release includes 79 merged PRs: 76 from 11 contributors, three of them first-time, plus three Dependabot bumps.

**Install:** `pip install -U mempalace==3.11.0`

Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm:
### Built-in LLM for Docker AnythingLLM Docker now has a default local LLM experience right out of the box. The same kind of built-in engine that ships with [AnythingLLM Desktop](https://docs.anythingllm.com/setup/llm-configuration/local/built-in) can now run **inside the container**: [Lemonade](https://lemonade-server.ai), the fully [open-source](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade) local inference server from AMD, running your models with [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp). You no longer need to run Ollama, LM Studio or any other inference server next to AnythingLLM. Pass your GPU into the container and the engine is accelerated on whatever hardware you have. It picks the fastest backend automatically: CUDA for NVIDIA GPUs, Vulkan for AMD and Intel GPUs, or the CPU. It runs on both `amd64` and `arm64` hosts. When it's turned on, **Built-in** becomes the default LLM provider during onboarding, with three models recommended for your hardware. You can download any model from the model table or pull any GGUF model from Hugging Face. It works everywhere a provider can be used: the system LLM, workspace and agent LLMs, the chat window model picker, and [Model Router](https://docs.anythingllm.com/model-router/setup). > [!TIP] > **The built-in LLM is off by default.** Turn it on by starting the container with `-e ENABLE_BUILT_IN_LLM=true`, and add `--gpus all` (or pass in your AMD or Intel GPU devices) for GPU acceleration. See [Built-in LLM for Docker](https://docs.anythingllm.com/installation-docker/built-in-llm) for the full setup for each kind of hardware. ### Color palettes Color palettes are straightforward thematic tinting you can apply to the entire UI. We plan to expand this functionality more so you can more heavily customize the UI and even layout. [Learn more](https://docs.anythingllm.com/features/branding)

MobileNativeFoundation/XCLogParser:
## Changes

- Fix quadratic diagnostic accumulation when parsing large activity logs ([#263](https://github.com/MobileNativeFoundation/XCLogParser/pull/263)). Join diagnostic continuation lines once, accumulate locations without repeatedly copying dictionaries, flatten notices without rebuilding growing arrays, and use a set for Clang-warning title lookup.
- Preserve diagnostic contents, notice ordering, and duplicate-location behavior without truncating output or introducing input limits. Public APIs and serialization formats are unchanged.

## Performance

Synthetic release-build benchmarks on an Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.3, Apple Swift 6.4; median parser-only elapsed time across three runs per revision:

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| One diagnostic with 40,000 × 1 KiB continuation lines | 30.508 s | 2.522 s |
| 40,000 distinct diagnostic locations | 53.349 s | 0.154 s |
| 60,000 notices | 18.464 s | 0.068 s |
| 40,000 Clang warnings, a duplicate title, and an unmatched note | 11.142 s | 0.156 s |

See [#263](https://github.com/MobileNativeFoundation/XCLogParser/pull/263) for raw samples, reproduction steps, and compatibility tests. These measure the affected parser paths rather than end-to-end activity-log processing.

The parser change passed macOS, Linux, and SwiftLint CI.

Molunerfinn/PicGo:
## Features

PicGo v3 is here! A brand-new UI, light & dark theme, built-in [PicGo Cloud](https://cloud.picgo.app/) uploader (free tier on sign-up), cloud album management, and more major updates, along with a bunch of feature improvements and bug fixes!

And we provide [PicGo Skills](https://github.com/PicGo/skills) — A new skill package for AI Agents to integrate with PicGo for uploading images and files! Enjoy!

**v3.0.3** lets the built-in HTTP server upload to a specific saved configuration per request, reduces idle GPU usage on macOS, and fixes PicGo launching twice at login on Windows.

- ✨ **Choose the upload configuration per request** — Add `uploader`, `configName` or `configId` as query parameters to `POST /upload` to send that upload to an existing saved configuration, without switching your default uploader or writing anything to disk. It works for file path uploads, clipboard uploads (empty body) and multipart uploads, so tools and scripts can send different images to different destinations, even concurrently. Invalid or ambiguous options return HTTP `400` instead of falling back to the default uploader. URL-encode names that contain spaces or non-ASCII characters. ([#1447](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/pull/1447)) See the [full guide](https://picgo.app/blog/2026/picgo-http-upload-config/) for parameter combinations, uploader IDs and error codes.

```bash
# Upload to the GitHub configuration named "Work"
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:36677/upload?uploader=github&configName=Work" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"list": ["/absolute/path/photo.png"]}'

# Upload the clipboard image to the same configuration
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:36677/upload?uploader=github&configName=Work"
```

| Upload options | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| None | Same as before: use the current default uploader. |
| `uploader=github` | Use GitHub's currently selected configuration. |
| `uploader=github&configName=Work` | Use the configuration named `Work` under GitHub (case-insensitive). |
| `configName=Work` | Search all uploaders; exactly one configuration must match. |
| `configId=<id>` | Match by configuration ID, which stays the same after renaming. |

## Performance

- Perf: Fixed the `PicGo Helper (GPU)` process on macOS continuously rendering frames and staying busy even after the window was closed. PicGo windows now use Electron's default background throttling again. Thanks [@WayneVoyager](https://github.com/WayneVoyager) for the detailed investigation and fix! ([#1435](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/pull/1435), closes [#1434](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/issues/1434))

## Bug Fixes

- Fix: PicGo launching twice and showing its window at login on Windows when "Launch at startup" is enabled — a leftover login item registered by older versions is now removed, so PicGo starts once and respects the startup mode setting. Thanks [@jincurry](https://github.com/jincurry) for the fix! ([5399f30](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/commit/5399f30))

---

## Features

PicGo v3 来了！全新 UI、明暗主题、内置 [PicGo Cloud](https://cloud.picgo.app/) 图床（注册即享免费额度）、云相册管理等重磅更新，还有一系列功能改进与问题修复！

并且我们提供了 [PicGo Skills](https://github.com/PicGo/skills) — 一个给 AI agent 使用的 skills 技能包，方便你的 AI Agent 接入 PicGo 并上传图片、文件！

**v3.0.3** 让内置 HTTP 上传服务可以按次指定上传到哪个已保存的图床配置，降低了 macOS 上空闲时的 GPU 占用，并修复了 Windows 开机自启时 PicGo 会启动两次的问题。

- ✨ **每次上传可单独指定图床配置** — 在 `POST /upload` 的 query 参数中加上 `uploader`、`configName` 或 `configId`，即可把这一次上传发到某个已保存的配置，不会切换你的默认图床，也不会写入配置文件。文件路径上传、剪贴板上传（空 body）和 multipart 上传都支持，脚本和工具可以把不同的图片发到不同的目的地，并发请求也互不影响。参数无效或匹配到多个配置时会返回 HTTP `400`，不会悄悄回退到默认图床。配置名里有空格或中文等字符时请做 URL 编码。（[#1447](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/pull/1447)）参数组合、图床 ID 和错误码的完整说明见 [这篇指南](https://picgo.app/zh/blog/2026/picgo-http-upload-config/)。

```bash
# 上传到 GitHub 图床下名为 "Work" 的配置
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:36677/upload?uploader=github&configName=Work" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"list": ["/absolute/path/photo.png"]}'

# 把剪贴板里的图片上传到同一个配置
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:36677/upload?uploader=github&configName=Work"
```

| 上传参数 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| 不带参数 | 和以前一样，使用当前默认图床。 |
| `uploader=github` | 使用 GitHub 图床当前选中的配置。 |
| `uploader=github&configName=Work` | 使用 GitHub 图床下名为 `Work` 的配置（不区分大小写）。 |
| `configName=Work` | 在所有图床中查找，必须恰好匹配一个配置。 |
| `configId=<id>` | 按配置 ID 匹配，配置改名后 ID 不变。 |

## Performance

- 优化：修复 macOS 上 `PicGo Helper (GPU)` 进程持续出帧、关闭窗口后占用也不下降的问题。PicGo 的窗口重新使用 Electron 默认的后台节流策略。感谢 [@WayneVoyager](https://github.com/WayneVoyager) 细致的排查与修复！（[#1435](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/pull/1435)，修复 [#1434](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/issues/1434)）

## Bug Fixes

- 修复：Windows 上开启「开机自启」后，登录时 PicGo 会启动两次并弹出窗口 — 现在会移除旧版本遗留的登录项，PicGo 只启动一次，并遵循启动模式设置。感谢 [@jincurry](https://github.com/jincurry) 的修复！（[5399f30](https://github.com/Molunerfinn/PicGo/commit/5399f30)）

# SkillSpector 2.13.2

This patch release builds on the published v2.13.1 maintenance release and
backports three fixes for false incomplete-analysis reports. It preserves the
existing maintenance fixes, third-party dependency lock, and provider defaults.

## Fixes

- [#779](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/pull/779): Recognize command wrappers
  with no wrapped command at a proven clause boundary. Markdown table cells and
  ordinary source references to `timeout`, `sudo`, `nice`, and `xargs` no longer
  cause false parser-limit reports. Redirections, unfinished fragments, and
  commands in subsequent clauses retain their existing checks.
- [#917](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/pull/917): Treat `sudo -n` as a flag
  and parse descriptor redirections such as `2>&1` as complete operators. Align
  the MCP TP4 batch limit with its existing 128-file limit so supported inputs
  are not prematurely truncated after 64 batches. Byte, token, declaration,
  file, runtime, and provider-error limits remain enforced.
- [#921](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/pull/921): Recognize direct template
  messages on verified built-in Node assertion imports, avoiding false shell
  substitution limits in JavaScript helpers. Classify `.mjs` and `.cjs` files
  consistently, including archive members. Raw security findings and their
  source locations are preserved. Ambiguous syntax, assertion aliases or
  mutations, effectful interpolation, and exceeded bounds remain conservative;
  TypeScript retains its existing parser path.

## Scope and upgrading

The JavaScript correction is a bounded assertion-message proof, not a general
JavaScript parser or dataflow analysis. It assumes ordinary built-in assertion
semantics and does not prove the absence of arbitrary runtime mutation or
object getters. Existing findings and independent inspection limitations remain
visible; these fixes do not suppress malformed provider responses.

Regenerate and review exact version-bound finding baselines for 2.13.2 rather
than relabeling baselines from another scanner version. The GitHub release
provides a wheel and source distribution; the publication workflow does not
publish to PyPI.

## Validation and known limitations

This release preserves every v2.13.1 commit and includes #779, #917 and #921. All six [candidate CI jobs](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/actions/runs/40539160128) passed, including 12,395 unit tests. Fresh local packaging checks, 72 offline acceptance scans and 22 additional boundary checks also passed.

Live acceptance completed all 28 planned cases: 26 passed and two large-skill TP4 cases failed under the unchanged 600-second workflow budget. The candidate planned 118 batches, but completed 65 from source and 66 from the installed wheel; all remaining ranges were explicitly reported as runtime-limited. The old 64-batch planning cap is removed, but complete live inspection of this large input is not established. Live LLM coverage used one configured model through the NVIDIA gateway; other provider routes were not qualified. The CAD checks exercised preparation plus TP4, not the entire CLI analysis workflow.

The batch cap is now 128, so a reported 145-batch workload still exceeds it. Large-skill runtime completion, remaining obfuscated-instruction limitations, evaluator binary-scope admission policy and deduplication limits, and general malformed-provider-response failures remain unresolved follow-up work. Independent content findings and missing-reference limitations remain visible; upgrading does not guarantee that a downstream admission gate passes.

See [release PR #922](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/pull/922) for validation details.

   - 暂存脚本改为复制完整的执行阶段 Python 源文件，减少 macOS 首次启动失败及发布包缺失文件的问题。

3. **修复任务列表 URL 显示问题**

5. **修正执行器循环调用参数名**
   - 将内部循环路径参数 `clickPath` 更名为 `loopPath`，避免循环路径与点击路径参数混淆。

6. **修复追加输出模式**
   - 执行器在追加模式下改为使用 `WriteMode.Append`，不再错误地按照新建模式初始化输出文件。

7. **升级 Electron 服务端依赖**
   - 将 `multer` 升级至 `2.0.0`。
   - 同步更新依赖锁文件。

8. **改进 macOS 浏览器和执行器打包**
   - 支持从本机 Chrome 应用读取主版本号，并自动匹配对应的 ChromeDriver。

    - 支持通过 API 创建执行实例。
    - 支持传入任务参数。

14. **加强安全性**

    - 改用系统 API 结束进程，避免通过 Shell 命令进行进程管理。

## Update Notes

1. **Improved screenshot execution**
   - Screenshot files are now consistently stored in the `screenshots` subdirectory under each task directory.
   - In headless mode, the browser window is automatically resized according to the actual scroll width and height of the page before taking a screenshot, allowing full-page screenshots to be captured.

2. **Improved first-run behavior and packaging on macOS**
   - Added a helper script to remove macOS quarantine attributes during the first launch.
   - The staging script now copies the complete Python source files required by the execution stage, reducing first-launch failures and missing-file issues in packaged macOS builds.

3. **Fixed URL display in the task list**
   - The task list now prioritizes the first URL in `links` instead of the top-level `url` field, which may be empty or outdated.

4. **Fixed window-state recovery after cross-window element lookup failures**
   - When an element cannot be found during a cross-window search, the executor now switches back to the original window handle.
   - This prevents subsequent operations from incorrectly continuing in another browser tab or window.

5. **Renamed the executor loop-path parameter**
   - The internal `clickPath` parameter used for loop execution has been renamed to `loopPath`.
   - This avoids confusion between loop paths and click paths.

6. **Fixed append output mode**
   - The executor now uses `WriteMode.Append` when running in append mode.
   - Output files are no longer incorrectly initialized using the new-file mode.

7. **Updated Electron server dependency**
   - Upgraded `multer` to `2.0.0`.
   - Updated the corresponding lock file.

8. **Improved browser and executor packaging on macOS**
   - The build process can now read the major version of the locally installed Chrome application and match the appropriate ChromeDriver.
   - OCR / ONNX files are now dynamically located from the active Python environment.
   - Permissions for the bundled Chrome installation can now be reset before repackaging.
   - Added ad-hoc signing support for macOS applications.

9. **Fixed the flowchart context menu**
   - Right-clicking a flow node no longer unintentionally triggers element focus or browser operations.
   - After scrolling the page, the context menu now uses page coordinates for positioning, preventing it from appearing at an incorrect location.

10. **Added a local remote-execution control API**
    - Added API support for creating execution instances.
    - Added support for passing task parameters.
    - Added support for starting one or multiple execution instances.
    - Added support for querying execution status.
    - Added support for reading execution logs.
    - Added support for sending stop signals.
    - The execution stage now provides a local IPC stop service protected by a randomly assigned port and secret-key validation.

11. **Fixed Linux and Docker execution paths**
    - Packaged Linux executors can now recognize Electron's `resources` directory layout and resolve runtime files using relative paths.
    - In Docker remote-driver mode, local Chrome binary and extension configurations are removed to prevent missing-file errors.

12. **Added compatibility with extension loading in Chrome 137+**
    - Chrome is now launched with the relevant feature disabled when it would otherwise prevent command-line extension loading.
    - This restores automated extension loading on Chrome 137 and later versions.

13. **Switched to Selenium WebDriver BiDi WebExtension API**
    - The unpacked EasySpider main extension is now installed using Selenium WebDriver BiDi's WebExtension API.
    - This replaces the previous command-line CRX injection mechanism.

14. **Security improvements**
    - The ChromeDriver updater now downloads files using HTTP requests with explicit timeouts.
    - Process termination now uses system APIs instead of shell commands.
    - Local services are bound only to loopback interfaces and restrict allowed cross-origin requests.
    - Replacements of `Field["field"]` expressions in Python / JavaScript now apply literal escaping to reduce code-injection risks.

15. **Fixed duplicated headers when importing task parameters from Excel**
    - Fixed an issue where loop text parameters were incorrectly displayed as `inputText_1`.
    - Loop text parameters are now correctly displayed as `loopText_1`.

Niko1221/Strata: # Strata 0.2.8: faster Arc B-series pairs and four-card Radeon servers, a Mac DeepSeek memory leak fixed, fewer lost tool calls The app is 0.2.8. Control and every engine package are 0.1.54. ## The numbers first - **Two Intel Arc Pro B65 cards: decode 17% to 23% faster, prompts about 7% to 13% faster.** Chat runs at 71 to 74 tokens per second, against 60 to 63 before, and JSON at 80 to 83, against 67 to 68. We tested two Arc Pro B65 32 GB cards with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, five paired runs, and every pair was faster. The answers are the same as before. This applies to exactly two Arc B-series cards; one card, A-series cards and three or more cards run as before. - **Four Radeon AI PRO R9700 cards serving many requests: 2.4 times the total speed at 32 requests at once** (155 to 370 tokens per second in total; at 8 at once, 157 to 261). One request alone runs at the same speed as before (67 tokens per second). Setup and the launcher pick this for exactly four R9700 cards running Qwen3.8 IQ3_S. All 32 answers matched a single-request run, and two soaks (25 and 12 minutes, 1,600 requests) had no errors. - **DeepSeek on the Mac no longer slows down after a few requests.** On the Metal engine every request left about 1.3 GB of GPU buffers behind, until the Mac ran short of memory and decode fell from 16 tokens per second to 3. Memory now stays flat at 76 GB over 34 requests, and decode stays at 18 to 22 tokens per second, with the same answers. Tested on an M5 Max with 128 GB, not on a 256 GB Mac Studio. - **Tool calls the model writes slightly wrong now still go through, by default.** Over 1,462 agent turns, 98.3% are now read as intended, against 92.9% before. This only applies to tools the request declared. - **RTX cards with 12 GB or less: the 0.2.7 routing speed-up is off again by default.** It made answers faster (RTX 3060: story +15%, code +37%), but your reports and our own checks tied it to repeated text in long sessions. With nothing set, the engine now routes exactly as 0.2.6 did. To get the speed back, turn on "Faster answers on 12 GB NVIDIA cards" under Models, Native engine settings, Speed (or run `strata launch --set STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5`). - **DeepSeek no longer stops in the middle of a word.** The server ended a reply on pieces such as `im`, `|` or `>`, so "Nerazim" came out as "Neraz" (#4576, #4137). It happened when a DeepSeek server was started from a config that did not name the model family. - **0.2.8 against 0.2.7.1, five paired runs each.** On one RTX A6000 with Qwen IQ3_S, decode went from 105.9 to 111.4 tokens per second on a story and from 139.8 to 145.2 on code; prompts are unchanged (1,927 and 1,924 at 4K, 2,571 and 2,569 at 20K). On one Radeon R9700, decode went from 73.7 to 79.7 on a story and from 106.3 to 107.8 on code; prompts are within 0.4% once the engine is warm. DeepSeek 2.25 decode is 4.3% faster on an RTX A6000, with the same output as 0.2.7.1 on our score check. ## What is new - **Arc B-series pairs.** The first card starts the next window while the second card is still checking the current one (`--pipeline-windows 2`), and setup writes `--spec 2` for the pair. Turn it off with `--pipeline-windows 0`; a `--spec` you set yourself is kept. The Arc engine also reads prompts about 5% faster on B-series cards with a new attention path, and three bugs that stopped `--pipeline-windows` from running at all are fixed. - **Four-card Radeon profile.** For four R9700 cards: 32 request slots in 4 groups, layer split 13,26,39, a prompt chunk of 2048 and three small switches. It only fills in what you have not set. Turn it off with `"four_card_profile": false` in the config. - **Bigger batch windows on AMD.** The HIP engines now check and batch up to 16 rows at once instead of 8, which is what the four-card profile needs. The answers are bit for bit those of the 8-row build on every card we ran (10 of 10 on R9700, RTX PRO 5000, A6000, A4000 and P100). NVIDIA, Intel and Mac builds stay at 8. - **DeepSeek prompt speed, opt-in.** `DS4_FAT_ROWS` (thanks to lyesrock, PR #4366) gives the busiest experts of a long prompt one bigger matrix multiply: +2% to +5% on two RTX A6000. It is off by default, because the gain is under our bar for a default and the output is not bit-exact. - **A clearer message on Arc and older CPUs.** A model folder without `native_experts.txt` is read as the AVX-512 pack, and the engine used to blame the CPU. It now names the real cause, and `strata doctor` warns before the start. - **One source for the driver floor.** Setup now reads the CUDA 12 driver floor from the engine package, so setup and the update agree. The floor itself has not changed: 575.51, or 576.02 on Windows. ## Fixed, from your reports - **App:** - DeepSeek no longer fails to load with picture reading off (#4358, #4359, #4505, #4507). The app now sends DeepSeek only the options it takes, and "GPU memory for other apps" goes out as `--reserve-mib` (#4504). - The wait for a big model to load now follows the model size, as `strata launch` does (#4191, #3459; thanks to miketgv, PR #3817). - "See engine log" no longer points at a log that was never written (#3714). - **Monitor:** with a model running, an AMD card on Windows showed load, memory and temperature as "Not available". The Monitor now fills in what the engine does not report, and reads the temperature on Windows AMD cards (#3727). On Linux, a server's remote-console chip no longer shows up as a graphics card. - **Terminal and setup:** - The update's test start skips DeepSeek configs (#4440; thanks to ai-bits, PR #4267). - A saved lower-case model tag such as `iq3_xxs` is found (#4209, PR #4317). - The packaged Terminal runs setup without `CMakeLists.txt`, and `strata install --source modelscope` passes its options on (#4188). - **Memory and cache:** - A 256K start on two cards no longer takes the Strix Halo reserve off the RAM store. On 2x A6000 the RAM store grew from 77.7 to 106.5 GB (#4147). - The conversation cache no longer runs short when the PLE table is locked (#4518). - Parking an idle `--batch` slot keeps the shared prefix, so the first token of round 2 takes 0.66 s instead of 3.3 s (#4420). - The automatic expert cache leaves the reserve you asked for (#4474). - A new engine waits for the old one to give its memory back (#4051). - **Tool calls and the server:** - An argument that quotes a tool call stays exact (#4078; thanks to Tsury, PR #4132). - Damaged arguments, a missing `` and a stray closing think tag no longer lose the call (#4427, #4077). - **DeepSeek on several cards:** - A layer split's chunked prompt no longer deadlocks (PR #4211). - `slot_load()` writes each tensor-parallel member's state under its own device (#4350; the single-card fault is still open). - **Mac:** the DeepSeek memory leak described above. ## Going back to 0.2.7.1 `strata components rollback` returns to the previous engine. The Qwen route prior and tool-call recovery can both be set the 0.2.7 way: `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5` and `"tool_call_recovery": false` in the model's run config. The 16-row windows are a build option (`-DSTRATA_WINDOW_MAX_T=8`); there is no switch at run time. ## Off unless you turn it on - `DS4_FAT_ROWS=N` (DeepSeek, CUDA). - Everything listed under "Off unless you turn it on" in 0.2.7 is unchanged. ## What we did not test - A 256 GB Mac Studio, or any Mac other than one M5 Max. - The four-card profile on anything other than four R9700 cards, and 64 slots at long context. - The Monitor fix on a Windows AMD graphics card. We tested it on Linux AMD cards and on Windows with NVIDIA and an AMD integrated GPU. If you have a Radeon on Windows, please tell us whether the Monitor now shows load, memory and temperature. - The Windows commit-limit side of #4518, the full #4051 wedge on a host with little RAM, and #4427 on a real model beyond the parser tests. - Metal and SYCL builds with 16-row windows; they stay at 8 and were only compile-checked. - The B-series pipeline on anything other than two Arc Pro B65 cards. - Strix Halo changes are not in this release. ## Updating - **App:** the in-app update offers 0.2.8, or download the installer below. - **Terminal:** run `strata update`. It fetches Control 0.1.54 and the 0.1.54 engine in the same run, and keeps the old engine for `strata components rollback`. If your Terminal is older than 0.2.0 (for example 0.1.45.x), run the install line again. - **DeepSeek engine:** it updates itself on the next `strata launch`. - **DGX Spark:** run `strata update`; it reads `strata-feed-linux-aarch64.json`. - **Mac:** the app, the Terminal and the DeepSeek engine are signed and notarized. ## Downloads 40 files. Chat2DB Community 5.3.8 reads, copies and exports complete large values instead of truncated previews - including for views, aggregations and tables without a primary key - adds the SQLX command line integration to Settings, and fixes table browsing and the KingbaseES procedure list.

## Added (1)

1. **SQLX command line integration**: install, update and locate the OtterMind SQLX CLI from Settings, import the connections Chat2DB already stores, and see the Skill command an agent needs; credentials go to the child process on stdin and are never written to disk, the renderer or the logs. by @openai0229 in #2959

## Optimization (1)

1. **Complete large values for view, copy and export**: JSON / LONGTEXT / BLOB values are completed from a snapshot captured while the query runs, so the grid, every copy format (cell, selection, `INSERT` / `UPDATE` / `WHERE`, IN Values, TSV, Markdown) and exports return the full content even when there is no primary key to re-query; the captured content is freed when the result is discarded or when it expires. by @openai0229 in #2972

## Fixed (2)

1. **KingbaseES procedure list**: procedures come from `sys_catalog.sys_proc` instead of the JDBC driver query that failed with `operator does not exist: boolean || oid`, covering V8R3 and V8R6+. by @openai0229 in #2956
2. **Table data tabs no longer re-browse on every switch**: switching tabs no longer re-issues the request and resets to page 1, a failed first page offers a retry, and a layout change keeps the pane's active tab. by @openai0229 in #2961

- 平台出错时，报错原话和自带的处理建议原样交给 AI，由 AI 用平台名告诉用户哪个平台暂时有问题；不再用 Reach 自己编的建议覆盖（"要登录"仍给 Reach 自己专用浏览器的登录步骤）。

English (technical):
- 28 of 40 actions passed real acceptance before release; these shipped untested with maintainer approval: Reddit (test network blocked), Instagram (rate limited), Bilibili subtitles, LinkedIn, Xueqiu hot posts/stocks (no login), Xiaoyuzhou (no key).
- Browser channels share one profile, close after ten idle minutes and reopen on demand.
- Adding a channel prepares its tools; removal clears only that site's login. Default platforms can be removed and updates won't add them back.
- Updating keeps tools that have a tested version at that version; other tools get the newest version inside their supported range.
- Public content remains public-first, with a compact capability receipt.
- Keep Xiaoyuzhou transcription; remove the extra planner and duplicate site extraction.
- Reuse existing local site sessions read-only; queries default to headless, with a visible window for human login.
- The dedicated browser is identified by the id its extension saves inside its own profile, so the user's own Chrome is never mistaken for it; a query no longer closes an open login window.
- Browser channels run queries in parallel: up to 2 per platform and 4 in total, with the rest queued instead of failing BUSY at once; login windows, logout and browser setup wait for running queries.
- Report NEED_LOGIN instead of UPSTREAM_BROKEN when not logged in: Xueqiu community (error 400016), Bilibili subtitles (no Bilibili login), LinkedIn (no LinkedIn login in the dedicated browser).
- Smoother upgrade from 1.5: install and update share one guide, install.md, which checks the version first (update.md, where 1.5 sends users, points to it); `agent-reach update` moves a pip/pipx install to uv by itself; `setup` removes the old Agent Reach program (only Agent Reach itself) and the install report explains what was kept, what changed and which old channels can be added back. Install URLs always point at the latest release.
- Upstream errors reach the agent unchanged (the original message and help); the agent tells the user which platform is temporarily unavailable, by platform name. Reach no longer replaces them with its own advice (NEED_LOGIN still gives Reach's dedicated-browser login steps).

### ✨ New / 新增

- **Unified entry / 统一入口**: `agent-reach <channel> <action>`, `agent-reach read <url>`, `agent-reach channels`. One JSON envelope per call, unified error codes with hints, per-call timeout, automatic fallback to the next backend.
- **Management / 管理命令**: `setup`, `add` / `remove <channel>`, `login` / `logout <channel>`, `doctor`, `check`, `skill`, `skill link <dir>`, `update`, `configure`, `uninstall`.
- **One-step setup / 一步装好**: `setup` adds every default channel through the same path as `add` (bili-cli goes into `~/.agent-reach/tools/`) and reports what works, which AIs can read the skill, optional channels and optional logins. / `setup` 用和 `add` 同一套逻辑开启全部默认渠道，并汇报哪些能用、哪些 AI 能读到 skill、可选渠道和可选登录。
- **Skill placement / skill 放置**: one real copy at `~/.agents/skills/agent-reach/SKILL.md` (read directly by Codex, OpenCode, Cline, Warp, Zed); a link to it in the skill folder of Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Windsurf when installed (a copy where links are not allowed, e.g. Windows). `agent-reach skill link <dir>` covers any other AI. / 只放一份真文件，其他 AI 的 skill 目录里放指向它的链接（链接：一个指向原文件的快捷方式）。
- **Private upstream installs, tested versions / 上游私有安装，用已测版本**: tools go into `~/.agent-reach/tools/`; the user's own copies are untouched. Tools with a declared tested version install at that version, and `update` keeps them there; other tools install the newest version inside `floor` and `exclude`, which also define acceptable existing tools. `state.json` records the version actually installed and `doctor` shows it. Single-instance tools (OpenCLI) reuse the user's copy; if it is outside the supported versions, it is upgraded only with `--allow-upgrade`. / 有已测版本的工具装已测版本，`update` 也保持不变；其他工具用兼容范围内的最新版；doctor 显示实际版本。
- **`add` gives a finished result / `add` 一步到位**: missing prerequisites are installed without an admin password: uv (official script), ffmpeg (`imageio-ffmpeg` in a private venv), Node.js (official release under `~/.agent-reach/tools/node/` when the system has none), CloakBrowser (falling back to installed Chrome on download failure). git is no longer needed (Boss installs from a GitHub archive). The user only logs in or enters a key. / 缺的依赖自动装好，用户只需登录或填 Key。
- **Login state under `~/.agent-reach/` / 登录状态统一管理**: CLI tool logins in `sessions/`, browser logins in a dedicated Agent Reach browser. The browser opens by itself when a channel needs it and closes after 10 minutes without use. The OpenCLI extension is loaded automatically on each CloakBrowser launch; Windows system-Chrome fallback may need one Web Store click. Only the requested site’s cookies are copied read-only from an existing connected local browser; the source remains unchanged. / 专用浏览器按需自动打开，10 分钟不用自动关闭；macOS/Linux 自动装好扩展。
- **remove cleans up / 去掉渠道会清理干净**: deletes the channel's private tools nobody else uses, its CLI session, its login keys and its site cookies in the Agent Reach browser. The shared browser profile is retained for explicit logout/reuse; unused private tools are pruned.
- **Removable default channels / 默认渠道可去掉**: `state.json` records `removed_defaults`; `setup` and `update` never add them back; `add` brings one back.
- **doctor states / 体检**: not_added, needs_setup, needs_login, unverified, ready, broken; plus `regressed` per channel (passed in the previous check, fails in the latest).
- **update** runs `uv tool install --force` on the latest release, reinstalls every added channel's tools at their declared versions (tested version when set, otherwise the newest version inside `floor`/`exclude`; also when Agent Reach itself has no new release), prunes tools no added channel uses, drops channels no longer in the registry, and refreshes the skill. `result.user_actions` lists in plain sentences what the user must do afterwards. Rollback: `uv tool install --force <previous release zip>`, then `agent-reach update --sync-only`. uv is the only supported installer. 1.5 and earlier installs are migrated on first `setup` / `update`; `config.yaml` keys are kept.
- **Update notice / 新版本提醒**: explicit `update --check` refreshes the release cache. Ordinary queries never start a background version check or update dependencies. Cached newer releases appear in `meta.update`; updating requires the user’s agreement. / 只在明确检查后提示新版本，用户同意才更新。
- **Release notes / 发布说明**: every CHANGELOG version section starts with a plain summary for users in Chinese and English; it becomes the GitHub release body the AI shows users.
- Xueqiu quotes and stock search via Tencent public quotes (no login); Xueqiu community data uses a session synced from the dedicated browser with `agent-reach login xueqiu --sync`.
- YouTube `transcribe`; LinkedIn reuses OpenCLI search and job-detail in the shared dedicated browser.

### 🔄 Changed / 变更

- Default channels: web (fallback only), YouTube, GitHub, V2EX, B站. Optional: 小红书, Reddit, LinkedIn, Boss直聘, 小宇宙, 雪球. Experimental: Twitter, Facebook, Instagram.
- The agent skill is generated from the channel list and replaced on every update.

### 🗑️ Removed / 移除

- RSS channel (agents read feeds themselves).
- xhs-cli, rdt-cli, twitter-cli backends: they read browser cookies by themselves.
- `configure --from-browser`, `twitter-cookies`, `xhs-cookies`, the old `install --channels`, the old `skill --install`, `format`, `check-update`, MCP server entry.
- `watch` (use `doctor`, which now reports `regressed`), `doctor --live` (use `check`), `browser start` (the browser opens by itself), pipx installs.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes / 修复

#### 🔐 Boss直聘 — 登录态误判（双凭据存储）

- **根因：** Boss 有两个互不代表的登录态存储——本地 `~/.boss-agent/auth/session.enc`
  和专用 Chrome profile 内的浏览器 cookie。`boss status` / `status --live` **只校验前者**
  （Bridge/httpx 时代的遗留凭据库），而 `existing-browser` 严格 CDP 模式下搜索走的是浏览器 cookie。
  「本地有旧凭据 + 浏览器未登录」时 `boss status` 会报 `logged_in: true`，误导 Agent
  跳过登录直接搜索，最终撞上 `AUTH_EXPIRED`；旧 runbook 又禁止把 `_security_check`
  当成未登录，两条规则叠加把 Agent 推向「反爬滑块」的错误分支。
- **修复：** `check()` 新增第 4 层只读探测 `_cdp_zhipin_login_cookie()`，用纯标准库
  实现的最小 WebSocket 客户端直接问 CDP 浏览器本体（`Storage.getCookies`）有无 zhipin
  的 `wt2` cookie，**以浏览器为准**，不引入新依赖、不拉起浏览器、不执行搜索。
  无 wt2 → 明确报「浏览器未登录，搜索会报 AUTH_EXPIRED」并指向「用户登录 +
  `login --cdp`」；探测失败 → 报「登录态未知」；安全校验页提示也附带浏览器 cookie 状态。
- **Runbook 修正：** 删除误导规则「判断登录态只信 `boss status`」，改为以 doctor 的
  浏览器 cookie 探测为准；拉起专用 Chrome 后**强制暂停让用户肉眼确认**登录状态；
  `AUTH_EXPIRED` 定为 ground truth（直接走登录流程，禁止往安全校验方向解释），
  `_security_check` 仅在无 `AUTH_EXPIRED` 时按滑块处理。

### ✨ Features / 新增

#### 🎯 Boss直聘 channel

- 新增 `boss` channel：经 boss-agent-cli + CDP 真 Chrome 搜岗位、取 JD 全文。
- `check()` 四层只读探测（boss-agent-cli 装没装 → 9222 端口通不通 → 有无 zhipin 页签
  → 浏览器内有无 `wt2` 登录 cookie）。
- 抓取走公开 API（`search_jobs` + `job_card_browser` + `browser_source="existing-browser"`）。
- `agent-reach install --system --channels=boss` 可安装锁定上游 boss-agent-cli
  （#403–#407 已合并入 master）固定提交的后端；上游发布正式版后切回版本约束。
- Skill 与安装指南支持“帮我配 Boss直聘”：Agent 启动仅监听回环地址的专用 Chrome，
  用户只负责手动登录，最后由 Agent 验证登录态与 CDP 链路。
- 固定依赖从 fork 快照 `8ff6bd3` 切换到上游 commit `4c991b7`（#403–#407 已合并入
  master）：已登录 CDP 会话可直接复用，搜索可通过 `--browser-source existing-browser`
  禁止 headless 降级。
- code 37 按原始文案分类：环境异常为 `ENVIRONMENT_RISK` 并立即停止；只有明确
  token/stoken 过期才允许一次刷新。专用 Chrome profile 应长期复用并降低频率。

  + We recommend to upgrade to later PostgreSQL versions.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> 增加了普通渠道和任务插件一起选择渠道的功能。同一个模型名，插件和普通渠道都有的时候，以前请求都发给插件，现在按优先级和权重选择渠道。
>
> 这个模型的定价如果还是按任务插件写的，普通渠道会报价格错误，不会扣额度。可以单独给普通渠道设置价格。
>
> 增加了 OpenAI 12 小时提示缓存单独计价的功能，按输入价格的 2.5 倍收费。
>
> 修复了视频任务超过 24 小时就被退款的问题。默认等到 72 小时才退款。
>
> Added selecting a channel from both a regular channel and a task plugin. On image, video, and Responses endpoints, a model both can serve used to send every request to the plugin. The channel is now selected by priority and weight.
>
> If that model's price is still written for the task plugin, a regular channel returns a price error and does not charge. Set a regular price for it in pricing.
>
> Added a separate price for OpenAI's 12-hour prompt cache, at 2.5 times the input price. It was charged at the 30-minute rate.
>
> Fixed the problem of video tasks being refunded after 24 hours. They now wait 72 hours. If you set TASK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES yourself, that time stays.

## 中文

* **渠道**：增加了图片、视频和 Responses 上，普通渠道和任务插件按优先级和权重一起选择渠道的功能。原生插件地址继续走对应的插件。普通渠道和插件各用各的价格。
* **计费**：增加了 OpenAI 12 小时提示缓存单独计价的功能，按输入价格的 2.5 倍收费。gpt-6-astra 的 12 小时写入是每百万 token 25 美元，超过 272K token 是 50 美元。修复了 Claude 缓存写入没拆成 5 分钟和 1 小时时不计费的问题，没拆开的按 5 分钟计费。
* **价格同步**：增加了按站点汇率调整上游价格的功能。可以保持来源价格，也可以乘以或除以汇率。价格相同的模型也能选出来一起改。
* **任务**：修复了视频任务超过 24 小时就被退款的问题，默认等到 72 小时。自己设过 TASK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES 的，还是用你设的数。修复了可灵按 metadata 里的时长生成、计费却按外面的时长算的问题。增加了任务插件原生接口接收文件上传的功能。任务插件可以读到客户端请求头，Authorization 和 Cookie 不会给插件。
* **流式**：修复了大段内容传得慢就被当成断开的问题。修复了 Responses 已经回复完、日志里却记成断开的问题，用量照常记。
* **其他**：修复了结构化输出和工具参数字段顺序被打乱的问题，按客户端原来的顺序发给上游。修复了 Chat 转 Gemini 时丢掉 imageConfig 的问题，图片尺寸和比例会带过去。修复了高级自定义保存后「透传请求体」丢失的问题。修复了编辑令牌或模型时，切到另一条还留着上一条内容的问题。修复了访问日志记下网址里的密钥的问题。增加了使用日志详情里复制模型名的功能。

## English

* **Channels**: Added selecting a channel by priority and weight between a regular channel and a task plugin, on image, video, and Responses endpoints. A plugin's own address still goes to that plugin. Regular channels and plugins keep separate prices.
* **Billing**: Added a separate price for OpenAI's 12-hour prompt cache, at 2.5 times the input price. gpt-6-astra bills 12-hour writes at $25 per million tokens, and $50 above 272K tokens. Fixed the problem of Claude cache writes going unbilled when they were not split into 5-minute and 1-hour amounts. The unsplit part is billed as 5-minute writes.
* **Price sync**: Added adjusting synced upstream prices by the site exchange rate. You can keep the source price, or multiply or divide by the rate. Models that already match can be selected and adjusted too.
* **Tasks**: Fixed the problem of video tasks being refunded after 24 hours. The default wait is now 72 hours. A TASK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES you already set is left as it is. Fixed the problem of Kling billing the outer duration while generating the duration in metadata. Added file uploads on a plugin's own routes. Task plugins can read the client's request headers. Authorization and Cookie are not given to the plugin.
* **Streaming**: Fixed the problem of a slow transfer of a large event being recorded as a disconnect. Fixed the problem of a finished Responses reply being logged as a disconnect. The usage is still recorded.
* **Also**: Fixed the problem of structured output and tool parameters having their field order rearranged. They are sent in the client's order. Fixed the problem of Chat requests losing imageConfig on the way to Gemini, so image size and aspect ratio are kept. Fixed the problem of Advanced Custom dropping Pass Through Body on save. Fixed the problem of an edit drawer keeping the previous token or model when you switch records. Fixed the problem of access logs storing keys from the URL. Added copying model names from a usage log's details.

---
