apolloconfig/apollo:
## Highlights

Apollo 3.0.0 takes a step toward **Agent First** configuration management, giving agents structured APIs, user-delegated access, and machine-readable capabilities for configuration workflows.

### A modern server foundation

The server baseline moves to Java 17, Spring Boot 4.1.1, Spring Framework 7, and Spring Cloud 2025.1.3, with updated discovery integrations. See [#5585](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5585) and [#5671](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5671).

### Portal moves to OpenAPI-first

Portal management flows now use generated OpenAPI contracts, including configuration items, namespaces, releases, gray branches, permissions, and import/export. Portal and external integrations share an API foundation that agents can use directly. See [#5608](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5608), [#5610](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5610), [#5612](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5612), [#5616](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5616), [#5617](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5617), and [#5618](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5618).

### User access tokens for AI agents

Users can delegate scoped access to agents and automation, with expiry, rate limits, revocation, and auditing. Each request is checked against the token scopes and the owning user's current permissions. Capability discovery exposes identity, scopes, and available OpenAPI actions. See [#5632](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5632) and the [user access token guide](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/blob/v3.0.0/docs/en/portal/apollo-open-api-platform.md#25-user-access-tokens).

Independent companion projects [apollo-cli](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo-cli) and [apollo-evals](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo-evals) provide command-line workflows and evaluation of agent task results and resource boundaries.

## What's Changed

* Change: migrate the server runtime to Java 17 and Jakarta APIs, and update official Docker runtime images to Java 17 by @nobodyiam in https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5555
* Fix: include super admin in hasAnyPermission semantics by @nobodyiam in https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5568

## Installation

Please refer to the [Distributed Deployment Guide](https://www.apolloconfig.com/#/en/deployment/distributed-deployment-guide).

## How to upgrade from v2.5.2 to v3.0.0

**Runtime and discovery changes:**

- Apollo server's Java runtime baseline has moved from **Java 8 to Java 17**. Upgrade the runtime for `apollo-configservice`, `apollo-adminservice`, and `apollo-portal` before deploying 3.0.0. This change concerns the server runtime; client SDK runtime requirements remain specific to the SDK in use.
- Official ConfigService/AdminService packages and Docker images now default to **database-discovery**. To keep an existing Eureka deployment, explicitly set `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=github` for both services before starting the new version. See [#5580](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/pull/5580).

**Database migration and deployment:**

The `v250-v300` migration scripts also apply when upgrading from v2.5.2. They add a ConfigDB index and the PortalDB `UserToken` and `UserTokenAudit` tables.

1. Apply [apolloconfigdb-v250-v300.sql](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/blob/v3.0.0/scripts/sql/profiles/mysql-default/delta/v250-v300/apolloconfigdb-v250-v300.sql) to ApolloConfigDB.
2. Apply [apolloportaldb-v250-v300.sql](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo/blob/v3.0.0/scripts/sql/profiles/mysql-default/delta/v250-v300/apolloportaldb-v250-v300.sql) to ApolloPortalDB.
3. Deploy the v3.0.0 executables in this order:
   1. `apollo-configservice`
   2. `apollo-adminservice`
   3. `apollo-portal`

## 🔐 Security update: eMudhra CA incident 🛡️

Trivy v0.76.1 includes mitigations for the [eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise](https://blog.cloudflare.com/emudhra-certificate-compromise/).

- Official binaries are built with Go 1.27.3, which includes the certificate distrust mitigation tracked as [CVE-2026-111943](https://go.dev/issue/82345).
- Official container images include an updated Alpine CA trust store that rejects the affected certificate chains.

We recommend upgrading to v0.76.1 and redeploying container images to apply these updates. If you build Trivy from source, use Go 1.27.3 or later and keep your runtime CA trust store up to date.

We are excited to announce the release of the Solidity Compiler [v0.8.38](https://www.soliditylang.org/blog/2026/10/22/solidity-0.8.38-release-announcement)!

This release fixes a security bug in the Yul optimizer, along with a few other bugfixes. In addition, it prepares for the upcoming Glamsterdam EVM fork, improves Yul optimizer performance, and slightly reduces the dispatch cost in the via IR pipeline.

## Changelog

## Important Bugfixes:
* Yul Optimizer: Fix knowledge about storage/memory address relations going stale in the `DataFlowAnalyzer` after a variable is reassigned in Yul, which could cause `LoadResolver` to replace loads with outdated values and `EqualStoreEliminator` to remove needed stores.

## Compiler Features:
* Commandline Interface: Remove the experimental `--yul-cfg-json` output.
* Commandline Interface: Selecting an ethdebug output no longer implicitly enables the `ethdebug` and `ast-id` components of `--debug-info`; without `ethdebug` in the selection the `--ethdebug-program` and `--ethdebug-program-runtime` outputs carry no semantic debug info.
* Standard JSON Interface: Remove the experimental `yulCFGJson` output.
* Standard JSON Interface: Selecting an ethdebug output no longer implicitly enables the `ethdebug` and `ast-id` components of `settings.debug.debugInfo`; without `ethdebug` in the selection the `evm.bytecode.ethdebug` and `evm.deployedBytecode.ethdebug` outputs carry no semantic debug info.
* Yul Analyzer: Warn about `swapn`, `dupn` and `exchange` being used as identifiers, since they are going to be reserved identifiers starting from the Amsterdam EVM version.
* Yul IR Code Generation: Use `gt(calldatasize(), 3)` instead of `iszero(lt(calldatasize(), 4))` in the external dispatch routine of IR codegen, saving one instruction per external call.
* Yul Optimizer: Improve performance of `DataFlowAnalyzer` using flat hash containers.

Bugfixes:
* EVM Assembly Import: Fix target EVM version being ignored when assembling imported experimental EVM assembly JSON.
* Parser: Fix inverted version pragma range comparison for components in the range [2**31, 2**32).
* Yul Parser: Fix `@use-src` source indices that are not decimal numbers being silently truncated instead of rejected.

Build System:
* Switch from C++20 to C++23 as the target standard.
* Update emscripten to version 3.1.54.
* Update minimum version requirement of Clang to 19.1.1.

Solc-Js:
* The wrapper now requires at least nodejs v16.

___

We would especially like to thank all the contributors that made this release possible:
ADou, Daeho Ro, Dmitry Rantovov, Faisal Firdani, Ferit, Kamil Śliwak, Mate Soos @ Argot, Matheus Aguiar, Nikola Matić, Philippe Laporte, PranaliPathak04, RAHUL KUMAR, Sean Billig, blishko, cdinhosbc98-cell, clonker, djole, dxo, jstcz, kediyalua, r0qs, riba2534, rodiazet,

- Reduce parsing overhead for build dependency and build backend settings ([#22848](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22848), [#22871](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22871), [#22879](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22879), [#22884](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22884))
- Reduce parsing overhead for project sources and workspace references ([#22880](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22880), [#22883](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22883))
- Reduce parsing overhead for cache, exclusion, cutoff, and preview settings ([#22876](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22876), [#22877](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22877), [#22878](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22878), [#22887](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22887))
- Reduce PyPI metadata parsing overhead ([#22874](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22874), [#22875](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22875))
- Speed up parsing tool receipt requirements ([#22885](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22885))

### Bug fixes

- Prevent `uv run --active --script` and `uv sync --active --script` from deleting non-virtual-environment directories ([#21464](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21464))
- Use `AMD64` for `platform_machine` when resolving for x86-64 Windows ([#22935](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22935))
- Preserve free-threaded and other non-default variants in `uv python upgrade` ([#22836](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22836))
- Allow `uv init --no-package` and `uv init --script` when `UV_INIT_BUILD_BACKEND` is set ([#22907](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22907))
- Prevent panics when rendering containment markers with local versions ([#22815](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22815))

### Documentation

- Update the Docker guide and reproduction examples to use uv 0.13.5 ([#22867](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22867))

# Release 9.3.1 (2026-10-20)

Bazel 9.3.1 is a patch LTS release. It is fully backward compatible with Bazel 9 releases starting from 9.0.1; see [Bazel 9.0.1 release notes](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/releases/tag/9.0.1) for a note on backward compatibility.


## General



* Removed distrusted eMudhra and Sectigo AAA root CA certificates from the bundled JDK, to address the private key leakage (see [https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/); [#31920](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31920))


## Core



* Preserve packages in top-level alias chains across pre-execution cache discards. ([#31912](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31912))


## External Deps



* Close the channel of a lock file when acquiring a lock fails ([#31896](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31896))


## Performance



* Rewind an action whose output was lost before it could be downloaded ([#31902](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31902))


## Acknowledgments

This release contains contributions from many people at Google, as well as Fabian Meumertzheim.

  `../` climb, a symlink out of it or a `LICENSE` that links out is refused
  before mining, with no hub request (#1836, PR #1838 by oxura).
- **`File.open(path, "x")`** creates a new file and fails with `EEXIST` if
  the path exists, in one step (#1821, PR #1824).
- **Non-UTF-8 arguments**: `IO.args_bytes` gives each argument's bytes, and
  `File.open_bytes` opens a path given as bytes (#1798, PR #1799 by
  viridale).
- **`Process.run` runs through one worker on Bun and Node**, so it no
  longer ends the run on Node, and a child that leaves stdin unread no
  longer hangs it (#1468, PR #1831 by oxura).
- **Metal: the lane spill of 2.0.38 is gone** (PR #1809): it made
  `bend -o` of a `!` program build 17% slower. A full lane fails with
  `ERR_DEEP` again, as in 2.0.37.
- **Fixes**:
  - The GPU build sees a closure in a later instance of the same datatype
    (#1513, PR #1542).
  - C: a read-only walk borrows its list when a sum type puts a word where
    another constructor has a box (#1805, PR #1806 by viridale); a memory
    fault ends the program by its signal (SIGSEGV, SIGBUS), not exit 1,
    after flushing output (PR #1828 by oxura).
  - `IO.get_env` refuses a name with a `=`, which read part of another
    variable on C and Node (#1794, PR #1795 by orezraey).
- **CLI**: `bend -o` never overwrites an input through a hard link or with
  the GPU archive `<out>.gpu` (PRs #1797 by sebastian-griego and #1826 by
  toprameen); a `$CC` that is not a usable clang 14+ ends the build with
  its reason, instead of a silent plain-clang build (#1802, PR #1804 by
  Yi-111-a).
- **Tools**: the formatter keeps body columns after `(`, `;`, tuple commas
  and in nested lambdas, and keeps a generic's `>` apart from a following
  `=` (PRs #1803 by toprameen, #1811, #1816, #1833, #1839 by vicmcorrea).
- **Docs**: BendTT proves adequacy, a checked law holds at each closed
  instance (PR #1627 by ScottMoore0); the guide and BendRT say a hot type
  counts the fields of every node, shared or not (#1559, PRs #1812 by
  vicmcorrea and #1813), and BendRT matches the runtime on the corpus, JS
  requests and the CUDA cube (#1822, PR #1823).

Install: `curl -fsSL https://bend-lang.com/install.sh | sh` (or Homebrew: `brew install bendlang/bend/bend`, or Nix: `nix profile install github:bendlang/bend`).

caddyserver/caddy:
This patch release fixes regressions from 2.11.6, including a crash when proxying over HTTP/2 and streams that were cut off after a minute. **If you're on 2.11.6, we recommend upgrading.** It also adds support for the brand new `Incremental` header field (RFC 10036).

**Huge thank you to our sponsors for keeping the project alive with resources, and for our maintainers who triage and assist tirelessly in this relentless new age of AI.**

## Highlights

- **Fixed: crash and dropped streams caused by the new idle timeouts.** 2.11.6 introduced default idle read/write timeouts, which caused some problems:
  - In 2.11.6, the request body's idle deadline could outlive the handler that set it:
    - Over HTTP/2, Caddy could panic with a nil pointer dereference when the reverse proxy was still reading a request body after the handler had returned. (#8101)
    - Over HTTP/1.1, streaming responses to requests with a body, such as SSE clients that open the stream with a `POST`, were cut off exactly 60 seconds after the body was read. (#8103)

    Both are fixed in #8107. Thanks @steadytao!
  - Over HTTP/2, streaming responses that paused between writes for longer than [`write_idle`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/options#timeouts) (1 minute by default), like quiet SSE streams, were reset with a stream error. As documented, only a write that stalls should count. Thanks @WeidiDeng! (#8118, #8119)
- **Fixed: placeholders for missing cookies are empty again.** Since 2.11.6, places that keep unknown placeholders as written, like [`respond`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/respond) headers, would output `{http.request.cookie.*}` literally when the cookie wasn't in the request. The same happened to `{http.request.tls.*}` on plain HTTP requests. Both are empty again. Thanks @steadytao! (#8019)
- **New: support for the [`Incremental`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10036.html) header field (RFC 10036).** It's the standard replacement for NGINX's proprietary `X-Accel-Buffering` header. If an upstream response has `Incremental: ?1`, [`reverse_proxy`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#streaming) forwards it immediately, the same as [`flush_interval -1`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#flush_interval), and [`encode`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/encode) streams it instead of holding it back. Great for [Mercure](https://mercure.rocks), SSE and other streaming apps.
  - If the [`request_buffers`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#request_buffers) or [`response_buffers`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#response_buffers) options would prevent incremental forwarding, Caddy responds with `501 Not Implemented` instead of silently buffering, as the RFC requires.
  - The new [`proxy_status_name`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#proxy_status_name) option adds a `Proxy-Status` header to those responses, explaining why the message was refused.

  Thanks @dunglas! (#8020)
- **Faster TLS handshakes:** When nothing subscribes to certificate events and debug logging is off, CertMagic no longer builds event data for every handshake. Certificate lookup per handshake is about twice as fast, with 10 allocations instead of 15. Thanks @u5surf! (#8010)
- **Unix sockets:** When a reload moves a listener (or the admin endpoint) off a Unix socket, the old socket now closes right away and its file is removed. Before, clients connecting to the old path would hang until the next garbage collection, about 2 minutes later. Thanks @littfed! (#8061)
- **Headers handler:** Multiple `Set-Cookie` values in a JSON config's `set` are now sent as separate header fields, instead of being joined with commas into one field that clients can't parse. Thanks @Indra55! (#8080)
- **`caddy fmt`** no longer deletes an opening brace at the very end of the input. Thanks @n0liu! (#8047)

## What's Changed
* events: tell CertMagic which events are worth emitting by @u5surf in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8010
* feat: implement the Incremental header field (RFC 10036) by @dunglas in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8020
* caddyfile: Keep an opening brace that ends the input by @n0liu in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8047
* listeners: close unix socket immediately and unlink file on reload by @littfed in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8061
* reverseproxy: stabilise half-close test by @steadytao in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8049
* caddyhttp: keep absent optional placeholders empty by @steadytao in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8019
* headers: Preserve separate Set-Cookie values by @Indra55 in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8080
* caddyhttp: end request-body deadline ownership with handler by @steadytao in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8107
* timeouts: fix idle writer terminate h2 response writers between writes by @WeidiDeng in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8119

* @n0liu made their first contribution in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8047
* @littfed made their first contribution in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8061

can1357/oh-my-pi:
## @oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

### Breaking Changes

- Removed the Bun event-loop workaround utilities from `@oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core/utils/yield`; agent loops no longer insert cooperative sleeps while streaming or between tool calls.

### Added

- Added `AgentTool.approvalRestrictionPaths` so tools can report the paths they read, allowing restricted-folder approvals to cover those paths without remembering approval separately for each path.
- Added `Agent.logContext`, which adds custom context fields to every log record written during an agent run.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-ai

### Breaking Changes

- Moved Anthropic header and endpoint helpers, along with Codex session/transport inspection and OpenAI Responses replay/storage helpers, to dedicated provider modules. Update imports from the previous locations.
- Updated auth-gateway model resolvers to receive `ModelResolveOptions`, including the route's native API wire and the scoped client's accepted grants. Scoped client IDs no longer fall back to scanning all models; resolvers now select the best permitted candidate.

### Added

- Added mTLS support for Anthropic connections through the `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT` and `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_KEY` environment variables.

### Changed

- Provider implementations are now loaded on demand, reducing startup and memory overhead while preserving existing stream timeouts, cancellation, and host overrides.
- Account policy `priority` now takes precedence when usage information is temporarily unavailable, keeping new sessions on the preferred account.
- Improved provider-specific credential usage lookups so they no longer wait for unrelated providers, while preserving cache freshness, cancellation isolation, and complete aggregate reports. The corresponding server-side latency improvement requires an updated auth broker.
- Credential usage is now prefetched during session setup without selecting, pinning, or advancing the OAuth account rotation.

### Fixed

- Fixed Mistral thinking-message replay requests that could be rejected by LiteLLM with a `422 extra_forbidden` error.
- Fixed native Judge API requests missing the `omp/<version>` User-Agent, so omp usage is correctly identified in upstream statistics.
- Fixed Codex capacity-error retries over WebSocket and SSE ignoring provider-supplied `Retry-After` delays and retrying too early.
- Fixed cancelled OAuth refresh requests aborting the entire session, and ensured requests joining an existing refresh can still use the refreshed credential when the original request is cancelled.
- Fixed Cursor models losing omp system-prompt context, including context files, skills, and rules, on subsequent turns or when earlier messages precede the active turn.
- Fixed short-lived commands that refresh OAuth credentials, such as `omp token --force-refresh`, remaining open for several seconds after completing.
- Fixed TypeSafe authentication when `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` is configured by validating keys against the correct `/v1/models` endpoint.
- Fixed forced tool calls on non-reasoning models causing an unhandled reasoning-effort error.
- Fixed interrupted turns reporting a transport error instead of the caller-provided cancellation reason.
- Fixed long-running pi-native turns being terminated before their first event by fetch or proxy timeouts by supporting keepalives and the configured first-event timeout.
- Fixed pi-native clients crashing when the auth gateway reports an upstream failure during streaming.
- Fixed Cursor turns failing after a mid-turn stream interruption when an automatic retry receives a zero-token provider error; retries now continue on the rotated conversation.
- Corrected auth-gateway debug logs so they no longer claim a retry occurred when a usage-limit error was returned without retrying.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

### Breaking Changes

- Removed the raw `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog/models.json` export; use the bundled model registry APIs instead.

### Added

- Added `nextBuildPriceChange(cost, now)` to identify when a model's dated pricing card may change, allowing callers to safely reuse earlier builds until that time.
- Added the `selector-revision-suffix` catalog axis for Google Vertex, so `google-vertex/claude-opus-4-8` resolves exactly to `claude-opus-4-8@default`.

### Changed

- Reduced the bundled model catalog size and loading overhead.
- Updated role defaults so Factory Droid image models are preferred for the `image` role, allowing `generate_image` to work with only a Factory login.
- Updated `smol` and `slow` role defaults to use the currently bundled Cerebras and OpenAI Codex model identifiers.

### Fixed

- Fixed Mistral reasoning models so streamed thinking appears in the transcript and is preserved for subsequent turns.
- Fixed later-turn HTTP 422 errors in Mistral-hosted DeepSeek conversations when assistant reasoning history is included.
- Fixed DeepSeek V4.1 Flash image attachments being dropped for publisher-namespaced model IDs such as `ds/deepseek-flash`.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

### Breaking Changes

- Custom tool loaders now resolve the injected host SDK themselves; constructors take cwd as their first argument instead of a pi namespace.
- WebMCP now uses Chrome's native WebMCP support through WebMcpController, which accepts a Puppeteer Page. The former page-hook installation helpers, bridge constant, and page-hook types have been removed; Tern tabs no longer support WebMCP.
- Provider-qualified model selectors in --model, settings, roles, and task agents must identify an exact model ID or alias. Near matches now fail with a helpful error and suggestions instead of silently selecting a sibling model. Bare selectors such as opus retain fuzzy matching, and the Google Vertex Claude alias remains supported. Older migrated web fallback chains replace the retired Codex entry with openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol.

### Added

- Agents can send an interim response without ending the current task by writing Markdown to out:// (or using > out:// in bash), with streaming output up to 64 KiB. This is enabled by default in the interactive TUI and can be configured with out.enabled; it is disabled by default in print, RPC, and ACP sessions.
- Added computer-tool approval modes: tools.approval["computer.control"] can allow unattended foreground control on dedicated machines or deny the request without prompting. The approval mode does not itself grant access.
- Added optional task-file input (task.file=true), allowing subagent instructions to be loaded from an absolute UTF-8 file path or local:// URL with the submitted path and SHA-256 recorded ([#17133](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/17133) by [@iliaal](https://github.com/iliaal)).
- Sessions can be pinned or unpinned from the resume picker with Alt+K and Alt+Shift+K, or the remappable app.session.pin and app.session.unpin actions. Pinned sessions move to the top and take priority in search results ([#9837](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/9837) by [@zhang17-24](https://github.com/zhang17-24)).
- Added PI_LINK_SCHEME and optional PI_LINK_HOST, allowing file links from SSH or tmux sessions to open through a desktop protocol handler ([#15855](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/15855) by [@KunoLu](https://github.com/KunoLu)).
- Extensions and RPC clients can start live voice sessions using their own WebRTC peer, including phone-browser clients, through ctx.startLive({ sdpOffer }) or live_connect ([#17013](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/17013) by [@materemias](https://github.com/materemias)).
- Extensions can customize assistant-text rendering and rerender individual replies through the opt-in extensionRenderers.assistantText setting ([#16238](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16238) by [@materemias](https://github.com/materemias)), and can register interactive link schemes with extension callbacks and renderer fallbacks ([#16239](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16239) by [@materemias](https://github.com/materemias)).
- /debug reports now include session-logs.txt containing all log records written by the reporting session and its subagents for the current day.
- Added prewalk.from and prewalk.into settings to choose the planning model and handoff target (default @default → @smol); /prewalk [into] and /prewalk restart [from] [into] override them for one command ([#17373](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/17373) by [@H4vC](https://github.com/H4vC)).

### Changed

- Improved startup responsiveness by deferring nonessential UI, accessibility, browser, provider, slash-command, and interactive-composer loading until needed, and by overlapping independent session preparation work.
- OpenAI live steering is now disabled by default for GPT models. Typed messages wait for the next tool boundary unless providers.openaiLiveSteering is enabled, avoiding unsupported in-flight message errors.
- HTML exports now match the /stats visual design with a higher-contrast light theme, timeline and full-trace views, and navigation for nested subagents and advisors. Packaged viewers use integrity-pinned shared assets and require network access; source checkouts continue to embed the viewer.
- tui.autoGraph now defaults to auto: charts are refined by the judge for supported native TypeSafe judge models and otherwise use the built-in estimate.
- Filesystem changes are detected automatically, so manual scan-cache invalidation after edits is no longer needed.
- Model refreshes use substantially less CPU by reusing unchanged models and avoiding repeated model-cache database opens.
- Overlapping sloppy-edit operations are now applied sequentially, with each operation matched against the result of the preceding operation.
- PI_INTENT_PROMPT and PI_INTENT_DESC can now customize the system guidance and tool-schema description for the i intent field.
- Printed JSON values in eval, including large Python dictionaries and lists, are displayed as collapsible JSON trees.
- Codex and Claude rate-limit reset warnings now appear once per reset across conversations and windows, only during the final six hours; the status line continues to show the countdown.
- The . and c continue shortcuts now simply answer an unanswered last message instead of adding a hidden continue directive.
- With bash.gitGuard enabled, checkout, switch, restore, reset, and stash operations run safely in linked worktrees, while discarded uncommitted changes are preserved for recovery.
- Sessions with computer use enabled receive the desktop guide before the first computer call.
- The Tern interface now presents warnings, errors, update notices, file reads, and completed background work consistently with chat messages.
- Muted live voice sessions remain visibly muted while the voice model starts work.

### Fixed

- Fixed live configuration reloads missing edits immediately after a symlink switches to another file in the same directory.
- Fixed auth-gateway model routing after catalog refreshes so bare model IDs select the highest-priority credentialed provider, with wire-format compatibility used as a tie-breaker.
- Fixed chart recommendations that incorrectly inferred whether higher or lower values were better from row or column names; smart charting now uses the judge and avoids charting unsuitable numeric text such as page or step numbers.
- Fixed binary data flowing through background Bash pipelines being displayed as corrupted text or counted as huge line output.
- Fixed browser-tab closing delays when reattaching after a worker exits.
- Fixed startup warnings being obscured by the Tern interface; they now appear as normal in-app warnings.
- Fixed todo init clearing existing flat items when list was empty.
- Fixed legacy extensions using detached event handlers failing to load.
- Fixed MCP tools connected during vibe mode being activated prematurely and exceeding provider tool limits.
- Fixed Bash services rejecting port 0 when a log readiness condition was also provided.
- Fixed context usage and automatic compaction overstating token usage for inline tool descriptors.
- Fixed terminal titles not being restored after exit on terminals without title-stack support, including Windows consoles.
- Fixed cached approval directory grants that did not cover every target in a request.
- Fixed text typed during startup being delayed until startup completed, including resumed drafts.
- Fixed pull-request metadata and diffs remaining stale after a successful git push.
- Fixed live voice playback clicks when audio stalls mid-word.
- Fixed read rejecting artifact URLs from truncation hints under cached approvals or restricted folders.
- Fixed peer task acknowledgements being mistaken for final answers, so wait continues until the peer replies.
- Failed Hindsight memory recalls and retention operations now produce visible warnings instead of silently continuing without memory.
- Fixed long conflict-path handling, conflict-content selectors, and stale conflict IDs after aborted merges or external file changes.
- Fixed cancelled MCP OAuth flows and authentication lookups from crashing the session.
- Fixed progress HUD entries for idle local-model workers that were no longer used.
- Improved LSP diagnostics reliability across cold starts, push-diagnostics servers, save-only servers, retries, multi-server and multi-file edits, and reopened files; incomplete results are no longer reported as clean, and repeated clangd checks are faster.
- Fixed live job widgets showing incidental text from files, web pages, or search results instead of the actual job status.
- Fixed repeatedly failing advisor batches being retried indefinitely; they are now dropped after three failures.
- Fixed thinking overrides on prefix-bound Claude models from losing their provider prefix behavior during compaction and retries.
- Fixed failed large-value JSON queries from displaying the rejected value instead of a useful error.
- Fixed F5 retry reporting no retry when a background result arrived after cancellation or interruption.
- Fixed WebMCP invocation errors being empty and timed-out page invocations continuing to run.
- Fixed HTTP 413 errors for Factory Droid GPT and Grok after computer-use sessions by removing obsolete screenshots from requests.
- Fixed unavailable configured default or dictation models being silently replaced; omp now warns and identifies the fallback model.
- Fixed LSP references for files in sibling Git worktrees by adding those checkouts to the active workspace.
- Improved macOS computer-use behavior for applications without windows by opening the app and inspecting its returned window in one operation.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-natives

### Breaking Changes

- Removed the `invalidateFsScanCache` API and the associated filesystem scan cache environment variables (`FS_SCAN_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `FS_SCAN_EMPTY_RECHECK_MS`, `FS_SCAN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, and `FS_SCAN_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`); filesystem listing caches are now managed automatically.

### Added

- Added a built-in `rsync` implementation to the bash tool, compatible with rsync 3.5.1 and protocol versions 29–33 across Linux, macOS, and Windows. It supports local copies, SSH remote shells via `-e`, and `rsync://` daemons without requiring an installed binary; daemon serving is not supported, and `PI_DISABLE_UUTILS_DESTRUCTIVE` continues to use the system `rsync`.
- Added built-in `ast-grep` (also available as `sg`) support to the bash tool for structural code search and rewriting, including pattern matching, rewrites, context, headings, and JSON output.

### Changed

- Improved native filesystem search performance, including faster globbing and more efficient grep, fuzzy finding, workspace listing, and structural search/edit operations, while preserving deterministic result ordering and streaming behavior.
- Native search and the bash tool's built-in `rg`, `grep`, `fd`, `find`, and `ast-grep` now stop filesystem work promptly when cancelled or timed out, including searches over JavaScript-provided filesystems and searches interrupted while reading large files.
- The bash tool's built-in `rg` and recursive `grep` now search files in parallel while retaining path-ordered output; `grep` can also stop promptly after reaching `maxCount`.
- Enabled safe reuse of unchanged directory listings when `cache: true`, with timestamp validation to prevent stale results.

### Fixed

- Fixed cancelled native directory searches leaving filesystem-provider requests running during startup.
- Fixed built-in bash commands such as `cat`, `grep`, `head`, `wc`, `read`, and `mapfile` hanging at the end of FIFO input on macOS; `read -t` now returns at EOF.
- Fixed ANSI text wrapping for styled underlines, background colours, and colon-form RGB colours.
- Fixed clicking in native audio playback when the queue runs dry mid-waveform by smoothly fading output to silence and back.

## @oh-my-pi/omp-stats

### Changed

- Improved `omp stats` session synchronization performance by approximately 2–5× on large histories. The first sync after upgrading may take up to a minute while the stats database is optimized.

### Fixed

- Fixed `/stats` and `omp stats` failing when another dashboard was syncing sessions or the configured port was already in use; busy dashboards are now reused, and a free port is selected when necessary.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-tui

### Breaking Changes

- Moved `PINNED_HUD_TOGGLE_ID` to the coding agent's task output manager so reserving subagent IDs no longer loads the interactive editor.
- Updated `StatusLineHost.resetExpiryNotice` to receive the session and manage warning deduplication; custom status-line components must use the new signature.
- Removed `ToolExecutionHandle.setToolActivityVisible`; tool-activity visibility is now controlled by transcript components, while reply blocks remain visible by default.
- Removed the `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/theme/defaults` export. Bundled palettes are now available through `getBuiltinThemes()` from `theme/defaults.json`.

### Fixed

- Fixed table-chart direction detection so measures are not incorrectly marked as better based on header words; single-measure tables are now sent for judging when local charting is appropriate.
- Fixed LSP diagnostics that incorrectly showed “No issues” before a language server had reported; such files are now shown as unverified. ([#17293](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/17293) by [@JustasMasiulis](https://github.com/JustasMasiulis))
- Fixed Esc-Esc rewind in Tern selecting interrupted turns with no visible output instead of the last displayed turn.
- Fixed streamed code blocks losing lines that scrolled off screen before the closing fence arrived; completed lines now remain available in scrollback. ([#17333](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/17333) by [@gzkGit777](https://github.com/gzkGit777))

## @oh-my-pi/pi-utils

### Added

- Added `logger.withContext(fields, fn)` to attach contextual fields to all records produced during a function and its asynchronous work, plus `logger.withoutContext(fn)` for work that should not inherit caller context.

### Fixed

- Fixed `untilAborted` so promises passed to an already-aborted signal are still observed, preventing later rejections from being reported as unhandled.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-wire

### Added

- Added the TSP `json` kind for displaying raw JSON values as interactive, expandable trees in the terminal.
- Added `TspEditorProps.typeahead` support so programs that cannot yet read input can preserve typed text, display it at the caret, and submit it when input becomes available.

# Catwalk v3, hooks! A big one! Crush now runs on Catwalk v3, hooks can see every part of a run, and editors that host Crush get a whole new set of tools to feel right at home. ## Small overview of [Catwalk v3][catwalk]: Crush now speaks [Catwalk v3][catwalk]. Provider `type` describes the API format a provider uses, not who made it: - `completions`: OpenAI-compatible APIs - `responses`: OpenAI, or anything routed through it - `messages`: Anthropic-compatible APIs Your config is migrated automatically when it loads, so `openai`, `openai-compat` and `anthropic` keep working. No edits needed. The `provider add` and `model add` flags follow along: ```bash crush provider add deepseek \ --type completions \ --base-url "https://api.deepseek.com/v1" \ --api-key "$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" crush model add deepseek/deepseek-chat --thinking toggleable --max-attachments 5 ``` - `--can-reason` is now `--thinking always|never|toggleable` - `--max-attachments N` is new - Reasoning levels show friendly names in the picker, like "X-High" [catwalk]: https://github.com/charmbracelet/catwalk/releases/tag/v3.0.0 ## Hooks, everywhere 🪝 Hooks are no longer just about tools. They can now follow the whole run: sessions, turns, permissions and more! Hooks are now checked against the list of known events, so a typo gets caught early. The docs cover each event and how it lines up with Claude Code. ## Client/server mode If you build something that runs Crush inside it, this release is for you: - Host themes: the host app can theme the TUI over the server API, so Crush matches your applications. - Host context: the host can tell Crush what's in view, like open files, and those files appear in completions. - Append to the next prompt: clients can add text the agent reads with the next prompt, without starting a run or cluttering the chat. - Shared viewing: clients can see which session other clients are looking at. - Piped permissions: set `CRUSH_PERMISSIONS_PIPED=1` and the host answers permission prompts, so you aren't asked twice. - `http://` addresses work as an alias for `tcp://` when starting the server. ## Steadier server - `SIGHUP` now reloads the config instead of stopping the server. - Closing the terminal or stopping Crush through a service manager now shuts down gracefully, so work in progress is saved instead of left looking stuck. That's all for now! ### ✨ New Features

- **feat(providers):** add the mainland BigModel.cn (Zhipu) chat-completions provider and correct Z.AI platform links (#12343) — thanks @jackjinke
- **feat(runtime):** new `REASONING_REPLAY_ENABLED` feature flag (Settings → Feature flags, on by default) to stop Reasoning Replay from caching and re-injecting real reasoning text across turns; upstreams that require the reasoning field on replay turns still receive the internal placeholder when it is off (#12486 — thanks @jacobsparts).
- **feat(providers):** add NoTrack (`notrack.ai`) as a free cookie-auth web provider — catalog id `notrack-web` (alias `ntw`), `/api/dispatch` SSE, session cookies `uid`/`si_usr_id`/`si_ses_id`. (#12534) — thanks @jeanbispo
- **feat(services):** Added an LLMLingua embedded-service supervisor + HTTP sidecar wrapping the real `@atjsh/llmlingua-2` prompt-compression package (ONNX TinyBERT model, downloaded from Hugging Face on first use). The compression engine dispatches `/compress` calls to the sidecar over HTTP, falling back to the existing in-process worker-thread backend when the sidecar is down. (#12967) — thanks @rqzbeh
- **feat(providers):** Hugging Face connections support an optional Bill-To account sent as the `X-HF-Bill-To` header for cost attribution (#13016) — thanks @Abhijeet1520
- **feat(auto-combo):** new `nadir` auto-router strategy (`config.routerStrategy: "nadir"`) asks [Nadir](https://getnadir.com)'s decision API which model in the candidate pool the prompt needs and routes to it, leaving the connection choice to `rules`; opt-in, fail-open with a 30 s cooldown after failures, only the last user turn and the model ids leave the box (#13051) — thanks @doramirdor
- **feat(codex):** Add explicit per-account paid-credit opt-in with an Extra credits On/Off button in the provider account list. Accounts with available OpenAI credits can continue after their subscription cutoff; credit availability is shown separately, while Spark limits and upstream cooldowns remain effective (#13337) — thanks @feci
- **feat(api-keys):** Allow per-key service-tier overrides for OpenAI OAuth requests, preserving inherited defaults and enforcing explicit tiers across combos, retries and Responses transports. (#13554) — thanks @JxnLexn
- **feat(sse):** opt-in per-model concurrency caps per connection — configure exact `modelConcurrency` ceilings inside `rateLimitOverrides` (dashboard editor or `PATCH /api/providers/[id]`), enforced as an atomic fourth gate alongside the global/provider/account semaphores with local queueing; unconfigured connections behave exactly as before. Also fixes `rateLimitOverrides.executionMaxWaitMs`: the schema accepted it but the DB allowlist rejected it, so saving it failed; a dashboard save now also preserves an API-set value (#13700) — thanks @Notaloop763
- **feat(sse):** a request no longer dies when the upstream rejects thinking by naming the model instead of the offending field. OmniRoute now drops whichever reasoning field the body actually carries (`reasoning_effort`, `reasoning`, `thinking`, `think`) and retries once. Ollama rejects this way for Instruct-only models such as Qwen3-Coder, where the 400 reads `"Qwen3-Coder:latest" does not support thinking`. Neither existing detector could see anything to strip there, so the error went straight back to the client and every Claude Code request carrying a thinking block failed against a self-hosted non-thinking model. (#13868) — thanks @cryptiklemur
- **feat(providers):** add Twinmind (`twinmind` / `tm`) unofficial web chat provider — Firebase refresh, grouped model discovery, SSE `text_delta` → OpenAI chunks, emulated tool calling for OpenCode/Claude Code (#14131) — thanks @artickc
- **feat(resilience):** skip CLIProxy-backed combo targets before dispatch using management account health, ignoring stale per-model quota rejections (#14206) (#14301) — thanks @sprintberlin
- **feat(providers):** WorkBuddy (`www.workbuddy.ai`, Tencent) is now a first-class provider with its own device-flow OAuth module, catalog entry and token refresh. It is a separate product from CodeBuddy CN (different host, account system and catalog, and a credential from one is not valid on the other), so it deliberately does not alias the CodeBuddy OAuth module — aliasing would point the state request at `copilot.tencent.com` and mint the wrong credential. The gateway is OpenAI-compatible but accepts only a single-turn request: it rejects the replayed history an agent client sends from turn two on, and reports each violation as a generic code that reads like a transport fault (`11148 tool_call_sequence_broken`, `11155 reasoning content from the previous turn must be passed back`, `11128 Illegal API invocation from an unapproved channel`, `11101` non-stream rejected). The repair therefore lands in core as two opt-in `RegistryEntry` flags — `strictChatHistory` and `bodyStringReplacements` — honoured by the existing `transformRequest` hook and inert for every provider that does not declare them, so no sidecar proxy is required. The catalog is left `models: []` with `passthroughModels: true` and discovered from the authenticated `GET /v3/config` the official CLI itself uses, because WorkBuddy serves no OpenAI-shaped `/models` endpoint (`/v1/models` and `/v2/models` both 404). That payload is an authenticated `GET /v3/config`, which returns 22 chat models (observed live via the desktop app's own log); that list replaces the membership of the 26-entry catalogue the CLI ships in `cli/product.json` rather than extending it, so the image and video entries that exist only in the built-in file are kept out of a chat roster by their capability tags. (#14212) — thanks @zeeshanhaque21

### Added

- Cloud tasks: Settings > API Configuration has a Local | Cloud toggle when cloud sessions are on. Cloud picks the Cline model new cloud tasks run on, saved separately from your local models. Clicking the model label in a cloud session's composer opens it there.
- Starting or resuming a cloud sandbox shows a progress card with the repo, branch and steps (start sandbox, clone repository, start agent). It collapses once the agent starts.

### Changed

- Cloud sessions hide the Plan/Act toggle and the auto-approve bar instead of showing them disabled.
- With no model chosen, the Cline provider uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 again, which is back at the top of Cline's recommended list.
- Model requests retry at most 3 times instead of 5.
- Kimi K3 now gets `max` reasoning for Extra High and Max, instead of an `xhigh` setting it rejects.
- Refreshed the model catalog. Adds the CommandCode, Reflection, Liquid Inference and Munito AI providers and drops CrofAI, iFlow and Llama. The Cline free list adds Reflection Beam, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Laguna S 2.1 and drops Mimo V2.6 Flash and Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor. ClinePass now defaults to Kimi K3.1 Pro and adds MiniMax M3.1 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Default models change for most other providers, mostly to Kimi K3.1 Pro, MiniMax M3.1 Flash or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. If you use a provider without pinning a model, expect a different default.

### Fixed

- GPT-6 models (such as `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol`) work on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and SAP AI Core no longer rejects requests with "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens'". Both now get `max_completion_tokens`.
- Gemini API keys (the `gemini` provider) no longer send native Google Search. Free-tier keys failed every turn with a 429 quota error on Gemini 3+, and on Gemini 2.x every Cline tool was dropped.
- Toggling Plan/Act while a task is starting no longer drops your first prompt, and the session no longer keeps running with the other mode's tools.
- Disabled rules stay disabled.
- Starting a command no longer moves keyboard focus into the terminal, so text you're typing in the chat no longer lands in the shell.
- Cancelling a task or opening another one while Cline is asking a question no longer lets your next message get taken as the answer to the old question.
- A turn whose connection drops after the model has streamed only reasoning is now retried instead of ending the task.
- Auto-compaction no longer runs for models with an unknown context limit, and it no longer runs again every few tool calls after the first compaction.
- `ask_question`: the model keeps going after you pick an option, and empty answers are rejected.
- `run_commands` with an empty command list now returns an error instead of a silent success. On PowerShell, the tool tells the model how quote escaping works and to confirm recursive deletes first.
- Task header badges wrap instead of hiding the close button, the GitHub connection check no longer flashes a loading indicator, and the Local/Cloud toggle's padding is fixed.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.25...v4.1.26
clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB:
## New Features

### Reusable TypeScript submodules

TypeScript modules can now use a collection of reusable submodules for common application needs. The initial packages provide cron-style and interval scheduling, retry with exponential backoff, fixed-window rate limiting, cryptographic and encoding helpers, and Resend email integration.

The packages include typed APIs, installation documentation, tests, and examples. They can be installed in projects using SpacetimeDB 2.12 or later.

([#5903](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5903>), [#6158](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6158>), [#6309](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6309>))

### C# module submodules and namespaces

C# modules can now compose separately built module assemblies as submodules. Assembly-level namespace declarations control how a dependency is exposed in C# and, optionally, its canonical database namespace.

Namespaced tables, indexes, views, query builders, reducers, procedures, schedules, generated clients, subscriptions, and row-level security are supported. A module assembly can be published independently or referenced as a dependency without requiring a separate library build mode.

([#5974](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5974>))

### SpacetimeAuth management from the CLI

The new `spacetime auth` command group lets Maincloud users manage a database's SpacetimeAuth configuration from the command line. It supports identity-provider configuration, project settings, and client creation, inspection, and deletion.

([#5251](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5251>))

## Improvements

### Confirmed HTTP calls now wait for durability

Confirmed HTTP reducer calls now report success only after their transaction is durable. Procedures using confirmed reads likewise wait for transactions opened through `withTx` to become durable before returning, preventing subsequent confirmed work from observing state that could still be lost in a crash.

Confirmation waits have a five-second deadline. A timed-out HTTP call returns `504 Gateway Timeout` with an unknown-outcome error. Callers that do not require this guarantee can continue to use `confirmed=false`.

([#6101](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6101>), [#6154](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6154>))

### Lower subscription memory overhead

The datastore no longer clones the full subscriber state for each transaction. It records transaction-local subscriber and timestamp changes instead, substantially reducing memory usage for databases with many subscribers while preserving subscription and view behavior.

([#6113](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6113>))

### Deterministic TypeScript shuffling

TypeScript modules now provide deterministic random shuffling alongside the existing deterministic random helpers, making shuffled behavior reproducible within module execution and tests.

([#6040](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6040>))

### More complete module unit testing

Rust module unit tests can now access declared environment values and exercise procedures that open transactions with `withTx`. A new guide documents module unit testing for both Rust and TypeScript.

([#6302](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6302>), [#6245](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6245>))

## Security

### Updated .NET XML cryptography dependency

The C# toolchain now uses an updated `System.Security.Cryptography.Xml` dependency that addresses a known vulnerability in the previous package version.

([#6290](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6290>))

## Bug Fixes

### Correct TypeScript `Result` types and serialization

TypeScript result builders now use the same `{ ok: value } | { err: value }` representation as the serializer and deserializer, and error values serialize with the correct variant. Code that compiled against the previous incorrect result shape may require adjustment, but the old shape could not work correctly at runtime.

([#6148](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6148>))

### Fixed TypeScript procedure HTTP edge cases

TypeScript module HTTP requests and handler responses no longer split header values at commas. This fixes headers such as webhook signatures, HTTP dates, and cookies with `Expires` attributes. `ctx.http.fetch` also accepts nonstandard status codes, such as proxy-specific 5xx responses, instead of throwing while constructing the response.

([#6140](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6140>))

### Fixed recursive C# struct type comparison

C# BSATN code generation no longer recurses indefinitely when comparing recursive struct type definitions.

([#6303](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6303>))

### Fixed generated project dependency paths

New projects created from templates now correctly rewrite module unit-test dependencies that use repository-local paths during development. Generated projects can once again build outside the SpacetimeDB source tree.

([#6307](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6307>))

## What's Changed

- Added reusable TypeScript cron, retry, rate-limit, crypto, and Resend submodules in [#5903](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5903>), [#6158](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6158>), and [#6309](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6309>)
- Added C# module submodules and namespace-aware generated APIs in [#5974](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5974>)
- Added the `spacetime auth` CLI management commands in [#5251](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/5251>)
- Made confirmed procedure transactions and HTTP reducer calls wait for durability in [#6101](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6101>) and [#6154](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6154>)
- Reduced subscription memory overhead by replacing full subscriber-state clones with transaction-local deltas in [#6113](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6113>)
- Added deterministic TypeScript random shuffling in [#6040](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6040>)
- Fixed TypeScript `Result` typing and error serialization in [#6148](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6148>)
- Fixed comma-containing HTTP headers and unknown status codes in TypeScript `ctx.http.fetch` in [#6140](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6140>)
- Fixed Rust module tests for procedure transactions and environment values in [#6302](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6302>)
- Fixed infinite recursion in C# BSATN type-definition comparison in [#6303](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6303>)
- Fixed repository-local dependency paths in generated CLI projects in [#6307](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6307>)
- Updated `System.Security.Cryptography.Xml` to address a known vulnerability in [#6290](<https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/pull/6290>)

([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) Continuing a synchronous task whose session was already deleted now fails at once with an error saying to start a new task, instead of waiting out the 30-minute sync poll timeout; a sync poll also stops when the server keeps reporting its session as not found. Completed sync task sessions now honor `background_task.taskCleanupDelayMs` instead of a fixed 10 minutes. Reported by @orgito. ([#11524](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11524), fixes [#11520](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11520)) **omo.dev deploys again after the document-shell change.** The `/design` showcase became a root layout of its own and lost the hourly revalidation it used to inherit, so one prerendered page had no expiry and the deploy's asset-retention check refused the build. ([#11587](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11587), fixes [#11585](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11585)) Release pull requests no longer fail the changelog gate when fragments for the next release land on the base branch after the cut. ([#11574](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11574)) - Release preparation no longer fails its own command-string audit when changelog fragments have been folded into the changelog. ([#11562](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11562)) **The frontend skill now builds in ten habits that design reviewers check for.** Before designing a new screen, a redesign, or a design system, it reads the guideline source in full, defines the ideal state per persona and journey step, and records every gap in a ledger. Controls keep the same box size in every state, and a spinner or arrow never adds padding. Pointer targets are at least 24 px, colour roles come before components (built from shadcn/ui anatomy), glass and dated trend surfaces stay out unless the brief asks for them, and the subtract pass counts the controls. Every UI or design-system deliverable states a per-criterion WCAG 2.2 AA result. ([#11536](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11536), fixes [#11534](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11534)) **macOS computer use releases the keys and buttons it holds even if the engine dies mid-call.** An input request that presses now starts the engine binary again as a hidden release helper and streams every press, drag move and release to it; when the engine is killed, crashes or a request unwinds with something still held, the helper posts the releases (within 2 seconds) through the same routes, leaving any key or button the user is physically holding to the user. The helper runs in its own session, ignores the hangup and terminate a group kill sends until its releases are out, and refuses to run unless the engine that spawned it is its parent and the stream carries its per-spawn token. Other platforms are unchanged. ([#11535](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11535)) **A process child whose provider has no usable sign-in now moves on to the next provider instead of failing.** When the engine refuses a child's first prompt with `provider_credentials_missing` or `provider_credentials_expired`, the task skips the remaining models on that provider and starts on the next provider in its fallback chain, ending on the parent session's model when nothing else is left. Each hop is recorded as a `task_model_fallback` event naming the provider. An engine that does not send these codes behaves exactly as before. Every other refused first prompt in process mode now also carries the engine's validated error code as `cause_code` in its `task_start_failed` event and in the start-failure message (for example `host_refused: host_memory_pressure`); this is diagnostic only and does not change what the task does. ([#11440](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11440), part of [#10806](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10806)) ([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) **A queued steer to a subagent keeps its own id across the child boundary, and a lost acknowledgment is checked before anything is sent again.** A message queued for a child that is still starting reaches it under the id it was queued with, so a drain repeated after a restart replays instead of delivering a second copy. When the child's acknowledgment is lost, omo asks the child whether it holds that id (`get_pending_inputs`): held settles it, not held resends the same id, and an unreadable answer keeps it uncertain instead of guessing. ([#11427](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11427), part of [sisyphuslabs/omo-desktop-app#2838](https://github.com/sisyphuslabs/omo-desktop-app/issues/2838)) ([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) **Model-profile notices no longer reach the model.** A notice such as "model profile ... has no available model" was sent as part of the conversation, so the model read it ahead of your first message, and on a slow start it could cost an extra model request. The notice now stays out of the conversation: when there is something to do, the desktop app shows it as a notice with the next step (sign in from Provider authentication settings, or choose a model in the composer), and a headless run logs it. ([#11365](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11365)) A stored login that failed while a working provider was used instead still reaches you as a notice naming the provider to re-authenticate, and a profile model the registry no longer finds is reported with the step to choose another model. ([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) **Memory read grants now check the file a raw-string tool actually opens.** Containment follows native filesystem traversal before normalizing paths, so a directory symlink followed by `..` cannot redirect a project-memory grant to another identity. ([#11339](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11339)) ([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) **Completed Momus review verdicts are now persisted as numbered Markdown artifacts next to the plan file.** Each `.omo/plans/{plan}.reviews/NNN-okay.md` or `NNN-reject.md` artifact captures the verdict, timestamp, model, plan sha256, review duration, reviewer session id, and the verdict block (the reasoning that precedes the verdict is not stored), so a finished review survives the end of the session. A `.gitignore` written next to the plans keeps the `.reviews` directories out of the user's own staging area. Momus itself stays read-only; persistence happens entirely on the orchestrator side after the review result returns. ([#11237](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11237), fixes [#3002](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/3002)) Thanks to [@surlymochan](https://github.com/surlymochan) for this contribution. ([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) **Release binaries may be up to 200 MiB, and 5.1.49 was not published.** omo 5.1.49's Linux binaries came out over the 182 MiB size budget (linux-x64 200.0 MB, linux-arm64 198.2 MB), so that release stopped before anything was published. ([#11491](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11491)) ([#11525](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11525)) **Every omo.dev page now declares its own language and the dark colour scheme, and starts with a skip link.** Korean, Japanese, Chinese and the other locales set `` to their language (it was always English), form controls and scrollbars render dark, the first Tab offers "Skip to content", focused controls no longer hide under the sticky header, and unknown pages show a 404 in the reader's language. ([#11490](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11490)) **Dimmed graph nodes and quiet labels on omo.dev are readable again.** Nodes off the highlighted path in the workflow graph recede by colour instead of fading to 20% (text contrast goes from 1.1:1 to 5.8:1), and step numbers and the corrected word in the demo no longer use the decoration-only grey. Top-level `test/` and `tests/` resources still ship. ([#11377](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11377), part of [#11373](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11373)) ([#11391](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11391)) - Running a bundled skill no longer writes files inside the installed app, so OmO Desktop no longer reports its files as changed and stops its local server after the coding-agent-sessions, ultimate-browsing or frontend skills run their Python scripts. A manual ast-grep install now downloads into a user cache folder instead of the skill folder. Python the agent runs now keeps its compiled bytecode in an OmO cache folder instead of next to the script, so your projects still start fast without `__pycache__` folders appearing in them; if you set `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` or `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` yourself, OmO leaves both alone. Thanks to @minerva32 for the report. Code v1.144.0

### Changed

- Update to Code 1.144.0

### Fixed

- `--socket-fd` now works: the inherited socket is passed on to the process
  that listens, and the address is logged as `fd:<n>`. Previously code-server
  failed with `listen EEXIST` or `Server has no address`.
- The cookie domain was not being set against the shared root host of proxy
  domains when proxy domains contained template variables like `{{port}}`,
  resulting in having to sign in multiple times per domain instead of only once
  as originally intended.
- When doing the web socket origin check, if the host does not already contain a
  port, fall back to `X-Forwarded-Port`.
- Fix default ports not matching in the web socket origin check (for example
  `https://coder.com` will now match `https://coder.com:443`).
codewhale-hq/Codewhale:
## What's in v0.10.2


Codewhale v0.10.2 adds an animated pet view (`/pet on`), a live Terminal work
dock, per-chat composer colors (`/color`) and a one-time note on the first
start after an update that says what changed. It closes three session
data-loss paths and a `codewhale web` session leak; adds the default Runtime
daemon socket locations to the sandbox deny-list; holds a `curl` or `wget` that uploads a
credential; refuses shell commands containing invisible Unicode; keeps the
Linux sandbox working when a hidden credential directory is a symlink; and
reduces idle TUI redraw work. `/undo` takes back a whole
request, including long and multiline prompts. `exec --auto` explains its
Full Access default, honors an explicitly stricter sandbox, and saves
tool-enabled runs and their failure receipts. Local runtimes appear during
onboarding, `/diff` works outside a Git repository, DeepSeek's Responses route
no longer rejects replayed tool history, and contributor fixes improve token
accounting, relay model lists, localized replies and Windows launcher
guidance. Delegated work continues without model-invented turn or time caps,
and independent workflow steps can continue after another child fails.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.2" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release. Both contain the same compiled runtime.

### Docker / GHCR

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
  -v codewhale-home:/home/codewhale/.codewhale \
  ghcr.io/codewhale-hq/codewhale:v0.10.2
```

The image exposes the same runtime as both `codewhale` and `codew`. The
`latest` tag is also updated on release.

### Cargo (Linux / macOS)

```bash
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The Cargo package installs `codewhale`. Cargo cannot create a second command
alias from one binary target; users who want the shorter spelling can add a
`codew` symlink to that installed executable. The npm, Homebrew, archive,
shell-installer, and container channels install both command names directly.

### Manual download — platform archives (recommended)

Each archive below contains the same runtime under the `codewhale` and
`codew` command names, plus an install script:

| Platform | Archive | Install script |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `codewhale-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Linux ARM64 | `codewhale-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Android ARM64 (Termux) | `codewhale-android-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS x64 | `codewhale-macos-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS ARM | `codewhale-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Windows x64 (installer) | `CodeWhaleSetup.exe` | NSIS setup |
| Windows x64 | `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows x64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-x64-portable.zip` | — |
| Windows ARM64 | `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows ARM64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-arm64-portable.zip` | — |

**Unix (Linux / macOS):**
```bash
tar xzf codewhale-<platform>.tar.gz
cd codewhale-<platform>
./install.sh
```

**Windows:**
- For the installer path, run `CodeWhaleSetup.exe`; it installs
  `codewhale.exe`, `codew.exe`, and `codewhale.bat` under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin`, adds that directory to the
  current-user PATH, and creates a Start Menu shortcut that prefers
  Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`) when it is installed.
- Extract the archive for your machine: `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` or
  `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip`
- Double-click `codewhale.bat` (not the raw `.exe`) to launch
- Run `install.bat` to copy the binaries and launcher to `%USERPROFILE%\bin`
- Add `%USERPROFILE%\bin` to your PATH

The **portable** Windows archive skips the install script — extract and run `codewhale.bat` from any directory. The NSIS installer is currently unsigned and may trigger Windows SmartScreen until a signing certificate is wired into the release pipeline.

Each platform also has **bare, unarchived** `codewhale-<platform>` and
`codew-<platform>` assets. The seven `codewhale-tui-<platform>` filenames
attached to v0.9.5 are byte-identical compatibility copies used only to let
already-installed v0.9.4 clients discover and cross this single-binary
transition; current installers do not expose a third runtime. The legacy npm
package `deepseek-tui` is deprecated and is not republished. For migration
from v0.8.x legacy binary names, see `docs/REBRAND.md`.

### Verify (recommended)

Download the checksum manifests from this Release and verify:

```bash
# Linux — archive bundles
sha256sum -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# Linux — individual binaries
sha256sum -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
```
