## What's Changed
For developers using the agent as a Go package, `Agent.Start` now requires a `context.Context`.

For authors of integrations, existing memory fields other than memory percentage are deprecated in favor of new fields which provide raw byte values. The deprecated fields are still populated, but will be removed from the API in a future version.

```go
type Stats struct {
  // Deprecated fields (populated on hubs <= 0.21.1; will be removed in a future version)
	Mem            float64     `json:"m" cbor:"2,keyasint"`  // Deprecated: GB, use MemBytes. Memory GB fields are kept for older hubs and integrations.
	MaxMem         float64     `json:"mm,omitzero" cbor:"-"` // Deprecated: GB, use MaxMemBytes.
	MemUsed        float64     `json:"mu" cbor:"3,keyasint"` // Deprecated: GB, use MemBytes.
	MemBuffCache   float64     `json:"mb" cbor:"5,keyasint"` // Deprecated: GB, use MemBytes.
	MemZfsArc      float64     `json:"mz,omitzero" cbor:"6,keyasint,omitempty"` // Deprecated: GB, use MemBytes.
	Swap           float64     `json:"s,omitzero" cbor:"7,keyasint,omitempty"`  // Deprecated: GB, use SwapBytes.
	SwapUsed       float64     `json:"su,omitzero" cbor:"8,keyasint,omitempty"` // Deprecated: GB, use SwapBytes.
  // New fields (populated on hub version 0.21.1+ for all agents)
	MemBytes       [4]uint64   `json:"mem,omitzero" cbor:"41,keyasint,omitzero"`  // [total, used, buff/cache, zfs arc] bytes
	MaxMemBytes    uint64      `json:"memm,omitzero" cbor:"-"`                    // max used memory bytes
	SwapBytes      [2]uint64   `json:"swap,omitzero" cbor:"42,keyasint,omitzero"` // [total, used] bytes
}
```

# HyperFrames v0.8.221

Released on 2026-10-30.

Snapshots of video projects take less time because each clip is read once for all the times you ask for. Preview now stops at once when you press Ctrl+C.

## Fixes

- **CLI:** Snapshot probes each video clip once for all the times it is asked for ([b3c47a36a](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/b3c47a36a2bd8dff5bbf3753e3e6fe97d013c42b), [#6798](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6798)).
- **CLI:** Preview stops at once on Ctrl+C after Studio was open ([3e795ece0](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/3e795ece0fec8ef5331058566893f85a50605070), [#6782](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6782)).
- **CLI:** Add takes several names in one call, and adopted audio is labelled voice or sfx ([7f7a4af7c](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/7f7a4af7c48b736fb678d83047ab76af7ca7983a), [#6791](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6791)).
- **CLI:** Check no longer flags a hidden scene child or a small animated sprite ([8c36f3254](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/8c36f3254f0b98aa097f9b02d229d69596a592c2), [#6783](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6783)).
- **Core:** Long cut-list edits play every cut without dropped or late frames ([9fd90d23c](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/9fd90d23c4cc1208965c2179cd25a6d871246df9), [#6785](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6785)).
- **CLI:** Hyperframes docs motion-blur shows the motion blur guide ([21eefcd00](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/21eefcd006f895ee41641de65392b56c7b7e6c0a), [#6779](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6779)).

## Docs & Examples

- **Studio App:** Pending video edits have no cap of 10 ([f43bec76e](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/f43bec76e7ceef13e65b930496f7e1f66779250b), [#6797](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6797)).

## Catalog

- **CLI:** A missing registry item names the closest ones, and a blocked browser says how to allow it ([47a1a9206](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/47a1a92064cef4cf6602199ece1b32b8c16a22ae), [#6799](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6799)).
- **Registry:** Caption components keep the last phrase until its last word ends ([32c01c99a](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/32c01c99a1bbe12e329c4d5812995b07600a1a8a), [#6792](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6792)).

## Internal

hugohe3/ppt-master:
The OpenAI image backend now defaults to `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, and image generation accepts any W:H aspect ratio. This release also brings a round of Edit Native, template-import, and source-conversion fixes that stop content from being silently dropped, plus PowerPoint-exact animation timing.

## AI image generation

- The OpenAI backend now defaults to `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`. Measured on the official endpoint at 1024×1024 medium, it used about a quarter of the output tokens of `gpt-image-2` (~$0.013 vs ~$0.053) and returned in about half the time. It also returns real RGBA for `OPENAI_BACKGROUND=transparent`. `OPENAI_MODEL` still overrides it (fc7aa7c5, 27be992f, af5029c7).
- `aspect_ratio` accepts any positive W:H, decimals included (e.g. `1.85:1`). Unsupported ratios no longer fail a request: each backend picks the nearest size its model allows, reports the adaptation, and placement crops to the requested shape (b1b7f1b2, be8a19da, e61c34ed).
- Rate limits are handled properly. `Retry-After` is honored by every backend and by manifest requeues. Waits are capped so that a huge header value can no longer crash the run or block it for a day, and a run that stops with items still pending exits non-zero (c02689f4, 230afab1, 4c3961a8, 625e05a9).
- `--filename` values containing dots (`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst_hero`) are no longer truncated at the last dot, which made each such run silently overwrite the previous file (c02689f4).

## Edit Native PPTX

- When only a chart's data changes, the imported chart is now patched in place instead of being rebuilt from JSON. Gradient fills, slice separators, legend layout, per-point data labels, marker outlines, and style and theme overrides now survive the edit (78759bf6).
- Charts that do get rebuilt keep the gap width, overlap, inner layout, axis label typography, and chart language. A rebuild no longer borrows an unrelated frame (0396656f). Theme font tokens such as `+mn-ea` stay in their East Asian and complex-script slots (78fcef9b). Charts whose source does not vary point colors are no longer imported as varied (351041e4).
- Editing any cell of an imported table with merged cells no longer makes `--native-charts-and-tables` fail (48ee45f9).
- New objects on a rebuilt slide keep their SVG stacking order. A new full-canvas rect is kept as an object instead of being dropped as a background (bc111480, 523e5bd9).

## PPTX import and Create Template

- Real-world PPTX files with zero-size geometry no longer hard-fail. This covers horizontal and vertical rules, collinear groups, and vertical CJK text groups. Geometry that cannot be recovered is kept and reported instead of silently dropped. Thanks @SunshineLin-li (#329; 5832c3a8, 6965c0db, cafb4ccf, 83ac084b, ce1a6222, e8ac905f).
- Theme line styles (`a:lnRef`) now resolve to the theme's width, cap, dash, and alpha instead of a 1px stroke (83ac084b). Imported custom-geometry connectors export correctly (3b865783).
- Content the author hid in PowerPoint no longer leaks into source Markdown, the Beautify inventory, or rebuilt speaker notes, and each exclusion is reported (2cdae003).
- Beautify now includes chart titles in its frozen inventory and verifier, so a dropped title fails `--verify` (694bdaca).

## Source conversion (source_to_md)

- PowerPoint: Office Math is kept as LaTeX, and the Fallback of `mc:AlternateContent` (3D models, ink, zoom) is read. Chart titles and picture alt text are used as labels (05011292, fd17372d, 6d1cb8ff).
- DOCX: text now matches what Word displays. Simple-field results (caption numbers, document properties) are kept, hidden runs are excluded, and footnote and endnote math is converted (1ad85c14).
- EPUB, ODT, and RTF: text the readers skipped is recovered, including EPUB footnote files (f3660bfc). HTML `<template>` markup no longer leaks into page text (b7a2d9fc).

## Animations

- Animation timing now follows PowerPoint's beat semantics. An after-previous row waits for every effect in its click group to finish, every with-previous delay counts from the beat start, and each beat's rows are grouped under one shared timing node, matching what PowerPoint writes. Thanks @Victor-Quqi (#331; 5b7e56b9, e897e762, dea06b93, 6615a22b).

## Finalize and live preview editor

- Splitting text rows, and other finalize or editor rewrites, now keep the element's id, name, role, visibility, and references, so hidden text no longer becomes visible and locators no longer break (06f0d112).

## Quality checker

- Hyperlinks are compared after XML decoding, so `&` in a query string, an alternate xlink prefix, or a numeric character reference no longer raises a false outline-hyperlink error. Thanks @I1eanch (#338).

## Installation and docs

- Supported Python is now capped at 3.14. The Windows guide adds troubleshooting for source builds: on 3.15, PyYAML has no wheel yet and pip falls back to compiling it (15baa7c5).

hypit-ai/hypit:
## Upgrade notice

Existing 0.3.0 project components may need SDK import and dependency updates. Read the [0.3.1 migration guide](https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit/blob/v0.3.1/migrations/0.3.1.md) before updating a production. Preserve existing Sources, Runs and Results; update the project lockfile deliberately.

## Changes

- Video-domain SDKs are independently versioned npm packages. Default video capabilities still install with Hypit; generic host APIs remain under @hypit/hypit.
- Studio resolves computed CaptionTiming references, displays named Instants even when no Track consumes them, and retains the compact unified Timeline header and projection rows. Windows remain visible through their consuming Track Items.
- Studio observes atomic Source-file replacement and updates watches as the loaded Source closure changes.
- Pricing reports Producer failures completely and exits unsuccessfully when planning fails.
- Skill and documentation use the current SDK package names and installed Studio paths. The Skill updates separately through `npx skills add hypit-ai/hypit -g`.

For an existing global CLI installation, use `npm install -g @hypit/hypit@0.3.1` after publication completes. For a project-local installation, update the existing package.json and lockfile using the project package manager and migration guide.

This release does not publish the optional partner Provider packages or the four optional ecosystem components.

icsharpcode/ILSpy:
In this point release, we kept focussing on improving decompilation accuracy and performance (raw performance as well as memory usage) across the board. This is why again a lot of work went in the category Testing / Infrastructure.

One major performance win to point out is that we now ship `ilspycmd` with native AOT packages for linux-x64 and win-x64. Measured on win-x64 against the same 3 MB input (`ICSharpCode.Decompiler.dll`), medians of five runs:

| Call shape | managed tool | AOT package |
|---|---|---|
| `--version` | 219 ms | 45 ms |
| `-l c` (list classes) | 384 ms | 93 ms |
| `--type` one large class | 1,446 ms | 199 ms |
| `--type` one small class | 1,797 ms | 315 ms |
| `-p` whole project (881 files) | 6.3 s | 2.9 s |

For an agent loop that spawns ilspycmd per question that is a 4x to 7x reduction per call! 

# New Features

* PR #4248: Add a search box to the Options tab
* PR #4241: Add opt-in RID-specific and Native AOT packages for ilspycmd
* PR #4197: Add cross-platform PDB dumping to ilspycmd

# Enhancements

* PR #4268: Native AOT fidelity follow-up: resolver lookup, culture independence, gate coverage
* PR #4259: Native AOT fidelity for the ICSharpCode.Decompiler package
* PR #4256: Make ilspycmd -il honor the --type and --member selection
* PR #4247: Report ilspycmd usage mistakes instead of crashing
* PR #4236: Transform `value.<Clone>$()` into `value with {}` even if there are no initializers
* PR #4222: Improved decompilation support for VB.NET closures
* PR #4201: Rewrite VB WithEvents WinForms initialization
* PR #4160: Decide extension method syntax in CallBuilder
* PR #4188: Detect generated closure cache types
* PR #4185: Handle required members on record copy constructors
* PR #4179: Include member context in decompilation error comments
* PR #4171: Recognize metadata property backing fields

# Testing / Infrastructure

* PR #4285: Fix decompdiff platform reference staging
* PR #4283: Improve Debug Steps and decompdiff workflows
* PR #4276: nugetfuzz: add parallelization + report caught exceptions
* PR #4274: Migrate ILSpy.sln to the SLNX solution format
* PR #4269: Cut the ILSpy.Tests wall clock: cheap fixtures, dead waits, duplicate tests, and process sharding
* PR #4261: Keep tests off the network unless a toolset download is actually needed
* PR #4255: Add top 500 NuGet package list
* PR #4254: Reenable LiftedOperators tests
* PR #4230: Add allocation trace viewer
* PR #4240: Use local .NET Framework assemblies in nugetfuzz
* PR #4235: Fallback from unsupported netcoreapp assets in nugetfuzz
* PR #4205: Clean up package restore (Diasymreader)
* PR #4187: Let decompdiff reports use full width
* PR #4184: Separate obfuscated names in nugetfuzz
* PR #4183: Stream nugetfuzz HTML report generation
* PR #4177: Index NuGet assemblies by contained name in decompdiff

# Contributions

* PR #4253: Fix #3702: Don't rewrite GetValueOrDefault() to == true in ?. chains — @dualfroz, thank you!
* PR #4251: Fix #4017: Look through LdObjIfRef on the operand of await — @dualfroz, thank you!
* PR #4231: Fix #4135: Keep bool-to-int conditional in its local — @dualfroz, thank you!
* PR #4216: Add option to highlight usages of the symbol at the caret — @pieroviano, thank you!
* PR #4228: Fix #4153: keep foreach when a named argument inlines the loop variable — @LiquidSnake0, thank you!
* PR #4232: Fix #4137: Keep nint in conditionals with mixed native int branches — @dualfroz, thank you!

# Performance

* PR #4266: Start the startup warm-ups before Avalonia's setup
* PR #3963: Substring optimizations: eliminate hot-path allocations (audit top 8)
* PR #4229: Avoid cloning settings for every method
* PR #4164: Coalesce the global command re-query
* PR #4157: Coalesce the assembly tree's selection and removal fan-out

# Bug Fixes

* PR #4250: Fix #4245: Ignore find-panel clicks when resolving reference clicks
* PR #4249: Fix #4246: Scope prefixes no longer leak into search keywords
* PR #4225: Fix #2829: Emit continue for leave through try-finally

iina/iina:
IINA 1.5.0 introduces the biggest interface redesign since its launch.

In-app auto update will be published within 24 hours.

## Redesigned Website

Check out our new website at [iina.io](https://iina.io) and read our [blog post](https://iina.io/blog/150-release/) about the 1.5.0 release!

## New

- Added a new Settings window #6016.
  - Added a confirmation prompt when deleting keybinding config files #5972.
  - Split the "Video/Audio" settings page into two pages #5310.
  - Added a new plugin store in Settings #6081.
- Updated the Quick Settings sidebar and added a new Layout pane #6132.
  - You can now freely change the window aspect ratio by unlocking it #6100.
  - In the new Layout pane, options are provided to dock sidebars, the OSC, and the titlebar.
  - All sidebars are now resizable #6161.
  - The sidebars no longer blocks top and bottom OSCs.
  - The standard window buttons are always visible when the leading sidebar is shown.
  - The mpv option table can now automatically parse pasted mpv options #6203.
- Added Liquid Glass support #6001.
- We now have a new set of icons which adapts the new liquid glass design #6401.
- Added Live Text support #6101.
- Added an option to configure thumbnail width #885.
- Show the chapter name on the slider alongside the video time #6078.
- You can now unshuffle the playlist if it hasn't changed since the last shuffle #6171.
- Added shortcut 'O' to show current time #5694.
- Added support for `tone-mapping-param` #6338.

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed OSC freeze when interacting with UI (slider, button, etc.) #168.
- Fixed unintended auto-play when connecting or switching Bluetooth devices #6025.
- Fixed Quick Settings controls not updating when a new subtitle is added #6035.
- Fixed IINA outputting to the wrong audio device #6034.
- Fixed opening an audio file a second time showing the main window #6065.
- Fixed a potential crash in `updateVideoTabControl` #6093.
- Fixed a crash when reloading plugins #6094.
- Fixed multiple playback histories not being recorded for online media #6116.
- Fixed a crash in `iina-plugin new` when using the `--url` flag #6241.
- Fixed several instances where the old preference was incorrectly shown #6254.
- Fixed mini player responds to scrolling events in the playlist view.
- Fixed the preview displays when cursor is not on the progress bar #6288.
- Fixed HDR tone mapping not working on SDR display #5119.
- Fixed wrong window control position for RTL languages #6192.
- Fixed a crash when connecting to external displays #6215.
- Fixed unwanted scroll actions on sliders #6324.
- Fixed artist and album info sometimes not being updated for Now Playing #6364.
- Fixed dragging multiple media onto initial window always opening them in one player window #6281.
- Fixed a crash in the font picker #6393.
- Fixed clipped font preview #6394.

## Improvements

- Render subtitles for media without a video track #6030.
- Improved performance when reading track lists from mpv #5820.
- Revamped the log viewer #6041.
- Revamped the playback history window #6117.
  - The history window now shows the media title #6113.
- Revamped the welcome window #6410.
- The OSC toolbar buttons now reflect the current state #6062.
- The action buttons in mini player also reflect the current state #6267.
- Changed the volume slider to greyscale #6071.
- Added action images for menu items on macOS 26 #6086.
- Updated the look and feel of the inspector window #6059, #5275.
- You can now select and copy the text from the inspector window #6092.
- Unified the font size in the inspector window #5275.
- When changing to a video with a different aspect ratio, the window now keeps the same window area instead of the same width #6105.
- The unsupported subtitle error is no longer shown for auto-loaded subtitles #6145.
- Hide the HDR switch when it's not available #6157.
- Richer OSD display with volume sliders etc.
- Improved handling of sub-second rollover in VideoTime time formatting #6239.
- Added warnings to the S/PDIF settings #6257.
- Improved the playlist progress indicator #6268.
- Show OSD even when applied volume is constrained #6195.
- Improved the error message in the open URL dialog #6189.
- Hide is the default behavior when entering Picture-in-Picture #6283.
- Target peak is splitted into two settings #6308.
- The settings window is now not movable by background #6323.
- Don't show permission alert when the plugin requires no permission.

## Updates

- Bumped system requirement to macOS 11 for Intel Macs #6019.
- Updated mpv to 0.41.0 and FFmpeg to 9.0.1 #6261.
  - Added the new `--sub-border-style` option from mpv 0.39.0, #6305.
- Updated Sparkle to 2.9.6 #6271.

## Plugin API

- Added plugin i18n support.
- Fixed the `.pipChanged` event sometimes not being emitted.
- Fixed a crash when trying to open a URL #6230.
- Fixed various permission issues #6372.
- Use main branch to check for updates.

### Deprecation Notice

IINA 1.5.0 now requires macOS 11 Big Sur or later for Intel Macs and macOS 12 Monterey or later for Apple Silicon Macs. Due to limitations of Xcode, we expect to deprecate macOS 11 in the following IINA release.

jamiepine/voicebox: ## The Capture release. Voicebox stops being just a voice-cloning studio and becomes a full AI voice studio. Hold a key anywhere on your machine, speak, release — the transcript lands in the focused text field. Flip the primitive around and any MCP-aware agent — Claude Code, Cursor, Spacebot — speaks back through an on-screen pill in one of your cloned voices. A local LLM sits between the two, so transcripts come out clean and voice profiles can carry a personality that reshapes what the agent says before it gets spoken. ### Dictation — speak anywhere, paste anywhere - **Global hotkey capture.** Hold a customizable chord anywhere on your machine (defaults: right-Cmd + right-Option on macOS, right-Ctrl + right-Shift on Windows), speak, release. A floating on-screen pill walks through recording → transcribing → refining → done with a live elapsed timer. The transcript lands as clean text. - **Push-to-talk and toggle modes, each with its own chord.** The default toggle chord adds Space to the push-to-talk chord. Holding PTT and tapping Space mid-hold upgrades a hold into a hands-free session without a gap in the recording. - **Auto-paste into the focused app.** Once transcription finishes, Voicebox synthesizes a paste into whatever text field had focus when you started the chord — not wherever focus drifted while you were talking. Works across Dvorak / AZERTY layouts. Your clipboard is saved before and restored after. - **Chord picker UI.** Customize either chord from Settings → Captures by holding the keys you want. Left/right modifier badges show whether a key is the left or right variant. - **Defaults stay out of your way.** macOS defaults avoid left-hand Cmd+Option chords so the system shortcuts they collide with stay yours. Windows defaults route around AltGr collisions on German / French / Spanish layouts. - **Accessibility permission is scoped.** If macOS Accessibility isn't granted, dictation still runs and transcripts still land in the Captures tab — only synthetic paste is disabled. The permission prompt lives inline next to the auto-paste toggle, not as a global banner. ### Personality — voice profiles that speak for themselves Voice profiles now carry an optional **personality** — a free-form description of who this voice is, up to 2000 characters. When set, two new controls appear next to the generate button, each powered by a new Qwen3 LLM running entirely locally: - **Compose** — the shuffle button drops a fresh in-character line into the textarea. Click again for variety, edit before speaking. - **Speak in character** — the wand toggle runs your input through the personality LLM before TTS, preserving every idea but delivering it in the character's voice. The same LLM doubles as the refinement model, so there's one local LLM in the app, not two. **API surface.** `POST /generate`, `POST /speak`, and the MCP `voicebox.speak` tool accept `personality: bool`. `POST /profiles/{id}/compose` powers the shuffle button. MCP client bindings carry a `default_personality: bool` that applies when `personality` isn't passed explicitly. ### Agents — any MCP-aware agent gets a voice Voicebox ships a built-in **Model Context Protocol** server at `http://127.0.0.1:17493/mcp` so Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, VS Code MCP extensions — any MCP-aware agent — can call into your local Voicebox install. Four tools ship with dotted names: - **`voicebox.speak`** — speak text in any voice profile, with optional `personality: true` to run through the profile's personality LLM first - **`voicebox.transcribe`** — Whisper transcription of a base64 blob or an absolute local path. Path mode is restricted to loopback callers so a Voicebox bound on `0.0.0.0` doesn't double as an unauthenticated arbitrary-local-file read primitive. - **`voicebox.list_captures`** — recent captures with their transcripts - **`voicebox.list_profiles`** — available voice profiles (cloned + preset) - **Streamable HTTP as primary transport.** Cursor / Windsurf / VS Code / Claude Code all support it out of the box — drop a `mcpServers` block with the URL and an `X-Voicebox-Client-Id` header. - **Stdio shim for clients that don't speak HTTP MCP.** A `voicebox-mcp` binary ships inside the app bundle as a Tauri sidecar. The Settings page renders the install snippet with the right absolute path pre-filled. - **Per-client voice binding.** Pin Claude Code to Morgan, Cursor to Scarlett, Cline to its own voice — the `X-Voicebox-Client-Id` header resolves to a bound voice whenever `speak` is called without an explicit `profile`. Managed in **Settings → MCP**. - **Profile resolution precedence.** Explicit `profile` arg (name or id, case-insensitive) → per-client binding → global default from `capture_settings.default_playback_voice_id` → error with a pointer to Settings. - **Speaking pill.** Agent-initiated speech surfaces the same on-screen pill as dictation, in a `speaking` state with the profile name and an elapsed timer. Silent background TTS is a trust hazard — the pill always shows what's coming out of your machine. - **`POST /speak` REST wrapper.** Same code path and voice resolution for shell scripts, ACP, A2A, GitHub Actions, or anything else that isn't MCP-native. **Claude Code one-liner:** ``` claude mcp add voicebox --transport http --url http://127.0.0.1:17493/mcp --header "X-Voicebox-Client-Id: claude-code" ``` ### Refinement A clean transcript needs more than Whisper. Each capture flows through a small Qwen3 LLM that strips fillers, fixes punctuation, and optionally rewrites self-corrections — all on-device. - **Loop-stripping before the LLM sees the transcript.** Whisper's "thanks for watching thanks for watching thanks for watching…" hallucination loops are collapsed at a six-identical-tokens threshold (case-insensitive) so a small refinement model can't echo them back. Coverage spans single-word runs, multi-word phrases, CJK character runs, and Japanese emphasis patterns; legitimate repetition ("no, no, no, no, no") doesn't cross the threshold. - **Per-capture flag snapshot.** `smart_cleanup`, `self_correction`, and `preserve_technical` are stored on each capture, so refinement can be re-run later with different flags without losing the raw transcript. - **Model picker** — Qwen3 0.6B (400 MB, very fast), 1.7B (1.1 GB, fast), 4B (2.5 GB, full quality). 0.6B is the default; 1.7B is the sweet spot for transcripts with code identifiers. ### Captures tab + settings Settings → Captures is now the home for the whole dictation flow: - **Dictation**: global shortcut toggle, push-to-talk chord picker, toggle chord picker, live pill preview, auto-paste into focused field (with inline accessibility prompt). - **Transcription**: model picker (Whisper Base / Small / Medium / Large / Turbo), language lock. - **Refinement**: auto-refine toggle, model picker, smart cleanup, remove self-corrections, preserve technical terms. - **Playback**: default voice for the Captures tab's "Play as" action — picking a voice from the split-button persists the choice across tab switches and restarts. - **Storage**: captures folder quick-open. ### Stories — timeline editor The Stories tab graduates from a TTS sequencer into a real timeline editor. Same generation-row backing, but clips now compose with imported audio, per-clip levels, and a flexible track stack. - **Import external audio.** Drag a music file onto the story content area or pick one from the new "Import audio" entry in the add-clip popover. Accepted formats: wav / mp3 / flac / ogg / m4a / aac / webm, capped at 200 MB. Imported clips show their filename instead of a profile name and skip the regenerate / version-picker controls — there's nothing to regenerate. - **Per-clip volume.** A `Volume2` icon in the clip-edit toolbar opens a 0–200% slider. Adjustments apply live and to exports. Split and duplicate carry the volume forward into the new clips. - **Regenerate** from both the clip's chat-list dropdown and the track-editor toolbar. Re-runs the underlying generation through the same path the History tab uses, with completion tracked in the global pending set. - **Add empty tracks above or below the timeline** via tiny `+` strips at the top of the topmost label cell and the bottom of the bottommost. Sticky in the label column so they follow horizontal scroll. - **Zoom bar tracks the project.** Min scope is 10 seconds visible (zoomed in cap), max is the entire project (zoomed out cap), default lands on 60 s. Both the +/− buttons and the scrollbar edge-drag handles clamp to those dynamic bounds. ### Interface - **Theme selector.** Light / dark / system in **Settings → General**, persisted across sessions. System mode listens for OS-level appearance changes and flips live without a restart. - **Scrubbable waveform player on captures.** The capture detail card now embeds a WaveSurfer waveform with click-to-seek and a current / total timestamp pair, replacing the static duration label. - **Capture pill light mode.** The on-screen pill gets a dedicated light palette so it stays legible against bright windows. - **Readiness checklist in the Captures settings sidebar.** The same six-gate checklist the Captures empty state uses mirrors into Settings → Captures so a red gate can't hide behind a green toggle. Hidden once every gate is green. macOS-only rows (Input Monitoring, Accessibility) hide entirely on Windows and Linux. ### Windows parity Same dictation flow on Windows. Right-hand default chord (Ctrl+Shift) avoids AltGr collisions on layouts where Ctrl+Alt is the compose key. Focus is captured at chord-start so paste lands in the original field even if focus drifts during transcribe/refine.

## Jan v0.8.8: security fixes, llama.cpp 0.7.0, and Trusted Hosts for the local API

A security update to v0.8.7. We recommend updating. Your data and settings carry over; a few behaviours change, listed under **What you might notice**.

### Security

- **Links in chat open in your browser.** Links in model replies, tool results, model cards and release notes now always open in your system browser, never inside Jan's window. Links that aren't web or email links are shown as plain text.
- **The local API server checks where browser requests come from.** A web page can only call it if its origin is trusted: the same machine, Jan itself, or a host you list in **Trusted Hosts**. Requests without a browser origin (SDKs, scripts, curl, Claude Code) work as before.
- **Server-side tool execution stays opt-in for every endpoint.** Requests to the local API run MCP tools only when **Settings > Local API Server** allows server-side tool execution.
- **Paths are checked before Jan reads or writes them.** Thread and assistant ids, and the file operations extensions use, stay inside Jan's data folder.
- **The Claude Code integration writes your shell profile safely.** Values are quoted, unusual variable names are refused, and Jan's lines are kept in one marked block that Reset removes completely without touching your own lines.
- **The agent's file tools no longer follow a link out of their workspace**, and folders such as your home, credentials and startup folders can't be attached as writable.
- **Windows: Jan runs system tools from the Windows system folder**, and sign-in links are opened without going through `cmd`.
- **MCP sign-in only uses web addresses** (`http`/`https`) for its endpoints.

### What you might notice

- **Trusted Hosts for browser-based clients.** A web app on another machine (for example Open WebUI's direct connection) or a browser extension calling Jan's API needs its host added to **Settings > Local API Server > Trusted Hosts**. Entries can include a scheme, so `app://obsidian.md` works for Obsidian plugins (thanks to [@SnowingFox](https://github.com/SnowingFox), [#8608](https://github.com/janhq/jan/issues/8608)). Pages without a normal origin (local files, sandboxed frames) can be allowed by listing `file://` or `null`.
- **The CORS switch now takes effect**, and it starts **on** after updating. In earlier versions it was shown but had no effect.
- **Custom environment variables for Claude Code:** keys that change how programs are found (`PATH`, `PATHEXT`, `SystemRoot`, `ComSpec`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`, `JAN_*` and the GPU runtime paths Jan uses) are refused with a message. Other variables, including `NODE_OPTIONS`, save as before.
- **Moving the data folder** to a system folder, your home folder itself or a drive root (for example `D:\`) is refused; choose a folder such as `D:\Jan`.
- **MCP servers whose sign-in endpoints aren't web addresses** now show a sign-in error.

### New

**llama.cpp engine 0.7.0.**

The bundled engine moves from 0.5.0 to 0.7.0 (b11669). New per-model settings: an **MoE expert GPU cache** for mixture-of-experts models, **Probabilistic draft sampling** and **Draft batch size** for speculative decoding. They default to the engine's own defaults, so nothing changes unless you set them. Saved prompt caches from the previous engine are discarded once and rebuilt. ([#9399](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9399))

### Fixes

**Local models failed to load on Windows when the user name had non-English characters** (for example Cyrillic). ([#9418](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9418))

**With an HTTP proxy configured, documents with "Use embeddings" failed**, because Jan's requests to its own engine went through the proxy. They now go direct; remote providers still use the proxy. ([#9353](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9353))

**An attachment was sent again on every turn**, adding a copy per message and defeating the prompt cache. It's now included once per request. Thanks to [@yaodong-shen](https://github.com/yaodong-shen). ([#9358](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9358))

**With Shell turned off, a model that called the shell ended its reply.** It now gets "Shell is turned off" and the reply continues. ([#9319](https://github.com/janhq/jan/issues/9319))

**macOS: quitting Jan left the MLX server running** with its model in memory. It's stopped on quit, and one left by an earlier Jan is stopped at startup; an MLX server you started yourself is left alone. ([#9355](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9355))

### Thanks

Fixes in this release include work from [@greatjourney589](https://github.com/greatjourney589) ([#8068](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/8068)), [@SnowingFox](https://github.com/SnowingFox) ([#8627](https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/8627)) and [@orenyomtov](https://github.com/orenyomtov).

### Known issues

- **Auto compact** needs **Max Context Tokens** set for remote models; Jan does not detect a remote model's context window yet ([#9317](https://github.com/janhq/jan/issues/9317)).
- Local models do not run on Intel Macs, as in v0.8.5.

jdx/mise:
Experimental daemons can now run container images with Docker or Podman, and named preset ports can get their own port per worktree. This release also adds `position = "append"` for `env._.path`, an `extra_ca_certs` setting for TLS-inspecting proxies, and a `registry_index` option for locking `pypi:` tools. It fixes several lockfile, PyPI, Homebrew and task issues.

## Added

- **Container images as daemons (experimental).** A custom daemon with an `image` key runs through `docker run` or `podman run`. It supports ports, readiness checks, `depends`, the proxy and `mise daemons logs`, just like other daemons. Every port is published on `127.0.0.1` only. Containers are named per project and worktree, so two checkouts never clash, and a stale container left behind by a killed run is removed before the next start. `runtime = "auto"` (the default) uses `docker` if it is on `PATH`, otherwise `podman`. You can set `MISE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` to use any Docker-compatible CLI. `data_mount` bind-mounts a per-checkout data directory, and `ready_cmd` can use `{{ runtime }}`, `{{ container }}` and port placeholders. Limitations: mise does not pull or build images or start the Docker/Podman service, only TCP ports are supported, and starting a container daemon on Windows fails. [#15182](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15182) (@jdx)

  ```toml
  [daemons.cockroach]
  image = "cockroachdb/cockroach:v25.1.0"
  command = ["start-single-node", "--insecure"]
  port = { auto = true, base = 26257 }
  ports.http = { container = 8080, auto = true, base = 27000 }
  data_mount = "/cockroach/cockroach-data"
  ready_cmd = "{{ runtime }} exec {{ container }} cockroach sql --insecure -e 'select 1'"
  ```

- **Per-worktree named ports for daemon presets.** Named preset ports such as `http_port` on `cockroachdb` or `monitor_port` on `nats` now accept `{ auto = true, base, stride }`, just like the primary port. Each linked worktree adds its slot to the port's own `base`. Before, these ports were either fixed or offset from the preset default. When `base` is omitted, it defaults to the preset's port. Integer overrides still work as before. mise now reports a load error if an `auto` named port collides with another daemon's port in the same project. [#15181](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15181) (@jdx)

  ```toml
  [daemons.cockroach]
  preset = "cockroachdb"
  version = "26"
  port = { auto = true, base = 26258 }
  ports.http_port = { auto = true, base = 27000 }
  ```

- **`position = "append"` for `env._.path`.** Appended entries go after tool paths and before the inherited `PATH`. This lets directories like `~/bin` or `~/.cargo/bin` stop shadowing tools that mise installs. The default is still `"prepend"`. [#15158](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15158) (@jdx, @Mossop)

  ```toml
  [env]
  _.path = [
    "bin",
    { path = ["~/bin", "~/.cargo/bin"], position = "append" },
  ]
  ```

- **`extra_ca_certs` setting.** `extra_ca_certs` (`MISE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`) points to a PEM bundle that mise trusts in addition to its usual roots, on every platform. Use it when you're behind a traffic-inspecting proxy such as Socket Firewall. It covers mise's own HTTP requests: downloads, version lookups, GitHub API calls, attestation checks and vfox plugins. Programs that mise runs, such as git and uv, keep using their own certificate settings. You can set it only in the environment or in global config. The path must be absolute or start with `~/`. If the bundle is unusable, mise warns and keeps its usual roots. [#15171](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15171) (@jdx, @abjectnotfound)

  ```sh
  MISE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/proxy-ca.pem mise install
  ```

- **`registry_index` for `pypi:` tools.** Set `registry_index = "priority"` to search a per-tool `registry_url` before PyPI when locking. This works for registries that host only your own packages, such as Gitea/Forgejo, pypiserver or a static index. The tool always comes from the registry, and only packages the registry doesn't have fall back to PyPI. The default, `"default"`, keeps the current behavior: the registry replaces PyPI. [#15157](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15157) (@jdx)

  ```toml
  [tools]
  "pypi:black" = { version = "25.9.0", registry_url = "<your-registry>/api/packages/org/pypi/simple/{}/", registry_index = "priority" }
  ```

- **`secret()` in `merge = "missing"` dotfile entries.** Tera templates in these entries can now call `secret()`. mise asks only for the secrets of keys missing from the target, so you can add a key to a private config later without entering the existing ones again. `mise dot status` and `mise dot diff` never read or prompt for a secret. Enforced `merge = true` entries still can't use `secret()`. [#15168](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15168) (@jdx, @thernstig)
- **Danger Swift libraries.** The `danger-swift` registry entry now uses Danger's official installer, so `libDanger` and the Swift modules are installed with the executable. You still need to install Node and Danger JS separately. [#15120](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15120) (@Mostafa-Ashraf97)

## Fixed

- **Lockfiles**
  - `mise upgrade` now updates every lock entry of a tool that is declared in more than one config file, such as `config.toml` and a `conf.d` fragment. Before, the old entry stayed in the lockfile and `mise outdated` kept offering the same upgrade. [#15164](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15164) (@jdx, @eliebleton-manomano)
  - `http:` tools with a `file://` URL and no `checksum` install and lock again under the default `lockfile_mode = "generate"`. mise now hashes the local file directly. [#15180](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15180) (@jdx, @hcrosse)
  - `mise install` no longer exits 1 when a git task include can't be loaded, for example a private repository in CI. It warns and leaves the lockfile unchanged. An explicit `mise lock` still fails. [#15166](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15166) (@jdx)
- **PyPI / pipx**
  - `mise lock` now locks a `pypi:` tool's dependency graph with the selected Python, even when that Python isn't on `PATH`. If a per-tool `python` isn't installed yet, uv may download it for resolution only, unless `offline` is set. [#15153](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15153) (@jdx)
  - Tools from registries that publish no upload times can now have their dependency graph locked when `minimum_release_age` is set. Dependencies still respect the cutoff. [#15159](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15159) (@jdx)
  - Repos that lock the same tool and dependencies on different days now share one install instead of each creating its own copy. Each affected tool gets one new install the first time you install it after upgrading. [#15179](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15179) (@jdx, @tecnobrat)
- **Homebrew**
  - Source builds of tap formulae whose `post_install` uses Homebrew's `MachO` no longer fail. These steps are skipped with a warning. [#15152](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15152) (@jdx)
  - `install_symlink` with a relative source, such as `bin.install_symlink "foo" => "bar"`, now resolves against the target directory, as Homebrew does, instead of failing with `different prefix`. [#15173](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15173) (@waynehoover)
  - Cask postflight hooks that use `staged_path` can now access the binary payload. This fixes installs such as `brew-cask:dynatrace-oss/tap/dtctl`. [#14837](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14837) (@azohra)
- **Tasks**
  - A remote file task (one whose `file` is an HTTP URL) with its own `env` no longer fails with exit 127 when it runs as a sub-task or dependency. [#15178](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15178) (@jdx)
  - mise now accepts comments in `turbo.json`, which is parsed as JSONC, and in `global.json`, which still rejects trailing commas. Before, a commented `turbo.json` printed a warning on every run and its task suggestions were dropped, and a commented `global.json` broke dotnet version detection. [#15141](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15141) (@jdx)
- `mise prune` no longer removes tool versions that tasks still need when those tasks come from `task_config.includes` files, default task directories, or executable scripts with `#MISE tools=...`. [#15156](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15156) (@jdx)
- `latest` for `gem:` tools no longer resolves to a RubyGems prerelease such as `4.1.0.beta3`. To get prereleases, request one explicitly or set `MISE_PRERELEASES=1`. [#15143](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15143) (@dennmart)
- When the active version doesn't provide a shim's executable, the error now names that version and the config that set it, and lists the installed versions that do provide it. Before, mise said "No version is set" and suggested switching versions with `mise use -g`. [#15165](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15165) (@jdx, @mzagaja)
- `mise upgrade` and `mise outdated` no longer say "All tools are up to date" when a version lookup fails. They now list the tools they could not check. [#15171](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15171) (@jdx, @abjectnotfound)

## Changed

- Homebrew formulae are now resolved from the bulk `formula.json` index, with caching for tap metadata and cask evaluations. In one large setup, warm `mise bootstrap packages upgrade --dry-run` dropped from about 7.7s to 3.7s, and `status` from about 4.0s to 1.5s. The first run on a machine downloads the index once. [#15183](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15183) (@waynehoover)

## Deprecated

- `lockfile_mode = "merge"` is deprecated in favor of the default `generate` mode. Nothing changes yet. mise will start warning in 2027.4.0, and the mode will be removed in 2027.10.0. To migrate, delete the `lockfile_mode = "merge"` line (or unset `MISE_LOCKFILE_MODE=merge`). [#15184](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15184) (@jdx)

## Documentation

- The dotfiles docs now show how to use profile variants to apply an entry only when several environments are active. [#15154](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15154) (@jdx, @miroslavkrysl)

## New Contributors

* @nurazon59 made their first contribution in [#15167](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15167)
* @Mostafa-Ashraf97 made their first contribution in [#15120](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15120)
* @dennmart made their first contribution in [#15143](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15143)

jgm/pandoc:
I'm pleased to announce the release of pandoc 3.13,
available in the usual places:

Binary packages & changelog:
https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/tag/3.13

Source & API documentation:
http://hackage.haskell.org/package/pandoc-3.13

This release fixes some regressions and makes many minor
improvements.  See the changelog for full details.

Behavior changes:

- Locations of errors in default files are now reported.
- YAML is now parsed with the yamlet library, which implements
  YAML 1.2. As a result, we'll get better error messages, and:

  + `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y` and `n` are strings, not booleans.
  + Duplicate keys in a mapping are an error. They were a warning.
  + `.5`, `.inf` and `.nan` are numbers.

  The most likely way this change will bite you is if you use
  `no` in a boolean field. This will be interpreted as a nonempty
  value, which will be treated as truthy in a template.

API changes:

- Text.Pandoc.Sharde: export `plainToPara` and `paraToPlain`.
- Text.Pandoc.Writers.Shared: export new functions `wrapColumns` and
  `rendereWithTemplate`.
- Text.Pandoc.Translations: `readTranslations` now takes the path
  of the file as argument.

Thanks to all who contributed, especially new contributors
Andrzej Rybczak, Patrick Creighton, Wleeaf, and enieuwy.

<details>
  <summary>Click to expand changelog</summary>

- Report the location of errors in defaults files (#8759, Andrzej Rybczak). An invalid value in a defaults file gave an error at the start of the file, with no indication of the field. The error now names the option and points at its value.

- Use yamlet for YAML parsing. Pandoc parsed YAML with the yaml package, which depends on the C library libyaml. It now uses yamlet, a pure Haskell YAML 1.2 parser. Values still go through the existing aeson instances. Note these behavior changes:

  - `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y` and `n` are strings, not booleans, as in YAML 1.2.
  - YAML errors now show the file, the line and the column, with the offending line. In metadata blocks the line is the line in the document.
  - Duplicate keys in a mapping are an error. They were a warning.
  - `.5`, `.inf` and `.nan` are numbers.

- Docx reader:

  - Read `w:fldSimple` fields (#11944, Aslak Hellesøy).
  - Keep grid columns that have no width (#11989, Patrick Creighton). `w:w` is optional on `w:gridCol`, but `elemToTblGrid` skipped the grid columns that had none. The table then had fewer columns than its rows had cells, and the extra cells were dropped. Every grid column is now kept. If any of them has no (readable) width, all columns get the default width.
  - Fix namespaces in notes and comments (#11991, Patrick Creighton). The contents of footnotes, endnotes and comments were read with the namespace prefixes declared in word/document.xml rather than in their own parts.
  - Records the indentation of each list level and track the open list levels; an unnumbered paragraph whose left indentation matches the text indentation of an open level is treated as a continuation of that level’s current item, rather than as a block quote (cf. #9197).
  - Recover from fields with a missing instruction (#11943, enieuwy). This fixes a bug that could lead to content being omitted.
  - Fix regression (from 3.11) in parsing column widths (#11969). The regression caused only the first column to get assigned its alignment; every other column received default alignment. In addition, in 3.11 alignment was taken from the header row if present; this changed behavior from earlier versions, which took it from the first body row. We revert to the earlier behavior, using the header row only if there are no body rows. It’s common for the header to have different alignment than the rest.
  - Keep tracked paragraph marks inside notes (#11971, Aslak Hellesøy).

- RST reader:

  - Allow inline markup and bare links after `:`, `/`, `'`, `"`, `<` (Wleeaf). Fixes a regression since 3.2.1; these characters could no longer precede an inline markup start-string or a bare URI or email address, although the reStructuredText spec allows them. Also implement the rule that a start-character between an opening character and its closing counterpart, as in `(*)` or `"*"`, does not trigger inline markup.

- RTF reader:

  - Fix tokenization bug (#11981). We were consuming certain symbols after `\uNNNN` during tokenization. This led to an *extra* character being consumed as the “fallback,” so letters went missing after encoded unicode characters.

- LaTeX reader:

  - Detect macro expansion loops across `doMacros` calls (#11088).

- ODT reader:

  - Fix start numbers with `text:continue-numbering` (#9595).

- Markdown writer:

  - Write wide tables as grid tables instead of falling back to HTML (#11945, Aslak Hellesøy).
  - Don’t drop notes in notes.
  - Fix regression with code block language (#11987). We try to identify which class is a language name and emit that as the gfm style info string. If none of the classes match a recognized language, before 3.10.1 we emitted the first class; fater 3.10.1, we emit nothing. This commit reverts to the pre-3.10.1 behavior.

- RST writer:

  - Don’t drop notes in notes.

- Haddock writer:

  - Don’t drop notes in notes.

- Docx writer:

  - Fix multi-paragraph list items (#9197). Previously the docx writer gave the second and subsequent paragraphs of a list item numbering from a separate list with an invisible bullet. This looked right, but semantically these paragraphs were items of another list, which is what Word, screen readers, and pandoc’s own docx reader saw; the list was also split in three. The writer now gives these paragraphs no numbering, just an indentation that lines them up with the text of the list item (as Word’s “List Continue” styles do).

- LaTeX writer:

  - Use braces around term containing `=` (#11954). This is needed for the new LaTeX list code, which is triggered by using `pdfstandard`.

- PowerPoint writer:

  - Add `clrMapOvr` to notes slides (#11935, Gaurav Vijay Jadhav). This makes them importable by Keynote.
  - Include `lang` in core document properties.

- DocBook, JATS, TEI writers:

  - Apply `writerIdentifierPrefix` prefix consistently.

- Typst writer:

  - Escape `...` and `-?` ligatures (#11979).
  - Use `getLang` to determine lang and region. Previously only the `lang` metadata field was consulted, so `lang` could not be set properly using a variable.

- Text.Pandoc.Translations:

  - `readTranslations` now takes the path of the file, for error messages \[API change\].

- Text.Pandoc.Writers.Shared:

  - Add `wrapColumns`, `renderWithTemplate` \[API change\]. These factor out code that was repeated in about 20 writers: computing the line length from writerWrapText/writerColumns, and rendering the body with or without the template.

- Text.Pandoc.Shared:

  - Export `plainToPara` and `paraToPlain`. \[API change\]

- Text.Pandoc.PDF:

  - Make `--presentational-hints` default for weasyprint. This is necessary to get list attributes (start, ordered list type, etc.) working properly (#11976).

- cabal.project:

  - Use bundle C option for zlib by default. This allows pandoc to be built without first installing the C library zlib. Those who want to use the system zlib can still compile pandoc that way by overriding this setting in cabal.project.local, or just installing directly from Hackage.
  - Default to `+http` on GHC \>= 9.14 (previously done only in CI), so local builds behave the same; `-f-http` still overrides it.
  - Pass wasm link flags for `pandoc-cli` as `ghc-options`. cabal only passes ld-options along when it finds an `ld` program on the PATH. In an environment without one (e.g. `nix shell` with just the ghc-wasm-meta toolchain), the flags were silently dropped and linking pandoc.wasm failed with undefined `setjmp` and clock symbols. Use `-optl- ghc-options` instead, which GHC passes to its linker regardless.

- Makefile:

  - Add `release` target.
  - Improve `make pandoc-templates` so it does the whole job.
  - Use bash as `SHELL` (`check-cabal` uses `pushd`, `check-version-sync` uses `==`).
  - Fix `$(id -u)` in `debpkg`, which make expanded to empty.
  - Fix missing `echo` in `validate-docx-golden-tests{,2}`.
  - Ensure pandoc is built before rules that run it to produce files.
  - Use `git ls-files` for `SOURCEFILES`, not the main branch’s tree.
  - Drop redundant `embed_data_files` flag in `quick-stack`.

- Use released citeproc 0.14.1.1, texmath 0.13.3.3, gridtables 0.1.1.1 (#9085).

- MANUAL.txt:

  - Clarify the effect of `raw_html` in commonmark formats (#8305).

- Bump bounds on crypton, crypton-x509-system, tasty-bench.

- Add `tools/circleci-build-release.sh`, `tools/github-build-release.sh`.

</details>

### About

jj is a Git-compatible version control system that is both simple and powerful. See
the [installation instructions](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/v0.46.0/install-and-setup/) to get started.

### Release highlights

* Jujutsu can now colocate workspaces besides the default one by creating Git
  worktrees. Use `jj workspace add --[no-]colocate` and the setting
  `git.colocate` to control this.

### Breaking changes

* The minimum supported `git` command version is now 2.42.0, up from 2.41.0.
  `jj workspace add` uses `git worktree add --orphan`, which was added in
  2.42.0.

* The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is now 1.97.1.

* `jj bisect run` now runs some consistency checks before proceeding to bisect.
  This helps ensure that the command can tell good and bad revisions apart,
  and that the working copy does go from bad to good over the provided revset.
  Use the new flag `--trust-endpoints` to disable these checks.

* `jj split` now opens a single editor session to edit descriptions for the
  split commits.

* `jj undo` and `jj redo` now refuse to undo/redo an operation that was
  performed in another workspace. Use `--allow-cross-workspace` to undo/redo
  it anyway.

* `jj workspace list`/`root` no longer omit unreachable paths. All recorded
  paths are now shown, with warnings displayed in `jj workspace root`.

* The `List.get()`, `.first()`, and `.last()` template functions now return
  `Option<T>` instead of throwing an error on out-of-bounds access.

### New features

* `jj workspace add` supports `--colocate`/`--no-colocate` flags to control
  whether a Git worktree is created alongside the workspace. The default
  colocates when the current workspace is colocated and the `git.colocate`
  config is `true`. `jj workspace forget` removes the corresponding Git
  worktree when one exists.

* `jj git colocation status`/`enable`/`disable` now work on child
  workspaces. `status` correctly reports colocation state and includes
  the workspace name. `enable` creates a Git worktree and `disable`
  removes it, allowing colocation to be toggled after workspace
  creation.

* `jj workspace remove` removes a workspace and its directory from disk. The
  working-copy state is snapshotted into a commit before removal.

* Added commands `jj file edit` and `jj file delete` for editing files in any
  revision without needing to change the working copy.

* `jj git push` now supports pushing to multiple remotes at the same time.
  This can be configured via `git.push` set to a string pattern
  or array of string patterns, or with the repeatable `--remote` flag,
  which also accepts string patterns.

* The default target revisions for `jj git push` can now be configured via
  `revsets.git-push`.

* Added the `TreeEntry.normal_value()` template method and the `TreeValue` type
  to access resolved tree values, formatted as their full object IDs, including
  Git submodule commit IDs.

* Diff hunk headers now include nearby source symbols for many common
  programming and markup languages.

* `fix.tools.<name>.line-range-args` (replaces `line-range-arg`) is an array of
  string template args to pass to the fix tool. This is more flexible in cases
  where you need to pass multiple arguments to the tool, such as separate args
  for the range start and range end.

* `jj run` now uses the sparse patterns from the workspace it's run from.
  Use the `--sparse-patterns` option to control this behavior (evaluated
  per each `jj run` invocation).

* `jj util diff <path1> <path2>` to compare files on disk.

* Aliases now support setting `aliases.<name>.enabled = false`, which will
  disable them. This can be used to disable built-in aliases or disable aliases
  in later layers (such as repo config files).

* `ui.editor` now supports `$path` and `$line` substitution variables. Example:
  `ui.editor = ["emacs", "+$line", "$path"]`

* `fill` template function now supports an additional named parameter
  `break_words`, that allows specifying if the template should break words
  longer than `width` passed in the input to ensure no words overflow the
  specified width.

* The `json()` template function now supports map literals: `json({'key' =>
  value})`

* The hunk headers of `diff.color-words.conflict = "pair"` now include the
  conflict labels of the compared terms.

### Fixed bugs

* On Windows, `jj` no longer hangs when a subprocess needs to prompt the user,
  such as `ssh` asking for a key passphrase or for confirmation of an unknown
  host key. Subprocesses started from a terminal now inherit its console, rather
  than being given an invisible one by `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` for the prompt to
  disappear into.
  [#6745](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/6745)
  [#8547](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/8547)

* On Windows, `jj git colocation enable` and `jj git colocation disable` no
  longer fail with "Access is denied (os error 5)" when the Git repository
  contains pack files.
  [#8661](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/8661)

* `jj undo` of `jj workspace forget` now correctly preserves the workspace's
  recorded path. Previously the path metadata was lost, leaving the workspace
  in a broken state after undo.
  [#9991](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/9991)

* `at_operation()` can now be used with operations that are not ancestors of
  the current operation (e.g. sibling operations created by concurrent
  commands). Previously, evaluating such expressions failed if they resolved
  to commits missing from the current operation's index.

* `.gitignore` files are now respected even if they aren't materialized in the
  working copy because they are excluded by the sparse patterns. Previously,
  ignored files could become tracked in a sparse working copy.
  [#2289](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/2289)

* In-tree ignore files (`.gitignore`) are no longer read through symlinks,
  matching `git` behavior. Such files are now silently skipped instead of having
  their symlink target applied. `$GIT_DIR/info/exclude` and `core.excludesFile`
  are unaffected and still follow symlinks, as `git` does.
  [#7161](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/7161)

* `jj workspace list` templates are now labeled with `workspace name`,
  `workspace root`, etc.

juanfont/headscale:
**Minimum supported Tailscale client version: v1.80.0**

### Security

This is a security release. It fixes findings from Anthropic's oss-scanner project and
the Tailworm report. None are critical, but some can cause denial of service in
Headscale. We recommend that all users upgrade to Headscale 0.29.7 **and** Tailscale
v1.104.4 or newer as soon as possible, especially those using Tailscale SSH.

Tailscale v1.104.4 fixes vulnerabilities in SSH forwarding, SSH session handling and
Serve. These fixes run in `tailscaled` on your nodes; upgrading Headscale alone does
not apply them.

See Tailscale's [security bulletins](https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins#ts-2026-014) and [Tailscale SSH: Findings and fixes](https://tailscale.com/blog/tailscale-ssh-findings-fixes).

To disable SSH agent and port forwarding on a node, set
`TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1` in the `tailscaled` service environment and restart
the service. This setting applies to all Tailscale SSH sessions on that node and
is also available in older clients. [#3624](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3624)

This release also fixes the issues that [oss-scanner](https://github.com/anthropics/oss-scanner/tree/main/projects/headscale)
reported in Headscale: ANT-2026-MLP8ZR5T, ANT-2026-LYVGXVSW, ANT-2026-AWGRB7O1, ANT-2026-QMCAFJ1Q, ANT-2026-RQS7JAPP, ANT-2026-5B6KE87K, ANT-2026-KFCFFM34, ANT-2026-K903ZEUA, ANT-2026-NM50ZP4N, ANT-2026-ZC18AF82, ANT-2026-NWTIBB02, ANT-2026-MX8FKG4K. [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)

### Changes

- Metrics are no longer exposed to unregistered clients through the Noise protocol. They remain available only on the configured metrics listener; an empty `metrics_listen_addr` disables that listener [#3623](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3623)
- Update the Tailscale dependency to v1.104.4, which bounds how much of an unexpected DERP HTTP response is read [#3577](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3577)
- Keep pending registrations and OIDC logins at capacity instead of evicting ones awaiting approval; new requests get a retry response, and registered nodes keep capacity for SSH checks [#3586](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3586)
- Cap stored pending registration data at 64 KiB, keeping tags and expiry; oversized interactive registrations are rejected [#3586](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3586)
- Check the OIDC login type before storing anything, accept each OIDC callback only once, and free an SSH check's slot once the client has read its result [#3586](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3586)
- Stop serving a route that is a single address inside the node IP ranges, such as `100.64.0.11/32` or `::ffff:100.64.0.11/128`, because it names a node, not a subnet; the route stays approved and listed, and wider routes are still served [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Require a valid pre-auth key to re-register an expired tagged node [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Another user's key or login on a tagged machine now creates a new device for that user instead of re-authenticating the tagged node [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Fix one node with a stored key expiry outside the years 0 to 9999 in UTC failing the map of every node that can see it; it is now left out of its peers' maps and the startup check names it with the fix command [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Refuse a key expiry outside the years 0 to 9999 in UTC on registration, on the OIDC token-expiry path and in `headscale nodes expire` / `POST /api/v1/node/{node_id}/expire` (HTTP 400); the latest accepted expiry no longer fails node listings on PostgreSQL in a zone east of UTC [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Keep the first 256 endpoints and 4096 announced routes from client reports; oversized hostnames, requested tags or other metadata return a registration error or HTTP 413 on map updates. Zoned IPv6 endpoints are refused [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- At startup, trim stored hostnames, endpoints and routes to the client-report limits and remove zoned endpoints. Hostinfo exceeding its size or tag limit is dropped until the next valid report [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Pending interactive registrations and follow-up waits keep only the hostname, OS and requested tags; other device details arrive with the first map request. Reauthentication preserves routes, services and endpoints [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Fix web reauthentication dropping the discovery key, so peers could not reach the device [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- A stalled request body, or a Noise tunnel with no open request, is closed after 30 seconds [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- A registration follow-up from a machine other than the one that started the registration is refused before it waits [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Only the newest follow-up waits on a pending registration or SSH check; older ones are answered at once [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Fix registration locks staying in memory after the registration ends [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Fix concurrent deletes of one node freeing its addresses and announcing its removal more than once [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- OIDC verifies an email against the document supplying it; an `email_verified` flag without an address no longer verifies another document's email [#3603](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3603)
- Fix release builds reporting their version with a `+dirty` suffix [#3584](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3584)
- Fix SSH policy `acceptEnv` having no effect, so allowed environment variables reach SSH sessions. Upgrade SSH destination nodes to Tailscale v1.104.4 or newer before using `acceptEnv`, because older clients can disclose forwarded values [#3569](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3569)

## Upgrade

Please follow the steps outlined in the [upgrade guide](https://headscale.net/stable/setup/upgrade/) to update your existing Headscale installation.

jumpserver/jumpserver:
## Improvements

- Update background task records to omit original args and kwargs at creation, reducing unnecessary parameter persistence
- Strengthen persistent write protection for databases and Redis in high availability deployments across container restarts, recreation, and failure recovery
- Improve redeployment completion checks to tolerate normal replication lag, and refine switchover waits and recovery coordination to reduce false failure detection

## Bug Fixes

- Validate Access Token format while preserving fallback compatibility with other Bearer Token authentication methods
- Fix NLA configuration and RDP service refresh during Tinker applet host deployment, checking Group Policy and disabling listener NLA before installation, then verifying the configuration afterward; stop deployment with clear guidance when Group Policy requires NLA
- Fix race conditions involving role callbacks, operation locks, and file synchronization acknowledgments during switchover, automatic rejoin, and startup recovery [JumpServer EE]
- Improve MySQL/MariaDB replication position handling and crash recovery, and fix a race condition in PostgreSQL replication slot cleanup during standby rebuilds [JumpServer EE]
- Fix local administrator credential recovery and health checks during MySQL/MariaDB maintenance, avoiding the use of peer credentials or stale application passwords [JumpServer EE]

Slash presets set the model and system prompt per command, so `/translate` can run a small model with a fixed prompt and copy the result for you. Vision models also take images pasted with Command-V. Turn it on in the macOS app under App > Ask AI. #4854 ## GPU Power Limit Working on battery? GPU Power Limit in Model Settings > Advanced caps the Mac's GPU power from 2 to 1000 W while that model generates, in both the web UI and the macOS app, and Ask AI has a limit of its own. The limit applies only while a capped request runs, comes off 15 s after the last one, and never applies to benchmarks. No root or helper app is needed. #4855 > M5 Max, decode speed and CPU+GPU energy per token against no limit. | Limit | 35B-A3B decode | Energy per token | 27B decode | Energy per token | |---|---|---|---|---| | 15 W | -6% | -25% | -7% | -29% | | 10 W | -14% | -37% | -18% | -43% | | 5 W | -36% | -49% | -48% | -52% | The GPU power target it sets comes from [m5gpu](https://github.com/beamivalice/m5gpu) by @beamivalice. ## Faster Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Ling 3.1 Flash and More Ling 3.1 Flash now loads straight from its original FP8 checkpoint, and Ling Flash 3.0 and 3.1 run their bundled nextn layer as Lightning MTP, which oQ keeps with Preserve MTP. On an M3 Ultra, Ling-3.1-flash oQ4 decodes 18.8 -> 34.3 tok/s (+82%) at 4K context and 18.1 -> 29.6 tok/s (+64%) at 32K, with real-use sampling and one request at a time. #4881 | Model | Change | Hardware | |---|---|---| | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next oQ4e | Decode 65.6 -> 81.5 tok/s (+24%), 4 requests 167.6 -> 186.5 tok/s (+11%) | M3 Ultra | | GLM-5.3-Flash, Macs before M5 | One-request decode, FP8 22.6 -> 25.2 tok/s (+12%), oQ4e 38.6 -> 41.7 tok/s (+8%) | M3 Ultra | | Flint oQ3e | Decode 91.0 -> 109.1 tok/s (+20%), with TurboQuant at 12K 23.5 -> 75.7 tok/s (3.2x) | M4 Max | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash oQ2e, Engram on SSD | Prefill at 128K 1512 -> 1719 tok/s (+14%) | M5 Ultra | Each figure is measured against the code right before the change. By @yohann-bearzi (#4880 from #4853, and #4843), @alan13367 (#4857, #4856) and @junmo-kim (#4745). On Macs before M5, GLM-5.3 now gives the same greedy output with Lightning MTP on and off (#4843). Also faster: DeepSeek V4.1 long prefill, +3.5% at 128K on an M3 Ultra (696d070cc with @N1k1tung), and M1 5-bit verify, +2.7% with DFlash2 on an M1 Ultra (@fneto1977 in #4830, measured by @jmmarkiewicz). ## New Features and Improvements - **Splash:** Splash 1.4.1's Ornith-1.5-122B and Flint with their DFlash2 drafts, MoE GGUFs pruned to fewer experts (@arnavprabhu in #4870), Flash-Next GGUF repos with PLE variant folders (@arnavprabhu in #4821, c5127a295), and Delete in the dashboard's SSD cache panel clears Splash's cache too (@arnavprabhu in #4824). The settings now say Splash's SSD cache limit applies per model (#4852). - **API:** `/v1/chat/completions` returns OpenAI `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` (up to 20) for streaming and non-streaming requests, including reasoning and tool-call tokens and with Lightning MTP on. Closes #1549, taking over from @popfido's #1591 and @ashokgelal's #4380 (#4859). - **M1 and M2 Macs:** Float16 Activations in Model Settings > Advanced converts a checkpoint's bfloat16 scales, norms and embeddings to float16, which these GPUs run natively. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B oQ4e decode goes 75.9 -> 82.4 tok/s (+9%) on an M1 Max (@parasew in #4819 from @pedroberaldo87's #3277, d1545cc4b, @yohann-bearzi in #4871). - **MoE expert offload:** Model Settings suggests a resident percent that still leaves room for a prompt, and clicking the hint fills it in (#4858, based on @beatakouchnir's #3676). - **Rerankers:** a per-model Context Window in the web and Mac Model Settings (@zviratko in #4826, 9401674d0). Jina rerankers follow the reference block window and v3.5's query and document limits, so a long query no longer fails (79bd8528c with @zviratko), and v3.5 runs its sliding layers in window-sized chunks (e4844fe56). - **macOS app:** updates download in the background and still ask before installing, and a failed install shows in the Status screen and the update sheet (685552051, c03d936c1 with @joshuabke, from #3144). - **Dependencies and builds:** transformers up to 5.20 (#4834), markitdown 0.1.9 (#4833), wheels built with Xcode 26.5 so they include the NAX kernels (@XXXXRT666 in #4836), and dead code cleanups (@shaanchander in #4847, #4848). ## Bug Fixes - Lightning MTP: GLM-5.3 on Macs before M5 and DeepSeek V4 verify drafts with their decode arithmetic (@yohann-bearzi in #4843, @Phenom300 in #4813), the DSpark ring GEMM uses the Steel kernel only where it matches bit for bit (@williamxie1989 in #4612), and mRoPE VLMs keep the running request's positions when a text prompt joins (@popfido in #4837). - A reply that ends inside an unclosed tool-call envelope returns an `incomplete_tool_call` error instead of the raw text with `finish_reason: stop` (@HeinrichvH in #4869, #3153). - `/v1/messages/count_tokens` counts the prompt `/v1/messages` actually renders, with tools, MCP and thinking settings (@richgoodson in #4875). - The memory guard re-reads `iogpu.wired_limit_mb`, so raising it while the server runs takes effect (@Woody-Hu in #4860, #4849). - Macs before M5 get the driver's relaxed compute context-store timeout at start, a setting other MLX apps use against Metal `0000000e` errors in long prefills and image prompts (#4872). - Model directories on a disconnected drive stay in settings, and the server starts when none of them is available (0fd347545 with @isnaenihidayat, #4873). An unavailable SSD cache dir falls back to the default one until restart instead of stopping the server (28f50bb2e with @pmjpmj). - Splash reports a missing draft or launcher version before memory admission, instead of a memory error sized from the GGUF files (#4876). - SigLIP and SigLIP2 embed text and images through their own towers (#4850), and Unlimited-OCR takes the model card's `` prompt (@tc3oliver in #4822). - `omlx restart` from a conda env under Homebrew's Caskroom no longer restarts the Homebrew service (009e75c00 with @ketpatil77, #3120). - Downloads: the speed readout no longer jumps above the real rate (@LXD-8 in #4844), and a refused retry keeps the row (@LXD-8 in #4845). - Web UI: long model names in the chat model picker truncate instead of running under the reasoning pill (@bercedev in #4812). ## Highlights from 0.7.3.dev2 - **MiniMax M3.1 Flash.** Served from NVFP4 or oQ with its DSpark draft as Lightning MTP, up to +87% for one request (#4777), plus fused decode kernels for another 14-23% (@yohann-bearzi in #4806). - **Faster M1 and M5 Macs, DFlash and GLM-5.3.** About 50% faster long-context prefill on M1 Ultra (@fneto1977 in #4496), DeepSeek V4 prefill attention on the M5 tensor units (@Phenom300 in #4808), fp16 DFlash +33% (@fneto1977 in #4773), and batched GLM-5.3 decode +17% (@jwiegley in #4801). - **Better low-bit oQ.** A new bit split lowers KL by up to 73% at the same size (#4776), and DeepSeek V4.1 Engram tables can stay FP8 (#4758). Benchmarks, the full feature and fix lists, and every contributor credit are in the [0.7.3.dev2 release notes](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/releases/tag/v0.7.3.dev2). ## Upgrade Notes - **Source installs:** run `make install` after updating. mlx-lm moves to 0d4d3d04, mlx-vlm to 0.7.10 and modelscope to 1.28 or newer, and transformers up to 5.20 is allowed (#4834). - **oQ:** new quants at the same level get a different bit split (#4776). Existing quants load and run as before. - **SSD cache:** blocks that earlier versions saved for gpt-oss, ERNIE 4.5 MoE, PhiMoE, PLaMo 3, FP8 Ministral 3 and Muse Spark (#4778) and for Ling Flash (#4881) are not reused, since their numerics changed. - **DeepSeek V4 on M5:** the tensor-unit prefill kernel is not bit-identical to the old one, so greedy output can differ at near-ties (#4808). - **Cache stats:** prefix hit rates can read lower than before, since an evicted or partial restore no longer counts as a full hit (#4782). - **Benchmarks:** CMMLU, JMMLU and KMMLU scores can be higher than in earlier runs (#4774). - **API:** an empty completion prompt now returns 400, and admin output token defaults must be 1 or more (19178d057). `logprobs` on an engine that cannot produce them (cluster, Splash, diffusion) returns 400 (#4859), an unclosed tool-call envelope returns `incomplete_tool_call` instead of `stop` (#4869), and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` can read higher where tools or thinking settings apply (#4875). - **macOS app:** updates now download in the background by default and still ask before installing. Turn off Download Automatically under Updates on the Status screen to only get notified. ## New Contributors @jwiegley in #4797, @kathsucurry in #4795, @wesbiggs in #4769, @Abelo9996 in #4753, @ChristianPraiss in #4737, @sampe-bot in #4804, @Phenom300 in #4808, @BrownMark in #4815, @parasew in #4819, @HeinrichvH in #4869. [Full changelog](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/compare/v0.7.2...v0.7.3rc1)

### Upgrade
Versions before Version 2.4.0 1. Start `WindTerm` and select the `profiles directory` and **quit**. 2. Replace the new `.wind/profiles` folder with the old `profiles` folder. 3. Restart `WindTerm` and all the sessions and configuration will be restored.
Versions after Version 2.4.0 1. Start `WindTerm` and select the `profiles directory` containing the old `.wind` folder. 2. It is recommended to choose the `Home Directory` to facilitate subsequent upgrades. If the `.wind` folder needs to be moved to another system: 1. Quit `WindTerm`. 4. Replace the new `.wind` folder with the old `.wind` folder. 5. Restart `WindTerm` and all the sessions and configuration will be restored. The **.wind** folder is cross-platform.
