knadh/listmonk:
[![listmonk-logo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/547147/134940003-1de03d83-8c7b-459b-8056-baa8d5f3b448.png)](https://listmonk.app)

v7 (beta) is a major release with a significant number of improvements and fixes. It's one of the biggest releases to date and has taken several months of work. Check out the [beta demo](https://beta.listmonk.app).

It fully [replaces](https://github.com/knadh/listmonk/issues/3073) the admin UI with a lightweight implementation. It is completely redesigned with major UI and UX improvements and is faster, significantly lighter, more accessible, with a much better mobile view. The admin UI bundle size is reduced by almost 80%.

**Important:** This is a beta release. If you encounter any issues or unintended behaviour, please report it by opening an [issue](https://github.com/knadh/listmonk/issues)

## How to upgrade
**As always, take a backup of your database before upgrading.**

**Binary**

Download the binary from this release. Stop and replace the old binary. Run `./listmonk --upgrade`. Start the app again.

**Docker**



```shell
# Edit your `docker-compose.yml` file and change the image name
# from `listmonk/listmonk:latest` to `listmonk/listmonk:beta`

docker compose down
docker compose pull && docker compose run --rm app ./listmonk --upgrade
docker compose up -d app db
```


## Breaking changes
- The `app.from_email` setting is now an array of addresses instead of a string, which changes the settings API `/api/settings`.
- Several i18n language keys have changed. If you have custom templates with `--static-dir`, the language strings will have to be changed. Refer to the upstream [directory](https://github.com/knadh/listmonk/tree/master/static) for changes.
- The old Vue frontend admin has been completely replaced. Certain Admin UI URLs have changed. There are changes to UX, for instance, new list and subscriber creation forms are standalone pages and not popup dialogs anymore.
- The TinyMCE richtext editor (~500KB) has been replaced with the light weight (~16KB) [Squire](https://github.com/fastmail/Squire). TinyMCE after v5, removed several important features from the open-source version, which essentially made upgrades and fixes impossible.
- For developers, the build steps have changed significantly after getting rid of most Javascript dependencies. The Docker developer environment has changed, and so have all the frontend e2e tests, which have now been ported to Playwright away from Cypress.


## What's new?

- Completely redesigned, fast, lightweight, responsive admin UI.
- Native dark mode and a dark theme for the code editor.
- Distinct generated avatars for subscribers, lists, campaigns etc. for easy visual comprehension.
- Filter campaigns by type, status, and tags; sort by creation, update, start, or scheduled-send date.
- Filter lists by visibility and opt-in type, subscribers by status or missing list memberships, and users by type, status, and role.
- Bookmarkable filter/sort links for all views.
- Subscriber, list, user and settings forms are now standalone pages with grouped cards instead of popup dialogs.
- Fully redesigned settings page with better grouping and instant search.
- A new list overview page with info, subscription stats, analytics etc.
- New list analytics: subscriptions, unsubscriptions, campaign views etc.
- Filter campaigns by type and status, and sort by created, updated, started and scheduled dates.
- New optional unique-count graphs on campaigns and lists analytics.
- Group by interval (day, week, month etc.), with a new date presets on the analytics page.
- Multiple `From` addresses configured in settings.
- New standalone subscriber info and activity page.
- Clear subscriber's view / click activity in bulk from the UI and API (`DELETE /api/subscribers/:id/activity/:type`).
- Fully redesigned bounces page.
- Configurable login session duration, including day units such as `7d`.
- OIDC: automatic role mapping based on claims, RP-initiated logout, PKCE support, and several auth fixes.
- Ability to exclude specific SMTP servers from the default `email` messenger pool.
- A one-click Gmail Relay SMTP preset, with support for a custom `HELO` hostname.
- Improved POP bounce processing that handles many new scenarios.
- Support for plain text notification emails via `*-text.txt` templates.
- Throttling for opt-in confirmation emails.
- One-click unsubscribe via the `List-Unsubscribe` header now also removes unconfirmed subscriptions.
- New i18n translations and improvements.

### Fixes
- Multiple security fixes: permission checks, tightening of `sql` permission etc.
- Fix realtime campaign stats and 'unsent' count tracking.
- String literals now work in subscriber search.
- Bulk deletion now respects tag, status etc. filters.
- Relative CID images load properly in public archive pages.
- Fix multiple `@TrackLink` Unicode edge cases.

And numerous other improvements and fixes ...

## New Features

- The table of content now displays the number of pages by default; there is no need to enable the “Total Pages” feature separately.
- Software security has been optimized to address an arbitrary code execution vulnerability caused by metadata.
- An additional confirmation step has been added when importing books via external links using the URL scheme to enhance security.
- The “Ask AI” feature now supports the Ctrl + Enter shortcut for submitting questions.
- Added an eraser tool to Doodle Mode
- Added support for 7 languages on the official website
- (Mobile) Added a feature to resync all book covers; go to Settings > Sync options
- (Mobile) Optimized the smoothness of page-turning animations
- (Mobile) Optimized the smoothness of certain app animations
- (Mobile) Added an option to download images in CBZ comic mode

- Fixed an issue where footnotes in some books did not appear in a pop-up window
- Fixed an issue where reading progress could not be tracked for some books containing special styles
- Fixed an issue where table of contents highlighting did not work after enabling “Total Pages”
- Fixed an issue where page numbers were not displayed in the table of contents for some TXT books
- (Mobile) Fixed an issue where authorization via the browser failed on older iOS versions, resulting in a blank page
- (Mobile Version) Fixed abnormal slider behavior on iOS

- (Mobile) Fixed an issue where reading progress could not be tracked for some books containing special styles
- (Mobile) Fixed an issue where page numbers were not displayed on the table of contents for some TXT books

### Highlights

* Add support for Kubernetes v1.36 and v1.37 (default: v1.37.0)

* Add Traefik Helm-based ingress addon

### Features

* Add support for Kubernetes v1.36 and v1.37 (default: v1.37.0) ([#23567](https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/pull/23567), [#23596](https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/pull/23596))

* Add `--mdns` flag to enable mDNS on every VM start ([#22964](https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/pull/22964), [#23208](https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/pull/23208))

* drivers: Start VM drivers in parallel ([#23112](https://github.com/kubernetes/minikube/pull/23112))

langgenius/dify:
Dify 1.18.0 brings **Agents that route workflows**, **portable app packages**, **deeper visibility into nested workflow runs**, and the opt-in **Agent Knowledge Base** experience. OpenAPI and the new difyctl expand how you build and manage apps from the command line. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Read the upgrade guide below before deploying.** Upgrade the API, workers, Agent Backend, and Agent runtime images together. Local Agent sandboxes require a non-empty authentication token, and Agent Backend uses a new run protocol. Source installations require Python 3.13. Install the new difyctl client and sign in again. Preserve your existing `PASSWORD_PEPPER` configuration. ### Release highlights #### Agents that choose the next step Let an Agent decide which workflow branch to take. Enable **Output Routes**, give each route a selection condition, and connect it to the next step—such as resolving a request directly or handing it to a specialist. The read-only `switch` output exposes the chosen route. (#42599) ![Agent Output Routes with Resolve directly and Escalate to team branches](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30480ac3-d53e-4522-b1c5-95eb1d9ac9f2) *Output Routes configuration with two branches in the workflow editor.* Plain Agent v2 nodes also stream text as it is generated. Structured results, routed results, and nodes using default-value error handling remain buffered. (#43986) #### Portable apps in one package Move an app with its supported resources in a single **`.ifpkg` package**. Workflow and Chatflow packages carry inline Agents, Skills, and their files; imports recreate those resources in the destination workspace and remap references. File and URL imports support both packages and YAML, and explicit YAML export remains available. (#42066, #42579, #42626, #42863) ![Studio Import App dialog with a portable-workflow.ifpkg package selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11ae78d4-c902-45ff-b875-7c91dd6a530f) *Studio's `.ifpkg` import preview.* #### See inside nested workflow runs Open a **Workflow Tool invocation** from the run history and inspect the child workflow's individual steps. Nested tools now run as child graphs with coordinated pause, resume, stop, and file outputs. Access checks protect the source app's details. (#40277, #42819, #42820, #42821, #42822) ![Nested Workflow Tool trace showing successful Start, Template, and End steps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90a2236f-2118-4bc4-82fe-20508167b636) *Trace drilldown into a successful Workflow Tool invocation.* Nested usage and step totals can still be approximate, particularly after a pause or stop. Console drilldown and external trace export have different scopes; see the full feature details below. #### Agent Knowledge Base · Beta Create a knowledge space for your agents, add files or connect sources, and inspect document processing, metadata, retrieval traces, and quality evaluations in one place. The new Knowledge Retrieval node and Agent integrations share access-controlled KnowledgeFS spaces. Classic Knowledge remains available. This is an opt-in integration with a separate service and database; see the deployment requirements below. (#44165) *Will soon be available on cloud.dify.ai* ### Developer spotlight **Build and manage apps with OpenAPI and difyctl.** The CLI discovers commands from the server's operation catalog, with searchable help and support for Workflow and Chatflow creation, DSL import/export, settings, environment variables, publishing, and version restoration. Draft hashes protect concurrent edits. (#42487, #42608, #43067) Install the bundled skill for agents building Dify apps: ```bash difyctl install skills ``` The new client requires a fresh sign-in; see the deployment instructions below. (#43819) --- ### Upgrade guide **Compatibility and Rollout** 1. **Back up first.** Retain the database, vector-store data, uploaded files, Agent snapshot/workspace storage, and all deployment secrets and env files. Use a maintenance window for a single-stack upgrade. 2. **Upgrade the Agent components together.** `/runs` now accepts composition v2 and rejects v1 requests. Existing session snapshots are converted on read and saved as v2; old runtimes cannot read newly saved v2 snapshots. Direct Agent Backend integrations must update their request format. The old Agent-specific AskHuman tool and deferred resume path are removed: historical Agent forms no longer resume execution, while shared Workflow Human Input nodes remain supported. (#43833) 3. **Retire old workflow consumers before admitting new-version traffic.** Let in-flight runs finish, then replace legacy workers/resume consumers so they cannot process the shared queue without the new cancellation guards. Legacy paused task IDs can be recovered from valid saved invocation snapshots within the existing access scope; missing or invalid snapshots require separate recovery. Nested usage totals retain the limitation noted above. (#40277) 4. **Configure the Local sandbox token before restart.** Supply a high-entropy secret through the shared Compose interpolation source. The `1.17.1` runtime image does not support the new `--require-auth-token` flag; deploy the matching `1.18.0` Agent Backend and Local sandbox images. (#44152) 5. **Preserve password hashing configuration.** Existing installations without a pepper should leave `PASSWORD_PEPPER` empty. Setting a new pepper during the upgrade is not a transparent migration and requires an explicit password-reset plan. Keep any configured pepper unchanged across all instances and restore it with the database. 6. **Review the proxy boundary.** Bundled Nginx replaces `X-Forwarded-For` with its resolved client address, and Compose enables forwarded-header handling. Keep direct API access restricted to trusted callers. If a load balancer or Cloudflare sits before Nginx, configure trusted real-IP handling there; otherwise visitors may share the proxy’s rate-limit bucket. See [client IP and trusted proxies](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.18.0/docker/README.md#client-ip-and-trusted-proxies). 7. **Enable KnowledgeFS deliberately.** Default Compose installations keep it off; local Community Edition development requires the explicit Community development opt-in. Configure its separate database and migrations, Capability v2 public verifier, Dify signing keys, model profile (embedding, reasoning, and rerank), and Workspace cutover gates before enabling traffic. The optional service must pass `/ready`, not only `/health`. Standard Dify API images do not contain the separate KnowledgeFS engine used by the optional engine-worker profile; the published default KnowledgeFS API image is currently amd64 only. Follow the [KnowledgeFS deployment and recovery guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/laipz8200/release-1.18.0/docker/README.md#knowledgefs-integration-service).
Deployment instructions · Docker Compose, source, and difyctl **Docker Compose** Once the 1.18.0 release images and tag are published, stop the old stack gracefully, switch to the release, merge the configuration changes above, and pull/start the new stack: ```bash cd dify/docker docker compose stop -t -1 git fetch --tags git checkout 1.18.0 # Merge required configuration changes into existing env files here. docker compose pull docker compose up -d ``` Keep database migrations enabled (`MIGRATION_ENABLED=true`) for the API startup, or run them through your managed migration process before starting new workers. The bundled Weaviate update from 1.17.1 is a patch update within 1.39. If coming from a version that still runs Weaviate 1.27, complete the [1.17.1 staged Weaviate upgrade](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/releases/tag/1.17.1) first. **Source Deployments** Use Python **3.13** for the API, Node.js **24.22.1** or later in the 24.x line, and pnpm **12.10.1**. Refresh the locked dependencies and apply the database migrations from the repository root: ```bash uv sync --project api --frozen uv run --directory api flask db upgrade pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` Rebuild the web application and restart API, worker, scheduler, and Agent services from the same release. If deploying Agent Backend separately from source, refresh its locked `server` dependencies as well. **difyctl** Install the matching 1.18.0 client. Its v2 implementation does not reuse v1 login state: ```bash difyctl login --server https://your-dify.example.com difyctl help ``` Update scripts to the current server-discovered command surface. The old mode-agnostic `/openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}:run` route is replaced by per-mode operations; use the catalog instead of hard-coded v1 routes. Refresh installed agent skills with `difyctl install skills `. (#42487, #42608, #43819)
Existing data that may need recovery - **Published triggers:** the draft-sync fix does not repair subscriptions already removed before upgrading. Rebind missing subscriptions and republish affected workflows as needed. (#44068) - **Document extraction:** re-import/re-index affected content to apply extraction fixes to existing documents. - **Built-in document metadata:** toggling built-in fields rewrites only enabled, non-archived documents whose indexing is complete. Other legacy rows can retain the old format and need a later rewrite when eligible; this release does not include a full backfill. (#44218)
### Detailed changes
New features · complete capabilities and availability **Agent Knowledge Base and KnowledgeFS** - Add the Beta knowledge-space experience with local upload preview, connected-source management, document availability and metadata, retrieval history/research, and quality evaluation. Settings control app, Agent, and Service API access. Classic Knowledge remains supported alongside it. (#44165) - Knowledge Retrieval v2 and Agent knowledge bindings use scoped capabilities; published Explore runs reuse published bindings without requiring ordinary viewers to reconfigure access. (#44165) - Classic Dataset upgrades have durable checkpoints, availability/metadata reconciliation, retry protection, and recovery through Beat. Run the dedicated upgrade worker with the documented prefork pool and task limits; apply `b9d3f7a5c102` before restarting API/workers/Beat. Opting into the service does not automatically migrate all Classic datasets. (#44165) **Portable App Packages** - App exports now default to `.ifpkg`, bringing the application configuration and its supported resources into one portable package. Explicit YAML export remains available, and imports accept both formats from files or URLs. (#42066, #42189, #42425, #42552) - Workflow and Chatflow packages include inline Agents, their Skills, and files from each node’s bound configuration snapshot. Imports recreate those Agents in the destination workspace and remap their resources. App icons, Site settings, and node plugin dependencies are included in the export flow. Missing resources are reported during import. (#42579, #42626, #42816, #42863, #42913) - Agent exports can target a published version. Agent version menus now offer Restore, and pending draft saves finish before restoration so autosave cannot overwrite the restored configuration. Skill duplication and export use the latest saved draft content. (#42485, #42567, #42424, #42502) **Nested Workflow Tools and Trace Drilldown** - Called Workflow Tools run as child graphs under the workflow engine, with coordinated pause, resume, stop, and file outputs. Source graphs are captured before execution, so republishing a tool does not change an in-flight run, including calls inside loops and iterations. (#40277, #42820) - Workflow, Chatflow, and history views can open a particular tool invocation and navigate its internal execution traces. Access to each source application is required before its details are returned. Human Input forms are tracked by execution identity, including repeated invocations of the same node. (#42819, #42821, #42822) - Nested Agent logs and usage records retain their source workflow identity and their relationship to the outer run. **Nested usage and step totals can still be approximate, particularly after pauses or stops.** (#42824, #42820) **Agent Output Routes and Streaming** - Agent v2 nodes can select a workflow branch as part of completing their task. Enable Output Routes, define at least two branches and their selection conditions, and use the read-only `switch` output to inspect the chosen route. With routing disabled, the normal success outlet remains available. Routed nodes support stopping on error or taking a failure branch; node-level default-value handling is unavailable with routes enabled. (#42599) - Plain Agent v2 nodes stream text as it is generated. Structured or routed results remain buffered, and nodes using default-value error handling stay buffered so the configured fallback can still replace a failed result. (#43986) **Build and Manage Apps with OpenAPI and difyctl** - `/openapi/v1` publishes a server operation catalog. difyctl discovers commands and their input fields from that catalog, provides searchable help, and follows server-provided next steps. Workflow and Chatflow authoring now covers app creation, DSL import/export, settings, environment variables, publishing, and version restoration. Draft hashes protect imports from overwriting concurrent edits. (#42487, #42608, #43067) - The CLI includes a `difyctl` skill for agents building Dify apps. Install it with `difyctl install skills `. Device login supports `--no-wait` and `--resume`, and folder uploads send one multipart part per file. (#43819, #44356) - Workspace owners can create resource access tokens bound to selected apps or knowledge bases. Tokens work with the supported Service API routes and app operations in difyctl; they do not grant workspace administration. The Settings entry is opt-in through `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, which defaults to `false`. (#42293, #44422) **Edit Agent Prompts from the Sandbox** - `dify-agent config prompt pull [--to PATH]` and `push [PATH|-]` read or replace the raw system prompt, preserving UTF-8, whitespace, and mention markers. Empty text clears it. Only the current account’s writable build draft can be changed; later requests use the saved prompt. (#44561) **Agent Execution Tracing** - Agent apps and Workflow Agent v2 nodes can export their Agent, model, and tool execution trees through the existing tracing providers. Monitoring adds shared tracing configuration, delivery status, retry controls, and links to the trace belonging to the selected execution. Agents referenced by a Workflow inherit the caller’s tracing policy. (#44144, #44186) - Application tracing is opt-in on both the API and Agent Backend. A separate deployment-wide OTLP trajectory exporter is also available, independently of system tracing. (#42651, #44144) - Called Workflow Tools’ internal nodes are excluded from external exports because those exports have no viewer identity for source-app access checks. Agents inside those called tools are also excluded from the new execution-tree export for now; authorized Console drilldown remains available. (#42823, #44144) **OpenShell Sandbox Backend and E2B Usage Collection** - Agent execution can use a self-hosted NVIDIA OpenShell gateway with `DIFY_AGENT_RUNTIME_BACKEND=openshell`. Each Binding has its own sandbox, with authenticated shell access, Home Snapshots on an operator-managed shared volume, and an optional egress allowlist. OpenShell gateway 0.0.106 or newer and a compatible runtime image are required. (#41076) - OpenShell lease release closes the connection but leaves the sandbox running. Enforcement depends on the Cloud policy service and Gateway; this is not a standalone Community Edition firewall. (#41025, #44464) - Cloud users can preview and try published Agent templates before importing them. Agent “Create from Template” is hidden in Community and Enterprise editions because its template data source is Cloud-only. (#42837, #44035) - In Cloud Workflow Log Archives, workspace owners can permanently delete a selected month, with confirmation, progress, and retry. lbjlaq/Antigravity-Manager:
-   **[Adaptive QoS Scheduling System via Pure Peer Calibration & Ladder Probing] (Fixes #3720, PR #3725, Thanks to @jeikl, @cubelikeplayDaniel, @lbjlaq)**:
    -   **Real-time Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) Metric**: Captured pure elapsed time from request dispatch to the first effective chunk, completely eliminating noise from output length or streaming transfer to serve as the physical benchmark for silent QoS throttling. (Fixes #3720, PR #3725, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **5-Tier Pure Peer Baseline & Anti-False-Positive Shield**: Peer baselines strictly exclude: self, heterogeneous tiers, disabled accounts, 429 rate-limited/zero-quota accounts, Jailed, Probing, Suspicious, and Half-Open accounts to prevent baseline poisoning; thinking models receive a dynamic 35s latency compensation to prevent false positives during deep reasoning; global outage brake halts strikes when the peer average exceeds 20s, coupled with an 8s~20s hysteresis deadband to prevent oscillation. (Fixes #3720, PR #3725, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Transient Tagging & Immediate Session Handover**: Tags account as `Suspicious` on the first strike (instantly excluded from peer calculations, with the scheduler activating drain mode); 2 strikes within a 5-minute window isolates the account in jail and triggers immediate sticky session unbinding, allowing P2C to rebind healthy accounts with 100% Prompt Cache efficiency. (Fixes #3720, PR #3725, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Background Ladder Probing & Half-Open Anti-Flapping**: Cooldown ladders scale at 2m -> 5m -> 10m -> 15m -> 20m -> 30m, resetting the timer at each step; dispatches lightweight synthetic "Hello" probes (< 5 tokens, 8s hard abort timeout); passing probes triggers `Half-Open` probation requiring 2 consecutive real requests under 8s before full release; 30-minute penalty memory retention prevents rapid looping. (Fixes #3720, PR #3725, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **One-Click QoS Jail Release & Remaining Cooldown Display**: Displayed real-time QoS cooldowns on cards, tables, and monitor logs, providing an instant manual release button and backend API (`release_account_qos_jail`) across all 12 supported locale catalogs. (Fixes #3720, PR #3725, Thanks to @jeikl)
-   **[Official Model Suite Upgrade, Tiered Thinking Protocol & Argon Standalone Quota Isolation] (Fixes #3735, Ref #3720, Fixes #3737, Thanks to @jeikl, @cubelikeplayDaniel, @xiaozhi-xmu, @chenshin166-arch)**:
    -   **Decoupled Model Ingestion from quotaInfo**: Completely eliminated the legacy `if let Some(quota_info) = info.quota_info` filter gate in `quota.rs`, benchmarking exclusively against official model catalogs to preserve Gemini models (`gemini-3.8-flash-*`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, etc.) when upstream omits model-level `quotaInfo`, permanently resolving local 503 scheduling rejections. (Fixes #3737, Thanks to @xiaozhi-xmu, @chenshin166-arch, @jeikl)
    -   **Tiered Thinking Protocol (Thinking Budget vs Thinking Level)**: Governed new-generation tiered models (Gemini 4 Argon, Claude 5.5) exclusively with `thinkingLevel` (`"LOW"`, `"MEDIUM"`, `"HIGH"`) and traditional models with `thinkingBudget`, eliminating HTTP 400 dual-field conflicts. (Fixes #3735, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Disabled Model Variant Ingestion Filtering & False Quota Elimination**: Ingested the `disabled: Option<bool>` field and `is_disabled()` helper in `OfficialModelInfo`, intercepting `-disabled` / `_disabled` suffixes at the top of the baseline check and stripping them from `normalize_to_standard_id` and the account pool; purged false badges and progress bars from frontend cards. (Fixes #3735, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Gemini 4 Argon Dispatch Closure & Standalone Quota Inheritance**: Extended candidate filtering with `token_supports_advanced_model` and standalone bucket checks (`normalized_target != "claude" && token.model_quotas.contains_key(...)`) supporting camelCase and snake_case properties, eliminating phase-two 503 rejections while preserving Claude 5.5 / 4.6 pool separation. (Fixes #3735, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Deprecate Obsolete gemini-pro-agent Codename**: Standardized `gemini-3.1-pro` mappings in `variant_mapping.rs` from deprecated internal codename `gemini-pro-agent` to official physical model `gemini-3.1-pro-high`. (Fixes #3737, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Claude Parity for Dynamic Model Candidate Rewriting**: Integrated `token_manager.resolve_dynamic_model_for_account` into the Claude handler post-scheduling to match OpenAI and Gemini parity for adaptive per-account model rewriting. (Fixes #3737, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Standardized Context Window & Output Limits**: Standardized context and output limits across OpenAI (`/v1/models`), Claude (`/v1/models`), and Gemini (`/v1beta/models`) metadata endpoints. (Fixes #3735, Thanks to @jeikl)
-   **[OpenAI Responses API Structured Outputs, Pipeline Tool Conflict Mitigation & Zero-Loss Unwrapping] (Fixes #3710, Ref #3723, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel, @jeikl)**:
    -   **Inbound Protocol Normalization**: Supported `text.format` specifications in `OpenAIRequest` for the Responses API, extracted `effective_response_format` in request mapping, and normalized it into Gemini native `generationConfig.responseSchema` and `responseMimeType: "application/json"`, unblocking Codex Desktop's automatic thread naming (`thread_title`) and summary generation. (Fixes #3710, Ref #3723, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)
    -   **Background Thinking Budget Convergence & Timeout Prevention**: Explicitly honored `reasoning.effort: "low"` to constrain the thinking budget to 1024 tokens for background short tasks, eliminating 30-second hard timeout aborts by the Codex client during thread title generation on high-effort models. (Fixes #3710, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)
    -   **Unified Tool Conflict Mitigation in Pipeline (Pipeline First)**: Moved the mutual exclusivity handling of `responseSchema` and `tools` / `toolConfig` down to `align_google_request_prefix_topology_with_model` in `src/proxy/pipeline/inbound.rs`, suppressing `canonical_tools` and `canonical_tool_config` across all protocols when `responseSchema` is active to eliminate upstream HTTP 400 rejections. (Fixes #3710, Ref #3723, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)
    -   **Guarded Outer Unwrap & Zero-Loss Conversational Protection**: Guarded `convert_chat_response_to_responses` with `is_structured_output` to preserve 100% of conversational commentary in normal turns (preventing conversational data loss), while applying `unwrap_outer_code_fence_if_structured` strictly when the entire response is enclosed in markdown fences to unblock Codex Desktop's native `JSON.parse` without corrupting embedded code blocks. (Fixes #3710, Ref #3723, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)
-   **[Mini Floating Window Native macOS Transparency, Bidirectional Millisecond Sync & Deadlock-Free Scheduling] (Fixes #3733, Ref #3718, #3721, Ref #3738, Ref #3741, Thanks to @lbjlaq, @cubelikeplayDaniel, @jeikl)**:
    -   **Native macOS Transparency & Window Drag Permissions**: Added Tauri `macos-private-api` and native `macOSPrivateApi: true` configuration, eliminating WebKit black background edges and bringing native frosted glass transparency; injected transparency scripts on the first frame and declared drag/always-on-top capabilities. (Fixes #3733, Ref #3718, PR #3738, Thanks to @lbjlaq)
    -   **Dark/Light Adaptation & Cross-Window Millisecond i18n Sync**: Mini view dynamically inherits theme changes; bound `app://theme-changed` and `app://language-changed` cross-window events for bidirectional seamless synchronization across all 12 localization files.     -   **Native Main Thread Scheduling & Win32 Deadlock Elimination**: Introduced `switch_to_main_window` and `hide_mini_view` commands in the Rust backend, dispatching main window reconstruction and reactivation (`exit_lightweight_mode`) fully onto the OS native UI main thread (`app.run_on_main_thread`), completely eliminating Win32 message loop deadlocks and spinlock hangs when creating windows cross-thread on Windows. (Ref #3733, Ref #3738, Ref #3741, Thanks to @jeikl)
    -   **Mini Window React Router 404 Fallback & Synchronous Resolution**: Enhanced synchronous resolution in `App.tsx` using `window.location.search` (`?mini=1`) and `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` to eliminate routing re-entry caused by asynchronous IPC window label delays; supplemented `createBrowserRouter` with `errorElement` and `index.html` wildcard fallbacks. (PR #3741, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)

    -   **流式巨型工具调用缓冲跃迁宽限期**: 放宽过渡断崖自动跃迁条件为 `matches!(phase, StreamPhase::Thinking | StreamPhase::Streaming)`，允许在 Streaming 阶段生成 10,000+ tokens 巨型 `functionCall` 缓冲静默时自动跃迁至 Transition 宽限期并赋予 180s 保护，彻底消除满 120s 滑动超时被提前截断的缺陷。(Fixes #3739, PR #3740, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)
    -   **响应头看门狗与总预算精准收敛**: 将流式首选端点 HTTP 响应头看门狗基准收敛至 30s（超大 payload 弹性放宽至 45s），备用回退预算 25s，全链路总预算大幅收敛至 55~70s（非流式严格 30s），彻底杜绝主端点在排队拥塞时长时间挂死。(Fixes #3713, PR #3714, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)

    -   **重构多账号跨天硬配额耗尽检测与全端点故障解绑**: 将 `quotaResetDelay > 30min`（如 68 小时）且包含 `quota_exhausted` 的响应准确识别为账号级硬配额枯竭，立即执行 50ms 闪电切号；在发生全端点超时时施加 30s 冷却并原子解绑粘性会话。(PR #3714, Thanks to @cubelikeplayDaniel)

lightpanda-io/browser:
## Behavior changes
- JS page errors now log under a new `page_error` scope at WARN (silence with `--log-filter`).
- Each top-level page now has its own session history; a second page no longer shows up in the first page's back/forward.
- `--block-private-networks` now blocks more non-routable ranges (CGNAT, benchmarking, multicast, reserved, NAT64).
- `no-cors` fetches with a non-safelisted method are now rejected.
- An unreadable `--http-cache-dir` database is now discarded instead of exiting.
- Console values written to the log are now escaped and capped.

## New Web APIs
- Web Crypto: Ed25519, X25519, ECDSA, RSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` + AES-KW; EC and RSA-OAEP import/export
- WebCodecs, `OfflineAudioContext`, WebVTT improvements
- XML document parsing
- `setRangeText()` on `<input>` and `<textarea>`; `textarea.textLength`
- `HTMLProgressElement` `value`/`max`/`position`; `HTMLOptionElement.index`; missing table APIs
- `document.hasFocus()`; `window.outerWidth/outerHeight/screenX/screenY/screenLeft/screenTop`
- `:nth-child(An+B of S)` and `:nth-last-child(An+B of S)`
- `PermissionStatus` is now an `EventTarget`; `DOMException` is now structured-cloneable; `ImageData` overload
- Missing global event handlers added to `window`, `document` and `body`

## Web API behavior / fixes
- Element widths are now resolved relative to their parent (block, inline, floats, %, min/max-width, basic flex)
- Client rects (`getBoundingClientRect`, `getClientRects`) are now viewport-relative
- Mouse events now reach into shadow DOM and iframes
- Escape now closes the topmost modal dialog
- Iframes inside a shadow root now load when their host connects
- `replaceWith` compliance and cross-document adoption; `isEqualNode(null)` now returns false
- `insertAdjacentHTML` now works on SVG elements
- Trusted key events now report Chrome's legacy `keyCode`/`which`/`charCode`
- Text selection offsets now count UTF-16 code units
- `TextDecoder` now only strips a BOM for UTF-8/UTF-16
- `form.elements` now lists fieldset, object and output
- Sequence arguments now accept any iterable
- Better `getComputedStyle().transform`
- Fixed CSS nested rule parsing; escapes are now decoded in unquoted attribute selectors
- Cookies are now sent longest path first, then oldest first
- 401/407 responses are now delivered as-is when no auth challenge header is present

## CDP
- `Fetch.continueRequest` `interceptResponse` is now supported
- `Fetch.continueWithAuth` with `Default`/`CancelAuth` now delivers the original 401/407, as Chrome does
- `Runtime.exceptionThrown` is now emitted for unhandled promise rejections, with the context the exception was thrown in
- `Log.entryAdded` is now emitted for resources that fail to load
- `DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` is now supported (previously a no-op)
- `LP.getPageStatus` added: page issue summary (JS errors, skipped resources, fetch stats). Also included in `fetch` output when `--json` is used
- Custom ARIA states and focusability are now exposed in the AX tree
- Non-UTF-8 status text and headers are now reported as strings rather than a byte array
- Permission overrides are now cleared when a browser context closes

## Serve / CLI
- `serve --unix-socket <path>` added: CDP over a Unix domain socket
- `--remote-allow-origins` added: allow CDP connections that send an `Origin` header (rejected by default), matching Chrome
- `serve` now honors `--cookie-jar`: the jar is saved when a connection closes. With multiple connections, last write wins
- `fetch --dump structured_data` added
- `fetch --markdown-alternate` added: follow a page's `text/markdown` alternate. `text/markdown` documents are now dumped as-is

## Tools
- `markdown` tool: `alternate` option added
- A failed `goto` now closes the page
- Tree tool: links kept inside headings, multi-line names kept on one line

## Performance / stability
- Reworked TaggedOpaque (less memory)
- The scheduler now runs from a snapshot and no longer runs after every script evaluation
- Faster forgiving base64 decode
- UAF fixes: blob navigation, attribute change, file→blob layout; recursive close during load
- Script rejects no longer run microtasks mid-evaluation

## English

### Summary

This stable release brings interactive HTML inside Markdown results to Web, Desktop and the browser extension, with a redesigned output pipeline for concurrent generation and large responses. It also improves backup integrity, adds import codes for selected cloud backups, preserves model selections and saved parameters, and refines image-editing and structured-input templates.

### Highlights

- **Interactive output in place:** use Preview or Source to inspect results. Explicit HTML code blocks and supported HTML content render as isolated web pages alongside the surrounding Markdown. Multiple blocks can remain interactive at the same time.
- **Interactive extension previews:** fix the beta's extension script restriction so generated buttons, forms and canvases work inside results without opening another tab.
- **Bounded streaming and rendering:** generation uses a dedicated output document, virtualized source views and background Markdown parsing. Oversized or expensive content falls back to source.
- **More reliable backups:** validate data and image resources before restoration, protect existing images from eviction, and restore workspace snapshots only after preceding import steps succeed.
- **Cloud backup import codes:** transfer a selected WebDAV, S3-compatible or Cloudflare R2 snapshot using a code, link or QR code when its size permits.

### Product Updates

#### Desktop

- Propagate cancellation from the interface through desktop IPC to model requests. Streaming completion now waits for asynchronous completion work.
- Use the shared Preview/Source output interface, inline HTML previews and backup import-code flow.

#### Web

- Render multiple HTML examples directly in Markdown results. Switching one result to Source leaves other results' previews intact.
- Keep in-progress responses in the source view; executable previews are created after generation completes.
- Allow HTML previews to request external data while retaining isolation from the application. Requests remain subject to browser CORS rules and the target service's authorization requirements.

#### Extension

- Display and run multiple HTML blocks inside results, including inline scripts, event handlers, external script libraries and modules.
- Allow external API requests while preventing preview pages from reading the main application, its storage or extension APIs. Keep the main extension pages' existing content security policy.
- Support Preview/Source switching, content replacement and fullscreen viewing. Release preview pages when their corresponding results are removed.

#### Core/Infra

- Separate streaming text from reactive workspace snapshots and publish final or interrupted results at explicit completion boundaries.
- Apply output-size, rendering and queue budgets, and cancel obsolete parsing work.
- Carry cancellation signals through OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic and Gemini streaming adapters.

### Fixes

- Resolve extension content security policy restrictions that blocked preview scripts, and reject forged content updates from preview child pages.
- Preview standalone HTML controls such as buttons, and keep output-toolbar actions within narrow mobile comparison columns.
- Reject invalid backup sections, conflicting image resources and insufficient image-storage capacity before publishing new references. Report partial restoration and rollback failures explicitly.
- Preserve relevant settings and image references across export and import. Keep workspace restoration as the final import step.
- Preserve model selections when refreshing lists, including empty responses and fallback lists. Retain saved parameters when provider definitions change while validating edited values against applicable definitions.
- Clarify reference-image roles, edit scope and preservation requirements in image templates. Keep structured JSON fields, types, control values and placeholders intact.
- Update Zod, body-parser, qs and the build tooling's Undici 6 dependency to patched versions for previously identified security advisories.

### Breaking Changes / Upgrade Notes

- This upgrade changes backup restoration and output processing. Export a backup of important workspaces before upgrading.
- Cloud backup import codes contain storage credentials; they are not restricted public sharing links. Give them only to trusted recipients. Google Drive backup import codes are not supported in this release.
- HTML scripts run in isolated iframes. Isolation protects the main document and restricts permissions, but does not impose hard CPU or memory quotas on arbitrary generated scripts. WebGPU availability still depends on the browser and device.
- Exceeding output or rendering budgets may stop generation or switch to source display. Interrupted and normally completed results remain distinct.
- The extension ZIP uses numeric version `2.13.0` without the beta display name. Replace manually installed `2.13.0-beta.1` packages manually. The release workflow does not automatically submit to browser extension stores.
- Stable Docker images use `2.13.0` and `latest` tags. The GitHub Release is published as stable and is available to the desktop stable update channel.
- The build-only deepmerge dependency still has an unpatched low-severity advisory; the identified path merges trusted Rollup configuration and is not part of the application runtime.

### Developer Notes

- The output pipeline uses bounded documents, CodeMirror source views, a shared Markdown Worker and isolated iframes. See the [output architecture](https://github.com/linshenkx/prompt-optimizer/blob/v2.13.0/docs/architecture/output-pipeline.md).
- The extension uses a manifest-declared sandbox page as its preview host; Web and Desktop retain their existing srcdoc path.
- The daily browser gate now builds the real extension, scans for sensitive configuration and loads it with an isolated browser profile. Coverage includes multiple interactive blocks, external resources, permission isolation, source fidelity, concurrent producers and CPU throttling.
- CPU throttling is simulated. Extension tests use page freeze/resume and visibility events; these do not constitute complete acceptance on low-end hardware or under native background-tab throttling.
- The release workflow validates tags and application versions, runs test gates and packages Desktop and the extension. It publishes the stable Release only after validating multi-architecture Docker images and latest tags in both registries.

## 中文

### 概括

本正式版支持在 Web、桌面和浏览器扩展的 Markdown 结果中直接交互 HTML 网页，并重构输出链路，以应对并发生成和长内容。同步增强备份完整性，新增指定云备份的导入码，修复模型选择与已保存参数的保留问题，完善图片编辑和结构化输入模板。

### 亮点

- **网页就地交互**：统一通过“预览 / 原文”查看结果，显式 HTML 代码块及支持的 HTML 内容会在周围 Markdown 之间显示为独立网页，多个块可同时交互。
- **扩展支持交互预览**：修复 beta 中扩展无法运行 HTML 脚本的问题，可直接操作生成的按钮、表单和画布，无需另外打开标签页。
- **限制输出与渲染开销**：生成过程使用独立输出文档、虚拟化原文视图和后台 Markdown 解析。内容过大或渲染过重时回退到原文显示。
- **更可靠的备份恢复**：恢复前校验数据和图片资源，保护已有图片不被自动淘汰，并在前置导入步骤成功后才恢复工作区快照。
- **云备份导入码**：为选定的 WebDAV、S3 兼容或 Cloudflare R2 备份生成导入码、链接，并在长度允许时生成二维码。

### 产品更新

#### Desktop

- 将取消生成从界面经桌面通信传递到模型请求，流式完成会等待异步收尾操作。
- 接入统一的“预览 / 原文”结果界面、就地 HTML 预览与备份导入码流程。

#### Web

- Markdown 中的多个 HTML 示例直接显示为网页。将某一列切到原文，不会重建其他列的预览。
- 生成期间显示原文，生成完成后才创建可执行的网页预览。
- 允许预览网页请求外部数据，同时保持与主应用隔离；请求仍受浏览器跨域规则和目标接口授权要求约束。

#### Extension

- 在结果中就地显示并运行多个 HTML 块，支持内联脚本、事件处理、外部脚本库和模块。
- 预览页面可请求外部接口，同时无法读取主应用页面、存储或扩展 API；主扩展页面继续使用原有内容安全策略。
- 支持预览与原文切换、内容替换和全屏查看，并在对应结果移除时释放预览页面。

#### Core/Infra

- 将逐片生成的文本与响应式工作区快照解耦，在明确的完成边界统一写入完整或中断结果。
- 对输出大小、渲染量和待处理队列设置预算，并取消过时的解析任务。
- 将取消信号贯穿 OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic 和 Gemini 流式适配器。

### 修复

- 修复浏览器扩展的内容安全策略拦截预览脚本的问题，并拒绝来自预览子页面的伪造内容更新。
- 支持单独输出的 HTML 按钮等控件进入网页预览，并修复手机窄列对比时工具栏按钮越界的问题。
- 在写入新的业务引用前，拒绝无效备份数据、图片资源冲突和图片存储容量不足的恢复操作；明确报告部分恢复与回滚失败。
- 完善设置和图片引用的导出与恢复，工作区恢复保持为最终导入步骤。
- 刷新模型列表时保留当前选择，包括返回空列表和使用回退列表的情况；模型参数定义更新时保留已保存的参数，并按适用定义校验修改后的值。
- 图片模板更明确地区分参考图作用、编辑范围和需要保留的内容；保留结构化 JSON 的字段、类型、控制值和占位符。
- 将 Zod、body-parser、qs 及构建工具使用的 Undici 6 更新至修补版本，处理此前发现的依赖安全告警。

### 破坏性变更 / 升级说明

- 升级涉及备份恢复和输出处理，建议先导出重要工作区的备份。
- 云备份导入码包含存储访问凭据，不是权限受限的公开分享链接，请只交给可信的接收者。本版本不支持为 Google Drive 导出备份导入码。
- HTML 脚本在独立 iframe 中运行。隔离可以保护主应用文档并限制权限，但不会为任意生成脚本设置 CPU 或内存硬配额。WebGPU 等能力还取决于浏览器和设备。
- 超出输出或渲染预算时，可能停止生成或改用原文显示；中断结果与正常完成结果会保持区分。
- 扩展 ZIP 使用数字版本 `2.13.0`，移除 beta 显示名称；从 `2.13.0-beta.1` 手动安装包升级时，请手动替换扩展包。现有发布流程不自动上传浏览器扩展商店。
- 正式 Docker 镜像使用 `2.13.0` 和 `latest` 标签；GitHub Release 按正式版发布，桌面稳定更新渠道可获取本版本。
- 仅供构建使用的 deepmerge 仍有一项上游尚未修补的低危告警；已确认的调用路径用于合并受信任的 Rollup 配置，不进入应用运行时。

### 开发者说明

- 输出链路使用有容量限制的文档、CodeMirror 原文视图、共享 Markdown Worker 和独立 iframe，设计见[输出链路架构](https://github.com/linshenkx/prompt-optimizer/blob/v2.13.0/docs/architecture/output-pipeline.md)。
- 扩展通过 manifest 声明的隔离页面承载预览；Web 与桌面继续使用原有 srcdoc 路径。
- 日常浏览器测试增加真实扩展构建、敏感配置扫描和独立浏览器配置下的扩展加载测试，覆盖多块交互、外部资源、权限隔离、原文一致性、并发生成和 CPU 降速。
- CPU 降速属于模拟；扩展测试使用页面冻结/恢复和可见性事件，不等同于低性能硬件或真实后台标签页限速的完整验收。
- 发布流程校验标签和各端版本，执行测试门禁，构建桌面与扩展安装包，并在两个仓库的多架构 Docker 镜像及 latest 标签校验成功后公开正式 Release。

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

## Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either `LLVM-` or `clang+llvm-` and ends with the platform's name. For example, `LLVM-23.1.4-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz` contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as `.tar.xz` or `.tar.zst` files. The `.tar.zst` files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where `LLVM-*.msi` is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive `clang+llvm-` contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. You most likely want the `LLVM-` installer, unless you are developing software which itself uses LLVM, in which case choose `clang+llvm-`.

In addition, source archives are available:
* To get all the `llvm-project` source code for this release, choose `llvm-project-23.1.4.src.tar.xz`.
* `test-suite-23.1.4.src.tar.xz` is an archive of the [LLVM Test Suite](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-test-suite)) for this release.

## Verifying Packages

All packages come with a matching `.sig` and/or `.jsonl` file. You should use these to verify the integrity of the packages.

If it has a `.sig` file, it should have been signed by the release managers using GPG. Download the keys from the [LLVM website](https://releases.llvm.org/release-keys.asc), import them into your keyring and use them to verify the file:
```
$ gpg --import release-keys.asc
$ gpg --verify <package file name>.sig <package file name>
```

If it has a `.jsonl` file, use [gh](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify) to verify the package:
```
$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name>
(if you are able to connect to GitHub)
$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name> --bundle <package file name>.jsonl
(using attestation file on disk)
```

Logseq 2.0.2 Beta brings smoother editing, faster startup, and more reliable everyday workflows to the DB version.

[Join the iOS TestFlight beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/eBcJ9Hpc), 2.0.2 is currently under App Store review.

Web app: https://app.logseq.com/

## Features

- Gallery cards can now use URL properties as covers.
- Added a "Clear heading" slash command.
- Improved video embeds, with resizable desktop players and clickable YouTube timestamps.

## Thanks

- **Special thanks to our community PR contributors!** Your fixes, performance improvements, translations, and careful reviews helped make this beta better. Contributors include [@yuxi-liu-wired](https://github.com/yuxi-liu-wired), [@ChipNowacek](https://github.com/ChipNowacek), [@Mancn-Xu](https://github.com/Mancn-Xu), [@hahaArthur17](https://github.com/hahaArthur17), [@maksym-dilanian](https://github.com/maksym-dilanian), [@qwist1233-cpu](https://github.com/qwist1233-cpu), and many others.
- **A heartfelt thank-you to everyone testing the DB beta.** Your bug reports, reproduction steps, feedback, and retesting of fixes have been invaluable. Thank you for helping us improve Logseq with your real-world graphs and workflows!

## Fixed issues

Ordered by impact on data integrity, reliability, and everyday workflows.

1. **Preserve unsaved edits:** Save pending text before following page or block references, switching blocks, or setting Deadline/Scheduled. Pasting multiple blocks no longer lets a stale editor buffer erase the first pasted title.
2. **Restore deleted content with undo/redo:** Restore deleted blocks and pages that reference each other, along with property schemas and values. Undoing block moves now preserves their original order and nested structure.
3. **Keep block trees intact when copying or moving:** Selecting an ancestor together with its descendants no longer pulls grandchildren out of their subtree. Copy/paste preserves the original child blocks, and embed actions operate on the embed rather than its source.
4. **Keep graph and asset downloads running:** One failed asset download no longer stops the remaining asset queue or fails the graph download. Sync also keeps property-value replacements together instead of splitting them across requests.
5. **Fix Windows installation:** Fix the NSIS installer crash affecting Windows 11 24H2 and newer, so the desktop app can be installed normally.
6. **Improve file-to-DB import fidelity:** Preserve headings, icons, journal timestamps, and PDF annotation identities/order. Asset links in property values are converted into asset references, and same-title classes and properties remain distinct.
7. **Correct scheduled dates and repeating tasks:** Deadline/Scheduled repeats now advance in the local calendar. Monthly repeats no longer drift permanently after a shorter month; date filters use local days, and clearing dates removes stale journal references.
8. **Prevent query errors from crashing the graph:** Incomplete query syntax, invalid regular expressions, and query-function rendering errors are isolated. Query-builder filters again show property/tag names and include custom Status and Priority choices.
9. **Fix property editing and choice selection:** Selected node values remain visible in property pickers, choice identities resolve consistently, and configuration toggles save the newly selected value. Empty multi-value slots and date values can be cleared without errors.
10. **Restore readable search results and references:** Resolve UUID references in search titles, breadcrumbs, and nested page references. References to deleted nodes remain visible as broken links, and opening search no longer clears its results.
11. **Restore settings and HTML publishing:** Settings can be saved when config.edn is missing or invalid, and the first export.css edit creates the file correctly. HTML exports no longer open as a blank page and honor the configured home page.
12. **Make desktop editing and keyboard input reliable:** Clicks during scrolling now open the editor. A click after Escape or Shift+Up/Down keeps the newly opened editor, and fixes cover international dead-key input and IME confirmation in search.
13. **Fix Android popup and layout issues:** Nested popups reuse the presented native sheet, sheet dismissal avoids re-entry, and the layout respects the status-bar safe area. Mobile cloud-graph download and sync triggers work again.

## Enhancements

- **Faster startup and smoother editing:** Improved desktop startup, journal loading, large-page rendering, table scrolling, and search, with fewer unnecessary updates while typing.
- **Better everyday workflows:** Improved flashcard practice, date and repeating-task handling, international keyboard input, plugin APIs, CLI behavior, and translations.

meta/zstd:
Zstandard `v1.5.7` is a significant release, featuring over 500 commits accumulated over the past year. This update brings enhancements across various domains, including performance, stability, and functionality, and is particularly recommended for 32-bit users due to a bug fix detailed below.

_edit_: man pages were not properly updated in this package, and are still pointing to `v1.5.6`. If you want the `v1.5.7` version, they are updated in `dev` branch, and can be cherry-picked using commit 6af3842118ea5325480b403213b2a9fbed3d3d74. Alternatively, they can also be built locally using `make manual` and `make -C programs man`.

## Performance Enhancements

### Enhanced Compression Speed for Small Data Blocks

The compression speed for small data blocks has been notably improved at fast compression levels, thanks to contributions from @TocarIP, further extended in #4165. Below are benchmark results illustrating the performance improvements for level 1 compression on the Silesia corpus, segmented into different block sizes:

| Block Size | v1.5.6 | v1.5.7 | Improv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|   4 KB | 280 MB/s | 310 MB/s | +10% |
|   8 KB | 328 MB/s | 364 MB/s | +11% |
|  16 KB | 360 MB/s | 396 MB/s | +10% |
|  32 KB | 383 MB/s | 458 MB/s | +20% |
|  64 KB | 423 MB/s | 474 MB/s | +12% |
| 128 KB | 460 MB/s | 485 MB/s | +5% |

These improvements are particularly beneficial in data centers and databases, where data is often divided into small segments to enhance seekability. A notable example is [RocksDB](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb), which is frequently configured with block sizes around 16 KB. Such systems will experience an immediate performance boost by updating their compression library to `v1.5.7`.

Additionally, the speed improvements partially extend to dictionary compression, with observed gains ranging from none to +15%.

### Substantial `--patch-from` improvements

The  `--patch-from`  functionality of the  `zstd`  CLI allows for differential compression of a file given an older version, similar to  `bsdiff`. While compression levels impact processing speed and compression ratio as expected, at high compression levels (18+), speed was previously reduced to uncomfortable levels.

`v1.5.7`  largely mitigates the speed impact of high compression levels 18+, as illustrated in the following scenario, which compresses  `linux-6.13.tar`  as a difference from  `linux-6.12.tar`  using 6 threads:

| level | v1.5.6 | v1.5.7 | Improv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | 210 s | 42.7 s | x4.9 |
| 19 | 273 s | 61.8 s | x4.4 |
| 20 | 310 s | 82.3 s | x3.8 |
| 21 | 365 s | 120 s | x3.1 |

Additionally, compression ratio of `--patch-from`  is also substantially improved across the board, including higher compression levels:

| level | v1.5.6 | v1.5.7 | Improv. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15 | 6,383,341 | 6,003,514 | 6.3% |
| 16 | 5,909,932 | 5,421,444 | 9.0% |
| 17 | 5,613,879 | 5,214,734 | 7.7% |
| 18 | 5,584,219 | 5,075,507 |10.0% |
| 19 | 5,322,658 | 4,724,116 |12.6% |
| 20 | 5,097,236 | 4,583,435 |11.2% |
| 21 | 4,648,583 | 4,297,672 | 8.1% |
| 22 | 4,560,051 | 4,225,283 | 7.9% |
| `--max` |  N/A | 3,999,476 |
    
### Compression ratio improvements for large files

The compression ratio has been enhanced slightly for large data across all compression levels, thanks to a refined approach in selecting block boundaries. This improvement is more pronounced at lower compression levels (≤ 15), where the previous boundary selection method was relatively basic. In contrast, higher compression levels (16+) already employed some analysis, but still benefit from the introduction of the new heuristic, resulting in marginally better compression ratios.

A comparison of the compression ratios between  `v1.5.6`  and  `v1.5.7`  is presented below:

| level | `v1.5.6` | `v1.5.7` | Improv. |
| --- | --- | --- | ---:|
| 1 | 73,492,125 | 73,292,801 | -199,324
| 3 | 66,555,241 | 66,217,754 | -337,487
| 6 | 61,614,472 | 61,350,571 | -263,901
| 8 | 60,089,890 | 59,816,878 | -273,012
|12 | 58,297,345 | 58,039,924 | -257,421
|15 | 57,290,517 | 57,031,235 | -259,282
|16 | 55,341,618 | 55,304,857 | -36,761
|19 | 52,876,557 | 52,840,800 | -35,757
|22 | 52,326,420 | 52,289,718 | -36,702


## Command-Line Interface Updates

Recognizing the prevalence of multi-core systems, `zstd` now employs **multiple threads by default**, thanks to #4211 by @daniellerozenblit
In `v1.5.7`, systems will see default threading scaled according to capability, but remains cautious to mitigate risks of overloading surprises on existing user base, with a maximum of 4 threads by default.
For example, a typical "low-end" system with 4 cores and hyperthreading will employ 2 threads by default. A "higher-end" system with 8 cores and hyperthreading will employ 4 threads by default. 

These modifications only impact default settings. As usual, the number of threads that `zstd` uses can also be set manually, either via command line or via environment variables.

Additionally, a new `zstd` command `--max` is available, designed to maximize compression ratios by leveraging all parameters, at the expense of time and memory. It's slower and more resource hungry than `--ultra -22`, but achieves denser compressed archives if that's the goal. For instance, compressing `enwik9` (1,000,000,000 bytes) at `--max` level on a i7-9700k platform yields:

| level | cSize | cTime | cMem |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ultra -22` | 213,898,083 | ~6 mn | ~ 3 GB |
| `--max` | 202,507,076 | ~72 mn | ~ 18 GB |

## Bug Fixes

`v1.5.7` resolves a long standing and very rare compression issue in 32-bit mode, which can be triggered during long-lasting sessions (same `ZSTD_CCtx*` being continuously reused). This issue required several conditions to be met and a large amount of data to occur, but at the scale of `zstd` usage, it has been observed and reported (#4292).
In summary, if you use `libzstd` in 32-bit mode, this update is highly recommended.

## Miscellaneous

The release also brings its lot of various improvements, impacting build scripts (cmake, meson, Apple Framework, Visual Studio), documentation and portability (QNX, FreeBSD, Hurd, icc/icx).
Notably, there are measurable performance gains for binaries produced with Visual Studio, as a cumulative result of several contributions.

* We got rid of the "new tab" animation, as it made the application appear slower (#20543)
* We have expanded our "built-in glyph" support to cover a large portion of the new Unicode "Symbols for Legacy Computing" block (we now cover `U+1FB00` through `U+1FB94`, all sextants, filled triangles and trapezoids, and eighth blocks) (#20424)
* When you close a tab, Terminal will now unconditionally jump to the previously most recently used tab (#20272) (thanks @Anshikakalpana!)

* IME candidate windows will no longer be positioned incorrectly when Terminal is maximized (#20627) (thanks @9enki!)
* Terminal will no longer send arrow key inputs (and others) in the middle of an IME composition (#20471) (thanks @sanguneo!)
* Custom shaders which depend on the `time` parameter will no longer experience an early rollover (#20360) (thanks @Zish19!)
* Media paths referring to icon resources such as `foo.exe,-1` will once again work (#20572) (thanks @arista-ms!)
* Terminal should no longer leak memory with some graphics adapters when you are scrolled back into history or experience rendering lag after the machine resumes from sleep (#20723)
* The "Open Current Working Directory" action will no longer attempt to open non-directories (#20697) (thanks @SebTardif!)
* The font face selector in the settings UI will no longer cause Terminal to undergo rapid unscheduled disassembly (#20255) (thanks @danyalahmed1995!)
   * ... it will also no longer instantly forget what you put in it (#20359) (thanks @danyalahmed1995!)
* The JSON settings schema has been updated to include `persistedLayoutAndContent` as a valid option for `firstWindowPreference` (#20475) (thanks @doterik!)

* We've fixed some visual artifacts experienced by users of the "QQ Wubi" IME (#20542)

### Reliability

* XBOX controllers will no longer cause Terminal to shuffle off this mortal coil (#20234) (thanks @phil-scott-78!)
* We will take fewer trips to a farm upstate when you use "terminal pane" shortcuts on the Settings, Markdown or Snippets UI (#20458)
* The experimental "reposition mouse cursor with click" settings will now result in fewer "bucket-kicking" events (#20442)

### VT Support

* An application initiating an OSC 52 clipboard write at the same time as a title change will no longer experience a 5-second hang (#20728)
* A VT soft reset (DECSTR) will no longer result in the uploaded soft font (DRCS) being cleared (#20607) (thanks @j4james!)

* ConPTY will no longer wait for a DA1 response before finishing initialization (#20536)

microsoft/winget-cli:
This is a servicing release of Windows Package Manager v1.29. If you find any bugs or problems, please help us out by [filing an issue](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli/issues).

## New in v1.29

# New Feature: Source Priority

> [!NOTE]
> Experimental under `sourcePriority`; defaulted to disabled.

With this feature, one can assign a numerical priority to sources when added or later through the `source edit`
command. Sources with higher priority are sorted first in the list of sources, which results in them getting put first
in the results if other things are equal.

> [!TIP]
> Search result ordering in winget is currently based on these values in this order:
> 1. Match quality (how well a valid field matches the search request)
> 2. Match field (which field was matched against the search request)
> 3. Source order (was always relevant, but with priority you can more easily affect this)

Beyond the ability to slightly affect the result ordering, commands that primarily target available packages
(largely `install`) will now prefer to use a single result from a source with higher priority rather than prompting for
disambiguation from the user. Said another way, if multiple sources return results but only one of those sources has
the highest priority value (and it returned only one result) then that package will be used rather than giving a
"multiple packages were found" error. This has been applied to both winget CLI and PowerShell module commands.

### REST result match criteria update

Along with the source priority change, the results from REST sources (like `msstore`) now attempt to correctly set the
match criteria that factor into the result ordering. This will prevent them from being sorted to the top automatically.

## Minor Features

### Preserve installer arguments across export and import

`winget export` now captures the `--override` and `--custom` arguments that were used when a package was originally installed and saves them into the export file. When subsequently running `winget import`, those values are automatically re-applied during installation — `--override` replaces all installer arguments and `--custom` appends extra switches — so packages can be reinstalled with the same customizations without any manual intervention. Both fields are optional and independent of each other; packages without stored installer arguments are unaffected.

### --no-progress flag

Added a new `--no-progress` command-line flag that disables all progress reporting (progress bars and spinners). This flag is universally available on all commands and takes precedence over the `visual.progressBar` setting. Useful for automation scenarios or when running WinGet in environments where progress output is undesirable.

### MCP `upgrade` support

The WinGet MCP server's existing tools have been extended with new parameters to support upgrade scenarios:

- **`find-winget-packages`** now accepts an `upgradeable` parameter (default: `false`). When set to `true`, it lists only installed packages that have available upgrades — equivalent to `winget upgrade`. The `query` parameter becomes optional in this mode, allowing it to filter results or be omitted to list all upgradeable packages. AI agents can use this to answer requests like "What apps can I update with WinGet?"
- **`install-winget-package`** now accepts an `upgradeOnly` parameter (default: `false`). When set to `true`, it only upgrades an already-installed package and returns a clear error if the package is not installed (pointing to `install-winget-package` without `upgradeOnly` instead). AI agents can use this to answer requests like "Update WinGetCreate" or, in combination with `find-winget-packages` with `upgradeable=true`, "Update all my apps."

### Authenticated GitHub API requests in PowerShell module

The PowerShell module now automatically uses `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variables to authenticate GitHub API requests. This significantly increases the GitHub API rate limit, preventing failures in CI/CD pipelines. Use `-Verbose` to see which token is being used.

### Default priority of installer types

Installer type selection no longer depends on the order defined on the manifest. Instead, preference is given in this order:
- MSIX
- MSI / Wix / Burn
- Nullsoft / Inno / EXE
- Portable

When a user configures installer type requirements or preferences, the order in which they are listed is now respected during installer selection.

### Improved `list` output when redirected

- `winget list` (and similar table commands) no longer truncates output when stdout is redirected to a file or variable — column widths are now computed from the full result set.
- Spinner and progress bar output are suppressed when no console is attached, keeping redirected output clean.

### Log file naming strategy

Added a user setting (`logging.fileNameStrategy`) for controlling the default naming strategy for installer log files. Supported values are `manifest` (default), `timestamp`, `guid`, and `shortguid`. Only applies to logs generated by installers if the installer itself supports the logging switch / parameter.

| Setting | Description |
| --- | --- |
| manifest | Uses the name of the manifest and a timestamp. Has the same behavior as WinGet 1.28 |
| timestamp | The log name is just a timestamp |
| guid | The log name is a GUID |
| shortguid | The log name is the first 8 characters of a GUID |

### Sortable `list` output

`winget list` now supports sorting results via `--sort <field>` (repeatable for multi-field sorting), `--ascending`/`--descending` direction flags, and a persistent `output.sortOrder` setting. Available sort fields: `name`, `id`, `version`, `source`, `available`, `relevance`. By default, results are sorted alphabetically by name when no query is present; use `--sort relevance` to preserve the previous source-determined ordering.

## Bug Fixes

* `winget export` now works when the destination path is a hidden file
* Fixed the `useLatest` property in the DSC v3 `Microsoft.WinGet/Package` resource schema to emit a boolean default (`false`) instead of the incorrect string `"false"`.
* `SignFile` in `WinGetSourceCreator` now supports an optional RFC 3161 timestamp server via the new `TimestampServer` property on the `Signature` model. When set, `signtool.exe` is called with `/tr <url> /td sha256`, embedding a countersignature timestamp so that signed packages remain valid after the signing certificate expires.
* File and directory paths passed to `signtool.exe` and `makeappx.exe` are now quoted, fixing failures when paths contain spaces.
* DSC export now correctly exports WinGet Admin Settings
* `winget validate` now performs case-insensitive comparison for file extensions where applicable
* `winget source reset` now properly resets default sources instead of removing them
* DSC v3 `Microsoft.WinGet/Package` resource now honors the `installMode` property to use silent or interactive installer switches as specified
* Fixed a crash (`0x8000ffff`) when using `--disable-interactivity` with the Resume experimental feature enabled during install operations.

## What's Changed
* Ensure relative paths are rooted (1.29) by @JohnMcPMS in https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli/pull/6467


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli/compare/v1.29.290...v1.29.380

# v0.14.0 Highlights

Thanks to @chiba233, @Daeil-Jung, @louisjia2008-ux, @Weathercold, and @LemonNekoGH for their contributions this release.

## Product updates

### Voice

- **You can now call your character.** In the web and mobile apps, press `+` in the composer and choose a voice call. AIRI listens the whole time and sends each thing you say right away, with no drafts. Mute stops new input but keeps the call open. On desktop web, the call has a panel above the composer and turns into a small capsule when you minimize it. On phones, the capsule sits under the header with hang-up, a timer, and a waveform.
- **One microphone button for every voice mode.** The web and mobile composers had drifted into different voice controls, including a hover menu, a full-screen blurred hold-to-record overlay, and a separate Hearing drawer. Now there is one microphone in the composer. Tap it to use the current mode. Long-press or right-click it to switch modes or turn on Auto send.
  - **Dictation** (default): the button becomes a stop button, and the waveform and timer appear beside it. Live text shows in the card above the composer and no longer jumps around inside the text field.
  - **Walkie-talkie**: the text field becomes a hold-to-talk bar. Drag up to cancel.
  - **Voice message**: records audio, like before.
  - No mode covers the page with a backdrop anymore.
- **A real "Use microphone" switch.** Some of you saw the system microphone light turn on when you hadn't asked AIRI to listen. That's worrying, and the old controls only stopped listening without closing the microphone. You can now turn microphone use off from the composer voice menu, the Island controls, the mobile Hearing drawer, or Hearing settings. When it is off, every recording stops at once, and nothing can open the microphone until you turn it back on. It also blocks voice calls and ends a call in progress.
  - We also stopped three cases where AIRI opened the microphone on its own: hovering the voice button, opening the mobile Hearing drawer, and turning on microphone input (which opened it twice).
- **Your first words are no longer cut off.** If you started talking the moment recording began, AIRI could lose the start of what you said, especially on a busy page. Recording now starts capturing much sooner.

### Desktop app

- The voice card and listening capsule were hard to read over a busy desktop because their background was very see-through. They now have a solid, readable background in both light and dark mode.
- When the chat dock stood beside the danmaku feed, it jumped about 20px every time it opened or closed. It now stays in place. The closed bar is also wider and easier to find, and button focus rings no longer get clipped.
- **Update channel fix:** if you switched from Dev to Canary in About and installed the Canary installer, the app could still start the Dev build after restarting, with the Dev badge still showing. It now starts the build from the channel you installed.

### Characters and stage

- On the Live2D stage, the presence bubble could hide behind the model, for example when you zoomed in until the head left the canvas. The bubble now always shows in front.
- Minecraft: when AIRI dropped an item for you, someone else picking up any item could make AIRI stop waiting and report a timeout even though you got it. AIRI now keeps waiting until you pick it up.

### Look, language, and polish

- Status messages (errors, warnings, success, loading) now look the same everywhere. About 35 hand-made banners used four different warning colors, and some broke in one color mode. For example, the Discord, X, and gaming "configured" boxes stayed light green in dark mode, and extension errors were unreadable on light backgrounds. They now share one consistent style that stays readable on see-through panels.
- Some banner text that was stuck in English is now translated.
- Chinese text in settings could mix two fonts, so some characters looked bold. This happened when your system language list put Japanese first. AIRI now tells the system which language it shows, so each language gets one font.
- The Korean translation is fixed and up to date. The sign-in button said "sign up", and eight connection settings were still in English. The Korean README now links to the Korean blog and docs pages.
- The chat panel on wide screens is now a more comfortable width.

## Under the hood

- Your recipes (skills) and long-term memories are now stored in IndexedDB, with one record per entry, instead of one big `localStorage` list that had a few megabytes of room. Existing data moves over automatically on first launch, and your recipe IDs stay the same. Changes now sync between open windows. A window that is out of date can't undo a deletion made in another window. Two memories can also no longer clash because they share a name.

## To contributors

- **`APP_IGNORE_FOCUS=1`** opens stage-tamagotchi windows without taking focus or bringing the app to the front, so Vishot, `testing-audio`, and agent-browser runs don't steal your keyboard. `testing-audio` and `pnpm capture:tamagotchi` turn it on by default. Set `APP_IGNORE_FOCUS=0` to test focus behavior.
- **`@proj-airi/ui` `Alert`** is the shared component for status messages, with `info`, `success`, `warning`, and `danger` tones. `Callout` is now only for intros and tips. The stage-ui `Alert`, `ErrorContainer`, and stage-pages `StatusBanner` are removed. `DESIGN.md` documents the rule.
- **Backdrop surfaces:** a component now marks itself as a backdrop surface with `useBackdropSurface(element)` and paints its own fill. The desktop app draws native glass behind it. This replaces the `kind`-based `useWindowBackdrop` and the `!important` opacity overrides. See `docs/ai/adr/2026-10-29-backdrop-surfaces.md`.
- **`@proj-airi/stream-kit`** (internal) now has buffers, trackers, and a catch-up feed for event streams. A catch-up subscriber whose listener throws is now removed.
- The web voice composer and call design is recorded in `docs/ai/adr/2026-10-29-web-voice-composer-and-call.md`. There is a new Voice Presence Histoire story, and stories now follow Histoire's dark mode.
- Test reliability:
  - The flaky `voice-messages` browser test is fixed (the shared capture `AudioContext` plus explicit timeouts), and the unneeded `vitest.browser.setup.ts` is removed.
  - Static asset path tests now compare real paths.
- Dependencies:
  - kirie 0.15.2 pulled in a second Vite and a second copy of vue-router. On `main`, airi.moeru.ai and accounts.airi.build then failed to load. kirie 0.15.3 fixes this. This bug was never in a release.
  - `@ergosphere-it/electron` is updated to 0.0.16.
  - The Nix `pnpmDeps` hash is updated.
