mozilla/DeepSpeech:
# General

This is the 0.9.3 release of Deep Speech, an open speech-to-text engine. In accord with [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/), this version is not backwards compatible with earlier versions. However, models exported for 0.7.X and 0.8.X should work with this release. **This is a bugfix release and retains compatibility with the 0.9.0, 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 models. All model files included here are identical to the ones in the 0.9.0 release.** As with previous releases, this release includes the source code:

[v0.9.3.tar.gz](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/archive/v0.9.3.tar.gz)

Under the [MPL-2.0 license](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/). And the acoustic models:

[deepspeech-0.9.3-models.pbmm](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-models.pbmm)
[deepspeech-0.9.3-models.tflite](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-models.tflite)

In addition we're releasing experimental Mandarin Chinese acoustic models trained on an internal corpus composed of 2000h of read speech:

[deepspeech-0.9.3-models-zh-CN.pbmm](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-models-zh-CN.pbmm)
[deepspeech-0.9.3-models-zh-CN.tflite](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-models-zh-CN.tflite)

all under the MPL-2.0 license.

The model files with the ".pbmm" extension are memory mapped and thus memory efficient and fast to load. The model files with the ".tflite" extension are converted to use TensorFlow Lite, has [post-training quantization](https://www.tensorflow.org/lite/performance/post_training_quantization) enabled, and are more suitable for resource constrained environments.

The acoustic models were trained on American English with synthetic noise augmentation and the .pbmm model achieves an 7.06% word error rate on the [LibriSpeech clean test corpus](http://www.openslr.org/12).

Note that the model currently performs best in low-noise environments with clear recordings and has a bias towards US male accents. This does not mean the model cannot be used outside of these conditions, but that accuracy may be lower. Some users may need to train the model further to meet their intended use-case.

In addition we release the scorer:

[deepspeech-0.9.3-models.scorer](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-models.scorer)

which takes the place of the language model and trie in older releases and which is also under the MPL-2.0 license.

There is also a corresponding scorer for the Mandarin Chinese model:

[deepspeech-0.9.3-models-zh-CN.scorer](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-models-zh-CN.scorer)

We also include example audio files:

[audio-0.9.3.tar.gz](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/audio-0.9.3.tar.gz)

which can be used to test the engine, and checkpoint files for both the English and Mandarin models:

[deepspeech-0.9.3-checkpoint.tar.gz](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-checkpoint.tar.gz)
[deepspeech-0.9.3-checkpoint-zh-CN.tar.gz](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/releases/download/v0.9.3/deepspeech-0.9.3-checkpoint-zh-CN.tar.gz)

which are under the MPL-2.0 license and can be used as the basis for further fine-tuning.

# Notable changes from the previous release

- Add CI testing for hot word boosting on .NET bindings ([#3416](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/pull/3416))
- Improve error message on generate_scorer_package tooling ([#3435](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/pull/3435))
- Enable support for building static iOS framework ([#3436](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/pull/3436))
- Change Java binding package name from org.mozilla.deepspeech to org.deepspeech ([#3454](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/pull/3454))
- Expose Stream type on TypeScript binding ([#3456](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/pull/3456))

# Training Regimen + Hyperparameters for fine-tuning

The hyperparameters used to train the model are useful for fine tuning. Thus, we document them here along with the training regimen, hardware used (a server with 8 Quadro RTX 6000 GPUs each with 24GB of VRAM), and our use of cuDNN RNN.

In contrast to some previous releases, training for this release occurred as a fine tuning of the previous 0.8.2 checkpoint, with data augmentation options enabled. The following hyperparameters were used for the fine tuning. See the 0.8.2 release notes for the hyperparameters used for the base model.

  * `train_files` [Fisher](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/a723/97679079439b075de815553c7b687ccfa886.pdf), [LibriSpeech](http://www.danielpovey.com/files/2015_icassp_librispeech.pdf), [Switchboard](http://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/225858/), [Common Voice English](https://voice.mozilla.org/datasets), and approximately 1700 hours of transcribed WAMU (NPR) radio shows explicitly licensed to use as training corpora.
  * `dev_files` [LibriSpeech](http://www.danielpovey.com/files/2015_icassp_librispeech.pdf) clean dev corpus.
  * `test_files` [LibriSpeech](http://www.danielpovey.com/files/2015_icassp_librispeech.pdf) clean test corpus
  * `train_batch_size` 128
  * `dev_batch_size` 128
  * `test_batch_size` 128
  * `n_hidden` 2048
  * `learning_rate` 0.0001
  * `dropout_rate` 0.40
  * `epochs` 200
  * `augment` `pitch[pitch=1~0.1]`
  * `augment` `tempo[factor=1~0.1]`
  * `augment` `overlay[p=0.9,source=${noise},layers=1,snr=12~4]` (where ${noise} is a dataset of Freesound.org background noise recordings)
  * `augment` `overlay[p=0.1,source=${voices},layers=10~2,snr=12~4]` (where ${voices} is a dataset of audiobook snippets extracted from Librivox)
  * `augment` `resample[p=0.2,rate=12000~4000]`
  * `augment` `codec[p=0.2,bitrate=32000~16000]`
  * `augment` `reverb[p=0.2,decay=0.7~0.15,delay=10~8]`
  * `augment` `volume[p=0.2,dbfs=-10~10]`
  * `cache_for_epochs` 10

The weights with the best validation loss were selected at the end of 200 epochs using `--noearly_stop`.

The optimal `lm_alpha` and `lm_beta` values with respect to the [LibriSpeech](http://www.danielpovey.com/files/2015_icassp_librispeech.pdf) clean dev corpus remain unchanged from the previous release:

  * `lm_alpha` 0.931289039105002
  * `lm_beta` 1.1834137581510284

For the Mandarin Chinese model, the following values are recommended:

  * `lm_alpha` 0.6940122363709647
  * `lm_beta` 4.777924224113021

# Bindings

This release also includes a Python based command line tool `deepspeech`, installed through
```
pip install deepspeech
```
Alternatively, quicker inference can be performed using a supported NVIDIA GPU on Linux. (See below to find which GPU's are supported.) This is done by instead installing the GPU specific package:
```bash
pip install deepspeech-gpu
```

On Linux, macOS and Windows, the DeepSpeech package does not use TFLite by default. A TFLite version of the package on those platforms is available as:
```bash
pip install deepspeech-tflite
```

Also, it exposes bindings for the following languages

* [Python](https://deepspeech.readthedocs.io/en/v0.9.3/USING.html#using-the-python-package) (Versions 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9) installed via
  ```bash
  pip install deepspeech
  ```
  Alternatively, quicker inference can be performed using a supported NVIDIA GPU on Linux. (See below to find which GPU's are supported.) This is done by instead installing the GPU specific package:
  ```bash
  pip install deepspeech-gpu
  ```
  On Linux (AMD64), macOS and Windows, the DeepSpeech package does not use TFLite by default. A TFLite version of the package on those platforms is available as:
  ```bash
  pip install deepspeech-tflite
  ```
* [NodeJS](https://deepspeech.readthedocs.io/en/v0.9.3/USING.html#using-the-node-js-electron-js-package) (Versions 10.x, 11.x, 12.x, 13.x, 14.x and 15.x) installed via
  ```
  npm install deepspeech
  ```
  Alternatively, quicker inference can be performed using a supported NVIDIA GPU on Linux. (See below to find which GPU's are supported.) This is done by instead installing the GPU specific package:
  ```
  npm install deepspeech-gpu
  ```
  On Linux (AMD64), macOS and Windows, the DeepSpeech package does not use TFLite by default. A TFLite version of the package on those platforms is available as:
  ```bash
  npm install deepspeech-tflite
  ```

* ElectronJS versions 5.0, 6.0, 6.1, 7.0, 7.1, 8.0, 9.0, 9.1, 9.2, 10.0, 10.1, and 11.0 are also supported

* [C](https://deepspeech.readthedocs.io/en/v0.9.3/C-Examples.html) which requires the appropriate shared objects are installed from `native_client.tar.xz` (See the section in the main [README](https://deepspeech.readthedocs.io/en/v0.9.3/USING.html#using-the-command-line-client) which describes `native_client.tar.xz` installation.)

* [.NET](https://www.nuget.org/packages/DeepSpeech/0.9.3) which is installed by following the instructions on the [NuGet package page](https://www.nuget.org/packages/DeepSpeech/0.9.3).

In addition there are third party bindings that are supported by external developers, for example

* [Rust](https://github.com/RustAudio/deepspeech-rs) which is installed by following the instructions on the external Rust repo.
* [Go](https://github.com/asticode/go-astideepspeech) which is installed by following the instructions on the external Go repo.
* [V](https://github.com/thecodrr/vspeech) which is installed by following the instructions on the external Vlang repo.

# Supported Platforms

* Windows 8.1, 10, and Server 2012 R2 64-bits (at least AVX support, requires `Redistribuable Visual C++ 2015 Update 3 (64-bits)` for runtime).
* OS X 10.10, 10.11, 10.12, 10.13, 10.14, and 10.15
* Linux x86 64 bit with a modern CPU (at least AVX/FMA)
* Linux x86 64 bit with a modern CPU (at least AVX/FMA) + NVIDIA GPU (Compute Capability at least 3.0, see [NVIDIA docs](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus))
* Raspbian Buster on Raspberry Pi 3, Pi 4
* Linux/ARM64 built against Debian/ARMbian Buster and tested on LePotato boards
* Java Android (7.0-11.0) bindings (+ demo app). Tested on Google Pixel 2 ; Sony Xperia Z Premium ; Nokia 1.3, TF Lite model only.
* iOS with Swift bindings (experimental). Tested on iPhone Xs.

* TFLite Delegation API is here as a preview: do not expect released models to work out-of-the box, but feedback / PRs is welcome.

# Documentation

Documentation is available on [deepspeech.readthedocs.io](https://deepspeech.readthedocs.io/en/v0.9.3/).

# Contact/Getting Help

1. [FAQ](https://github.com/mozilla/DeepSpeech/wiki#frequently-asked-questions) - We have a list of common questions, and their answers, in our FAQ. When just getting started, it's best to first check the FAQ to see if your question is addressed.
2. [Discourse Forums](https://discourse.mozilla.org/c/deep-speech) - If your question is not addressed in the FAQ, the Discourse Forums is the next place to look. They contain conversations on [General Topics](https://discourse.mozilla.org/t/general-topics), [Using Deep Speech](https://discourse.mozilla.org/t/using-deep-speech), [Alternative Platforms](https://discourse.mozilla.org/t/alternative-platforms), and [Deep Speech Development](https://discourse.mozilla.org/t/deep-speech-development).
3. [Matrix](https://chat.mozilla.org/#/room/#machinelearning:mozilla.org) - If your question is not addressed by either the FAQ or Discourse Forums, you can contact us on the `#machinelearning:mozilla.org` channel on Mozilla Matrix; people there can try to answer/help
4. [Issues](https://github.com/mozilla/deepspeech/issues) - Finally, if all else fails, you can open an issue in our repo if there is a bug with the current code base.

mpv-player/mpv:
We are excited to announce the release of mpv 0.41.0.

Key highlights:

* The libplacebo based `gpu-next` is now the default, instead of `gpu`
* Vulkan hardware decoding is preferred over other APIs
* New context_menu.lua script for right-click context menus
* AAudio backend for modern, JNI-free audio output on Android
* Improved default color management for gpu-next, and handling on Wayland
* Color representation protocol support for Wayland
* Tablet input support for Wayland
* Clipboard writing support for Wayland and a clipboard backend for X11
* Ambient light support on Linux (using sysfs ALS)
* Built-in helpers to register mpv as a media app on Windows

This release requires FFmpeg 6.1 or newer and libplacebo 6.338.2 or newer.

# Features

## New

- clipboard-wayland: support clipboard writing
- wayland: add support for wp-color-representation-v1
- wayland: tablet input support
- vo_gpu_next: add support for blend-subtitles=video
- meson: add mpv-register and mpv-unregister helpers on Windows
- context_menu.lua: add this script
- select.lua: add edit-config-file and edit-input-conf
- osc.lua: add indicator for buffering/loading
- osdep/linux-als: support 'ambient-light' property on Linux
- clipboard-x11: add x11 clipboard backend
- ao/aaudio: implement native AAudio backend for Android

## Changed

- vd_lavc: prefer Vulkan hwdec when available
- vd_lavc: prefer non-copy hwdec before falling back to -copy variant
- vo: move vo_mediacodec_embed to not be the default on Android
- sub/osd_libass: don't rerender OSD if not changed
- vo: prefer vo_gpu_next over vo_gpu by default
- vo_gpu_next: respect ICC profile color space over any metadata
- vo_gpu_next: linearize sRGB as a pure 2.2 power function
- meson: warn if building with SDL2 due to known problems
- osxbundle: make bundle category configurable and default to video
- ao_pipewire: avoid setting any media.role by default


# Options and Commands

## Added

- sub: add control for libass caching options (glyph-limit, bitmap-max-size)
- vo: add options to control background tile appearance (transparency)
- command: add default and forced flags to the track add commands
- vo_gpu_next: add options to control subtitle peak for HDR output
- video/out/d3d11: add d3d11 composition mode support
- vd_lavc: add --hwdec-threads
- stream_bluray: add --bluray-angle
- vo_gpu_next: add options to control output colorspace metadata more precisely
- sub: make --sub-fix-timing configurable
- vo_gpu_next: add --hdr-reference-white
- audio/out: add --audio-set-media-role

## Changed

- options: revert --prefetch-playlist default back to 'no'
- vo_gpu_next: change --target-colorspace-hint to 'auto' by default
- options: handle runtime --wid change
- options: reduce swapchain-depth to 2 by default
- screenshot: add osd and scaled flags to screenshot commands


# Fixes and Minor Enhancements

- vo_kitty: add auto-multiplexer-passthrough option
- vd_lavc: enable FFv1 hwaccel by default
- clipboard-wayland: prevent reading from hung up fd
- demux_mkv: fix compilation after deprecated definitions removal
- filters: handle flipping video if displaymatrix indicates so
- player/scripting: fix race condition when destroying clients
- {osd,msg}: use PU codepoints for escape codes instead of invalid UTF-8
- vo_dmabuf_wayland: only load needed hardware decoding drivers
- video/image_writer: tag accurate bit depth
- demux_lavf: fix unconstrained cache size with wrapped AVFrame packets
- libarchive: fix reading name of certain UTF-8 files
- sub/sd_lavc: fix decoding with libaribb24
- ao_avfoundation: fix memory leak
- osc.lua: fix volume icon not updating while paused
- context_wayland: implement target_csp for wayland
- vo_gpu: fix target colorspace for redrawn frames
- vo_dmabuf_wayland: don't set HDR metadata on SDR transfers
- vo_gpu_next: don't do partial updates on hint luminance
- sub/ass_mp: add missing padding for ass packer
- stream_dvb: allow to enforce DVB-S/T for old zap format channels.conf
- demux_libarchive: fix reading archives with '%' in stream URL path
- vo_gpu_next: allow UINT upload if no other format is supported
- ytdl_hook.lua: fix incorrect default format used with yt-dlp
- vo_gpu_next: allow unsetting LUTs
- stream_bluray: use bd_get_main_title() to get main title
- vo_gpu_next: when tone-mapping, set better maxCLL value
- stream_libarchive: seek source stream to 0 before probing
- path-unix: support ~~desktop path expansion
- ytdl_hook.lua: don't crash if playlist entries don't have an usable URL
- mac/vulkan: fix frame not displayed when paused
- mac/common: render first frame on init if possible
- video/out/w32_common: support --wid=0
- demux_mkv: map and expose hearing/visual impaired flags
- player/misc: show percentage progress for --stream-dump
- command: fix null dereference for invalid command in input-commands
- cplugin: fix missing init of pfn_mpv_get_time_ns
- vo_dmabuf_wayland: actually reuse OSD buffers
- mp_image: add support for AVAlphaMode
- vo_gpu_next: add --border-background=blur and --background-blur-radius
- demux/cue: fix crash when there are no tracks
- vf_format: add some basic HDR10 metadata
- vo/context_android: fix surface tearing on resize
- meson: remove redundant 'sdl2' option
- mac/common: fix window position on multi monitor setups
- vo_gpu_next: limit min_luma to 1000:1 contrast ratio in SDR mode
- ao_pipewire: fix some incorrect channel mappings
- wayland: correct geometry handling for rotated outputs
- demux: clear packet pool when upper memory limit is lowered
- mp_image: add ycgco-{re,ro} support
- wayland: convert luminance values to libplacebo space
- vo: trigger manual redraws at most at slightly over display fps
- osxbundle: add new macOS 26 compatible App icon
- wayland: support color-management-v1 version 2


This listing is not complete. Check DOCS/client-api-changes.rst for a history of changes to the client API, and DOCS/interface-changes.rst for a history of changes to other user-visible interfaces.

A complete changelog can be seen by running `git log v0.40.0..v0.41.0` in the git repository or by visiting <https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/compare/v0.40.0...v0.41.0>.

<hr>

Note that the release binary assets are our [CI builds](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/actions/runs/20414542745). These builds are reasonably useful, but don't include everything which mpv supports (e.g. there's no _encoding_ support).

Patch release v4.12.1. Security fix only.

**Security**

- Hardened the external URL policy for user-supplied URLs (chat vision image/audio/video URLs, image and audio endpoints). Redirect targets are now validated on every hop, 100.64.0.0/10 and 0.0.0.0/8 are treated as non-public, and the connection goes to the address that was validated. See #12853. Credits to @spicysharkco for the discovery.

# NautilusTrader 1.231.0 Beta

Released on 2nd August 2026 (UTC).

### NautilusTrader v2 transition notice

This release is intended to be the final NautilusTrader `1.x` release with support for the legacy Cython v1 core. If final validation finds a serious blocker, maintainers may take another `1.x` release rather than force the cutover.

The v2 Rust + PyO3 runtime has reached the release-candidate stage for the supported workflows: Python strategy authoring, backtesting, live operation, core risk and execution, portfolio/accounting, data catalog usage, and the current adapter set. Some lower-use and newer surfaces remain deferred, and those are tracked in the [v2 roadmap](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/4042) rather than treated as blockers for the cutover.

After this release, `develop` will move to v2-only. The legacy v1 core will move to a `develop_v1` branch, where maintainers will accept critical security backports for approximately three months after the v2 cutover.

**New feature work will now target v2.**

The paired `2.0.0rc2` wheels are being released alongside `1.231.0` for community testing with normal `--pre` installation. Follow‑up `2.0.0rcN` wheels are likely to ship at a higher cadence than normal releases as feedback arrives, before the final `2.0.0` release.

#### Migration contracts

The v2 cutover makes the Rust + PyO3 package the primary path for new installs and source builds. In the current checkout it lives under `python/` and uses `python/.venv`; the root package and root `.venv` still provide the legacy v1 Cython environment. Both packages import as `nautilus_trader`, so test the migration in a separate virtual environment. See [Migrate from v1 to v2](MIGRATION_V2.md) for the current imports and build commands.

The accepted v2 contract differences are native `CustomData` without v1 wrapper semantics, `OptionGreeks` cache writes, no Python `Bar.is_revision`, and a cross-zero `Position.apply` entry price that resets to the flipping fill. V2 also prefers mark prices by default. Catalog order-event data written before `activation_price` and `OrderFilled.info` were added is not readable with the new schema and must be regenerated or migrated before an in-place upgrade. `OrderFillVoided` replay requires the referenced fill locally before reopening and treats `VOIDED` as terminal. Regenerate v2 order streams that contain a reopened correction before its referenced fill, or a cancel or update after `VOIDED`.

The migration guide includes the v1-to-v2 identifier, collection, lifecycle, callback, subscription, historical-batch, and removed-hook mappings. Typed historical requests use batch callbacks; generic custom data continues through `on_historical_data`.

#### Cutover limits

The supported cutover workflows cover Python strategies, actors, backtests, live nodes, core risk and execution, portfolio/accounting, data catalogs, reports, tearsheets, and the current Rust-backed adapter set.

The following limits remain deferred:

- Python request callbacks omit v1 joined‑response, pending cleanup, and late or duplicate delivery conveniences.
- Direct Python `LiveNode` injection for Redis cache databases and external message-bus backing.
- SQL cache position and synthetic loads, state persistence, and heartbeat.
- External message-bus publication of serialized order and position snapshots.
- V1 `StreamingConfig` and `DataCatalogConfig` iterator wiring on the v2 `BacktestNode`.
- V1 adapter instrument-provider filters; Hyperliquid v2 loads the configured universe.
- Published tutorials still use v1; generated v2 stubs and `python/examples/` show the current API.
- Static typing does not cover three Kraken batch methods or adapter wire DTO runtime attributes.

navidrome/navidrome:
This is a bug fix release. The main fix is for users on slow storage (USB disks, remote drives), who have seen floods of `database is locked` errors, UI freezes and failed full scans since 0.64.0. Scans now cause much less lock contention: the artwork worker pauses while a scan runs, and `ANALYZE` no longer holds the write lock for a long time. It also fixes scans that always failed on 32-bit builds (armv5/6/7, 386) when a file had a broken track or disc number.

## Security
- Sanitize user-controlled names (playlists, albums, artists, track titles) in the `Content-Disposition` header of downloads, so a crafted name cannot change the name of the downloaded file. ([#5895](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/5895) by [@zapisanchez](https://github.com/zapisanchez))
- Stop writing the admin password to the log when the initial admin user cannot be created. ([#5897](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/5897) by [@zapisanchez](https://github.com/zapisanchez))

## Scanner
- Fix `database is locked` errors, UI freezes and failed scans on slow storage. The artwork worker now pauses during scans, `ANALYZE` runs one index at a time, `@eaDir` thumbnail folders are ignored, and folder saves are retried when the database is busy. ([#6201](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/6201) by [@deluan](https://github.com/deluan))
- Fix scans failing with `value out of range` on 32-bit builds when a file has an invalid track number, disc number or BPM. A migration resets existing invalid values. ([#6202](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/6202) by [@deluan](https://github.com/deluan))

## Server
- Fix a failed initial admin creation that marked the initial setup as done, leaving the server without an admin user. Also fix invalid JSON in some delete responses and the missing `Content-Type` on shared playlist (M3U) downloads. ([#5897](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/5897) by [@zapisanchez](https://github.com/zapisanchez))

## Jellyfin API
- Honor the `IsPublic` flag when creating a playlist. Before, all playlists created through the Jellyfin API were private. ([#6204](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/6204) by [@deluan](https://github.com/deluan))

## New Contributors

- [@zapisanchez](https://github.com/zapisanchez) made their first contribution in [#5895](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/pull/5895)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/compare/v0.64.1...v0.64.2

## Helping out

This release is only possible thanks to the support of some **awesome people**!

Want to be one of them?
You can [sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/deluan), pay me a [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/deluan), or [contribute with code](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/developers/).

## Where to go next?

* Read installation instructions on our [website](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/installation/).
* Host Navidrome on [PikaPods](https://www.pikapods.com/pods?run=navidrome) or [Zenith](https://zenith.hosting/host/navidrome?ref=navidrome) for a simple cloud solution.
* Reach out on [Discord](https://discord.gg/xh7j7yF), [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/navidrome/) and [Twitter](https://twitter.com/navidrome)!

netbirdio/netbird:
# Release Notes for v0.82.0

## Highlights

### 🛣️ Latency-aware HA routing that holds stable routes

Routing peers in an HA group with equal metrics are meant to be chosen by latency, but the client used to sample latency only once, when the connection was set up, and moved the route on events that did not need it. Every switch between masquerading routing peers resets the TCP connections using the route, so SSH sessions and other long-lived flows dropped more often than they had to.

The client now samples the latency of connected routing peers continuously and smooths it, and moves a route for latency only when the gain clears a margin: at least 20ms, 20% of the current latency, and the measurement noise of both paths. After a latency-driven switch it keeps the new peer for at least 30 seconds. A routing peer that drops from direct to relay keeps the route for a grace period before it moves to an equivalent direct peer, and a peer that comes up over relay first is held the same way while the others turn direct. Failover, better metrics and connected-over-idle still switch immediately.

The grace period is set on the client with `NB_HA_RELAYED_SWITCH_DELAY` (a duration, `0`, or `never`; default `30s`). Routing peer switches are now logged at warning level with the reason and published as system events, so they show in `netbird status -d` and in debug bundles.

<!-- TODO: screenshot of netbird status -d showing a routing peer switch event -->

📖 [High availability for routing peers](https://docs.netbird.io/manage/networks/how-routing-peers-work#high-availability) · [#7689](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/7689), [#8192](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8192)

### 📋 `netbird status --table`

`netbird status --table` (`-t`) lists peers in a table with their name, IP, status, connection type, latency and traffic, which is easier to scan than the detailed output on a large network. It works with the existing filter flags, so `netbird status -t -S connected -T P2P` shows only connected peer-to-peer peers.

```text
Peers (3/5 connected):
NAME          IP            STATUS       CONN      LATENCY   RX / TX
web-01        100.64.0.12   Connected    P2P       12ms      1.2 MiB / 3.4 MiB
db-01         100.64.0.15   Connected    Relayed   48ms      54.0 KiB / 12.1 KiB
ci-runner     100.64.0.40   Connecting   -         -         0 B / 0 B
```

`--table` cannot be combined with `-d`, `--json`, `--yaml`, `--ipv4` or `--ipv6`.

📖 [CLI: status, table view](https://docs.netbird.io/get-started/cli#table-view) · [#8305](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8305)

### 🗄️ A dedicated database for reverse proxy access logs

Reverse proxy access logs are now read and written through their own database connection instead of the main store's, and can live in a separate database. Nothing needs to change on upgrade: by default the access log store follows the main store engine, as a separate `access_logs.db` file in the data directory on SQLite, or the main store DSN through its own connection pool on PostgreSQL.

To point it elsewhere, set `server.accessLogStore` (`engine`, `dsn`, `file`) in the combined server's `config.yaml`, or the environment variables below:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `NB_ACCESS_LOG_STORE_ENGINE` | `sqlite` or `postgres` |
| `NB_ACCESS_LOG_POSTGRES_DSN` | a dedicated PostgreSQL database |
| `NB_ACCESS_LOG_SQLITE_FILE` | the SQLite file, `access_logs.db` by default |
| `NB_ACCESS_LOG_SQL_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` | pool size, falling back to `NB_SQL_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` |

📖 [Reverse proxy access logs](https://docs.netbird.io/manage/reverse-proxy/access-logs) · [#8303](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8303)

### Removal: MySQL store

The MySQL store engine for management, deprecated in v0.81.0, is removed. A management server configured with the `mysql` engine refuses to start on v0.82.0 and points to the migration guide.

**Migrate to PostgreSQL before upgrading.** The `netbird-mysql-migrate` tool is no longer part of the release, so run the migration while still on 0.81.x, with the tool from the [v0.81.5 release](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/releases/tag/v0.81.5), then upgrade.

📖 [Migrate from MySQL to PostgreSQL](https://docs.netbird.io/selfhosted/migration/mysql-to-postgresql) · [#7914](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/7914)

### Deprecation: Rosenpass

Rosenpass support is deprecated. It keeps working for now, but it may be removed in a future release, so avoid making new deployments depend on it. `--enable-rosenpass` and `--rosenpass-permissive` are hidden from `netbird up --help` and print a deprecation warning whenever they are used, and the desktop app shows a notice under the quantum-resistance toggle in **Settings → Security**.

> An alternative solution is in the works and we will update you in the coming weeks.

<!-- TODO: screenshot of the deprecation notice in Settings → Security -->

📖 [Post-quantum cryptography (Rosenpass)](https://docs.netbird.io/client/post-quantum-cryptography) · [#8372](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8372)

## What's New

### 🔒 Security and Access Control

* **Applied the SSH root-login setting to every uid 0 account**, not only to the account named `root`, so aliases such as FreeBSD's `toor` are covered; an account whose uid cannot be parsed is treated as privileged. [#8390](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8390)
* **Refused path-bearing `LANGUAGE`/`LC_*`, `TERM` and `TZ` values from SSH clients** before they reach the privileged `login`/`su` call for a session. [#8388](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8388)
* **Matched the account id from the request against the service configuration** in the reverse proxy's auth and access log middleware. [#8386](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8386)
* **Masked credentials in URLs written to the management logs**. [#8250](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8250)

### 🖥️ Client Improvements

* **Detected default route changes in the Linux network monitor**. [#8216](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8216)
* **Kept the `resolv.conf` watch armed while repairing DNS in file mode**. [#8207](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8207)
* **Fixed a deadlock when shutting down the Signal reconnect listener**. [#8257](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8257)
* **Called the disconnect callback on every connection teardown**. [#8178](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8178)
* **Skipped peers without a PTR record in the Kubernetes commands**. [#8360](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8360)
* **Stopped the service and the UI before the Windows installer extracts files**. [#8255](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8255)
* **Moved the macOS Homebrew cask to Homebrew install steps**. [#7477](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/7477)
* **Migrated the desktop UI to Tailwind CSS 4** and fixed the frontend npm audit findings, and bumped the wails fork to v3.0.0. [#8277](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8277), [#8370](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8370)
* **Added Hebrew to the language picker**, and fixed the grammar of the post-install message. [#8102](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8102), [#8242](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8242)
* **Removed the non-functional `--admin-url` flag**; it is now deprecated and ignored. [#8267](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8267)
* Bumped wireguard-go and removed the replace directives from the embedded client module. [#8229](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8229), [#8280](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8280)

### ⚙️ Management Improvements

* **Moved network map data reads onto a PostgreSQL read replica** when `NB_STORE_ENGINE_POSTGRES_REPLICA_DSN` is set; without it, reads stay on the primary. [#8302](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8302)
* **Sped up common queries** with new indexes for groups, events, personal access tokens and access logs, an index-friendly inner groups query, a faster posture check cache and fewer last-usage writes for users and tokens. [#8289](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8289), [#8297](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8297), [#8366](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8366), [#8290](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8290)
* **Pushed network maps when an integrated validator changes a peer's approval** outside a login, for example during a periodic EDR sync, so a newly approved peer no longer waits for an unrelated update. [#8299](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8299)
* **Gave the `/api/setup` owner account the single account mode domain**, so the first JIT user joins it instead of getting an account of their own. [#8147](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8147)
* **Used the account owner as the inviter for service user invites**. [#8276](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8276)
* **Added pagination to the `GetAllPeers` call**. [#8190](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8190)
* **Skipped the inactivity expiration rescan on connect** when a job is already scheduled, and cancelled peer expiration for accounts that no longer exist. [#8287](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8287), [#8218](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8218)
* Handled a possible nil peer when returning an empty network map, and cleaned NUL bytes from peer metadata strings. [#8285](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8285), [#8219](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8219)

### 🔀 Reverse Proxy

* **Added `--external-ip-map` to the proxy's embedded client** (`NB_PROXY_EXTERNAL_IP_MAP`), so a proxy in a container or behind NAT can advertise its public address and peers reach it directly instead of over relay. It needs a fixed, forwarded `--wg-port`, so it applies to single-account deployments. [#8185](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8185)
* **Returned the reason when custom domain validation fails**. [#8122](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/8122)

netdata/netdata: Netdata v2.12.2 is a patch release to address issues discovered since [v2.12.1](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/releases/tag/v2.12.1). This release tightens SNMPv3 authentication in the SNMP traps receiver, stops alert evaluation from keeping obsolete charts alive indefinitely, makes Cloud reliably see disconnected children as offline and receive every alert transition, restores the intended backoff when the Agent reconnects to Cloud, requires Function and dynamic configuration requests to carry strict JSON, keeps external plugins running after a single malformed line of output, keeps Kubernetes state charts and their alerts from disappearing when a similarly named object is deleted, makes long-range queries return data from newer tiers after a gap in older ones, and fixes static 64-bit ARM builds that could crash at startup on Cortex-A53 boards such as the Raspberry Pi 3. ## Streaming and Netdata Cloud - Fixed a race where a child that disconnected from its Parent could stay live in Netdata Cloud. The node state update was scheduled before the child was marked offline, so under CPU contention the offline state was sometimes never sent ([#24285](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24285), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - A Parent now waits 125% of a disconnected child's expected reboot time, capped at 30 seconds, before reporting it offline to Netdata Cloud. Integer arithmetic had reduced the margin to 100%. A child with no recorded reboot time no longer schedules a zero-delay timer, which can cause high CPU usage with older libuv versions ([#24343](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24343), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed alert transitions being lost on the way to Netdata Cloud. A message the MQTT layer refused, for example while offline or with a full buffer, was treated as delivered and removed from the queue; it is now retried. The alert snapshot also could announce more chunks than it sent, and is now built from a single consistent query and sent only after a successful rebuild ([#24224](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24224), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed the reconnect backoff to Netdata Cloud. Once the backoff reached its cap, the clamp was returned in seconds but slept as milliseconds, so a disconnected Agent retried about once per second instead of waiting up to the intended maximum (currently 20 minutes) ([#24340](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24340), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed the Cloud connection handing out MQTT packet id 1 twice when the packet id counter wrapped around. Two messages in flight with the same id lose their acknowledgement and timeout tracking ([#24341](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24341), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed the `t-rx` timestamp in the Agent's HTTP replies to Netdata Cloud, which had been sent as 0 since v2.0.0 instead of the time the request was received ([#24252](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24252), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) ## Health - Fixed alert evaluation keeping obsolete charts alive. Every evaluation pass refreshed the chart's last-access time, so an obsolete chart with an alert attached was never old enough to be cleaned up. On Kubernetes nodes with pod churn this kept growing the number of `k8s.cgroup` charts, and the metadata on Parents along with it ([#24273](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24273), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed several health persistence bugs: a prepared statement leaked on every alert transition on hosts without an ACLK configuration, 64-bit event ids were bound as 32-bit values, and the next alarm event id fell back to 0 instead of the alarm id when there were no detail rows ([#24223](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24223), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) ## Database - Fixed metadata cleanup passes that could stall. A dimension, chart or label cleanup pass never completed if the first row of its snapshot was deleted before being read, and an interrupted context cleanup dropped the context from its queue, leaving the rest of its dimensions unchecked. Failed chart label stores are now retried, and the WAL size is checked far less often during cleanup ([#24227](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24227), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed a deadlock when freeing a dictionary whose delete callback destroys a nested dictionary that still has referenced items. Tier backfill could reach it when a chart of a removed host was freed while one of its dimensions was still referenced ([#24344](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24344), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - `dbengine`: corrupted gorilla-compressed pages whose length is not a multiple of the buffer size are now rejected instead of being read past the end of their allocation ([#24310](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24310), [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456)) - Fixed completed points of higher tiers staying invisible to queries for a full extra tier period. They were published only when a collection landed exactly on a tier boundary, which slow or offset collectors can miss every time; overdue points are now published on the next collected sample ([#24405](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24405), [@ktsaou](https://github.com/ktsaou)) - `dbengine`: gaps of a single second are now cached like longer ones, so repeated queries over them no longer search the journals again, and a cached gap no longer overlaps the first point of the page that follows it ([#24370](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24370), [@ktsaou](https://github.com/ktsaou)) ## Queries - Fixed the `dimensions=` filter of `/api/v1/context` and `/api/v1/contexts`, which ignored every metric whose name equals its id (most of them) and so returned all dimensions, instances and contexts ([#24245](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24245), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed `instance@node_id` patterns in the weights API (metric correlations, anomaly rates), which matched nothing ([#24245](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24245), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed label filters that combine a bare label name with a `name=value` term, so matching charts are kept while negative `name=value` terms still take precedence ([#24202](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24202), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed `/api/v1/info` reading the analytics strings (build info, release channel, notification methods, exporting connectors) without their lock, so a request that overlapped an analytics refresh could read freed memory ([#24342](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24342), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Fixed queries returning empty rows for the rest of their time range when an older tier ran out of data well before the planned switch to a newer tier. The query now continues into the newer tier, and SES/DES no longer extend stale values to the end of a query whose tier switch failed ([#24406](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24406), [@ktsaou](https://github.com/ktsaou)) ## Functions - Function and dynamic configuration requests now accept only strict JSON request bodies (RFC 8259). Any other body, such as YAML, form data or plain text, is rejected with HTTP 400. The dashboard, Netdata Cloud and the Agent's own callers already send JSON. A saved dynamic configuration that is not strict JSON fails to re-apply, with a warning in the log. Bodies are checked again where they are passed to plugins and streaming children, so update Parents as well as their children ([#24409](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24409), [@ktsaou](https://github.com/ktsaou)) - `go.d.plugin`: the body of a Function request is now treated as data up to its end marker. A line in the body that looked like a plugin command could replace the running Function call, cancel another one, or stop the plugin from reading further requests. Malformed or oversized requests are now skipped as a whole, without their bodies being parsed as commands ([#24410](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24410), [@ilyam8](https://github.com/ilyam8)) ## Collectors - External plugins: a protocol error, such as a single corrupted line of plugin output, permanently disabled the plugin until the Agent restarted. Protocol errors now follow the same policy as error exits: the plugin is restarted after 10 × `update_every` seconds, and disabled only if it never produced useful output or fails more than 10 consecutive runs ([#24051](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24051), [@ilyam8](https://github.com/ilyam8)) - SNMP traps: SNMPv3 messages are now rejected and counted as `usm_failures` when they skip authentication for a user configured to require it, or declare a non-USM security model. Rejected messages are not acknowledged and do not register engine IDs ([#24188](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24188), [@ilyam8](https://github.com/ilyam8)) - SNMP: community strings and SNMPv3 passphrases are no longer included in the connection details written to debug logs ([#24217](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24217), [@ilyam8](https://github.com/ilyam8)) - Disk statistics: fixed detection of the discard and flush fields in `/proc/diskstats`. Kernels before 4.18 got six `disk_ext.*` charts of zeros, and kernels 4.18 to 5.4 got `flushes` dimensions stuck at zero. The fields are now detected per disk, and `flushes` dimensions are added when a disk starts reporting them ([#24243](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24243), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - `proc.plugin`: reduced overhead on kernels where some `/proc` files are not seekable, such as Ubuntu 24.04 HWE (6.14). Rewinding such a file no longer resolves its name again on every read, cutting `proc.plugin` busy time by about 9% ([#24212](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24212), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Kubernetes state: deleting a node, pod, deployment or cronjob no longer removes the charts of live objects whose names start with the same name, such as pods `web-10` to `web-19` when `web-1` is deleted. Those charts did not come back until the object was recreated or the Agent restarted, and their alerts, such as `k8s_state_deployment_condition_available`, silently stopped. Scheduling a pod also no longer rewrites the node label on such charts ([#24402](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24402), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - `log2journal`: JSON input with arrays nested deeper than the parser's maximum depth is now rejected with an error instead of overrunning its key stack ([#24290](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24290), [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456)) ## Installation and packaging - Static builds for 64-bit ARM now enable the linker workarounds for Cortex-A53 errata 835769 and 843419, including for the Rust plugins. Depending on code layout, a static build could die with `SIGILL` at startup on Cortex-A53 boards such as the Raspberry Pi 3 and ODROID-C2. CI now scans the aarch64 static archive for unfixed instruction sequences, and Rust functions are aligned to 8 bytes so the linker's erratum stubs cannot shift them back onto an affected sequence ([#24207](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24207), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag), [#24387](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24387), [@vkalintiris](https://github.com/vkalintiris)) - Windows packages now bundle the `msys-2.0.dll` from MSYS2's own `msys2-runtime` 3.6.11 package, pinned by URL and checksum, instead of building a patched 3.6.10 runtime from source. 3.6.11 carries the upstream fixes for the startup crash addressed in v2.12.1, and the source build no longer compiled with MSYS2's current toolchain ([#24390](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24390), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag)) - Updated the vendored IBM MQ client libraries to 9.4.5.1 ([#24294](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24294), [@Ferroin](https://github.com/Ferroin)) ## Acknowledgments We would like to thank our dedicated, talented contributors that make up this amazing community. The time and expertise that you volunteer is essential to our success. - [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456) for bounding the array nesting depth of the `log2journal` JSON parser and for rejecting corrupted gorilla pages in `dbengine`. ## Support options As we grow, we stay committed to providing the best support ever seen from an open-source solution. Should you encounter an issue with any of the changes made in this release or any feature in the Netdata Agent, feel free to contact us through one of the following channels: - [Netdata Learn](https://learn.netdata.cloud): Find documentation, guides, and reference material for monitoring and troubleshooting your systems with Netdata. - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues): Make use of the Netdata repository to report bugs or open a new feature request. - [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/discussions): Join the conversation around the Netdata development process and be a part of it. - [Community Forums](https://community.netdata.cloud/): Visit the Community Forums and contribute to the collaborative knowledge base. - [Discord Server](https://discord.gg/2eduZdSeC7): Jump into the Netdata Discord and hang out with like-minded sysadmins, DevOps, SREs, and other troubleshooters. More than 2000 engineers are already using it!

Meet Skill Discovery: describe what you want to create, and Open Design finds the relevant Skills to guide the work—from your first idea to the next revision.

Your idea should be the starting point. In 0.26.1, **Skill Discovery helps Open Design understand the kind of work you want to make and choose the Skills that fit.** You can focus on the result, with less manual setup before creating and more continuity as you refine it. Alongside this, smoother project starts, connected feedback, and steadier previews keep your work moving.

## 🧠 Skill Discovery: the right Skills for what you have in mind

Describe the result you want. **Skill Discovery selects the deliverable type and reads its native Skill guidance**, giving Open Design a task-specific starting point. It supports eleven deliverable types, including interactive prototypes and motion work. (#8804)

- **Start with your intent.** Your explicit request takes priority when it conflicts with a selected task type. Skills and templates you mention provide compatible guidance and references while keeping the requested deliverable in focus.
- **Bring the right guidance into the work.** Open Design reads the relevant Skill instructions for the chosen type, so you spend less time finding and selecting them yourself.
- **Keep the direction as you iterate.** Follow-up work carries the chosen Skill guidance forward, keeping revisions consistent. If you ask only for a plan or clarification, that request does not silently become permission to produce the final work.

## 🔥 Highlights

- 🔗 **Share the work, not a pile of screenshots.** Publish a design file as one public link, stop it when the review is over, and resume the same link later. Comments left on the shared page flow back to the file, with unread feedback waiting where you work. (#8408, #8859, #8867, #8904) Thanks @alchemistklk.
- 🤖 **Bring your own connection — and keep the Agent in the loop.** Open Design can use available registered runtimes, and the same BYOK connection works from the app or the `od` CLI. Your project preview stays isolated to its own work, even when two projects use the same browser storage. (#8702) Thanks @itscheems.
- 🚪 **Home now opens straight into the real project.** Send an idea from Home and the project is already there: one steady workspace, one Working state, and no disappearing first message while creation or uploads catch up. (#8267) Thanks @Siri-Ray.
- 🎬 **Motion keeps its rhythm.** Video-motion previews stop jumping through music when the browser hiccups; while a video is still being made, you can watch the picture without unexpected sound, then hear the finished result normally. (#8777) Thanks to the Open Design crew.

## ✨ Added

### 🎨 Studio, prototypes and media

- **Use your organisation's image sources without a key hunt.** Open Design can use configured company stock sources while retaining source information and keeping credits out of the finished page unless you ask for them. (#8691)
- **Chinese community help now leads to Feishu.** Simplified and Traditional Chinese entry points point to the official Feishu community, while other locales continue to use Discord. (#8884) Thanks @joeylee12629-star.

### 🧠 Agents, workspaces and CLI

- **Your MCP tools follow the workspace you selected.** Switch workspaces, reconnect, and the bridge now sees the projects and artifacts you actually have open. (#7619) Thanks @roian6.

## ⚡ Performance

- **Spend less time waiting for a Motion export.** Desktop video capture is faster while preserving the requested frame size, frame rate, and image quality. (#8798) Thanks @PerishCode.

## 🐛 Fixed

### 🧩 Home and projects

- **Task choices and the More menu feel like Home again.** The task-type controls, cancellation behaviour, compact-window layout, and keyboard navigation are back where your draft can rely on them. (#8947)
- **Artifact actions stay visible in chat.** Project conversations keep the familiar action styling for generated artifacts, and Home no longer surfaces the obsolete plugin hover card. (#8978, #8911) Thanks @alchemistklk.
- **Finished work stays finished.** A brief history lookup failure no longer turns an existing delivered run into a failure when you reopen the project. (#8804)

### 🎞️ Preview and sharing

- **Keep commenting while the preview changes.** A saved artifact can refresh with a comment draft open; a missing target asks for reselection instead of throwing the draft away. (#8904) Thanks @alchemistklk.
- **An existing shared file keeps its identity.** If local share bookkeeping is missing, Open Design recovers a verified cloud file and its original link rather than silently minting a replacement. (#8859, #8867) Thanks @alchemistklk.

## 🙏 Thanks to everyone who shipped 0.26.1

@alchemistklk · @itscheems · @roian6 · @Siri-Ray · @PerishCode · @joeylee12629-star

---

## 中文

全新 Skill Discovery，从你的创作意图出发，发现并选用合适的 Skill。少一些手动配置，从第一个想法到下一轮修改，让创作更贴近你想要的结果。

说出你想做什么，让 Open Design 更懂得如何开始。0.26.1 带来 **Skill Discovery：理解你想创作的作品类型，选择对应 Skill，并在后续修改中延续创作方向。**从开始创作前的能力选择，到作品生成后的继续打磨，你可以把更多注意力留给想法本身。更顺畅的项目启动、分享反馈和预览体验，也让整个创作过程更加连贯。

📥 [下载正式版安装包](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/releases/tag/open-design-v0.26.1#assets)

## 🧠 Skill Discovery：更懂你的想法，也更懂该用什么能力

描述你想要的结果，**Skill Discovery 会识别作品类型，选择并读取对应的原生 Skill 指引**，让 Open Design 带着适合这类任务的方法开始创作。目前覆盖 11 类交付物，包括交互原型、动效等创作场景。 (#8804)

- **从你的意图出发。** 当明确需求与手动选择的任务类型不一致时，优先尊重你说出的需求；你提到的 Skill 和模板会作为相容的指导与参考，让创作围绕你真正想要的作品展开。
- **让合适的能力参与创作。** 根据作品类型读取对应 Skill 的具体指引，减少你在开始前查找、选择技能的操作。
- **继续修改，延续创作方向。** 继续修改时，沿用已选 Skill 的创作指导，保持前后连贯。你只想讨论方案或澄清需求时，也会尊重这个阶段的意图，不擅自开始制作。

## 🔥 重点更新

- 🔗 **分享作品，而不是一堆截图。** 把设计文件发布为一个公开链接；评审结束时停止分享，需要继续时仍沿用同一个链接。公开页面上的评论会同步回文件，未读反馈就在你工作的地方等你处理。 (#8408、#8859、#8867、#8904) 感谢 @alchemistklk。
- 🤖 **带上自己的连接，把 Agent 留在流程里。** Open Design 可以使用已注册且可用的运行时；同一套 BYOK 连接既能在应用中使用，也能通过 `od` CLI 使用。即使两个项目用了相同的浏览器存储键，预览状态也各自独立。 (#8702) 感谢 @itscheems。
- 🚪 **从 Home 发送，直接进入真实项目。** 从 Home 发出想法后，项目工作区立即就位：只有一个稳定的界面、一个 Working 状态；创建或上传较慢时，第一条消息也不会消失。 (#8267) 感谢 @Siri-Ray。
- 🎬 **动效预览终于跟得上节奏。** 浏览器短暂卡顿时，视频动效不会反复跳音；生成期间可以看画面而不会意外出声，完成后仍可正常听到成片声音。 (#8777) 感谢 Open Design 团队。

## ✨ 新增

### 🎨 工作台、原型与素材

- **使用团队素材库，不必再找 Key。** Open Design 可以使用已配置的公司素材来源，保留来源信息；除非你明确要求，成品页面不会出现署名。 (#8691)
- **中文社区入口现在前往飞书。** 简体中文和繁体中文的入口会打开官方飞书社区，其他语言继续使用 Discord。 (#8884) 感谢 @joeylee12629-star。

### 🧠 Agent、工作区与 CLI

- **MCP 会跟随你正在使用的工作区。** 切换工作区并重新连接后，工具看到的是当前项目和产物，不再误落到其他工作区。 (#7619) 感谢 @roian6。

## ⚡ 性能

- **少等一会儿动效导出。** 桌面端视频抓帧更快，同时保持请求的分辨率、帧率和画面质量。 (#8798) 感谢 @PerishCode。

## 🐛 修复

niri-wm/niri:
Niri is a scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor. Windows are arranged in columns on an infinite strip going to the right. Opening a new window never causes existing windows to resize. As you may have noticed, niri now lives in a [GitHub org](https://github.com/niri-wm) rather than my (@YaLTeR) personal account. The primary reason was the ability to give out issue triage permissions: I'd like to give a **massive thanks** to @Sempyos for triaging *all* of our issues and pull requests, answering many, many questions, and helping people diagnose their problems with niri. We've also moved a few niri-adjacent projects to the GitHub org, like the [awesome-niri](https://github.com/niri-wm/awesome-niri) list of related projects maintained by @Vortriz and a new [artwork](https://github.com/niri-wm/artwork) repo by @bluelinden and @HumpityDumpityDumber—two of the creators of our project logo. In the artwork repo, you can find a badge and several [wallpapers](https://github.com/niri-wm/artwork/tree/main/wallpapers), including two stunning 3D works created by @Duncan-Rose in Blender: | pool | cut | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/niri-wm/artwork/blob/main/wallpapers/Niri%20pool.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/niri-wm/artwork/blob/main/wallpapers/Niri%20cut.png?raw=true) | The main niri repo also flew past 20,000 stars in February! 🌟 Thanks everyone for support. > [!NOTE] > Packagers: > - our minimum supported Rust version is now 1.85. > - `niri.service` no longer hardcodes `/usr/bin/` in the niri binary path (thanks @Axlefublr). > - @markK24 restructured the dinit service files: https://github.com/niri-wm/niri/commit/3bfa4a71ffb4457ce092454dfad6938f70028c28 Now with introductions out of the way, here are the improvements from the last release. ## Blur It's here. The most requested niri feature by far. Our highest upvoted issue on GitHub. After tireless fork maintenance by @visualglitch91 and @Naxdy, blur is in mainline niri for everyone to use! Windows and layer-shell components can request blur through the [`ext-background-effect`](https://wayland.app/protocols/ext-background-effect-v1) Wayland protocol with no extra niri configuration. Many already do: - [Dank Material Shell](https://danklinux.com/) v1.4.5: enable background blur [in settings](https://danklinux.com/docs/dankmaterialshell/compositor-blur) - [Noctalia](https://noctalia.dev/) shell: enable in settings and [see docs](https://docs.noctalia.dev/getting-started/compositor-settings/niri/#blur) - [Vicinae](https://vicinae.com/) launcher - [foot](https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot/) terminal v1.26: set `blur=true` in colors config - [kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/) terminal v0.46.2: set `background_blur 1` - [Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/) terminal: will have support in v1.4 Toolkits: - [Quickshell](https://quickshell.org/): will have support in v0.3 - [winit](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit): will have support in v0.31 For apps that don't support `ext-background-effect` yet, you can enable blur through the niri config: ```kdl // Enable blur behind the Alacritty terminal. window-rule { match app-id="^Alacritty$" background-effect { blur true } } // Enable blur behind the fuzzel launcher. layer-rule { match namespace="^launcher$" background-effect { blur true } } ``` Keep in mind that niri-configured blur needs the right [`geometry-corner-radius`](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Configuration%3A-Window-Rules.html#geometry-corner-radius), and it won't work with complex surface shapes. See the [Window Effects](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Window-Effects.html) wiki page for details.

Have I seen this screenshot before?..

We have both normal blur and xray blur that always shows the wallpaper. Xray blur is the default because it's much more efficient: niri computes the blurred wallpaper once, and then reuses it as a static image, which is extremely cheap. Only if the wallpaper changes, the blur is recomputed (so an animated background will shrink the efficiency gains). If you prefer non-xray (normal) blur, you can enable it with a window/layer rule. For example, you can set it on top and overlay layers (that usually overlap other content), via the new `layer` matcher: ```kdl // Make top and overlay layers use the regular blur (if enabled), // while bottom and background layers keep using the efficient xray blur. layer-rule { match layer="top" match layer="overlay" background-effect { xray false } } ``` So, if blur is so good, where's blur 2? Err, I mean, why did it take so long to add? In short, background blur turned out to be a massive undertaking. Not because of the blur algorithm itself (by the way, if you want to learn about different blurs, including the widely used Dual Kawase, I highly recommend [this blog post](https://blog.frost.kiwi/dual-kawase/)), but because window background effects in general required a lot of thinking and additions to the code, especially to make them as efficient as possible. This is one of the most complex niri features thus far. Xray and non-xray effects are also pretty much two *entirely separate* and very different beasts, code-wise. Non-xray reads back the just-rendered pixels in the middle of a frame, blurs them, then continues drawing the frame. This required extensive refactors of Smithay's rendering architecture (big thanks to @Drakulix!). Xray on the other hand requires threading the window positions all throughout the rendering code to draw the right cut-out of the background. But it gets worse: we have our [Overview](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Overview.html). It was quite a challenge figuring out how to support xray blur in the overview, while maintaining the property that it is never re-rendered. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5b18398-04a2-4af5-8440-15ce3b4bd87a I also had to get both of them working with all other niri features, like [blocking out from screencasts](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Screencasting.html#block-out-windows). When the window itself is blocked out that's easy, but what if something *in the background layer*, inside the blur, is blocked out? An unusual case for sure, but hardly a good exclude if your sensitive data gets accidentally leaked. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71980240-eda0-48de-80ad-dae06b6aa4b4 By the way, I made it so xray can be used on its own, without the blur. As well as the noise and saturation effects (normally for reducing blur color banding and bumping the vividness). For example: ```kdl window-rule { match app-id="Alacritty" // Xray without the blur! background-effect { xray true } } ``` One more thing you can do starting from this release is to configure niri to apply transparency and background effects to pop-up menus, using the new `popups` block in [window](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Configuration%3A-Window-Rules.html#popups) or [layer](https://niri-wm.github.io/niri/Configuration%3A-Layer-Rules.html#popups) rules. ```kdl // Blur the background behind pop-up menus in Loupe. window-rule { match app-id="Loupe" popups { // Matches the default libadwaita pop-up corner radius. geometry-corner-radius 15 // Note: it'll look better to set background opacity // through your GTK theme CSS and not here. // This is just an example that makes it look obvious. opacity 0.5 background-effect { blur true } } } ``` Keep in mind that pop-up rules tend to bump even more into problems with application behavior and surface shapes. For example, web apps or Electron don't use Wayland pop-ups at all; they're entirely emulated inside the client—niri cannot do anything with them. Shape-wise, in GTK 4, pop-ups with `has-arrow=true` won't look right because they aren't rounded rectangles. Thankfully, clients implementing `ext-background-effect` can shape their blur [in any sort of elaborate pattern](https://mastodon.online/@YaLTeR/116375472874381064). Well, enough about blur, we've got more interesting things to cover!
