pathwaycom/pathway:
### Added
- `pw.io.chroma.write` writes a Pathway table to a [Chroma](https://www.trychroma.com/) collection, keeping the collection in sync with the table as rows are added, changed, and removed. The columns are mapped onto Chroma's record fields explicitly: the optional `primary_key` becomes the record id (when omitted, the row's internal Pathway key is used instead), `embedding` the vector, the optional `document` column the stored text, and `metadata_columns` the record metadata. The collection must already exist. The server is addressed with `host`/`port` (plus `ssl`, `headers`, `tenant`, and `database` for authenticated deployments such as Chroma Cloud).
- `pw.io.qdrant.write` writes a Pathway table to a [Qdrant](https://qdrant.tech/) collection. Each row addition is upserted as a point and each deletion removes the corresponding point, so an update replaces a point rather than duplicating it. The pre-created collection's schema drives the writing: every named vector slot of the collection is bound to the table column with the same name — dense slots to `list[float]` (or 1-D `numpy.ndarray`) columns, sparse slots to `list[tuple[int, float]]` columns of `(index, weight)` pairs — and all vectors of a point are written atomically in one upsert, enabling native hybrid (dense + BM25) search. The remaining columns are stored in the point payload. The connector fails fast on a missing collection or any slot/column mismatch instead of degrading silently. The `batch_size` parameter bounds how many points are sent per request, and an optional `api_key` authenticates against Qdrant Cloud or a secured instance.
- `pw.io.duckdb.write` writes a Pathway table into a DuckDB database file through a native, in-process connector, in either `"stream_of_changes"` or `"snapshot"` mode. Embeddings stored as `numpy` arrays or `list[float]` columns land in native `DOUBLE[]` list columns, so the result is directly searchable with DuckDB's vector-distance functions for RAG retrieval. The `detach_between_batches` option makes the writer close the database after every minibatch commit and reopen it for the next one, releasing the file lock in between — so a separate process (e.g. a query server) can read committed data with short-lived read-only connections while the pipeline keeps running; the writer retries the reopen with a backoff when a reader momentarily holds the lock.
- `pw.io.weaviate.write` writes a Pathway table to a [Weaviate](https://weaviate.io/) collection, keeping it in sync with the table: additions and updates upsert objects (keyed by a UUID derived from the required `primary_key`), and deletions remove them. An optional `vector` column is stored as the object's embedding; the remaining columns become object properties. The target collection must already exist. The connector writes in parallel across workers (`pathway spawn -n`), with `batch_size` and `concurrency` to tune throughput, and supports `api_key`/`headers` authentication for self-hosted and Weaviate Cloud deployments.
- `pw.io.pinecone.write` writes a Pathway table to a [Pinecone](https://www.pinecone.io/) index for use as a vector store in RAG pipelines. It keeps the index in sync with the current state of the table: a row is upserted under its record id and a row removed from the table is deleted from the index. By default the id is the table's internal row key (unique, and written in parallel across workers); pass a `primary_key` column to use your own ids instead, in which case the values must uniquely identify rows (a collision raises an error) and writing runs on a single worker. The `vector` column holds either a dense embedding (`list[float]` or a 1-D `numpy.ndarray`), written to a dense index, or a sparse vector (`list[tuple[int, float]]` of `(index, weight)` pairs), written to a sparse index — so a hybrid (dense + BM25) setup is two indexes fed by two `write()` calls off the same table, with the same record ids landing in both for client-side fusion. The remaining columns — or just those listed in `metadata_columns` — are stored as record metadata. Targets both Pinecone cloud and the local Pinecone emulator via the `host` parameter; the index must already exist, with a matching dimension for a dense one, and a mismatch between the index's kind and the column's type is reported at start-up.
- `pw.run` and `pw.run_all` accept a new `udf_cache_directory` parameter. When set, the memoization cache of non-deterministic UDFs (any `pw.udf` without `deterministic=True`, whose results are stored so that row deletions replay the originally produced values) is kept in SQLite files in the given directory instead of in memory, so the pipeline's memory usage no longer grows with the number of cached results. Note that on many systems `/tmp` is a RAM-backed `tmpfs` — point the cache directory at a real disk to actually save memory. The on-disk cache is a runtime working set, not a durability mechanism: persistence snapshots remain the source of truth on restart, the cache files are recreated on every run and removed on shutdown. The default (`None`, in-memory cache) is unchanged.
- `pw.io.s3.read`, `pw.io.s3.read_from_digital_ocean`, `pw.io.s3.read_from_wasabi`, `pw.io.minio.read`, `pw.io.pyfilesystem.read`, and `pw.xpacks.connectors.sharepoint.read` now support the `format="only_metadata"` option (already available in `pw.io.fs.read` and `pw.io.gdrive.read`). In this mode the connector tracks additions, modifications, and deletions of objects in the source but does not download their contents — the resulting table contains only the `_metadata` column. This is useful for monitoring changes in large buckets or directories without spending time and traffic on fetching the objects themselves. For S3 and MinIO this also skips the object downloads entirely at the engine level, not just the parsing of their contents.
- Promoted `TwelveLabsVideoParser` and `MarengoEmbedder` out of the Video RAG example template and into the native `pathway.xpacks.llm` core library. You can now build Video RAG applications directly in Pathway by installing `pip install pathway[twelvelabs]`. The parser processes videos concurrently on an async executor and accepts the `capacity`, `retry_strategy`, `async_mode`, `video_format` and `on_error` parameters (`on_error="skip"` lets the pipeline continue when a single video fails to parse); oversized videos are rejected before the upload. `TwelveLabsVideoParser` requires a license key with the `advanced-parser` entitlement.

### Changed
- **BREAKING**: `pw.io.airbyte.read` replaced the `refresh_interval_ms` parameter (milliseconds) with `refresh_interval`, which takes a number of seconds or a `datetime.timedelta` / `pw.Duration` and defaults to 60 seconds (equal to the previous default of 60000 ms). Passing `refresh_interval_ms` now raises an error that includes the converted value to use. Migration: replace `refresh_interval_ms=60000` with `refresh_interval=60` (or `refresh_interval=datetime.timedelta(seconds=60)`).
- Duration parameters of connectors and xpack components now uniformly accept a number of seconds (`int` or `float`) or a `datetime.timedelta` / `pw.Duration`. This covers `refresh_interval` in `pw.io.gdrive.read`, `pw.io.pyfilesystem.read`, `pw.xpacks.connectors.sharepoint.read` and `pw.io.airbyte.read`, `poll_interval` and `max_transaction_duration` in `pw.io.elasticsearch.read`, `quick_access_window`, `compression_frequency` and `retention_period` in `pw.io.deltalake.TableOptimizer`, `idle_duration` in `pw.io.SynchronizedColumn`, `asset_poll_interval` and `asset_timeout` in `TwelveLabsVideoParser`, and `timeout` in `DocumentStoreClient` and `RAGClient`. Plain numbers keep meaning seconds wherever they did before; the new public alias `pw.io.DurationLike` names the accepted type. Invalid durations (negative, non-finite, wrong type) are now rejected at call time with an error naming the parameter. A zero polling interval stays allowed and means polling as often as possible; timeout parameters (`asset_timeout`, client `timeout`) must be strictly positive. This also fixes `pw.io.pyfilesystem.read` rejecting an integer `refresh_interval` (e.g. `refresh_interval=30`).
- `pw.xpacks.connectors.sharepoint.read` now supports the `max_backlog_size` parameter, already available in the other input connectors. It limits the number of entries read from SharePoint and kept in processing at any moment, which helps to avoid memory spikes when the source emits a large initial burst of data.
- `pw.io.mongodb.write` now distributes writes across all workers when Pathway runs with several workers (`pathway spawn -n N`), so write throughput scales with the worker count up to the capacity of the target MongoDB/Atlas deployment. Each document is still written by a single worker, so the result is identical to a single-worker run. Output that requests a global `sort_by` order continues to run on a single worker, since that is required to preserve the order.
- `pw.io.fs.read` now reads in parallel when Pathway runs with several workers and persistence is not enabled. Each file is assigned to exactly one worker by a stable hash of its path, so the read scales with the number of workers instead of running on a single one. The assignment is deterministic across workers and processes, requiring no coordination between them. All files present at start-up are still delivered as a single minibatch at one shared timestamp across every worker, so stateful operators see the initial snapshot atomically rather than split across the parallel readers. When persistence is enabled, the read runs on a single worker to keep recovery exactly consistent.
- `pw.io.postgres.write` now streams each batch into PostgreSQL through the binary `COPY` protocol instead of issuing one `INSERT` per row, giving a large throughput improvement (up to ~100x) on bulk writes. Both output modes use it: stream-of-changes copies straight into the target, while snapshot mode stages each batch in a temporary table and merges it with a single set-based upsert/delete.
- `pw.io.mssql.write` now streams each batch into SQL Server through the native bulk-load protocol (`INSERT BULK`) instead of issuing one `INSERT`/`MERGE` per row, giving a large throughput improvement (roughly ~25x) on bulk writes. Stream-of-changes mode bulk-loads straight into the target table when it is safe to do so (the connector created the table and no column name needs quoting), otherwise it stages each batch in a temporary table and applies it with a single set-based `INSERT ... SELECT`; snapshot mode stages each batch and applies it with one set-based `MERGE`/`DELETE` upsert.
- `pw.io.mysql.write` no longer issues one `INSERT` per row; it now sends each batch in bulk, giving a large throughput improvement. At start-up the connector probes the server and picks the fastest write path it permits: when the server allows `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE` (the `local_infile` setting is on), batches stream through it — straight into the target in stream-of-changes mode, or via a temporary staging table merged with a single set-based upsert in snapshot mode; otherwise it falls back to chunked multi-row `INSERT` statements, which work against any reachable server. Both paths produce identical results and require no configuration change.

### Fixed
- Constructing a KNN index factory (`BruteForceKnnFactory`, `UsearchKnnFactory`, `LshKnnFactory`) with an `OpenAIEmbedder` no longer sends a request to the OpenAI API. To learn the vector size, the factory used to ask the embedder to embed `"."`, so building the dataflow graph required network access and a working API key, and a transient network failure aborted the whole pipeline before it started. For the known embedding models the dimension is now taken from a lookup table; the embedder is still queried for unknown models, and when an explicit `dimensions` parameter shortens the returned vectors.
- Errors raised inside `get_embedding_dimension` are no longer swallowed. When the call was made from a context with a running event loop (most notably a Jupyter notebook), the coroutine ran in a helper thread whose exception was discarded, so an API timeout surfaced as an unrelated `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` with the real cause only printed to stderr. The original exception is now re-raised to the caller.
- `pathway.xpacks.llm` (including `pathway.xpacks.llm.parsers` and `pathway.xpacks.llm.document_store`) imports again in an environment with only `pathway[xpack-llm]` installed. The module used to fail at import time with `ModuleNotFoundError` for `pdf2image` and `unstructured`, which belong to the `xpack-llm-docs` extra; these imports are lazy again, so parsers that need the missing packages fail only at construction, with an error naming the extra to install.
- `pw.io.nats.write` no longer loses messages or fails with a "too many requests" (429) error when writing to a JetStream stream at scale, especially with several workers (`pathway spawn -n N`). The JetStream writer used to fire every publish in a minibatch without waiting for acknowledgements, so a large batch — multiplied across workers publishing to the same stream — overwhelmed the server and most of the batch was dropped. The writer now bounds the number of un-acknowledged publishes in flight (applying backpressure) and retries transient failures with exponential backoff, so the whole batch is delivered.
- A failed run no longer leaves the failing input connector running in the background. When an input connector exhausts its error retries, the error is reported and `pw.run` raises — but the connector kept retrying and logging the same error inside the process indefinitely, which polluted logs and could destabilize subprocesses started afterwards. The connector now stops as soon as it reports the fatal error.
- `pw.io.mqtt.read` and `pw.io.mqtt.write` are now more robust: payloads larger than 10 KB are handled by default, the reader re-subscribes and rides out transient broker disconnects instead of stalling, and the writer no longer blocks the pipeline indefinitely when the broker keeps the connection alive but never confirms deliveries. Publish topics are also validated up front (empty or wildcard topics are rejected with a clear error).
- `pw.io.milvus.write` no longer intermittently fails with a "server unavailable" / "connect failed" error when pointed at a local `.db` file. The embedded local Milvus server reports itself as started before it actually accepts connections, so under load the first connection could lose the race against the server coming up; the connector now retries the initial connection until the local server is ready.
- `BedrockChat` now correctly routes `top_k` and other model-specific arguments to the AWS Converse API via `additionalModelRequestFields`.
- Improved concurrent write handling in pw.io.sqlite.write for SQLite databases. Writes to the same database file now produce deterministic output in multi-worker and multi-table setups.
- `pw.io.elasticsearch.write` no longer fails when a minibatch is big enough that its Elasticsearch `_bulk` request would exceed a server-side limit. The connector reads both the cluster's `http.max_content_length` (the `413 Request Entity Too Large` limit) and `indexing_pressure.memory.limit` (the `429 Too Many Requests` limit, which on a small-heap node trips well below 100 MB) at start-up, and splits the buffered documents across as many bulk requests as needed to stay under whichever is hit first — so large batches are still written in as few requests as possible instead of being rejected. (Both limits fall back to a conservative default if they cannot be read.)
- `pw.io.elasticsearch.write` now retries transient bulk failures with backoff instead of failing the run on the first hiccup. A whole-request rejection or an individual document failing with `429`/`503` (back-pressure / temporary unavailability) is retried — resending only the documents the server reports as not yet applied, so a retry never duplicates data — while deterministic per-document failures (e.g. a type-mismatched value rejected with `400`) are now logged and skipped rather than silently dropped.
- `pw.io.kafka.read` in `mode="static"` no longer intermittently reads zero rows (or fewer rows than were present) from a topic. The static reader subscribed to the topic and relied on a consumer-group rebalance to assign partitions before its first fetch; under load that assignment could fail to complete within the reader's polling budget, so the read finished having consumed nothing. The static reader now assigns its partitions explicitly and reads each up to the end offset captured at start-up, removing the consumer-group dependency entirely.
- Glob pattern filtering in KNN LSH has been optimized; a polynomial algorithm is used instead of exponential.
- `pw.io.airbyte.read` with `execution_type="local"` (venv method) no longer hangs indefinitely when the download of the connector package from PyPI stalls. Each `pip install` attempt now runs with a timeout and is retried, and a clear error is raised once all attempts fail. The connector package is also installed exactly once instead of three times, making the connector start-up faster.
- Pipelines with persistence enabled no longer intermittently lose the most recent input when a `pw.iterate` is present. The internal snapshot of the iterated state was written on a branch of the computation graph that no output depends on, so a checkpoint could be committed before those writes finished; after a restart the affected rows were neither replayed nor found in the snapshot, surfacing as "key missing in output table" errors. Checkpoint commits now wait for these writes. Additionally, tables passed to `pw.iterate` as extra (non-iterated) arguments are now included in the persisted state, so the iteration logic sees them correctly after a restart.
- Under `pw.PersistenceMode.OPERATOR_PERSISTING`, joins that preserve the left side's keys (`id=left.id`), including `join_left`, no longer misreport a row update arriving after a restart as a duplicate key. Previously the update was logged as a duplicate-key error and the affected row was replaced with an error value.
- With persistence enabled, a pipeline that is restarted more than once in quick succession no longer risks losing input rows. A restarted run could commit a checkpoint whose logical time fell into the previous (killed) run's range, accidentally certifying that run's partially-written state: the next restart then resumed from input offsets whose data was missing from the persisted operator state, so those rows were never replayed. Checkpoint commits are now clamped to the current run's own time range.
- With persistence enabled, data read right after a restart (new or modified files) now enters the computation at one shared timestamp across all input sources. Previously each source resumed on its own clock, and cross-source operators with key contracts (`.ix`, join with `id=...`, `with_universe_of`) could observe intermediate states, producing spurious "key missing" or duplicate-key errors on restart. When `autocommit_duration_ms=None` is set explicitly, the previous per-source behavior is kept, since there is no timer to close the shared start-up batch.
- Bumped the `beartype` dependency upper bound from `< 0.16.0` to `< 0.22.9` to allow installation with recent Beartype releases. Closes #243.

pnpm/pnpm:
This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it. - `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store. - `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#17402](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch. - Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#17422](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ## Platinum Sponsors

pocketbase/pocketbase:
> _To update the prebuilt executable you can run `./pocketbase update`._

- Replaced the GitHub update command with update from the new host in relation to [#7841](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/7841).
    ⚠️ Note that this will be most likely the last release here on GitHub. The next time when you run update, new releases will be fetched from `https://ganigeorgiev.com` _(there is nothing there yet)_.

- Additional fileblob bucket escape checks for just in case if the filesystem abstraction is used as standalone without the PocketBase validations.

- Added a global restriction for the max `WxH` pixels size when generating a thumb to reduce the risk of excessive memory usage.
    The issue was initially privately reported by @reload3d but it is treated as regular public issue since it is a [known Go caveat](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/27830).
    The default limit is pretty generous and currently set to max `250<<20 (262144000)` pixels and can be changed with the env `PB_THUMBS_MAX_SOURCE_PIXELS`.
    **The workaround is not bulletproof and thumbs generation remains one of the main culprit for potential OOMs in PocketBase**, so better solutions will have to be investigated in the future, including eventually switching to [libvips](https://github.com/libvips/libvips) or other similar library once there is [better CGO portability](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81450) _(if you have better suggestions, please open a discussion)_.

portainer/portainer:
## Known issues

- On Async Edge environments, an invalid update schedule date can be displayed when browsing a snapshot

### Known issues with Podman support

- Podman environments aren't supported by auto-onboarding script
- It's not possible to add Podman environments via socket, when running a Portainer server on Docker (and vice versa)
- Support for only CentOS 9, Podman 5 rootful

## Changes

### Breaking changes

- Portainer no longer trusts TLS certificates issued by eMudhra (emSign), following the compromise of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943). Connections to services that present an affected certificate, including OAuth/OIDC and LDAPS providers, registries and Git hosts, will fail after the upgrade. If your single sign-on or LDAP provider is affected, only the initial admin will be able to sign in. Check your services before upgrading. [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)

### Security improvements

- Rejected Compose and Swarm stacks using `volumes_from` when non-administrators create, update, start or redeploy them with `Hide bind mounts for non-administrators` enabled, which let them inherit another container's host bind mounts
- Updated the Go toolchain to 1.26.10, fixing CVE-2026-56857 and CVE-2026-78663 (both Critical), along with CVE-2026-111943, CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-97031, CVE-2026-94440, CVE-2026-94439, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-56866, CVE-2026-94448 and CVE-2026-97030
- Removed the eMudhra emSign root certificates from the CA bundle in Linux images, and rejected certificate chains that contain the compromised eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943). [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)
- Updated [golang.org/x/net](http://golang.org/x/net) to 0.60.0, fixing CVE-2026-78663 (Critical), CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78660 and CVE-2026-78659 (all High)
- Updated helm in the kubectl shell image to v4.3.1, taking its Go toolchain to 1.27.2 and oras.land/oras-go/v2 to 2.6.2, fixing CVE-2026-39821 (Critical) and CVE-2026-50163 (High)
- Restricted kubeconfig tokens to the /api/endpoints/{id}/kubernetes proxy, so they are rejected with a 403 on every other API route, including admin-only routes and the Docker proxy. Kubeconfigs downloaded after upgrading carry a separate token per environment, limited to that environment 

### Bug fixes

- Fixed starting a container with an empty request body failing with a 400 error on Docker standalone and Swarm agent environments 
- Fixed GitOps sources starting a new poll while the previous one was still running, which could pile up overlapping redeploys on slow repositories. A poll that is still running now causes the next scheduled poll to be skipped
- Fixed GitOps workflows showing the Git reference and file path status as unknown after a stack was manually redeployed from Git. A manual redeploy now records these statuses for the stack's workflow artifact
- Fixed the YAML tab on the Kubernetes node details page going blank after switching tabs or refocusing the browser, and restored the missing gap between the tab content and the Applications table
- Fixed DockerHub pull rate limits and agent version detection failing on Docker engines newer than API 1.47, and, in BE, non-admin users with environment access getting 403 errors on `/agent/docker` and `/agent/host` routes, which left Swarm node selectors empty
- Fixed the search box on the Authentication logs page not filtering events by username

## Deprecated and removed features

None.

psf/black:
### Highlights

This release fixes a security issue in Black's bundled GitHub Action. Repositories that
use the action are encouraged to update to the latest version of Black immediately. This
update is received automatically when using `psf/black@stable`, and is independent of
the version of Black installed by the action.

When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from `tool.black.required-version`, it
now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for `black` requirements
in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now rejected. This issue
has been registered as `GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2`; a CVE identifier is pending.

### Stable style

- Fix a long Jupyter notebook assignment magic (for example `x = !ls -la`) being wrapped
  in parentheses, which IPython can no longer run; such cells are now left unchanged
  (#5481)
- Keep repeated lines outside the selected `--line-ranges` unchanged (#5436)
- Fix `--line-ranges` formatting lines that follow a statement when formatting joins or
  re-indents that statement (#5484)
- Fix `--line-ranges` crashing with an internal error when an unselected statement has a
  `# fmt: skip` comment on the last line before a closing bracket (#5477)
- Prevent moving an encoding declaration (for example `# -*- coding: latin-1 -*-`) onto
  the first two lines of a file (#5487)
- Fix adding an extra trailing blank line inside a multi-line module docstring when its
  last line is near the line length limit (#5494)

### Preview style

- Do not split short expressions on delimiters (such as binary operators, comparisons,
  or comprehensions) inside brackets when preceded by a standalone comment (#5455)
- Fix the unstable `string_processing` feature removing backslash-newline sequences from
  raw strings, which changed their value (#5482)
- Avoid adding unnecessary parentheses around unbreakable right-hand side expressions in
  assignments (such as annotated assignments or subscript targets) (#5473)
- Parenthesize expressions with parameter comments when they exceed the line length
  under `--preview` (#5442)
- Fix `wrap_long_dict_values_in_parens` dropping the parentheses around a right-hand
  side that contains a dictionary, leaving a line over the length limit (#5492)
- Fix the unstable `string_processing` feature adding a space after `*` or `**` in a PEP
  695 type parameter (`* Ts = ...`) when it splits a string in the parameter's default
  (#5504)
- Avoid unnecessary line splits of trailers (such as indexing/subscripts) when an
  earlier bracket split exceeds the line length only due to a trailing comment (#5498)

### Configuration

- Add `--cache-dir` to configure the cache directory from the command line (#5433)
- Don't cache a file as formatted after formatting or checking it with `--line-ranges`,
  which made a later full `black --check` pass and `black` skip the unformatted lines
  (#5476)
- Respect a `.gitignore` that starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark. The mark became part
  of the first pattern, so that pattern never matched and Black formatted files that git
  ignores (#5497)

### Performance

- Avoid quadratic runtime when splitting very long lines with many trailing bracket
  pairs (such as consecutive subscripts) (#5475)

### Integrations

- Fix the GitHub Action crashing on dependency-group includes when `use_pyproject` is
  enabled (#5479)
- When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from `tool.black.required-version`, it
  now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for `black`
  requirements in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now
  rejected. (#5510)

# PyTorch 2.15.0 Release Notes - [Highlights](#highlights) - [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes) - [Deprecations](#deprecations) - [New Features](#new-features) - [Improvements](#improvements) - [Bug fixes](#bug-fixes) - [Performance](#performance) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Security](#security) - [Developers](#developers) # Highlights
Rewritten NCCL backend becomes the default, with a flight recorder that dumps on hangs and TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or nccl-legacy as rollback paths
One-sided transports for torch.distributed, with a NIXL backend and CUDA-graph-capturable transfers
FSDP2 and pipelining gain finer memory and communication control, with fp32 for precision-sensitive parameters, CUDA-graph-captured gradient accumulation, and gradient reduction overlapped with compute
Faster 4-bit (NVFP4) LLM decoding on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs through fewer, better-overlapped kernel launches in NVGEMM
Apple Silicon gains FP8 and faster decode, with float8_e4m3fn and _scaled_mm, a new grouped_mm with a decode fast path (1.32–1.34x tokens/s on MoE decode), and public torch.mps.Stream APIs
Broader platform support with FlyDSL kernels on AMD gfx950, Tensor Data Mover support for gfx1250 (MI450), ROCm 10.0 wheels, simpler SYCL kernel authoring and multi-GPU profiling on Intel GPUs, CUDA 13.2 as the default wheel with CUDA 13.4 alongside it, and torch.compile on Python 3.15
For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release. # Backwards Incompatible Changes ## Python Frontend ### `import torch` can no longer be re-executed in the same process, including via `importlib.reload(torch)` (#194654) `importlib.reload(torch)` and `del sys.modules["torch"]` + re-import now raise, as does retrying `import torch` after it failed. Re-running the module body was already unsafe in exactly the same way as the retry, so the new check does not distinguish the two. Normal use is unaffected: a successful import leaves `torch` in `sys.modules` so the body never re-runs, and re-entrant imports from a backend extension during autoload still short-circuit on `sys.modules` without reaching the check. Version 2.14: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # RuntimeError: Only a single TORCH_LIBRARY can be used to register the namespace triton; ... # (re-importing after a failed `import torch` failed with similarly misleading errors or could segfault) ``` Version 2.15: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # ImportError: `torch` can only be initialized once per process, so this module cannot # be imported again: neither via `importlib.reload(torch)`, nor by re-importing after # a failed `import torch`. ``` ### Nested tensors are no longer allowlisted for `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` (#194380) Nested jagged and strided nested tensors are no longer on the default `weights_only` allowlist. Loading a checkpoint that contains one with `weights_only=True` (the default) now fails with `Unsupported global: GLOBAL torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor._rebuild_njt was not an allowed global by default` (or `GLOBAL torch._utils._rebuild_nested_tensor` for strided nested tensors). To load checkpoints containing nested tensors, allow them explicitly with `torch.serialization.safe_globals` (see below), or use `weights_only=False` for trusted files. Version 2.14: ```python loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) # works ``` Version 2.15: ```python from torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor import _rebuild_njt, NestedTensor with torch.serialization.safe_globals([_rebuild_njt, NestedTensor]): loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) ``` ### Operators called through `torch.ops.*` and `torch._C._dispatch_call_boxed` now use PyTorch's own warning and exception translation instead of pybind11's (#193451) We make `torch.ops.*` calls go through the same exception and warning translation as the rest of the library. This means that some exception translation that used to be handled by pybind is now handled natively. User-defined pybind exception translation is thus lost. Restoring it may be done in a future release as part of a broader exception handler improvement. In addition, `TORCH_WARN` warnings from these operators now reach Python's `warnings` module, so they raise when warnings are turned into errors (`-W error`). `std::out_of_range` still becomes `IndexError` (#195713). Version 2.14: ```python # C++ op: throw std::invalid_argument("bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: # pybind11 translation ... ``` Version 2.15: ```python # C++ op: TORCH_CHECK_VALUE(false, "bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: ... # TORCH_WARN from the op is now a Python warning with warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter("ignore") torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) ``` ## Autograd ### Selective activation checkpointing now saves, rather than recomputes, the outputs of operators with an ordered effect unless the policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` (#196956) In eager mode, if a `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts` policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE` for a non-aliasing operator with an ordered effect (e.g. via `register_effect(torch.library.EffectType.ORDERED)`), that choice is now overridden and its outputs are saved, so the side effect is no longer replayed during backward. This can increase activation memory. To keep the 2.14 behavior, return `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` for that operator. Operators in the `c10d` namespace are excluded. Under `torch.compile`, `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` on an effectful operator now raises at compile time: `RuntimeError: AOTAutograd does not support MUST_RECOMPUTE for effectful operations because forward effects cannot join the backward effect-token chain.` Use a save policy instead. ```python policy = lambda ctx, op, *args, **kwargs: CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE checkpoint(fn, x, use_reentrant=False, context_fn=lambda: create_selective_checkpoint_contexts(policy)) # 2.14: an effectful op in fn runs twice; 2.15: once (use CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE to replay) ``` ## Distributed (c10d) ### The `nccl` backend now uses a rewritten, cleaned-up NCCL implementation by default (#192281, #192895, #193237, #193241) `backend="nccl"` (also the default CUDA backend of `init_process_group()`) now creates the new implementation. The legacy implementation is available as `backend="nccl-legacy"` for this release only: **`nccl-legacy` and `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` will be removed in the next release**, so migrate to `nccl` or `nccl-lazy`. Use `nccl` (eager initialization) by default. Use `nccl-lazy` when you need independent point-to-point communicators: collectives run on one eagerly created communicator, and each send/recv peer pair gets its own lazily created communicator and stream, so concurrent P2P to different peers can overlap (as in the legacy backend). Differences from the legacy backend: - Communicators are created eagerly in `init_process_group()`/`new_group()`, allocating GPU memory even for unused groups. - Each group is bound to one CUDA device: `device_id`, else `LOCAL_RANK % torch.cuda.device_count()` (or the global rank modulo the device count); `torch.cuda.set_device()` is not used. Tensors on another GPU fail with `Expected tensor on cuda:X but found tensor on cuda:Y` or `ProcessGroupNCCL is bound to device cuda:X but an operation was issued on cuda:Y`. Pass `device_id` if needed; several GPUs per process requires `nccl-legacy`. - `dist.get_backend_impl(...)` returns the new backend class, so `isinstance(..., ProcessGroupNCCL)` is `False` and legacy-only methods such as `comm_split_count()` are missing. - An async `all_gather`'s `work.get_future()` value is the list of per-rank outputs, not a one-element list holding a stacked tensor; read the output list passed to `all_gather` instead (works on both backends). To temporarily restore the legacy behavior in 2.15, set `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` on every rank before creating the process group, or use `nccl-legacy`: Version 2.14: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl") # ProcessGroupNCCL ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # new implementation dist.init_process_group("nccl-lazy", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # independent P2P communicators dist.init_process_group("nccl-legacy") # legacy implementation, removed in the next release ``` ## Distributed Checkpointing ### Distributed checkpoint metadata now records tensor strides, so checkpoints saved with PyTorch 2.15 cannot be loaded by PyTorch 2.14 or earlier (#194251) `TensorProperties` gains an optional `strides` field in the pickled `.metadata` file. In older versions `dcp.load` raises a `CheckpointException` reporting `too many values to unpack (expected 5)`. There is no flag to write the old format. Version 2.14 (loading a 2.15 checkpoint): ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # CheckpointException: ... too many values to unpack (expected 5) ``` Version 2.15: ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # loads 2.14 and 2.15 checkpoints ``` ## Distributed FSDP2 ### With `MixedPrecisionPolicy(reduce_dtype=None)`, `fully_shard` now accumulates and reduces gradients in the parameter's `grad_dtype` (its original dtype by default) instead of in `param_dtype` (#194434) **This is BC-breaking**: `mp_policy.reduce_dtype=None` no longer defaults to `mp_policy.param_dtype`. * [popular case] fp32 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=bf16)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 (2x reduce-scatter bytes) * [rare case] bf16 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=fp32)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 How to deal with BC: explicitly set `mp_policy.reduce_dtype`. In grad accumulation (no reduce-scatter), the unsharded param's `.grad` always holds the accumulated value, visible via `model.parameters()` while unsharded. Before this change, `.grad` was `None` when `reduce_dtype` was set and differed from `param_dtype` (FSDP kept the sum in a hidden `reduce_dtype` buffer). Version 2.14: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in bf16 ``` Version 2.15: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in fp32 # to keep the 2.14 behavior, set reduce_dtype explicitly mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16, reduce_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) ``` ## Distributed Pipelining ### `torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p` is renamed to `pipeline_per_edge_p2p` and now uses one communicator per directed rank-to-rank edge (#196666) The old names were removed with no alias: setting the attribute raises `AttributeError: torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p does not exist`, and `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_DIRECTION_P2P` is silently ignored. Version 2.14: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_edge_p2p = True # or TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_EDGE_P2P=1 ``` ## Profiler ### C++ stack traces are now symbolized with `dladdr` instead of `addr2line` by default (#195462) `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE` now defaults to on, since `addr2line` is slow and can hang. C++ frames in `TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1` errors and CUDA memory snapshots now show the library path and offset, plus the symbol name only if exported (otherwise `??`). To restore `addr2line`, set `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0` or `TORCH_SYMBOLIZE_MODE=addr2line`. ```bash TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1 TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0 python train.py ``` ### CUDA memory snapshots record the allocator's `mallocWithAddress` tag in a new `internal_metadata` field instead of appending it to `user_metadata` (#193432) `user_metadata` in `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` trace entries is now exactly what was set with `torch.cuda.memory._set_memory_metadata` (which now also accepts a dict). Tools that searched `user_metadata` for `mallocWithAddress` must read `internal_metadata` instead. ```python # 2.14 tagged = [e for e in trace if "mallocWithAddress" in e["user_metadata"]] # 2.15 tagged = [e for e in trace if e.get("internal_metadata") == "mallocWithAddress"] ``` ### Remove the deprecated `FunctionEvent.metadata_json` property (#198265) Accessing it now raises `AttributeError: 'FunctionEvent' object has no attribute 'metadata_json'`, and the `metadata_json` constructor argument is removed. Use `FunctionEvent.metadata`, a dict populated when `_ExperimentalConfig(expose_kineto_event_metadata=True)` is set (not the deprecated `event_metadata`). ```python metadata = event.metadata_json # 2.14: JSON string metadata = event.metadata # 2.15: dict[str, Any] or None ``` ### Rename the experimental CUPTI monitor profiler backend to Cuspy, without aliases for the old names (#195881) In `_ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config=...)`, `"cupti_monitor"` is now `"cuspy"` and `"cupti_monitor_async_export"` is now `"cuspy_async_export"`; old names silently fall back to the default Kineto backend. `prof.take_pending_cupti_export()` is now `take_pending_cuspy_export()` (the old name raises `AttributeError`). Prefer the new `torch.profiler.CuspyConfig`. ```python # 2.14 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cupti_monitor"}') # 2.15 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cuspy"}') ``` ## Dynamo ### Higher-order ops now reject input mutation and aliasing in their bodies unless the op opts in (#185738) Before, Dynamo let any higher-order op body mutate or alias its inputs by default. Ops that do not implement those semantics could silently produce invalid graphs. Mutation and aliasing are now off by default. The built-in wrappers that support them (`wrap`, checkpoint, `autograd.Function`, autocast/set-grad wrappers) opt in. A `flex_attention` `mask_mod` may read captured views but must not mutate inputs or return aliases. Under `fullgraph=True`, unsupported mutation or aliasing raises `Encountered input mutation during higher order op tracing` or `Encountered aliasing during higher order op tracing`; otherwise, Dynamo graph breaks and falls back to eager execution. Rewrite the higher-order op body to avoid mutation or aliasing. For example, rewrite an in-place `flex_attention` score modifier as an out-of-place operation: Version 2.14: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): score.add_(1) return score.clone() ``` Version 2.15: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): return score + 1 ``` ## Inductor ### `torch.compiler.nested_compile_region(options=...)` now accepts only an allowlist of Inductor config patches (#195864, #195865) Patches passed through `get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches=..., bw_inductor_config_patches=...)` used to accept any `torch._inductor.config` key, though many were silently ignored. Only `fallback_by_default` and `max_autotune` are now accepted; other keys raise `ValueError: Inductor config key '' is not supported in forward nested compile-region options` (or `backward`). Apply other options to the whole compiled function. Patch dictionaries are now snapshotted when the options are created, so later mutation has no effect, and the default no longer implicitly sets `triton.autotune_at_compile_time=True`. Version 2.14: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` Version 2.15: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"max_autotune": True}) compiled = torch.compile(fn, options={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` ### `torch.compiler.precompile` is now a module instead of a callable; capture with `torch.compiler.precompile.capture(...)` and reload with `torch.compiler.precompile.load(...)` (#197993, #198135, #198213) Calling `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` now raises `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable`. `capture(fn, *, artifact_path, cache_path)` returns a context manager that you call once inside the `with` block; it writes both files when the block exits cleanly (or on `cap.save()`), and `load` now takes those paths. `decompositions=` moves to `tracer=MakeFxTracer(decompositions=...)`. Version 2.14: ```python python_code, cache = torch.compiler.precompile(lambda m, x: m(x), model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load(python_code, cache) ``` Version 2.15: ```python with torch.compiler.precompile.capture(lambda m, x: m(x), artifact_path="m.py", cache_path="m.cache") as cap: cap(model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache") ``` ## Composability ### Under functionalization, a regenerated output of `split`, `split_with_sizes` or `unbind` is now rebuilt as a single `slice` or `select` of its base, so its `grad_fn` is `SliceBackward0`/`SelectBackward0` instead of `SplitBackward0`/`SplitWithSizesBackward0`/`UnbindBackward0` (#194037) This greatly reduces compile time for code that mutates many `split()` views (for example 32s to 15s with 128 views). Gradients are unchanged, but the in-place error now names the new op with output index 0: `RuntimeError: Output 0 of Select is a view and is being modified inplace.` Code that inspects `grad_fn` names, matches the old error text, or pattern-matches `split`/`unbind` nodes in functionalized graphs needs updating. There is no option to restore the previous behavior. Version 2.14: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) # f returns base.unbind(0)[1] after base.add_(1) >>> out.grad_fn ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) >>> out.grad_fn ``` ## Release Engineering ### PyPI wheels now ship with CUDA 13.2, and CUDA 12.6 and CUDA 13.0 wheels are no longer published (#196249, #198913) The default PyPI wheel moves from CUDA 13.0 to CUDA 13.2. The 2.15 wheels are `cu132` and `cu134`; `cu126` and `cu130` are no longer built. CUDA 13 wheels need NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and a GPU of Turing (`sm_75`) or newer, so Maxwell, Pascal and Volta GPUs and hosts with a CUDA 12.x driver should stay on 2.14. Version 2.15: ```bash # PyPI wheel now uses CUDA 13.2 pip install torch # CUDA 13.4 wheels pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu134 # To stay on CUDA 12.6 or CUDA 13.0, pin PyTorch 2.14: pip install torch==2.14.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126 # or cu130 ``` ### Python 3.10 wheels are no longer published (#198233, #199398) PyTorch 2.15 raises the minimum supported Python version for binaries to 3.11: no `cp310` wheels are built for `torch` or the Triton wheels, and CI no longer tests on Python 3.10. On Python 3.10, `pip` cannot find a 2.15 wheel. Upgrade to Python 3.11 or newer, or stay on PyTorch 2.14. Version 2.14: ```bash python3.10 -m pip install torch # cp310 wheel available ``` Version 2.15: ```bash python3.11 -m pip install torch==2.15.0 # Python 3.11 through 3.15 (including 3.14t and 3.15t) ``` ### ROCm wheels move to ROCm 7.14 and 10.0; ROCm 7.2 wheels and gfx900/gfx906 kernels are dropped (#194919) gfx900 (MI25) and gfx906 (MI50/MI60, Radeon VII) users can stay on 2.14 (`rocm7.2`) or build from source with those targets in `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH`. ```bash pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.14 # or rocm10.0 ``` ### Linux CUDA wheels no longer depend on the cuRAND library (#194850) PyTorch only uses the cuRAND device API, so `torch` no longer links `libcurand`, no longer preloads it on `import torch`, and the wheel's CUDA requirements no longer include cuRAND. Extensions or libraries that call the cuRAND host API (for example `curandCreateGenerator`) and relied on `pip install torch` bringing in the cuRAND library can fail to load `libcurand.so` and must now install it themselves. Version 2.15: ```bash pip install torch pip install "cuda-toolkit[curand]==13.2.2" # match the toolkit version of your wheel ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.histc(..., out=...)` on CUDA now raises an error when `out` does not have the same dtype as the input (#196100) CUDA used to silently cast into any `out` dtype. It now matches CPU and MPS and rejects mismatches, even widening ones. Compute without `out` and cast instead. Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0, out=int64_out) # silently truncated ``` Version 2.15: ```python RuntimeError: torch.histogram: input tensor and hist tensor should have the same dtype, but got input float and hist long int >>> int64_out.copy_(torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0)) # workaround ``` ### On CUDA, cuBLAS and cuBLASLt workspaces are now allocated for each operation instead of being cached per handle and stream (#194311) Graphs captured separately on one stream could share the cached workspace and fail on replay with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Workspaces are now freed after each op, so `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` excludes them and the handle from `torch.cuda.current_blas_handle()` has no ATen workspace attached. Set `TORCH_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CACHE=1` to restore caching (unsafe with multiple graphs on one stream). `TORCH_CUBLASLT_UNIFIED_WORKSPACE` now only takes effect with caching enabled. ROCm has a matching change (#196920). Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.mm(a, a, out=out) >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before > 0 # workspace stays allocated True ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before # freed after the op 0 ``` ## CPU (AArch64) ### Float32 `torch.sin` and `torch.cos` on Arm CPUs (NEON and SVE) now use SLEEF's 3.5-ULP kernels instead of the 1.0-ULP kernels, matching the accuracy of the x86 AVX2 implementation and running 1.7x-2.4x faster on Neoverse V1/V2 (#196315) Float32 `sin` and `cos` results on Arm can now differ from earlier releases in the last bits. Bit-for-bit comparisons against stored golden outputs, `torch.equal`, or `torch.testing.assert_close` with `rtol=0, atol=0` may fail; default `assert_close` tolerances are unaffected. There is no switch to restore the previous kernels; if you need tighter accuracy, compute in float64 and cast back. Version 2.14: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 1 ULP ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 2 ULP >>> x.double().cos().float() # workaround: correctly rounded ``` ## MPS ### The MPS backend now requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer (#199261, #200290) macOS 14 has reached end of life, so its MPS workarounds were removed. On macOS 14, `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` returns `False` and allocating on `mps` raises the error below. To keep using MPS, stay on PyTorch 2.14 or upgrade macOS; CPU builds still run on older macOS. C++ extensions: `at::mps::MacOSVersion::MACOS_14_4` was removed. ```python >>> torch.ones(2, device="mps") # 2.15 on macOS 14 RuntimeError: The MPS backend is supported on macOS 15.0+. Current OS version can be queried using `sw_vers` ``` ## XPU ### Remove the `allocator` property from `torch.xpu.MemPool`, aligning with other accelerators (#192041) `torch.xpu.MemPool` no longer exposes the allocator it was constructed with, so `pool.allocator` now raises `AttributeError`. Keep your own reference to the allocator instead; passing one to the `MemPool` constructor is unchanged. Before: ```python pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(allocator.allocator()) my_allocator = pool.allocator ``` After: ```python my_allocator = allocator.allocator() pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(my_allocator) ``` ## Complex Frontend ### Ops that are undefined for complex inputs now raise `TypeError` instead of `RuntimeError` (#192350) This covers order-dependent ops (`sort`, `argsort`, `topk`, `argmax`/`argmin`, `max`/`min` with `dim`, `maximum`/`minimum`, `fmax`/`fmin`, `aminmax`), `isposinf`/`isneginf`, `view_as_real`/`imag` on real tensors, and `view_as_complex` on complex tensors, matching Python (`1j < 2j` is a `TypeError`). `except RuntimeError:` no longer catches these; catch `(RuntimeError, TypeError)`. Ops not yet implemented for a dtype (e.g. `rad2deg`, `nansum`, `heaviside` on complex, `topk`/`argmax` on bool) now raise `NotImplementedError`, which `except RuntimeError:` still catches. Full `max()`/`min()`/`amax`/`amin` are unchanged. ```python torch.sort(torch.randn(3, dtype=torch.cfloat)) # 2.14: RuntimeError: Sort does not support complex dtypes on CPU # 2.15: TypeError: Sort does not support complex dtypes on CPU ``` # Deprecations ## Optimizer ### Passing a bare `set` of parameters to an optimizer is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning`; it will become an error in a future release (#198710) Set iteration order can change between runs, so optimizer state could silently mismatch parameters on reload. The warning reads: `optimizer parameters need to be organized in ordered collections, but the ordering of tensors in sets will change between runs. Please use a list instead.` ```python opt = torch.optim.Adam(set(model.parameters())) # 2.15: FutureWarning opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(model.parameters())) # recommended ``` ## Linear Algebra Frontend ### MAGMA is deprecated for LU factorization with pivoting on CUDA: `torch.linalg.lu_factor`, `torch.linalg.lu`, and the ops that use it internally (`torch.linalg.solve`, `torch.linalg.inv`, `torch.linalg.det`, `torch.linalg.slogdet`) now always use cuSOLVER (#190661) This only affects code that sets `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("magma")`: pivoted LU now uses cuSOLVER anyway; a new built-in batched LU kernel replaces MAGMA's for large batches. When MAGMA is preferred, the first call warns: `linalg.lu_factor: MAGMA, as a linear algebra backend, is deprecated and will be removed in future releases.` `pivot=False` still uses MAGMA when it is preferred. To avoid the warning, use the default or cuSOLVER backend. ```python torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("magma") LU, pivots = torch.linalg.lu_factor(A) # 2.14: MAGMA; 2.15: cuSOLVER + UserWarning torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("default") # recommended ``` ## Profiler ### `torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof`, `parse_nvprof_trace` and `EnforceUnique` are deprecated and will be removed in PyTorch 2.17 (#198396) `nvprof` does not support recent GPUs. They now emit a `FutureWarning` such as `` `torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof` is deprecated and will be removed in PyTorch 2.17. `` Use `torch.profiler.profile` or Nsight Systems with `torch.autograd.profiler.emit_nvtx()`. ```python events = torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof("trace.prof") # 2.14 with torch.profiler.profile() as prof: # 2.15 run_workload() ``` ### `FunctionEvent.event_metadata` is deprecated in favor of `FunctionEvent.metadata` (#198405) `metadata` is a typed `dict[str, Any]` with everything `event_metadata` had. Accessing `event_metadata` emits `FutureWarning: `event_metadata` is deprecated. Use `metadata` instead.` ```python grid = event.event_metadata.grid # 2.14 grid = event.metadata["grid"] # 2.15 ``` ## Inductor ### Deprecate `torch._inductor.config.triton.use_block_ptr` because Triton removed its block-pointer API (#191007) With a Triton that no longer provides block pointers, `use_block_ptr=True` is now a no-op that falls back to the default indexing path with a one-time `FutureWarning: config.triton.use_block_ptr=True but the installed Triton no longer provides the block-pointer frontend API`, instead of failing with `CompilationError: ... Block pointers have been removed in favor of the tensor descriptor API`. Use tensor descriptors instead. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.triton.use_block_ptr = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python torch._inductor.config.triton.use_tensor_descriptor = True ``` ### Deprecate the no-op `torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm` and `torch._inductor.config.mixed_mm_choice` settings (#193721) These settings have been ignored since the tuned `mixed_mm` path was removed. Reading or setting either now emits a one-time `FutureWarning` such as `torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm is deprecated and does not do anything`. `autoheuristic_collect.mixed_mm` and `autoheuristic_use.mixed_mm` were removed, and `"mixed_mm"` is no longer the `TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOHEURISTIC_USE` default. Delete these settings from your code. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm = True # silently ignored ``` Version 2.15: ```python # FutureWarning; delete the line ``` ### Rename `torch._inductor.config.benchmark_epilogue_fusion` to `benchmark_template_fusion` and `max_epilogue_benchmarked_choices` to `max_template_fusion_benchmarked_choices` (#198430) The settings also cover prologue fusion, so the old names were misleading. The old names remain as deprecated aliases that emit a one-time `FutureWarning`. The environment variable is now `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_TEMPLATE_FUSION`; `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_EPILOGUE_FUSION` is still read as a fallback. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.benchmark_epilogue_fusion = False ``` Version 2.15: ```python torch._inductor.config.benchmark_template_fusion = False ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.cuda.graph_annotations.clear_kernel_annotations()` is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning` (#195398) The CUDA graph kernel annotation registry now cleans up after itself: annotations are rekeyed to the executable graph when it is instantiated and dropped when that graph is destroyed. A global clear also discards annotations for graphs that are still live. Remove the call, and reset or delete a graph to drop its annotations. Version 2.14: ```python annotations = get_kernel_annotations() clear_kernel_annotations() ``` Version 2.15: ```python annotations = get_kernel_annotations() # No clear needed; g's annotations are dropped when g is reset or destroyed. ``` # New Features ## torch.nn - Add `torch.nn.functional.scaled_addmm` and in-place `scaled_addmm_`, which compute `beta * input + alpha * scaled_mm(mat1, mat2)` in a single cuBLASLt GEMM on CUDA with the same scaling recipes as `scaled_mm`; also supported under `torch.compile` (#195409, #195410) ## Optimizer - Add `torch.optim.functional`, a public module of functional optimizers (`adam`, `adamw`, `sgd`, `muon` and others) that run the same implementations as the optimizer classes while the caller manages parameters, gradients and state (#194986) ## Autograd - Add `ctx.input_grad_buffers` to custom `torch.autograd.Function` backward, exposing the engine's gradient accumulation buffers (or `None` when unavailable) so a fused kernel can accumulate an input's gradient in place and return `None` for it. Fix a stack buffer overflow in `torch_shm_manager` (libshm) when the Unix socket path is too long (e.g. a long `TMPDIR`); it now raises an error (#195183) - After `import torch.distributed`, `torch.load(weights_only=True)` and `get_unsafe_globals_in_checkpoint` no longer treat builtin exceptions as safe globals (a process-wide allowlist added in 2.14), and loading no longer calls overridden `append`/`extend` on allowlisted `list` subclasses. Checkpoints with pickled exceptions now need `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals`; object collectives are unchanged (#200956) # Developers ## Distributed (c10d) - Make `FakeProcessGroup` support `all_to_all_single` with any sizes and add a `simulate_uniform_ranks` option (#193985, #194545) - Fix a clang build error and add `amd_smi` as a ROCm 7.14+ build dependency (#194104, #192520) - Add the private `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.wait_tensors`, which waits on all outputs of a multi-output functional collective at once; `torch.compile` uses it for coalesced collectives and `batch_isend_irecv` (#193892) ## Profiler - Kineto source now lives in `third_party/kineto` instead of a git submodule (#198648) - Remove the ignored `profiler_metrics` and `profiler_measure_per_kernel` `_ExperimentalConfig` arguments (now a `TypeError`), and deprecate the no-op `adjust_profiler_step` option (#198262, #193042) ## FX - Fix type annotations on `Tracer(autowrap_modules=...)` and `CodeGen.process_inputs` (#195467, #188287) ## Inductor - Add `DeviceInterface` and `DeviceOpOverrides` extension points for out-of-tree accelerator backends (#190326, #190614, #192896, #193908, #190615) - Add declarative `implies` support to Inductor/Dynamo `Config` (#196663) ## Ahead-Of-Time Inductor (AOTI) - Add `DeviceOpOverrides.aten_device_type()` so backends provide their ATen device type to AOTInductor C++ codegen (#193904) ## C++ Frontend - `c10::List` iterators satisfy `std::random_access_iterator`, and `List::emplace` now constructs a `T` (#196002) ## Developer Experience - Add `spin test` to run `pytest` or `test/run_test.py` like CI (#198649) ## Build Frontend - Add an opt-in `USE_CMAKE_INSTRUMENTATION=1` build option to collect build metrics (CMake >= 4.3) (#189455) - Turn off `USE_FLASH_ATTENTION` automatically when no target CUDA architecture is sm80 or newer (#194502) - Fix the misspelled `CUDA_LIMIT_GPU_ARCHITECTURE` in CUDA architecture autodetection (#195695) - Honor `USE_MIMALLOC=OFF` on Windows and AArch64 (#199064) - Fix the FlashAttention CUDA build on Windows with MSVC in C++20 mode (#197382) ## Release Engineering - Move the CD wheel build scripts under `.ci/wheel/` (`.ci/manywheel/` to `.ci/wheel/linux/`, `.ci/macwheel/` to `.ci/wheel/mac/`, and the Windows pipeline to `.ci/wheel/windows/`) and share one `numpy` build pin (#189275) - Add a native-AOT stage to CUDA builds that exports CuTeDSL and Triton kernels ahead of time and embeds them into `libtorch_cuda`. The stage skips itself when it does not apply (for example CUDA older than 13 or no supported GPU architecture), but once it decides to export, a missing `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` (or Triton, installable with `scripts/install_triton_wheel.sh`) is a hard error; set `TORCH_NATIVE_AOT=0` to skip the stage (#194243, #196747, #196507) - Fix the CMake C and C++ compiler flag checks sharing one cache variable, so a result for one language could be reused for the other; the generated `HAS_` variables are now prefixed `HAS_C` and `HAS_CXX` (#197614) - Add a persistent `[no-ci]` PR title prefix that skips build, test and lint jobs, and make `@pytorchbot merge -i` ignore current failures across every PR in a ghstack stack (#196534, #197143) ## CUDA - Update the bundled CUTLASS to v4.8.0 and CUTLASS-Operators to v0.3.0 (#198179) ## CPU (AArch64) - Add the `AT_VEC_CUSTOM_MATH` compile definition, which hides the built-in vectorized math functions on AVX2, AVX512, NEON and SVE256 builds so that a vectorized math library other than SLEEF can be plugged in (#197419) ## MPS - Fix building with clang 16 and Apple clang 15 (#199115) - Fix building with a Metal 4 toolchain against older macOS SDKs, and deprecation warnings with the macOS 27 SDK (#196104, #197200) - `at::mps::MPSProfiler` `begin*`/`end*` methods take the `MPSStream*`; stream-less `begin*` overloads are deprecated (#192525, #193611) - Fix macOS builds failing on SDKs that lack the Metal 4 cooperative-tensor APIs (#195302) - Fix stale embedded Metal shaders in incremental macOS builds (#196202) - Fix MPS shader includes in editable installs (#195295) ## ROCm - `torch.utils.cpp_extension.ROCM_VERSION` now uses the ROCm SDK version instead of the HIP runtime version, and `collect_env` reports both (#194985, #193602) ## XPU - Build XPU with pure SYCL compilation and support Clang as the host compiler; expose `USE_SYCLTLA` and enable oneMKL sparse in the build system (#194185, #198720, #196387, #198200) - Upgrade oneDNN to v3.13 (#196712) ## Caffe2 - Fix source builds with CUDA 13.3 (#194659)

### Czkawka GTK Deprecation Notice
**Version 12.0 is the last released version of Czkawka GTK.** No new binaries will be provided from this point on. All users are encouraged to migrate to Krokiet, the new Slint-based GUI frontend.

## Legend:
- If you are a beginner or don't know which version to use, start with one of these depending on your OS (if they don’t work, try different builds):
  - **Windows** – `windows_krokiet_on_windows_skia_opengl.exe`, `windows_krokiet_on_linux.exe`, `windows_czkawka_gui_gtk_412.zip`  
  - **Mac** – `mac_krokiet_skia_vulkan_x86_64`, `mac_krokiet_skia_vulkan_arm64`, `mac_czkawka_gui_x86_64`, `mac_czkawka_gui_arm64`
  - **Linux** – `linux_krokiet_x86_64`, `linux_krokiet_all_backends`, `linux_czkawka_gui_x86_64`
- `krokiet` – primary graphical version of the application, fully supported and actively developed, includes new features and ongoing improvements
- `gtk_gui` – legacy GTK-based graphical version
- `cedinia` - new android app
- `cli` – command-line version of the app
- `arm`, `x86_64` – CPU architecture. Most Windows/Linux uses `x86_64`, while on Mac the `arm` version is becoming the most common choice. 
- `heif`, `raw`, `avif` – additional features that require extra libraries installed on the OS
- `skia_opengl`, `skia_vulkan`, `femtovg_wgpu`, `all_backends` – alternative Krokiet backends, use different, when you have problem with current
- `deps` - scripts that you can run, to install required/optional apps/libraries

You can read more about 12.0.0 version on Medium:
- English article – https://medium.com/@qarmin/krokiet-czkawka-12-0-6fa09c43c3b9
- Polish article – https://medium.com/@qarmin/krokiet-czkawka-12-0-c5dad2116793

qdrant/qdrant:
# Changelog

## Features 🎶

- [#10750](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/10750) - BM25 scoring directly on the full-text payload index [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/search/text-search/full-text-search/)]
- [Milestone #57](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/milestone/57?closed=1) - TurboQuant: new `turbo8` and `turbo16` vector datatypes [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/vectors/#turboquant-datatypes)]
- [#11125](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/11125) - Per-element payload indexes: new `nested` index parameter, faster nested condition filtering.  [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/indexing/#per-element-index-for-arrays-of-objects)]
- [#11180](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11180), [#11263](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11263) - New `code` tokenizer for full-text index [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/indexing/#code)]
- [#10466](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10466) - Configurable audit log output: `audit.output` writes audit events to `file` (default), `stdout` or `stderr`  [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/security/#audit-log-output)]
- [#10992](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10992) - Collection creation time: `created_at` is recorded and returned in collection info [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/collections/#collection-info)]
- [#10711](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10711) - Substring filter condition: `match: { substring: "..." }` (full-scan only) [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/search/filtering/#substring-match)]
- [#10231](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10231), [#10287](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10287), [#10296](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10296) - New formula query expressions: `acosh`, `max`, `min` [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/search/search-relevance/#max-and-min)] and [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/search/search-relevance/#hyperbolic-distance)]
- [#10597](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10597), [#10598](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10598) - Configurable ID tracker memory placement [[docs](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/ops-configuration/memory-tiers/#id-tracker)]

## Improvements 🎵

- [#11009](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11009), [#11020](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11020) - Faster HNSW payload links build - builder sized to the block, not the segment, and reused
- [#11083](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11083) - Faster HNSW healing - payload blocks reuse old graph links; `m = 0` graphs can heal too
- [#11166](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11166) - Smaller HNSW upper layers - `floor()` in level assignment matches the HNSW paper (6.25% of points on level 1 at `m = 16`, not 25%)
- [#10976](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10976) - Faster PQ training - k-means sample gathered in one pass, not one per chunk
- [#10975](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10975) - Faster scalar quantization search - AVX512-VNNI and AVX-VNNI kernels for int8 dot product
- [#10977](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10977) - Less search slowdown during optimizations - the whole optimization job runs at low thread priority
- [#11078](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11078), [#11080](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11080) - Fewer cancelled optimizations - optimizers are recreated only when their config changes
- [#11234](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11234) - Faster point retrieval - ids resolved in one batch per segment
- [#11070](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11070) - Faster snapshot transfers and downloads - 4 MiB stream buffers instead of 4 KiB
- [#11253](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11253) - Faster shard transfers - `transfer_raw_points` and `transfer_raw_payloads` on by default
- [#11206](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11206) - Safer snapshots - unique snapshot names, and a stored snapshot is never overwritten
- [#11221](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11221) - No stuck snapshot downloads - 60s timeout when the server never responds
- [#11163](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11163) - No blocking thread leak on telemetry timeout - the timeout also applies inside the blocking task
- [#11164](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11164) - Clearer tar unpack errors - release builds report the error kind (e.g. `timed out`) instead of "malformed archive"
- [#11118](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11118) - Log timestamps respect timezone - set with the `TZ` environment variable, UTC by default
- [#10235](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10235) - `timeout` parameter for the get points API
- [Milestone #58](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/milestone/58?closed=1) - Less disk usage with `hnsw_config.inline_storage` - vectors are stored only inside the HNSW graph file, without a separate vector storage copy
- [#10790](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10790) - Faster `enable_hnsw` change on payload indexes - updated in place instead of dropping and rebuilding the index
- [#10906](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10906) - Faster search over on-disk vectors - batches of vectors are prefetched with `madvise(WILLNEED)` before scoring
- [#10907](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10907) - ACORN on `m = 0` graphs - search uses the payload-block links of the graph
- [#11255](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11255) - Better shard distribution in small clusters - auto-sharded collections get 2 shards per node in 3+ node clusters while collections are fewer than nodes
- [#11273](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11273) - No internal request stalls behind NAT and load balancers - HTTP/2 keepalive on internal p2p gRPC
- [#11289](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11289) - Configurable snapshot storage timeouts and retries - new `timeout_sec`, `connect_timeout_sec`, `max_retries`, `retry_timeout_sec` in S3, GCS and Azure config

- [#10932](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10932), [#10971](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10971) - Fix collection reads stalling while a shard transfer holds the shard holder lock
- [#10949](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10949) - Fix live-lock between shard transfer start and consensus operations
- [#10956](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10956) - Fix collection being blocked while a shard snapshot is extracted
- [#11075](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11075) - Fix `must_not` conditions being ignored when equal to an indexed `must` condition
- [#11101](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11101) - Fix datetime filters with microseconds behaving differently with and without a payload index
- [#10948](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10948) - Fix renaming an alias to an existing collection name being accepted
- [#10887](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10887) - Fix transfer staying registered after crash replay of replica removal during transfer abort
- [#11121](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11121) - Fix S3 snapshot upload completing truncated on a local read error
- [#10796](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10796) - Fix Japanese tokenizer ignoring `min_token_len`, `max_token_len`, `stemmer`, `ascii_folding` and case-insensitive stopwords
- [#10754](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10754) - Fix quantization build with MSVC-like compilers (clang-cl)

## Security 🔑

- [#10854](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10854) - Internal auth is enforced by default: `service.enforce_internal_auth` now defaults to `true` when an API key is configured
- [#10718](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/10718) - Startup warning when distributed mode has an API key configured but `enforce_internal_auth` is off
- [#11275](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11275), [#11290](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11290) - Reject vector names that escape the segment directory, including `.` and `..`

qpdf/qpdf:
This is qpdf version 12.4.2. In addition to a few small bug fixes, this release features two significant improvements: inclusion of several new binary platform releases and substantial improvements to linearization. We now include official release binaries for MacOS (intel and arm64), Windows arm64, and Linux aarch64 (arm64) both as an AppImage and as stand-alone binaries. For linearization, for certain types of files, qpdf is vastly more memory efficient (we've seen 30× improvements in some cases) and slightly faster. Also, there are a few small fixes to linearization object ordering, so linearized output may differ for some rare files relative to previous releases.

For a full list of changes from previous releases, please see the [release notes](https://qpdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/release-notes.html). See also [README-what-to-download](./README-what-to-download.md) for details about the available source and binary distributions.

This release was signed by ejb@ql.org.

raysan5/raylib: # raylib 6.2 release notes After almost 6 months since latest raylib release, here it is a new installment of the library. It was supposed to be just a patch version to address an issue with CMake build system but it took way longer than expected and included +300 changes and improvements. Some numbers for this release: - **~100** closed issues (for a TOTAL of **+2240**!) - **+500** commits since previous RELEASE (for a TOTAL of **+10280**!) - **+20** new functions ADDED to raylib API (for a TOTAL of **619**!) - **+10** new examples to learn from (for a TOTAL of **+225**!) - **+100** new contributors (for a TOTAL of **+950**!) Highlights for `raylib 6.2`: - **Code gardening**: A lot of work has been done to improve small library details, for consistency and coherence. Many comments have been reviewed, some function parameters have been renamed with more clear naming, some pointers reviewed for const-correctness, functions reordered in the API for more clarity and also several functions have been completely redesigned. - **REDESIGNED: Image drawing API more alignment with Screen drawing API**: Image API has been reviewed to be aligned with Texture API, now most Texture-based functions (GPU accelerated) have a counter-part to work over Image structures (CPU), also following same parameters order. All the following functions are equivalent: | Module | Screen draw (GPU accelerated) | Image draw (CPU software rendering) | | -------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- | | `rshapes` | `DrawPixel()` | `ImageDrawPixel()` | | `rshapes` | `DrawPixelV()` | `ImageDrawPixelV()` | | `rshapes` | `DrawLine()` | `ImageDrawLine()` | | `rshapes` | `DrawLineV()` | `ImageDrawLineV()` | | `rshapes` | `DrawLineEx()` | `ImageDrawLineEx()` | | `rshapes` | `DrawLineStrip()` | `ImageDrawLineStrip()` | | `rshapes` | `DrawLineBezier()` | -
