| | `rtext` | `DrawTextCodepoints()` | - | _NOTE: All `ImageDraw*()` functions require an `Image` pointer to draw to as first parameter: `ImageDrawImage(Image *target, ...)`_ This API alignment could allow in the future faster 2D software rendering over an `Image` buffer, as an alternative to the already included `rlsw` Software Renderer that implements a pseudo-OpenGL 1.1 pipeline. - **REDESIGNED: File API using more standard return result values**: File API return values have been unified to follow C conventions, returning 0 if everything worked as expected and other values for potential issues on the file processes. - **REVIEWED: Multiple security concerns reported by ROS (Radically Open Security)**: Recently raylib went through a professional security audit by Radically Open Security, most of the reported security concerns have been addressed. Make sure to check raylib [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/raysan5/raylib/blob/master/CHANGELOG) for a detailed list of changes! Again, I want to **thank all the contributors (+950!**) that helped improving raylib, this time there have been **more than 100 new contributors** sending fixes and improvements! After 13 years of development, `raylib 6.2` is today probably one of the bests libraries to enjoy **games/tools/graphics/AI programming!** **Hope you keep enjoying programming with raylib!** :)

readest/readest:
## Release Highlights
* Text-to-Speech: Added Readest Voice premium read-aloud voices for Plus and Pro, you can now connect your own OpenAI-compatible voice service, and Edge voices work again
* Annotations: You can now handwrite and draw on your pages, and share passages as quote card images
* Library: Books now show their page count with a new Pages sort and filter that syncs across devices, and numbered titles sort in natural order
* Sync: Custom fonts download when you need them and can be removed from the cloud, custom theme edits now sync, and deleted books no longer come back
* Sync: KOReader progress sync and WebDAV sync are more reliable, and signing out only logs out the current device
* Reading: Very large or link-heavy chapters no longer freeze the reader, and fixed layout issues with headings, blockquotes, footnotes, and background textures
* Audiobooks: Audiobookshelf playback now works in the web app, chapters are detected more reliably, and you can pair audiobooks with books streamed from Audiobookshelf
* Linux: Fixed a freeze with two open windows, the main window reopens maximized, and Reveal in Folder works again
* PDF: You can hide page thumbnails in the PDF table of contents
* More: The share sheet opens again on iOS 16, with polish for the drawing tools, bottom sheets, and bookshelf header

realm/SwiftLint:
### Breaking

* `Configuration.IndentationStyle` moved to `SwiftLintCore.IndentationStyle`.
  Rules can now read the global `indentation` setting via `CurrentRule.configuration`.  
  [GandaLF2006](https://github.com/GandaLF2006)

* Remove the deprecated `allow_multiline_func` option from the `opening_brace`
  rule. Use `ignore_multiline_function_signatures` instead.  
  [Brett-Best](https://github.com/Brett-Best)

### Enhancements

* Speed up the `collection_alignment` rule, which read the whole file's
  source lines once per element of a dictionary literal.  
  [Brett-Best](https://github.com/Brett-Best)

* Compare the two operands of a comparison by walking their token streams in
  the `identical_operands` rule instead of rendering both operands to strings,
  so differing operands stop at the first mismatching token.  
  [Brett-Best](https://github.com/Brett-Best)

* Add `#examples` and `#corrections` macros that expand lists and
  dictionaries of code strings into `Example`s, reducing boilerplate when
  defining a rule's triggering/non-triggering examples and corrections. Adopt
  them across the built-in rules.  
  [ZevEisenberg](https://github.com/ZevEisenberg)

* Add `allow_compact_empty_blocks` option to the `no_empty_block` rule to
  allow empty blocks written compactly as `{}` while still flagging empty
  blocks with any whitespace or newlines between the braces.  
  [arimu1](https://github.com/arimu1)
  [#6839](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6839)

### Bug Fixes

* Add an opt-in `allow_explicit_unsafe_unowned` option to let the
  `unowned_variable_capture` rule accept explicit `unowned(unsafe)` captures.  
  [Yurii Bakurov](https://github.com/Yurii201811)
  [#6817](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6817)

* Fix `line_length` with `ignores_urls` enabled incorrectly ignoring property
  accesses whose member names are valid top-level domains.  
  [Arthur Liu](https://github.com/thliu21)
  [#6811](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6811)

* Fix baseline writing to store file locations as paths relative to the current working directory,
  restoring baseline portability and avoiding absolute `file://` paths in generated baseline files.  
  [SimplyDanny](https://github.com/SimplyDanny)
  [#6812](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6812)

* Fix correction behavior of `closure_spacing` rule when a closure contains only trivia (e.g. comments).  
  [SimplyDanny](https://github.com/SimplyDanny)
  [#6798](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6798)
  [#6799](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6799)

* Fix `closure_end_indentation` moving closing braces to column 1 in files
  with CRLF line endings when running `swiftlint --fix`.  
  [sjh9714](https://github.com/sjh9714)
  [#6598](https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint/issues/6598)

Changelog for restic 0.19.1 (2026-07-05)
=======================================

The following sections list the changes in restic 0.19.1 relevant to restic users. The changes are ordered by importance.

Summary
-------

 * Fix [#5234](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5234): Prevent mounting over the repository directory
 * Fix [#5667](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5667): Skip inaccessible `backup` source paths
 * Fix [#5722](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5722): Update `mount` latest symlink after snapshot reload
 * Fix [#21866](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21866): Hide `stats` progress bar in JSON mode
 * Fix [#21869](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21869): Restore old behavior of `snapshots --latest <n>` without `--group-by`
 * Fix [#21876](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21876): Show timezone location in `snapshots` output
 * Fix [#21879](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21879): Prevent crash in mountpoint validation if mountpoint is inaccessible
 * Fix [#21895](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21895): Remove read-only files via the SFTP backend on Windows servers
 * Fix [#21899](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21899): Make `backup` respect excludes for duplicate directory entries

Details
-------

 * Bugfix #5234: Prevent mounting over the repository directory

   Using a local repository directory as the `mount` target — or a path that contains it, or that it contains — caused the FUSE server to read its own backend files through the new mount, deadlocking the kernel and requiring a long reboot to recover.

   Restic now resolves both paths and refuses any such overlap with a clear error before mounting.

    [#5234](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5234) [#5348](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5348) 

 * Bugfix #5667: Skip inaccessible `backup` source paths

   The `backup` command only skipped source paths that did not exist. A path that could not be accessed for another reason, such as a malformed path on Windows, was kept and produced an empty snapshot. Restic now skips any such path and aborts if none remain.

    [#5667](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5667) [#21852](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21852) 

 * Bugfix #5722: Update `mount` latest symlink after snapshot reload

   When `restic mount` was kept running while new snapshots were created, the new snapshots appeared in the mountpoint, but the `latest` symlink could still point to the previously latest snapshot. Restic now invalidates the cached snapshot directory entries after a snapshot reload so that `latest` points to the newest snapshot.

    [#5722](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5722) [#21873](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21873) 

 * Bugfix #21866: Hide `stats` progress bar in JSON mode

   Since restic 0.19.0, the `stats` command shows a progress bar. This progress bar was unintentionally displayed also when using the `--json` option, mixing regular text output with JSON. This is now fixed.

    [#21866](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21866) [#21871](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21871) 

 * Bugfix #21869: Restore old behavior of `snapshots --latest <n>` without `--group-by`

   Restic 0.19.0 accidentally changed the behavior of `snapshots --latest <n>` to no longer group snapshots by host and paths by default.

   The `snapshots --latest <n>` command now again uses the old behavior of grouping by host and paths when `--group-by` is not specified. However, when specifying `--group-by` the output is still grouped as requested, as in restic 0.19.0.

    [#21869](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21869) [#21875](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21875) 

 * Bugfix #21876: Show timezone location in `snapshots` output

   With restic 0.19.0, the `snapshots` command printed the current timezone when listing snapshots. However, that timezone label might change during the year, for example with daylight saving time. Restic now prints a more consistent and shorter version of the text.

    [#21876](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21876) https://forum.restic.net/t/possible-bug-in-timezone-naming/10867

 * Bugfix #21879: Prevent crash in mountpoint validation if mountpoint is inaccessible

   Since restic 0.19.0, the `mount` command validates a mountpoint before loading the repository. If restic was unable to stat the mountpoint, this would result in a crash. This has now been fixed to correctly return an error instead.

    [#21879](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21879) 

 * Bugfix #21895: Remove read-only files via the SFTP backend on Windows servers

   Since restic 0.19.0, repository files on the SFTP backend are marked read-only after save. On Windows SFTP servers, removing them failed with a permission error. The SFTP backend now clears the read-only flag before removing the file.

    [#21895](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21895) [#21897](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21897) 

 * Bugfix #21899: Make `backup` respect excludes for duplicate directory entries

   Since restic 0.19.0, backing up a directory with duplicate directory entries always produced "Warning: at least one source file could not be read", even when those files were excluded. This has now been fixed.

    [#21899](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21899) [#21900](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21900)

# v0.31.3 — Grayscale annotators, OpenCV-exact fallbacks, and merged YOLO polygons

Grayscale scenes work with more annotators, the pure NumPy fallback matches OpenCV pixel for pixel, and YOLO export handles multi-part masks.

- **YOLO export** merges multi-part masks into one polygon and skips crowd annotations, with flags for the old output.
- Background overlay and comparison annotators draw on grayscale scenes.
- Without OpenCV, resize, blur, blending, drawing and connected components give the same pixels as OpenCV.
- Invalid input fails early: `ImageSink`, the video frame generator and depth arrays now raise clear errors.
- Short hex colors such as `"#f0f"` work in annotators.

Drop-in upgrade unless you export YOLO labels: the default output changes, see the Migration guide.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### YOLO export merges multi-part masks and skips crowd annotations

`DetectionDataset.as_yolo` now omits detections whose `iscrowd` flag is set and writes a mask with several disconnected parts as one merged polygon line instead of one line per part. Both are on by default. The merge is done by the new `sv.merge_multi_segment`, which joins the parts through zero-width seams at their nearest vertices. (#2786)

```python
import supervision as sv

dataset = sv.DetectionDataset(...)
dataset.as_yolo(
    images_directory_path="images",
    annotations_directory_path="labels",
    data_yaml_path="data.yaml",
)  # 0.31.3: crowd skipped, one merged polygon line per mask

dataset.as_yolo(
    images_directory_path="images",
    annotations_directory_path="labels",
    data_yaml_path="data.yaml",
    ignore_crowd=False,
    merge_segments=False,
)  # the 0.31.2 output
```

### `sv.merge_multi_segment`

New public function. Pass it the polygon parts of one mask and get back a single polygon. (#2786)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

a = np.array([[0, 0], [10, 0], [10, 10], [0, 10]])
b = np.array([[30, 30], [40, 30], [40, 40], [30, 40]])
sv.merge_multi_segment([a, b]).shape
# (10, 2)
```

### Annotators on grayscale scenes

`BackgroundOverlayAnnotator` and `ComparisonAnnotator` now draw on scenes shaped `(H, W)` or `(H, W, 1)`, or given as a Pillow `"L"` image, instead of raising `ValueError`. Short hex colors such as `"#f0f"` now work in annotators and `sv.hex_to_rgba`. (#2832, #2803, #2801)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20, 20, 60, 60]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.BackgroundOverlayAnnotator().annotate(scene.copy(), detections).shape
# (100, 100)  (0.31.2: ValueError)
```

### The NumPy fallback matches OpenCV pixel for pixel

Without OpenCV installed, `resize` (`INTER_LINEAR` on `uint8`), `blur`, `addWeighted`, thin lines, circles, filled polygons that leave the canvas, `connectedComponents` and `mean` now give the same pixels as OpenCV. `BlurAnnotator`, `HaloAnnotator`, `HeatMapAnnotator`, `PixelateAnnotator`, the blending annotators, `sv.resize_image`, `sv.letterbox_image` and `PolygonZone` masks are affected. (#2833, #2836, #2811, #2808, #2810, #2812, #2820)

### Bad input fails early

`sv.ImageSink(overwrite=False)` raises `FileExistsError` instead of replacing an existing image, `sv.get_video_frames_generator` rejects a stride below 1, and `DepthMap.from_ultralytics` rejects unwrapped integer arrays. (#2800, #2819, #2795)

```python
import supervision as sv

for frame in sv.get_video_frames_generator("video.mp4", stride=0):
    ...
# ValueError: stride must be >= 1, got 0
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

One default behavior changes: YOLO export. No public symbol was removed or renamed in this release, and nothing is deprecated.

**YOLO export defaults** affect `sv.DetectionDataset.as_yolo`, and `save_yolo_annotations` and `detections_to_yolo_annotations` in `supervision.dataset.formats.yolo`. Before 0.31.3 export skipped nothing and wrote a mask with several disconnected parts as one polygon line per part. From 0.31.3 export drops detections whose `iscrowd` flag is set in `detections.data`, and writes the parts of a mask as one merged polygon line. Label files exported with 0.31.3 can therefore differ from those exported with 0.31.2 for the same dataset. (#2786)

- Nothing to do if you want crowd annotations dropped and one polygon line per mask.
- To keep the 0.31.2 output, pass `ignore_crowd=False` and `merge_segments=False` to `as_yolo`.
- Re-export datasets you trained on from 0.31.2 labels only if the crowd or multi-part masks matter to your training run.

Three bug fixes also turn silent behavior into an error: `ImageSink(overwrite=False)` raises `FileExistsError` for an existing image (#2800), `get_video_frames_generator` raises `ValueError` for a stride below 1 (#2819), and `DepthMap.from_ultralytics` rejects unwrapped integer arrays (#2795).

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🚀 Added

- **`sv.merge_multi_segment`** — joins the disconnected polygon segments of one mask into a single polygon. (#2786)
- **`ignore_crowd` and `merge_segments`** — new parameters on `DetectionDataset.as_yolo`, `save_yolo_annotations` and `detections_to_yolo_annotations`. (#2786)
- **Depth showcase example** — `examples/depth_showcase` runs Depth Anything V2 Large, Apple Depth Pro and a YOLO depth model through `sv.DepthAnnotator` on video files, webcams and streams. (#2804, #2818)

### 🌱 Changed

- `DetectionDataset.as_yolo` now skips crowd annotations and writes multi-part masks as one merged polygon line. Pass `ignore_crowd=False` and `merge_segments=False` for the previous output. (#2786)

### 🔧 Fixed

**Annotators**

- `BackgroundOverlayAnnotator` and `ComparisonAnnotator` raised `ValueError` on grayscale scenes. (#2832, #2803)
- Annotators and `sv.hex_to_rgba` rejected 3- and 4-digit short hex colors such as `"#f0f"`. (#2801)

**Input validation, I/O and metrics**

- `ImageSink(overwrite=False)` silently replaced an existing image, including through a dangling symlink; it now raises `FileExistsError`, and a path with an embedded null character raises `ValueError`. (#2800)
- `get_video_frames_generator` could yield frames past `end` for `stride=0` or a negative stride; it now raises `ValueError`. (#2819)
- `DepthMap.from_ultralytics` accepted unwrapped integer arrays as depth values. (#2795)
- `KeyPoints.as_detections` and `with_nms` let an extra coordinate change the boxes; they now use x/y only. (#2817)
- `MeanAverageRecall.compute()` raised `IndexError` when filtering by object size with shared scalar metadata. (#2791)
- `download_assets(VideoAssets.GROCERY_STORE)` failed MD5 verification; the catalog now holds the checksum of the hosted file. (#2804)

**NumPy fallback without OpenCV**

- `resize` with `INTER_LINEAR` on `uint8` images now matches OpenCV pixel for pixel; arm64 builds that hand some grayscale and RGBA resizes to the Carotene HAL can differ by up to two levels. (#2833)
- `addWeighted` rounds 8-bit, 16-bit and float32 blends like OpenCV. (#2836)
- `blur` rounds 8-bit results like OpenCV. (#2811)
- `line`, `polylines`, `drawContours` and `circle` at thickness 1, and filled circles, match OpenCV; a negative circle radius raises `ValueError`. (#2808)
- `fillPoly` and filled `drawContours` match OpenCV for polygons that leave the canvas. (#2810)
- `connectedComponents` and `connectedComponentsWithStats` number 8-connected components in OpenCV's order. (#2812)
- `mean` keeps small values when large positive and negative `float32` pixels cancel. (#2820)

ruvnet/RuView:
@ruvnet/ruview 0.9.2

Maintenance fixes from [PR #2248](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/pull/2248), which records the exact source heads for 38 integrated contributor PRs.

- Accept official C6 firmware bundle filenames while preserving checksum and board-variant validation.
- Correct CSI loss accounting, observed capture duration, dominant stream selection, and synthetic-data provenance; reject malformed auxiliary packets.
- Correct ESPHome units and entity roles, report incomplete serial captures, and fix LiDAR/mmWave summaries and stream completion.
- Validate CLI numeric arguments, preserve gaps in watch history, report corrupt manifests through doctor, and honor SDK strict errors.
- Replace inherited and explicit Windows hosts-file ACL grants with verified current-user-only access. Paths are passed as data to the bounded helper, including Unicode and shell-special characters.
- Preserve source recordings during transcoding, avoid capture-session filename collisions, and retain complete relayed UDP datagrams.
- Exercise the contributor harness on Linux and Windows and correct CI snapshot release metadata.

Install the exact package with `npm install @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.2`, or run its CLI using `npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.2 --help`.

Repository-only changes also improve Home Assistant client topic compatibility and the MTK bridge test lifecycle. These changes do not imply that a new Python wheel or hardware-qualified firmware was published with this npm package.

The release commit also contains the separately reviewed [calibration and sensing fixes](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/pull/2246): failed recording or baseline-save sessions finish as aborted, and diagnostic fields follow the actual occupancy decision without changing the accepted decision rules.

Compatible board images are available separately in the [ESP32 firmware 0.8.14 prerelease](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/releases/tag/v0.8.14-esp32). Its S3 8 MB, S3 4 MB, and C6 4 MB bundles have verified archive and image checksums. They have CI build and host-test coverage, with no new physical-board qualification.

Published by the [npm release workflow](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/actions/runs/38280634481) from commit [`0f95193190261a8966ad5f52e188aa6a480c2968`](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/commit/0f95193190261a8966ad5f52e188aa6a480c2968). Registry signatures and the provenance attestation verified successfully and bind the downloaded tarball to this exact commit and workflow. The attached tarball is identical to the tested, published npm package; verify it with the attached `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

A fresh installation passed package-manifest, CLI, SDK, and read-only firmware-bundle checks for all three published board variants. No hardware operations were performed. No learning proposal or experimental Dream Machine candidate is promoted by this release.

# ShadowsocksX-NG2 2.0.0-alpha.2

## Breaking Changes

### Custom rules and rule enablement settings are not migrated

Custom rules and rule enablement settings from alpha.1 are **not migrated**. Recreate them in the appropriate routing preset after upgrading.

Your previous files are retained, and your existing routing choice maps to the equivalent preset.

### Subscription date fields have changed

Expiration and traffic reset dates now use `x_shadowsocksx_ng.expires_at` and `x_shadowsocksx_ng.traffic_reset_at`, with `schema_version: 1`. The previous top-level fields are no longer read.

## New Features

### Independent routing presets

Rule mode now offers three presets:

- **Proxy GFWList Targets Only** — the default for new installations.
- **Direct for Mainland China**
- **Proxy Mainland China Targets**

Each preset keeps its own custom rules and rule enablement settings. Manage and test presets independently on the Rules page, then choose the active preset in the proxy controls.

### Automatic subscription updates

Keep subscriptions updated on a daily or weekly schedule, or turn automatic updates off, subject to your provider’s policy.

Updates run while the app is running, even with its windows closed. Overdue updates are checked at launch and after your Mac wakes.

## Interface and Diagnostics

- Open Diagnostics directly from the menu bar.
- Inspect logs in a selectable table, view entry details, and copy selected entries.
- See runtime status indicators on the Home page.
- Reduced flicker caused by brief status changes.
- Improved diagnostic log formatting and severity detection.

## Fixes and Updates

- Improved launch and window activation behavior.
- Allowed more time for the local proxy to start before reporting a startup failure.
- Updated the bundled **v2ray-plugin to 1.5.0** and disabled its access logs by default.

## Requirements

- macOS 15 or later
- Apple Silicon Mac

## Features
- Add `--ignore-parent` option to override `--no-ignore-parent`, see #1958 (@tmchow)
- Add `--exact` option to match the entire filename exactly (literal, non-substring).

## Bugfixes
- Sanitize control characters and bidirectional override characters in filenames
  when output goes to a terminal, to prevent terminal escape-sequence injection.
  Also reject a placeholder as the executable for `--exec-batch`, while still
  allowing it for `--exec`.
- Handle invalid working directories gracefully when using `--full-path`, see #1900 (@Xavrir).
- Fire the "search pattern contains a path separator" diagnostic for any pattern containing `/`, not just patterns that happen to name an existing directory. Preserves the legacy Windows behaviour that also flags native `\` separators when the pattern resolves to a real directory. See #1873.
- Also fire the "search pattern contains a path separator" diagnostic for `--and` patterns, not only the primary positional pattern. `--and` patterns are matched against the file name just like the primary pattern, so a path separator in them silently returned zero results. See #1873.

- Fix panic when `--changed-before`/`--changed-within` is given an out-of-range `@` Unix timestamp; the value is now rejected gracefully, see #2081 (@nikolauspschuetz).

sharkdp/hyperfine: See the breaking changes below when migrating from hyperfine 1.x. ## Features - Add support for alternative performance metrics (peak memory usage, instructions, CPU cycles, cache misses, branch misses, ...). By default, hyperfine will now display wall-clock time and peak memory usage, but users can use the [new `--metrics` option](README.md#choosing-metrics-and-units) to select different performance metrics. The terminal output now shows an overview of all selected performance metrics (see [here](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/pull/986) for a run with more metrics enabled). - Add [`--env` to set environment variables](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine#environment-variables) even without an intermediate shell (which is the new default behavior, see below). For example: ```sh # Parameterized benchmark, comparing different thread counts: hyperfine -P threads 1 8 --env 'OMP_NUM_THREADS={threads}' 'my_command' ``` - The plotting and analysis scripts now support different metrics as well, see #981 and #984 (@sharkdp). ## Breaking changes - Benchmarked commands are now executed directly by default, without an intermediate shell (`--shell=none`). Use `-S` (an alias for `--shell=default`) to restore the previous behavior (`sh` on Unix, `cmd.exe` on Windows), or select a shell with `--shell `. See [the rationale for this change](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/issues/787#issuecomment-6038898252). - Always run `--setup`, `--prepare`, `--conclude`, and `--cleanup` commands in a shell, even when using `--shell=none`, see #990 (@sharkdp). - The JSON format for `--export-json` has changed (schema version 2). The [new format](README.md#json) now includes metadata, per-run measurements, and statistical summaries for all measured quantities, see #790 (@sharkdp). Code that reads those exported JSON files must be updated. For example, `results[i].mean` is now `results[i].summary.time_wall_clock.mean`, and `results[i].times` is replaced by `results[i].measurements[j].time_wall_clock.value`. The new structure looks like this: ```python { "schema_version": 2, "primary_metric": "time_wall_clock", "metadata": { "hyperfine_version": "2.0.0", "start_time": "2026-10-06T12:00:00Z", "platform": {"os": "Linux", "architecture": "x86_64"} }, "results": [ { "command": "sleep 1", # Actual command after parameter substitution "name": "wait 1s", # Optional custom or automatically generated name "parameters": {"duration": {"value": "1"}}, # For parametrized runs "environment": {"OMP_NUM_THREADS": "8"}, # Only present with --env overrides "measurements": [ # One entry per run, excluding warmups { "time_wall_clock": {"value": 1.0, "unit": "second"}, "time_cpu": {"value": 0.0, "unit": "second"}, "time_user": {"value": 0.0, "unit": "second"}, "time_system": {"value": 0.0, "unit": "second"}, "memory_peak_resident": {"value": 1048576.0, "unit": "byte"}, "cpu_cycles": {"value": 5000000}, # Hardware counters, when available "instructions": {"value": 10000000}, "exit_code": 0 }, ... # Further runs omitted ], "summary": { "time_wall_clock": { "unit": "second", "count": 30, "mean": 1.0, "stddev": 0.0, "median": 1.0, "min": 1.0, "max": 1.0 } # Other metrics have the same summary structure. } } ] } ``` Times are always exported in seconds and memory in bytes. Hardware counters and their summaries have no `unit` field. Unavailable memory measurements and hardware counters are omitted; other available counters may also be included. `stddev` is `null` for a single run. - `--time-unit`/`-u` has been removed. Units can now be selected using the `--metrics METRIC[:UNIT],…` option, e.g. `--metrics time_wall_clock:ms,memory_peak_resident:MiB`. - `--sort` has been removed. It complicated hyperfine significantly and doesn't make too much sense with the new output format. - `--reference` and `--reference-name` have been removed (for now). The first command is always considered as the reference command. Invocations using `--reference` now show migration guidance to put the reference command first. - The format of [Markdown](README.md#markdown), AsciiDoc and org-mode, and [CSV](README.md#csv) exports has also been changed. Markdown, AsciiDoc, and org-mode contain only the primary metric (the first metric selected by `--metrics`). CSV exports all selected metrics side by side.

> Installable catalog update for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and related assistants. Adds **5** reviewed skills, refreshes two existing workflows, and fixes the three canonical dependency alerts before publication; regenerated plugin copies include the same fixes.

### Start here

- [Best skills by tool](https://github.com/sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills/blob/v20.2.0/README.md#best-skills-by-tool)

- [Workflows](https://github.com/sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills/blob/v20.2.0/docs/users/workflows.md)

### Added

- **bifrost-gateway** - run and configure Bifrost as a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway, with fallbacks, virtual-key budgets, caching, observability, MCP routing, and explicit credential and public-exposure boundaries.
- **comment-to-dm-cta** - plan an Instagram comment-to-DM CTA locally, then require explicit confirmation before creating or changing the automation through CommentKeyword.
- **landing-page**, **web-design-system**, and **web-review** - adaptive UXKIN-derived workflows for truthful landing-page copy, a documented design system, and a prioritized rendered-page review. The optional UXKIN MCP path requires a user-selected account and plan.

### Changed

- **cloudish** - synchronize the official 0.1.6 workflow with server-side builds, verified log checks, custom domains, replicas, instance sizing, OIDC sign-in, credit operations, and retained MIT notice.
- **datacircle** - refresh the GTM API-plan model, cached API coverage, search and SERP rows, pricing semantics, and query examples against the current public skill.
- **animated GitHub profile and Satori updates remain on their prior reviewed catalog versions** - the proposed updates were not shipped because their exact-head content did not meet current structural, safety, provenance, or license-notice gates.

### Security and reliability

- Fix Dependabot's `qs` denial-of-service advisory in the three canonical Loki, Telegram, and WhatsApp boilerplate lockfiles by moving from **6.16.0** to **6.16.1**. The protected release snapshot propagates the patched lockfiles into both plugin mirrors.
- Add retained MIT notices for imported skill bundles and replace Bifrost's secret-shaped examples with process-environment reads so the trusted SEC009 gate passes without weakening the scanner.
- Encode the two `pentest-tools` XSS reference payload archives as explicit UTF-8 Base64 companions to remove raw test markup from the cloneable Markdown; a fresh Windows Defender clone check remains an explicit acceptance boundary. The Markdown entrypoints retain authorization, data-minimization, and decoding boundaries, and a regression verifies byte-exact round trips.
- Complete two protected maintenance cycles: merge **#2164** and **#2172**, and close the remaining batch PRs with exact-head owner rationale where superseded or not admissible. Protected-main CI, CodeQL, required merge gates, and the release-cycle barrier are green on the verified source commit.

### Upgrade notes

- The verified runtime archive is attached below as `package.tgz`.
- Existing projects install only the skills they select. Re-select or refresh a stack to receive catalog changes.
- The optional CommentKeyword, UXKIN, Cloudish, and Bifrost workflows use external services with their own account, credential, data-transfer, cost, and confirmation boundaries.

### Thanks

Thanks to **@commentkeyword** for `comment-to-dm-cta`, **@Swpn0neel** for `bifrost-gateway`, **@ronaldmanlupig30-web** and UXKIN for the three website-workflow adaptations, **@waynehamadi** for the Datacircle refresh, and **@javierluraschi** plus the Cloudish team for the official upstream synchronization. Thanks also to **@MetcalfSolutions** and **@shivamnamdev** for their submissions; those updates remain available for a corrected resubmission.

## Final Release (v1.5.0)

** this project wil be archived soon **

when i started this project 9 months ago, it was really just a side project to help indie devs make better demos and share what they were building. i never expected it to get anywhere close to where it is today. somehow it ended up at 120k+ downloads and almost 40k stars, which is still kind of crazy to me.

i've genuinely enjoyed building it, but i also feel like i've achieved everything i originally set out to do with the project. i guess that's also part of why i'm comfortable ending it.

there are already plenty of successors and forks carrying the torch in their own way and I highly encourage you to check [them](https://github.com/webadderallorg/Recordly) out. 

thanks to **everyone** who contributed 🙏 , used the app and helped maintain the project, making it truly community first.

even though i'm stepping away, i'd still love to see what people continue building with OpenScreen. if you're using it for your demos, products, walkthroughs, feel free to tag me on X and share what you've made. seeing how people used OpenScreen was always one of the most rewarding parts of working on it.

- Annotation text animations.
- Language support: English, Arabic, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Portuguese (Brazil), Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional)
- Audio waveform for easier hinting.
- deprecated Blurs. 
- Vertical HUD layout (toggle)

siyuan-note/siyuan:
## Upgrade notice

Document titles can now include `/`. Use the new version to open and edit these documents. We recommend updating the devices that access the same data and checking that your plugins are compatible, to avoid older versions overwriting your changes. See [the compatibility details](https://github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/issues/19938).

## Overview

This release adds support for `/` in document titles and improves mind maps, database automations, mobile editing, and file change detection.

### Mind maps and editing

Mind maps gain themes, global styling, node selection and clipboard operations, improved summaries, and list-style editing interactions.

Tables support adjustable row heights, with improvements to cell activation, text formatting performance, and Markdown list copying and export.

### Databases and navigation

Database automations support collecting block references, attribute name substring and regex matching, and subdocument depth limits.

Backlinks can be filtered by database fields, new database items have configurable opening behavior, and mobile documents can display backlinks at the bottom.

### Platforms and reliability

This release improves iOS text selection and editing, mobile search navigation, sync progress and cancellation, and file change detection for snapshots, sync, and restoration.

It also adds Windows title bar overlay, macOS system proxy detection, TIFF previews, and custom lock screen wallpapers, and updates runtimes and CA certificates.

spmallick/learnopencv:
Updates the LearnOpenCV SAM-3 companion to Meta SAM 3.1 Object Multiplex.

Highlights:
- stateful start/add-prompt/propagate/close video lifecycle
- streamed OpenCV rendering with stable object IDs and bounded mask memory
- source-audio preservation without short-audio video truncation
- compatibility guard for the current upstream multiplex start-session mismatch
- refreshed tutorial notebook and Python 3.12 dependency pin
- 10 deterministic tests, validated in the release archive

The archive is reproducibly built from merge commit d19e6de5598ab9474243bee50205770d23eedd10. Full gated-checkpoint accuracy and throughput still require compatible CUDA hardware and are not claimed by the CPU-only contract tests.

stablyai/orca:
## A faster Orca, plugins & background computer use ⚡

- ⚡ **A faster Orca:** Launch smoothly with hundreds of chats, with less lag as you type and switch tabs.
- 🧩 **Customize Orca** with icon themes, syntax highlighting and custom editors.
- 🖱️ **Keep working** while agents use Chrome, Blender and other Mac apps in the background.
- 🎙️ **Dictate on your phone** and see your words as you speak.
- 💬 **Try the new Chat UI:** Search for “Chat UI” in Settings to turn it on, then right-click a tab to switch live between Chat UI and TUI.

## Highlights

- **A faster Orca:** Fast app with hundreds of chats. Typing stays more responsive, and hidden chats do less work while you use other tabs.
- **Plugins:** Add icon themes, syntax highlighting and custom editors from Settings → Plugins. Community publishing is coming soon, so you’ll be able to share your own plugins.
- **Background computer use on Mac:** Let agents work in Chrome, Blender and other apps while you keep using your mouse and keyboard. Orca’s in-app browser already works in the background; now computer use does too. Some actions still need the app brought forward.
- **Chats:** Enjoy a very polished Chat UI, send again after Stop, and preview links in chat. Search for “Chat UI” in Settings to turn it on, and right-click a tab to switch live between Chat UI and TUI.
- **Terminals:** Set a running terminal limit for each computer in Settings → Terminal → Advanced.
- **WSL:** Stopped distros stay stopped until you choose Start. Terminals remember their folder.
- **Browser:** Press Cmd+Opt+B on Mac for a browser split. Send shorter annotation feedback, now with pasted images.
- **Workspaces:** Your workspace name becomes its branch name again. Source Control actions get Model and Effort controls.
- **Phone:** See dictation as you speak, and read clearer code, tables and diagrams.

## Compatibility & upgrade notes

- **New terminal host:** This release starts a fresh terminal host for new terminals. Terminals already open before the update keep running on the previous host and stay attached. The new running terminal limit setting needs the new host, and so do fixes such as the ble.sh startup fix and lighter process checks on macOS. Those apply to terminals you open after updating.
- **Plugins are on by default:** Installing a plugin, including from an `orca://plugins` link, only opens a review screen first. Plugins that run code ask for your consent before they install, and once approved they run with full access to your computer.
- **Running terminal limit:** The default now follows each computer: half of its system terminal limit, up to 4096, or 256 as before when Orca can’t read that limit. A value you set in Settings or with an environment variable takes priority. Raising or lowering it never closes running terminals. A remote server running an older Orca keeps working, but the limit can’t be changed there until it updates.
- **Chat naming:** Chats are now named by their own agent and account by default. A naming agent, custom command or arguments you saved before keep working, and the naming agent choice moved under Advanced in Settings → Chat → Chat naming.
- **Codex history across accounts:** A new switch, Settings → Agents → Share Codex history across accounts, is on by default and keeps today’s behavior. With it on, history from Orca’s managed accounts now also shows up in your own ~/.codex when you switch back to system default. Turning it off stops new sharing and removes nothing. On an SSH or WSL host running an older Orca, the switch stays disabled until that host updates.
- **Codex on macOS and Linux:** Orca now starts Codex with its paste guess turned off, so prompts typed from a phone or another client send instead of staying in the composer. Real pastes still arrive as pastes.
- **Computer use on a Mac:** Agents now act in the background by default. Agents can still ask for the old foreground mode with `--restore-window`, which drags into Chromium and Electron apps still need.
- **Browser annotations:** Send and Copy now give agents a short summary per note. Check **Include page details** in the Send menu to get the old full output; the choice lasts for that browser pane.
- **Workspace branch names:** A name you type for a new workspace is used as its branch again, even when Auto-rename branch from work is on. Auto-rename only replaces names Orca made up.
- **Automations:** Agents started by an automation skip their CLI’s startup update prompt, so the prompt can’t swallow the task. Agents you start yourself are unchanged.
- **Source Control actions:** Model and effort flags saved in an action’s Arguments move into the new Model and Effort controls when Orca loads; other Arguments stay as they are. A phone or remote server on an older Orca may launch these actions with a different model or effort until it updates.
- **New shortcuts:** Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X opens Plugins (outside text fields), and Cmd+Opt+B on macOS opens a browser tab in a split to the right. Cmd+Opt+B can be changed in Settings → Keyboard.
- **Known limitation, downgrading:** If you go back to v1.4.244, custom model and effort choices on Source Control AI actions reset to the agent’s defaults, and updating again won’t bring them back.

steipete/CodexBar:
### Highlights

- Cursor works again with Cursor 3.27, which now encrypts its stored app token: CodexBar decrypts it through Cursor's Safe Storage Keychain item, prompting at most once on a manual refresh and never in the background.
- Updates: automatic checks and automatic installs are now separate choices, and saved choices survive relaunches and Settings visits.
- Usage and cost: OpenCode's local history can optionally feed Codex cost history, Codex usage reported over a fixed 30-day window gets pace, Kimi's monthly Total breaks down into Kimi Code and other features, and OpenCode Go can use the active CLI login.
- Plugins and accounts: plugins can choose which quota window drives the menu-bar percentage and show native pace markers, Command Code keeps several saved subscription sessions, and the CLI gains `config set-cookie` and `config clear-credential`.

### Added

- Updates: separate automatic checks from automatic installs, preserve saved choices across relaunches and Settings visits, and retain the existing default-on behavior (#4777, #4778). Thanks @harveyrandall!
- Codex: optionally include this device's recorded OpenCode usage in local cost history, preserving recorded $0 costs and keeping scoped accounts and Usage & Spend excluded (#4757, #4752). Thanks @Danielweng0902!
- Plugins: choose which reported quota window drives the menu-bar percentage and switcher gauge, with automatic fallback when that window is unavailable (#4781). Thanks @coygeek!
- Plugins: allow detail progress bars to display native pace markers, respecting Show pace (#4776). Thanks @KLIEBHAN!
- Kimi: break the monthly Total usage pool down into Kimi Code and other features in menu and CLI details (#4759). Thanks @Redwinam!
- Command Code: manage multiple saved subscription sessions in Settings and select them from the CLI (#4774). Thanks @JavaGT!
- CLI: add `config set-cookie` and `config clear-credential` for stored manual cookies and API keys, preserving saved accounts and unrelated provider settings (#4765). Thanks @johan456789!

### Changed

- OpenCode Go: use the active CLI login for server quotas when no configured key or usable browser session is available, preserving account selection and local cost history (#4771). Thanks @sreejithraman!
- Settings: fade the provider reorder Undo banner after inactivity, pausing while hovered or focused and respecting Reduce Motion (#4760). Thanks @elijahfriedman!

### Fixed

- Cursor: read encrypted Cursor.app tokens without background Keychain prompts, preserving account validation and browser fallback (#4755). Thanks @micheltriana!
- Alibaba/Qwen: skip Safe Storage Keychain lookups when the browser-cookie fallback finds no matching encrypted cookies (#4790).
- Codex: calculate pace for explicitly reported fixed 30-day usage windows using their actual duration (#4766). Thanks @johan456789!
- Settings: hide the Version row for web-only Cursor and Raycast providers instead of showing "not detected" for a detection they do not support (#4769, #4779). Thanks @LeoLin990405!
- Trae CN: distinguish the Usage meter from the Credits details in Visible usage items while preserving hidden choices (#4764, #4780). Thanks @LeoLin990405 and @liuyuplus!
- WorkBuddy: keep resets on the paid subscription cycle instead of an earlier trial or reward expiry (#4767). Thanks @codertesla!
- WorkBuddy: use the official mascot instead of the placeholder letter icon (#4768). Thanks @codertesla!

strukturag/libheif:
v1.23.7 is a security and bugfix release. It is ABI- and API-compatible with v1.23.6 and is a drop-in replacement.

**Fourteen of the fixed issues are rated high, so all users are advised to upgrade.**

## Security fixes

(CVE numbers will be added when assigned.)

- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-xwcv-cp39-m2w4) Out-of-bounds read in the OpenH264 decoder plugin. An AVC SPS that libheif's coded-size check could not parse was skipped and still passed to OpenH264, which accepts cropping offsets whose sum wraps around and returns plane pointers far outside of its frame buffer. An SPS that cannot be parsed is now an error, also in subset SPS NAL units. The VVC SPS check had the same pattern and fails closed as well. Introduced with the coded-size check of v1.23.5. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-jx54-6rm6-2cgj) The AV1 coded-size check of v1.23.5 could be bypassed with libaom through an OBU without a size field. libheif stopped scanning at that OBU, while libaom continued and decoded a later, larger sequence header and frame. The last OBU of a sample is now given an explicit size before the data is scanned and decoded, so that both see the same framing. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-fpr5-xpfr-vcq3) The AV1 coded-size check of v1.23.5 could be bypassed with libaom. `num_ticks_per_picture_minus_1` was read with a UVLC reader that stops after 20 leading zero bits, although AV1 allows 31, and the error was ignored. The sequence header was then skipped, or scanned from the middle of the code where it could yield a small decoy size, and libaom allocated the real, much larger frame. The AV1 UVLC reader now follows the AV1 specification, and a sequence header that cannot be scanned completely is rejected. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-35mc-3887-rr37) Heap use-after-free when grid tiles are decoded in parallel. Several derived tiles (`iovl`, `iden` or `grid`) can share one coded input image. Their bit-depth queries read the decoder data of that input while another tile thread replaced it during decoding. A crafted file could crash the application or corrupt the heap with default options. The bit-depth queries now lock the decode mutex of the queried item. Only v1.23.6 is affected. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-hpg4-g2gc-pq42) Heap buffer overflow when padding an image to a size that is larger in one dimension and smaller in the other. `heif_image_extend_padding_to_size()` could be reached with such a size by re-encoding a sequence whose frames have different sizes with the x265 or x264 sequence encoder. Padding now refuses a size below the image or any of its planes, checks all planes before changing them, and the sequence encoders refuse a frame whose size differs from the first frame. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-9rpf-2x22-78m9) `heif_context_encode_thumbnail()` returned success without setting the output handle when the image already fits into the bounding box. Callers that released the handle, among them `heif-enc -t` and the C++ wrapper, freed an uninitialized or stale pointer (use-after-free, double free). The handle is now set to NULL in that case, as the API documentation says. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-48p4-gj45-w9v6) CPU exhaustion through derived images that decode a large image again and again and use only a few pixels of it, for example a grid of 1x1 tiles that are each a `clap` crop of an 8192x8192 overlay. A 2.6 kB file took 26 seconds to decode. Each decode now has a pixel budget of twice the size of the distinct images it uses (at least 2048x2048, at most `max_image_size_pixels`), single-tile decodes get their share of it, an exceeded security limit in a grid tile is an error also without strict decoding, and grid tiles outside of the image are not decoded. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-2g6j-vhr6-6wrj) CPU exhaustion through many coded pictures in one image item or sequence sample. The decoder decoded all of them, although only one image is returned: a 16 kB file with 1000 hidden HEVC pictures of 4096x4096 took 14 seconds. More than eight coded pictures per decode are now refused. HEVC, AVC and VVC count picture starts, AV1 counts frame OBUs, and AVC data with embedded start codes is refused. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-7qm8-hj35-269r) CPU exhaustion through repeated transformations. An item could carry many associations of the same `irot`, `imir` or `clap` property, and `iden` chains multiplied them: a 28 kB file took 73 seconds to decode. An item may now have at most one association of each of these properties, as HEIF requires, and at most 32 transformations are applied along a decode path. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-hhg3-fxg7-3gxw) CPU exhaustion while opening a file whose images have many `colr` associations. Reading the file regenerated and compared a colour profile property for every association. Reading and encoding now store colour profiles separately, so that opening a file does not create properties. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-73j7-gvm9-x8q6) CPU exhaustion in sequence decoding through samples that produce no output, for example when an edit list repeats a sample that the decoder does not display. One call of `heif_track_decode_next_image()` could run for minutes, also with `ignore_sequence_editlist`. The number of samples that are decoded without returning frames is now limited per codec, and `ignore_sequence_editlist` stops after the original samples. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-74mj-m37q-h3q9) Quadratic CPU time when opening a file with a `moov` box. The `stsc` entry of every chunk was looked up by a linear scan, so a file with many chunks and `stsc` entries took seconds to minutes to open, also when the application only reads the still image. The lookup is now a binary search, and an `stsc` table whose `first_chunk` values decrease is refused. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-rcqc-842v-m26h) Deadlock when decoding a grid image with parallel tile decoding and non-strict decoding. A tile that was skipped because it is not valid left an empty entry in the job queue, which was dispatched as a decode of item ID 0 and could deadlock with the other tile threads. Skipped tiles no longer create decode jobs. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-pfcm-ffqg-84hx) CPU exhaustion through cyclic Exif IFD pointers in the `heifio` helper of `heif-dec`, `heif-thumbnailer` and `heif-enc`. The tag search followed IFD pointers in loops. The traversal is now bounded by the size of the Exif data. Applications that use only the library, and the gdk-pixbuf loader, are not affected. (high)
- CVE-2026-XXXXX (GHSA-gff5-3vgr-p8h2) The gdk-pixbuf loader ignored the error of `heif_image_scale_image()` and used an uninitialized image pointer, which gdk-pixbuf later released. A small valid file made the scaling fail when an application loaded it with a fixed width or height and kept the aspect ratio (a 1x65536 AVIF loaded at a width of 3840 requests a 2.9 TB image), which crashed the application. The loader now checks the result and refuses output sizes above `max_image_size_pixels`. (medium)
- (GHSA-r9cg-w542-g7hj) `heif-dec -S` and `heif-info` printed and released an uninitialized URI pointer when a `urim` sample entry has no `uri ` box. Depending on the build, they crashed, or read and freed the URI of a previous track a second time. The library is not affected. (low)

All of these issues were found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner. Thanks also to @iPlayForSG and @SounLabs, who reported GHSA-74mj-m37q-h3q9 independently.

## Hardening

- `heif_image_scale_image()` and `heif_track_get_urim_sample_entry_uri_of_first_cluster()` set their output pointer to NULL on error, so that a caller that misses the error check does not use an uninitialized pointer
- A JPEG stream whose SOF marker cannot be parsed is refused instead of being passed to the decoder without a size check
- The libde265 plugin refuses NAL units of 2 GB or more. libde265 takes the size as `int`, and versions 1.1.0 to 1.1.2 did not reject the negative value
- Reading sample auxiliary information with a constant size from `saiz` is bounded by the sample count of the `saiz` box, as it already was for variable sizes
- The chroma bit depth query of a grid image whose first tile is missing returns -1 instead of dereferencing a null pointer
- heif-enc: the WebVMT parser was rewritten without `std::regex`, whose recursion overflowed the stack for long sync data (about 30,000 characters). Timestamps are checked as the WebVMT specification defines them (minutes and seconds up to 59, three fraction digits, hours that fit the 32-bit millisecond counter), invalid hex and base64 data and payloads that are not JSON are reported, and a missing file or a file without WEBVMT signature is an error (#1941)
- heif-enc: the PNG loader read past the end of the row for 16-bit grayscale images with alpha

## Bug fixes

- Image sequences:
  - The colour metadata of the sample entry (`colr`, `clli`, `mdcv`, `amve`, `ndwt`, `pasp`) is attached to the decoded frames, and an NCLX profile in the sample entry takes precedence over the bitstream, with the same full-range correction and mismatch warnings as for still images (#1938, @dlemstra)
  - A decoder is drained before the decoding switches to a chunk with another sample description, and at the end of the input the last active decoder is flushed. Frames at the end of a chunk were lost before (#1939, @dlemstra)
  - Repeated playback through an edit list works with all decoders, and the FFmpeg plugin recognizes the end of the stream
  - The `data_reference_index` of the `urim` sample entry in URI metadata tracks was written uninitialized; it is now 1
  - The `stsc` table that libheif writes for a track with several chunks numbers its entries instead of letting all of them start at chunk 1
- libde265: images with NAL units larger than 16 MiB could not be decoded, not even with the security limits disabled. The NAL size limit is now taken from `max_memory_block_size`, and an error of libde265 for a NAL unit is reported (#1936)
- SVT-AV1: odd image sizes are no longer padded with SVT-AV1 3.0.0 and later, so that no `clap` crop is written (Firefox does not display AVIF images with `clap`) (#1945). 10-bit images with alpha could not be encoded
- heif-enc: the transparency of RGB and grayscale PNG images with a `tRNS` chunk was dropped (#1947), and 16-bit grayscale PNG images with alpha were encoded wrong
- heif-enc: the WebVMT parser started cues at the wrong time and dropped cues in files with CRLF line endings and sync commands that span two lines
- C++ API: `ImageHandle` gets functions for the nominal diffuse white luminance (@therahedwig)
- Rotations by 90 and 270 degrees are three to five times faster: the planes are rotated in cache-sized blocks, and plane strides that are a multiple of 512 bytes get one cache line of padding (#1934, @m6w6)

## Behavior changes

- Decoding refuses with `heif_suberror_Security_limit_exceeded`:
  - a decode that would produce more than twice the pixels of the distinct images it uses (at least 2048x2048 are always allowed)
  - more than eight coded pictures in one image item or sequence sample
  - more than 32 transformations along a decode path
  - a sequence decoder that consumes too many samples without returning frames (32 for video codecs, 64 for VVC, 1 for still-image codecs)
- An item with more than one association of `irot`, `imir` or `clap` is refused
- An exceeded security limit in a grid tile is an error also without strict decoding. The tile was left blank before
- An AVC or VVC SPS, an AV1 sequence header or a JPEG SOF marker that libheif cannot parse is an error
- An `stsc` table with decreasing `first_chunk` values is refused
- `heif_image_extend_padding_to_size()` returns an error when a requested dimension is smaller than the image
- The x265 and x264 sequence encoders refuse a frame whose size differs from the first frame
- `heif_context_encode_thumbnail()` returns a NULL handle when no thumbnail is needed
- Metadata items (Exif, XMP, other `mime` items) are decompressed when they are first read instead of while the file is opened. A file with a compressed metadata item that cannot be decompressed now opens: the item is listed, `heif_image_handle_get_metadata()` returns the error and `heif_image_handle_get_metadata_size()` returns 0. Before, a corrupt Exif or `mime` item made the whole file fail to open, and an item with an unsupported content encoding was left out of the list
- The gdk-pixbuf loader refuses output sizes above `max_image_size_pixels`
- The vvdec plugin parses at most 8 pictures ahead

t8y2/dbx:
### 新功能

- 连接参数新增可视化编辑器：独立弹窗内搜索、编辑参数并查看说明，支持重复参数、原始文本模式和敏感值隐藏，通用 JDBC 连接可读取驱动属性元数据 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13892](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13892))
- MySQL 数据导出新增「省略表名中的数据库前缀」选项，INSERT 语句中的表名不再携带 `db.` 前缀 (contributed by @yiqiui) (PR [#13601](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13601))

### 改进

- Elasticsearch/EasySearch 的 REST 请求体支持 JSON 语言，提供语法高亮、嵌套折叠和语法诊断，执行内容保持不变 (contributed by @OOMEcho) (PR [#10749](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/10749))
- 数据网格底栏的选中统计精简为单项指标（默认求和），其余指标收进弹出面板，所选指标自动记住并在重启后沿用 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13951](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13951))
- 更新被配置弹窗阻止时明确指出需要关闭的对话框名称（包括弹窗位于其他窗口的情况），不再显示笼统的「请先完成当前配置编辑」 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13907](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13907))
- PostgreSQL 原生查询错误信息附带 SQLSTATE 错误码，便于对照定位问题 (contributed by @imcman) (PR [#13922](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13922))
- 选择自定义或系统 Java 时，驱动管理对话框隐藏 Dbx 托管的 JRE 运行时列表，避免展示与当前选择矛盾的条目 (contributed by @yiqiui) (PR [#13949](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13949))
- 侧边栏搜索结果不再显示原生作业和用户权限管理等管理入口节点 (contributed by @yaoxinghuo) (PR [#13916](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13916))

### 修复

- 修复 JDBC 分页查询收尾时回滚 DROP TABLE、CREATE TABLE AS 等语句的问题，此前显示执行成功但改动实际未生效 (contributed by @dienaso) (PR [#13709](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13709))
- 修复已知总行数大于已加载行数时首屏被误判为完整结果、「导出全部数据」只导出已加载页的问题 (contributed by @misxzaiz) (PR [#13878](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13878))
- 修复 Windows ARM64 版打开查询页即因主线程栈溢出闪退（0xC00000FD）的问题 (contributed by @Acd-kk) (PR [#13918](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13918))
- 修复 MySQL 导入 SQL 文件时文件内 `SET NAMES utf8` 将连接切换为三字节字符集、中文和 emoji 写入报 ERROR 1366 或变成 `????` 的问题 (contributed by @MomentarySixthSense) (PR [#13946](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13946))
- 修复 MySQL 分区表生成数据时产生不属于任何分区的值、插入报 ERROR 1526 的问题 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13910](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13910))
- 修复 MySQL 等无 schema 数据库在生成数据的外键参数中表和列下拉列表为空的问题 (contributed by @yiqiui) (PR [#13948](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13948))
- 修复 Oracle US7ASCII 数据库中按 GBK 等历史编码存储的中文读取为 `????` 的问题，新增连接级遗留编码兼容选项 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13799](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13799))
- 修复 Oracle 未安装 Spatial 组件时查询 SDO_GEOMETRY 表报 ORA-04067 的问题，改为以占位符读取几何列 (contributed by @jeff377) (PR [#13919](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13919))
- 修复 Oracle 通过数据库链接（`TABLE@LINK` 及指向链接的同义词）查看表结构不显示列信息的问题 (contributed by @jeff377) (PR [#13758](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13758))
- 修复 openGauss MySQL 兼容模式无法查看表索引的问题，限定名改用 textcat 拼接以兼容未开启 pipes_as_concat 的实例 (contributed by @thailoc-dev) (PR [#13932](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13932))
- 修复 Spanner SEARCH 全文索引被渲染为 UNIQUE INDEX、生成 DDL 无法执行的问题 (contributed by @dienaso) (PR [#13931](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13931))
- 修复达梦克隆表时确认的目标表名被强制转为大写的问题 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13909](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13909))
- 修复表名为 apply 时被误当作 APPLY 表运算符、FROM apply 之后不再提示 WHERE 等子句关键字的问题 (contributed by @ericbyz) (PR [#13889](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13889))
- 修复 JDBC 别名补全丢失表 schema、从错误的 schema 加载列的问题 (contributed by @zipg) (PR [#13861](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13861))
- 修复 MCP 严格客户端因 Nacos 注册实例 metadata 以布尔 schema 发布而拒绝整个 tools/list 响应的问题 (contributed by @lcq928) (PR [#13893](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13893))
- 修复 AI 插件工具待审批卡片被长回复滚出视野、找不到批准入口的问题，审批卡固定在输入框上方并在取消请求时同步清理 (contributed by @imcman) (PR [#13905](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13905))
- 修复选中多条 SQL 执行后手动事务等无语句编号的结果不显示成功或失败标识的问题 (contributed by @Acd-kk) (PR [#13913](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13913))
- 修复仅调整排版的内置 SQL 片段不再按当前数据库方言转换、SQL Server 下仍插入 LIMIT 语法的问题 (contributed by @seaways1015-afk) (PR [#13936](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13936))
- 修复侧边栏搜索结果中的表首次展开无反应、下级对象不显示的问题 (contributed by @yiqiui) (PR [#13953](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13953))
- 修复编辑或查看 Redis 连接时切换页签界面卡死的问题 (contributed by @onenewcode) (PR [#13863](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13863))
- 修复 Redis 键列表后台补全类型和过期信息失败导致进行中的扫描中止的问题 (contributed by @Gaiokane) (PR [#13868](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13868))
- 修复设置页无待保存改动时「应用并关闭」按钮置灰、看似无法关闭的问题 (contributed by @yiqiui) (PR [#13950](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13950))
- 修复 PostGIS 空间字段提示文案换行导致表结构编辑器排版错位的问题 (contributed by @thailoc-dev) (PR [#13864](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/pull/13864))
tailwindlabs/tailwindcss:
### Fixed

- Support `--watch --poll[=ms]` in `@tailwindcss/cli` when filesystem events are unreliable or unavailable ([#20297](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20297))
- Canonicalization: match arbitrary hex colors against theme colors case-insensitively (e.g. `bg-[#fff]` and `bg-[#FFF]` → `bg-white`) ([#20298](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20298))
- Prevent Preflight from overriding Firefox's native `iframe:focus-visible` outline styles ([#20292](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20292))
- Ensure `theme('colors.foo')` in JS plugins resolves correctly when both `--color-foo` and `--color-foo-bar` exist ([#20299](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20299))
- Ensure fractional opacity modifiers work with named shadow sizes like `shadow-sm/12.5`, `text-shadow-sm/12.5`, `drop-shadow-sm/12.5`, and `inset-shadow-sm/12.5` ([#20302](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20302))
- Parse selectors like `[data-foo]div` as two selectors instead of one ([#20303](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20303))
- Ensure `@tailwindcss/postcss` rebuilds when a preprocessor like Sass changes the input CSS without changing the input file on disk ([#20310](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20310))
- Ensure CSS nesting is handled even when Lightning CSS isn't run, such as in `@tailwindcss/browser` and Tailwind Play ([#20124](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20124))
- Prevent achromatic theme colors from shifting hue when mixed in polar color spaces like `oklch` ([#20314](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20314))
- Ensure `--spacing(0)` is optimized to `0px` instead of `0` so it remains a `<length>` when used in `calc(…)` ([#20319](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20319))
- Load `@parcel/watcher` only when needed in `@tailwindcss/cli --watch` mode, so one-off builds and `--watch --poll` work when `@parcel/watcher` can't be loaded ([#20325](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20325))
- Use explicit platform fonts instead of `system-ui` and `ui-sans-serif` so CJK text respects the page's `lang` attribute on Windows ([#20318](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20318))
- Prevent `@tailwindcss/upgrade` from rewriting ignored files when run from a subdirectory ([#20329](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20329))
- Ensure earlier `@source` rules pointing to nested files are scanned when later `@source` rules point to files in parent folders ([#20335](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20335))
- Prevent `@tailwindcss/vite` from triggering full page reloads when scanned files are processed by Vite but haven't been loaded as modules yet ([#20336](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20336))

## Spotube V6 Beta is here 🎉🚀

### 🔥Highlights

- Migration from Flutter to Compose Multiplatform, [learn why we did it](https://spotube.cc/blog/compose-multiplatform-migration/)
- UI redesign, introducing [Millennium](https://github.com/team-spotube/millennium/) UI. 2000s look and feel with 2026's modernity
- Jam session integration, play music with friends and family
- Full Android Auto integration. Browse, Library, Search all are there now, not just queue
- Migration from hetu_script to Kotlin for plugin development. Powered by [Zipline by Cashapp](https://github.com/cashapp/zipline/)
- More extensibility, plugin support for Lyrics provider and Scrobbling providers
- Native Android APK, with reduced apk size, performance improvements and more native android integrations.
- Relicensed from BSD-4-Clause to AGPL-3.0-or-later for a more Open Source friendly licensing. And for preventing distribution of closed source and maliciously modified Spotube.

### 💫 Features

- Migration to Compose Multiplatform
- Add ChipTab component and refactor SearchScreen to use it
- Add AutocompleteTextField component and integrate it into SearchScreen
- Enhance AutocompleteTextField with focus management and dropdown behavior
- Enhance AppSidebar with improved button interactions and visual feedback
- Implement endless playback recommendations in DeviceAudioPlayerQueue
- Add GhostIconButton component and enhance button interactions in TrackList
- Replace IconButton with GhostIconButton in AppExpandedPlayer and AppLargePlayer for improved visual consistency
- Replace IconButton with GhostIconButton in PlayerQueueContent and PlayableCard for visual consistency
- Enhance UI components with LocalBaseUITheme for consistent styling and improved interactions
- Enhance button styles and interactions in Buttons and Theme components for improved UI consistency
- Simplify highlight implementation in UI components for improved readability and maintainability
- Add genre selection and tabs to HomeScreen for improved content navigation
- Implement artist overview screen with loading, error handling, and pagination for albums, related artists, and featured playlists
- Add genre and featured browsing capabilities to MediaBrowseHelper
- Implement playlist creation and editing functionality with UI components
- Add 'Add to Playlist' functionality with UI components and dialogs
- Add Toggle component and update UI to use it in place of Switch
- Implement settings section cards for updates, desktop, language, caching, and plugins
- Update icons in settings sections to use Iconsax library for improved UI consistency
- Replace FeatherIcons with Iconsax in PluginCard and PluginPermissionsDialog for improved UI consistency
- Refactor PluginPermissionsDialog to use custom UI components for improved consistency and readability
- Enhance UI with shared element transitions and improve state management in album and playlist screens
- Integrate Uniffi for audio metadata reading and writing with Lofty library
- Replace FeatherIcons with Iconsax in window controls and update sidebar with better design
- Implement haze effect and UI enhancements in AppLargePlayer and AppShell
- Enhance haze effect integration in AppShell and AppSidebar for improved UI experience
- Add adaptive dialog bottom sheet component and enhance plugin installation UI
- Enhance AdaptiveDialogBottomSheet with dismiss icon and improve plugin screen layout
- Implement CollectionView component and refactor Album, Playlist, SavedTracks screens for improved UI consistency
- Add current time management in AudioPlayer for improved playback control
- Simplify playback control logic in AudioPlayer by removing redundant state checks
- Introduce AudioPlayerInterface and refactor AudioPlayer implementations for better abstraction
- Update skipToNext and skipToPrevious methods in AudioPlayer for improved media item management
- Refactor LyricsViewModel to use AudioPlayerInterface for improved abstraction
- Add Discord Rich Presence integration for enhanced media playback visibility
- Implement System Tray integration for window management and media controls
- Add hover effect to menu items in System Tray for improved user experience
- Add SSH debug session setup on failure for improved troubleshooting
- Implement blacklist functionality for tracks and artists with UI updates
- **systemtray**: Self-manage tray lifecycle via Koin DI
- **plugin_interfaces**: Update Maven publishing configuration and add GitHub Actions workflow
- **plugin_discovery**: Implement GitHub plugin discovery and add logo support in UI
- **plugin_discovery**: Implement GitHub plugin discovery and add logo support and information dialog in UI
- **plugin_install**: Add plugin installation dialog and release fetching functionality
- Update dependencies and configure compose hot reload settings
- Improve NewPipe video rank matching
- Integrate Nucleus framework for enhanced window management and webview support
- Implement system tray functionality with Compose Native Tray integration
- **mediacontrol**: Implement SystemMediaControlService for OS media integration
- **devices**: Add device discovery and remote control features
- **deeplinks**: Implement deep link handling for jam sessions
- **remote-control**: Implement remote playback functionality and UI components
- **remote-control**: Enhance queue management and player state synchronization
- **remote-control**: Enhance remote playback functionality with new commands and UI integration
- **webrtc**: Update ICE server configuration and enhance logging for peer connection events
- **jam-session**: Add connection state management and update UI feedback for session status
- **jam-session**: Enhance jam session functionality with improved playback synchronization and error handling
- **remote-control**: Refactor service registration and cleanup logic for improved reliability
- **jam-session**: Integrate MQTT broker configuration and enhance jam session settings

timescale/timescaledb:
This release contains performance improvements and bug fixes since the 2.30.2 release. We recommend that you upgrade at the next available opportunity.

**Highlighted features in TimescaleDB v2.31.0**
* Improved performance for `UPDATE` and `DELETE` queries on the columnstore with vectorized key processing for bulk decompression. The vectorized aggregation makes DML and recompression operations faster through parallelism, when a single-chunk query groups by an expression, resulting in up to 6.5 times faster queries.
* Preview of the new Adaptive Integer Compressor (AIC), which chooses the best encoding for each block of integer values. This results in the up to 20% improvement in compression ratios for integers, while queries benefiting from faster decompression perform up to two times better. AIC is disabled by default in this release and will be enabled by default in the `2.32.0` release.

**Loader changes**
This release allows controlling extension hook order to improve compatibility with other extensions. To ensure pgaudit hooks work together with timescaledb, pgaudit must come after timescaledb in `shared_preload_libraries` setting. This loader change, requires a PostgreSQL restart to enable the compatibility, but if you have no need to control the hook order, the previous loader version is enough, and you don't require a service restart.

**PG16 AL/10 found broken**
Binaries for PG16 AL/10 were found to be broken on October 22, they are currently fixed and uploaded to packagecloud, re-trying the upgrade should be enough to install 2.31.0

**Backward-Incompatible Changes**
* [#10666](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10666) Rename `timescaledb.enable_columnarscan` to `timescaledb.debug_enable_columnarscan` to make its debugging-only purpose explicit
* [#10772](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10772) Make the direct-compress batch sorting GUCs available only in debug builds

**Features**
* [#9737](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/9737) Speed up aggregation with `time_bucket_gapfill()` by performing aggregation per chunk
* [#10412](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10412) Exclude chunks at execution time when a hypertable is on the parameterized side of a nested-loop join
* [#10512](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10512) Block `ALTER` and `DROP` operations on a granular-refresh tracking column
* [#10517](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10517) Block granular refresh on a continuous aggregate's materialization hypertable

* [#10589](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10589) Add informational views for granular refresh
* [#10626](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10626) Add the experimental Adaptive Integer Compressor (AIC)

* [#10797](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10797) Preserve default values when splitting or merging compressed chunks after `ADD COLUMN`
* [#10806](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10806) Do not push parallel-unsafe aggregate expressions below a `Gather` during chunkwise aggregation
* [#10808](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10808) Speed up chunk creation in databases with many constraints

**New Settings**
* `timescaledb.cagg_refresh_stats_level`: controls continuous aggregate refresh statistics. Valid values are `off` (the default), `summary`, and `verbose_log`.

Attention maintainers!

We have released a new [client specification](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/v2.3/CLIENT-SPECIFICATION.md). In this release we are adding a new client-side syntax to allow the clients to show either shortform or longform options. This should remove a lot of clutter. It would also allow power users to view shortform options by default while showing longform options to new users. The syntax is backwards compatible so there is no need to rush support.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The old https://tldr.sh domain will stop providing assets at the end of this year.

## Changelog
- Added longform/shortform specifications ([#15253](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/pull/15253)) (by @Managor)
- Specify `common` as a supported platform option ([#15855](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/pull/15855)) (by @kbdharun)
- Add the date of removal of the old asset website ([#15862](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/pull/15862)) (by @acuteenvy)
- Various grammar fixes

## Option placeholders
Previously we have used a basic placeholder such as `{{-h|--help}}` to show both the short and long options to the user. While this gave the user more information, it also caused a lot of clutter and reduced the pasteability of the commands. The new option placeholder adds single square brackets inside the placeholder (`{{[-h|--help]}}`) where clients are allowed to pick which one to show. It is recommended for the clients to show only longform options by default, but if a client wants to brand itself as a power user tool they can default to showings shortform options. There is also a backwards compatible presentation style for showing both, which is just the curly braces removed (`[-h|--help]`).

----

## Style guide improvements
If you are a contributor to the tldr pages, do check out the [style guide](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/contributing-guides/style-guide.md).
We have made several improvements and restructuring to it such as [standardizing keypress notation](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/contributing-guides/style-guide.md#keypress-syntax), adding instructions for [disambiguation](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/contributing-guides/style-guide.md#disambiguations) and [grouping](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/contributing-guides/style-guide.md#grouping-commands) pages, instructing to avoid using `=` in [option arguments](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/contributing-guides/style-guide.md#option-syntax) whenever possible, [example.com clarification](https://github.com/tldr-pages/tldr/blob/main/contributing-guides/style-guide.md#general), and much more.

topjohnwu/Magisk:
This release brings official support for Googlebooks (Aluminium OS), including automatic firmware download suggestions and the ability to patch recovery GPT images directly onto a connected USB drive. Bringing Magisk to Googlebooks also meant supporting Android's Headless System User Mode (HSUM), where user `0` operates strictly as a non-interactive background system user while human users run in secondary user profiles. Adapting Magisk to HSUM created several architectural challenges, as many longstanding features and internal mechanisms were built around the assumption that user `0` is always the primary interactive user.

To address this, the way superuser access is granted to apps has been redesigned, and the traditional interactive root request prompt has been removed. The existing reactive `su` request flow, which relies on intercepting a root call in the background daemon and launching a blocking UI prompt in the right user session, is fundamentally incompatible with HSUM, especially when handling non-app UIDs like `adb shell` that are not tied to a foreground user. Instead, superuser access is now explicitly granted to applications ahead of time directly from the Superuser tab in the Magisk app.

Finally, the app hiding (package repackaging) feature has also been removed. Like interactive `su` prompts, the repackaging and stub management mechanisms are fundamentally incompatible with HSUM. More importantly, truly hiding an installed package from detection is nearly technically impossible on Android. Since interactive root prompts no longer require the Magisk app to remain installed at runtime and Magisk no longer automatically reinstalls the app if it is missing, the most effective way to hide the Magisk app is to simply uninstall it after configuring your superuser policies and modules.

## Changelog

- [General] Support Headless System User Mode (HSUM) devices
- [General] Drop support for Android 6.0; Android 7.0 is now the minimum supported version
- [General] Remove the app hiding (repackaging) feature and the stub app; Magisk no longer reinstalls the app automatically if it is missing
