vorssaint/vorssaint-utils:
### Summary
More reliable window switching, audio, screenshots and display recovery, with safer file handling and app removal. New options include an all-windows shortcut, Claude account selection, scroll-to-zoom, a Quit apps panel and more flexible calendar countdowns.

### Added
- The window switcher has an optional All windows shortcut that cycles through individual windows across apps in every layout, including Large icons. Settings → Window switcher → All windows. Thanks to BrainAPP for the suggestion.
- AI Agents can select an existing Claude Code account profile and show the monitored account. Local usage and plan limits follow the selected profile. Settings → Dynamic Island → Content → AI Agents → Claude account.
- Dynamic Island level controls and the menu panel's mixer can be adjusted with a mouse wheel or trackpad. Thanks to @JB-OD.
- Dynamic Island can start event countdowns 15, 30, 60 or 120 minutes before an event and keeps longer countdowns fully visible. Thanks to @Aryan-Saini.
- An optional Pinch Zoom feature turns a modifier and mouse-wheel movement into pinch gestures in supported apps, with a choice of modifier and scroll exceptions. Thanks to @ahmadhatahet.
- An optional Quit apps panel can request normal quits for one app, all apps or all except the current app, with a saved list of apps to keep running. Thanks to @thedankest.
- Command Bar converts days, weeks and fixed 365-day years, with English and Portuguese unit names. Thanks to @asim-sde.
- Settings backups can be exported or imported with `--export-settings FILE` and `--import-settings FILE`; importing requires the app to be closed. Thanks to @DrakeEvans.
- Clipboard history can show source app icons in list view. The option starts off and preserves file icons and selection controls. Settings → Clipboard history → Show source app icons in list view. Thanks to @ywu73.
- Dynamic Island can show a volume row below the music player. Settings → Dynamic Island → Content → Music → Show volume in the player.
- Screenshots can copy the image, including edits, without a file URL for apps that otherwise paste an attachment. Settings → Screenshot → Copy as image only.
- Quit on close can handle selected menu bar apps that keep a Dock icon after their last window closes. The list starts empty, and existing exceptions still apply. Settings → Quit on close → Menu bar apps to quit.
- Window layout can reserve space for Stage Manager when maximizing or arranging windows, including the green-button override. Settings → Window layout → Reserve space for Stage Manager.
- Switch Spaces by dragging a button now accepts the middle mouse button, including upward drags for Mission Control and downward drags for App Exposé. A short click keeps its normal behavior. Settings → Mouse → Mouse button shortcuts.

### Changed
- Homebrew opens installation, setup and password-required commands in your default terminal, without requiring Terminal Automation permission. Thanks to @hertza-haeon.
- Snippet lists in Settings and the library use alphabetical order. Thanks to @Zekuath.
- Clipboard history keeps fewer decoded thumbnails in memory to reduce its memory use.
- Command Bar accepts British unit spellings and spaced fluid-ounce names.
- The window switcher's icon row, previews and hints use Liquid Glass when available and enabled.
- The window switcher allows up to 10 columns while preserving Auto and screen-width limits. Settings → Window switcher → Options → Maximum columns. Thanks to @EugeneCarldotme.

### Fixed
- Display controls keep manually disabled monitors off after wake while protecting the last usable display. You can still turn a monitor back on explicitly. Thanks to @Fenrir200678.
- Network readings avoid double-counting traffic on mirrored virtual interfaces and false spikes when switching connections. Thanks to @Zekuath.
- Super key modifiers reach session-based hotkey tools regardless of startup order, including after login. Shortcut recording still owns the source key and its solo actions. Thanks to @complicat9d for the diagnosis.
- Dynamic Island's clipboard supports Control-N and Control-P to move through history, matching the separate clipboard panel. Thanks to @avgrpg for the report.
- The uninstaller checks Homebrew again for each app and pauses removal when its package status cannot be verified, with a refresh action to retry. Thanks to @tzimpel.
- URL Cleaner cleans Safari links that carry rich previews, preserving supported previews and removing tracking from their navigation addresses. Thanks to @anschmieg for the diagnosis.
- Shelf copies files dragged from inside app packages or libraries, preserving the originals. Ordinary files and whole packages can still move. Thanks to @Dexist-hub.
- Media image exports and newly saved image profiles preserve a zero watermark margin. Thanks to @JeanBaeez.
- URL Cleaner rules added from links with login details or ports now match the intended site. Previously saved rules containing login details or ports need to be added again. Thanks to @g1obalworlds.
- The radial menu's action editor keeps its file picker over the editor window, avoiding an invisible panel on multi-display setups. Thanks to @saiganeshreddy7.
- Mic Mute describes its device-control limits and reports known failures even when no microphone could be changed. Siri and some apps may still hear audio. Thanks to @sarat03 for the diagnosis.
- The onboarding feature picker stays responsive when scrolling. Thanks to @yousefhamza.
- Wallpaper previews for ultra-wide images stay within their grid cells. Thanks to @ozanuslan.
- Dynamic Island keeps volume, brightness and keyboard-light notices at a stable width as the percentage gains a digit. Thanks to @nikigan.
- AI Agents cards keep "left" or "used" beside limit percentages, even in narrow layouts. Thanks to @sakemyali.
- AI Agents settings previews show example limit percentages when account limits are unavailable. Thanks to @hrithiksaini99.
- Command Bar finds English built-in commands and system answers when the interface uses another language. Thanks to @ywu73.
- Clicking outside Dynamic Island dismisses its screenshot preview while preserving active sharing, pinned surfaces and clicks in copies on other displays. Thanks to @samanyudas.
- Extra Brightness keeps app windows visible in Mission Control's desktop thumbnails. Thanks to @othmanehousni.
- The Features page keeps its scroll position when restart and unused-feature notices appear or disappear.
- The window switcher reaches fullscreen windows and windows on other Spaces more reliably, shows their titles and avoids sending duplicate close requests.
- The window switcher opens more efficiently when many windows are open.
- The window switcher's search field stays within its panel and remains readable on light backgrounds and Liquid Glass.
- Focus follows mouse preserves window order when Bring the window to the front is off.
- Quit Protection follows changes to macOS app-switcher shortcuts and respects required Fn, preventing unprotected quits after Vorssaint's switcher closes. Thanks to @ruvelro.
- Quit on close no longer mistakes leftover entries from closed windows for open windows. Minimized windows and windows on other Spaces still count as open.
- The menu bar panel recovers from interrupted closes so later clicks can open it again.
- Recent captures keeps its Clear history confirmation open and removes a pending confirmation when the palette closes.
- Dynamic Island moves between displays without stretching, losing mouse input or restarting the music bars.
- Dynamic Island's timer ruler fills the available width near its minimum and maximum durations, keeping the selected minute visible.
- Volume keys advance supported USB outputs that round volume changes into fixed steps, and feedback follows the device's confirmed level.
- Volume mixer keeps volume adjustments working on supported multichannel outputs and recovers when audio formats or sample rates change.
- Low disk-space alerts use refreshed capacity readings to avoid false warnings.
- System monitor improves CPU temperature sensor detection on M1 and 14-core M4 Max Macs.
- Power can use DC input readings on desktop Macs when adapter readings are unavailable.
- Fan Control attempts to restore System control after hardware failures, offers a retry if restoration fails and hides outdated temperatures when its helper stops responding.
- The menu bar panel no longer draws a second background with mismatched corners on macOS Sonoma and Sequoia.
- Scrolling screenshots preserve the selected width, keep sparse Terminal output aligned and continue through smaller overlaps on long pages, including blank spacing and low-contrast content.
- The cleaner leaves system log files out of app leftovers.
- Command Bar handles extreme date calculations without crashing and preserves very small results in non-temperature unit conversions.
- Clipboard history ignores marked temporary content and restores the previous copy without another notice, while preserving ordinary copies and sensitive-text filtering.
- Pinned GPU, temperature and fan menu bar readings follow the selected System monitor update interval.
- Dynamic Island's full-screen hiding recognizes games whose windows cover the desktop without entering a separate full-screen space.
- Dynamic Island's Hide content in full screen blocks hover opening again. Hidden until hover in full screen is a separate option under Settings → Dynamic Island → Behavior → Display.
- Dynamic Island stays responsive during slow Bluetooth discovery and ignores outdated connection alerts after sleep or when alerts are turned off.
- Volume mixer recognizes headphones from their Core Audio device information, including models whose names do not say headphones.
- Volume mixer leaves Discord and Teams audio untouched by default to prevent call echo when sharing audio. Their app menus can re-enable volume control, with a reminder to turn it off before sharing; saved levels and outputs are preserved.
- Volume mixer avoids audio cutouts and delayed playback after brief interruptions in captured sound.
- Screen recordings avoid loud noise from 16-bit USB microphones.
- Screenshot area selection keeps its crosshair over other apps, and card shadows follow the captured window's own rounded corners.

wavetermdev/waveterm:
Wave v0.14.5 introduces a new Process Viewer widget, Quake Mode for global hotkey, and several quality-of-life improvements.

- **Process Viewer** - New widget that displays running processes on local and remote machines, with CPU and memory usage, sortable columns, and the ability to send signals to processes
- **Quake Mode** - The global hotkey (`app:globalhotkey`) now toggles a Wave window visible and invisible
- **[bugfix] Settings Widget** - Fixed a bug where config files that didn't exist yet couldn't be created or edited from the Settings widget UI
- **Drag & Drop Files into Terminal** - Drag files from Finder (macOS) or your file manager into a terminal block to paste their quoted path ([#746](https://github.com/wavetermdev/waveterm/issues/746))
- New opt-in `app:showsplitbuttons` setting adds horizontal/vertical split buttons to block headers
- Toggle the widgets sidebar from the View menu; visibility persists per workspace
- F2 to rename the active tab
- Mouse button 3/4 (back/forward) now navigate in web widgets
- Terminal sessions now set `COLORTERM=truecolor` for better color support in CLI tools
- [bugfix] Trim trailing whitespace from terminal clipboard copies
- Package updates and dependency upgrades

waydabber/BetterDisplay: This version brings a larger collection of user requests from the enhancement backlog, focusing on everyday usability, alongside bug fixes and improved compatibility with macOS 27.2. A notable new feature is an **experimental, driverless Software Audio controller** that provides volume control for compatible displays whose audio cannot be controlled through DDC or network protocols. ### Upgrading to BetterDisplay 5 **BetterDisplay 5 is a free upgrade for Pro licenses purchased on or after January 1, 2025.** Read the [BetterDisplay v5 upgrade FAQ](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/licensing/v5-upgrade-faq/) for details about license coverage, existing activations, and upgrade options. **BetterDisplay 5 supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 26.3 or later, including macOS 27.2.** Explore **[betterdisplay.pro/guide](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/)** for a detailed [App Menu reference](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/interface-reference/app-menu/) and [Settings reference](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/interface-reference/settings/), [step-by-step tutorials](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/tutorials/), and [answers to frequently asked questions](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/faq/). Learn what each BetterDisplay 5 feature does, set up your displays, and find practical troubleshooting advice. ### Experimental Software Audio - **Driverless software volume and mute.** Added a Software Audio controller for compatible audio outputs, including display speakers without usable DDC, network, or native volume control. Adjust volume and mute through BetterDisplay without installing an audio driver. (#5902) - **A quieter minimum volume.** Optional Combined Volume Control combines hardware and software adjustment, extending the quiet range for displays whose lowest hardware volume is still too loud. (#5910) - **Audio tuning and meters.** Added gain, bass and treble, balance, channel trims, stereo width, mono audio, channel swapping, polarity inversion, 10-band EQ, bass boost, loudness compensation, frequency filters, compressor, noise gate, soft clipping, and audio meters. Software volume and mute, gain, simple bass and treble, meters, and combined routing are available without Pro; advanced audio tuning requires Pro. (#5911) To try it, open **Settings > Displays > [display] > Device Control > Add or Remove Controllers…** and add **Software Audio**. Configure its associated audio output and enable audio access. The controller is experimental, requires macOS audio-recording permission, and can display the macOS audio-capture indicator while active. Compatibility depends on the audio device. See the [Software Audio setup guide](https://betterdisplay.pro/guide/interface-reference/settings/displays/display/device-control/software-audio/). ### Usability Improvements - **Put the current display first.** Added options to prioritize the display containing the app menu and automatically expand its controls when opening the menu. (#4789) - **Choose which quick toggles stay visible.** Customize individual toggles, including Auto Brightness, so frequently used controls can remain visible without expanding the display menu. (#5073) - **Easier-to-read sliders.** Added optional adaptive scale marks to suitable menu sliders, making common values and neutral positions easier to identify. (#5290) - **More flexible menu bar icons.** Set separate custom icons for light and dark appearance, choose an icon for the active display group, and optionally disable shaded SF Symbol rendering for a single-shade appearance. (#2170, #3944, #5888) - **Favorite color profiles.** Added favorite slots to the Color Profile menu, with keyboard shortcuts and CLI commands for quick switching. (#2393) - **Global Prevent Sleep control.** Keep the Mac awake using a new action in Tools or a keyboard shortcut, without configuring a particular display. (#3935) - **More selective screen-saver and lock dimming.** Added options to skip dimming the main display or the only connected display. (#1502) - **Precise HDR calibration.** Added numeric value entry to the HDR brightness upscaling calibration slider. (#4048) - **Smoother display corners.** Display corner rounding now uses a continuous curve, matching the style of macOS windows and improving the appearance at larger radii. (#5919) - **Separate keyboard targeting for mirror and stream destinations.** Added an option to exclude automatically included mirror and stream targets from brightness and other video adjustments. (#4614) - **Configurable media-key shortcuts.** Added controls for captured media-key combinations that open System Settings or toggle mirroring. (#5547) - **Floating remote controls.** Open supported TV and HDMI-CEC remotes in separate windows from the app menu, a keyboard shortcut, or the CLI. (#4766) - **Crop selected-content streams.** Added live crop editing to Stream Selected Content. (#5865) - **Clearer PiP and crop highlighting.** Added an optional highlight for the PiP window containing the pointer, plus accent-color and strength controls for window highlights and crop frames. (#4559, #5918) - **Disconnect virtual screens when PiP closes.** Added an option to disconnect a virtual screen when its automatically started PiP window is closed. (#5041) - **Visible paused-stream status.** Paused streaming is now reflected in the menu bar icon and the stream/PiP icons in the app menu. (#1940) - **Updated macOS 27.2 OSD details.** Updated filled icon variants and added appropriate Apple audio-device and headphone icons for native volume control. (#5889) - **Device names in the rounded OSD.** Added an option to identify the display or audio device being adjusted in the macOS 27.2-style OSD. (#5893) - **Fixed light or dark OSD appearance.** Added appearance choices for the OSD when its adaptive background is disabled. (#4906) - **Dynamic targets in macOS Shortcuts.** Relevant actions can now target the display under the pointer, the focused display, or the main display. (#4092) - **PiP alignment through the CLI.** Added horizontal and vertical alignment options for positioning PiP windows. (#3464) - **Virtual-screen associations through the CLI.** Configure which displays are associated with a virtual screen from scripts and automation. (#2809, #3193) - **Pro status in About.** The About pane now identifies the app as BetterDisplay Pro when Pro is active. (#5423) - **More reliable media-key handling.** Fixed a crash when pressing media keys while BetterDisplay Settings or a PiP window has focus. (#5877) - **New audio-device detection.** Fixed newly connected audio devices sometimes not being recognized for volume control. Anatomy can now share what it makes. Ask your agent to publish a finished figure and it lands in the [community gallery](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy-community), with its prompt, model, and how long it took.

### Install or update

```bash
npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy
```

Or download `anatomy.zip` below and unzip it into `~/.claude/skills`. The latest zip is always at https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/releases/latest/download/anatomy.zip

### New

- **Publish to the community gallery.** Make a figure as usual, then say *"publish this figure to the Anatomy community gallery"*. Your agent asks for a title, an id and your GitHub name, shows exactly what it will send, and opens the pull request after you say yes; it makes a fork for you if you need one. Only the figure's source is sent: the gallery rebuilds it in a locked sandbox, checks it, and photographs it. (`scripts/publish.mjs`, `references/publish.md`)
- **Time and tokens, recorded for you.** In Claude Code, publishing reads how long the figure took and how many tokens it used from the session's own log, from your request to the request to publish, leaving out idle gaps and cache reads. The plan shows both before anything is sent; `--minutes` and `--tokens` set them by hand in other agents.
- **More agents.** Anatomy runs in OpenCode and Codex as well as Claude Code, and the gallery knows Antigravity too.

### Fixed

38 fixes, mostly in the checks that keep figures honest:

- **Browser checks** start on Linux, fail when a page doesn't load or a step throws, time out cleanly, reject unknown or misspelled actions, and clean up after Chrome exits early.
- **The geometry audit** measures transformed, arced, clipped and tapered shapes by their true bounds, converges on large figures, and keeps sliding parts and pipe clearances honest.
- **Reduced motion** is respected by the arcade cabinet and the turning dial, even when switched on while the page is open.
- **React components** keep per-point opacity, seamless tone regions and the first readout write.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Features

### AI

- Improved ACP configuration defaults to apply only to new conversations, preserving session settings when reopening existing conversations. ([#65850](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65850))
- Improved fuzzy searching in agent model and configuration option pickers for Zed Agent and third-party ACP agents, while keeping search preparation off the UI thread. ([#64147](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/64147); thanks [JacobNWolf](https://github.com/JacobNWolf))
- Improved OpenCode compatibility when replaying DeepSeek reasoning and disabling thinking for Google models. ([#65922](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65922))
- Improved thinking controls to explain when thinking cannot be disabled at the selected effort level. ([#62480](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/62480))

### Debugger

- Added DWARF debugging to the JavaScript debugger to support debugging WebAssembly sources. ([#65371](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65371); thanks [SGumbles](https://github.com/SGumbles))
- Improved debugger hovers with an expandable, keyboard-accessible variable tree. ([#53198](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/53198); thanks [Tortes](https://github.com/Tortes))

- Improved SQL syntax highlighting in Rust `sql!` string literals. ([#58778](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/58778); thanks [kuskhan](https://github.com/kuskhan))

zellij-org/zellij:
This is a small patch release (mostly) set to address some issues discovered in the latest `0.45.0`.

### Notable changes
1. The nested session detection now works over SSH without having to forward environment variables
2. It's now possible to opt-out of the newly introduced behavior, where scrolling with the mouse inside a pane enters scroll mode. To do so, add `scroll_mode_sync false` to the configuration.
3. It's now possible to set an explicit theme hue in the config (i.e. dark or light) that will be used if the system doesn't know which theme we're in. To do so, add `explicit_theme_hue light # or dark` to the config.
4. New feature: it's now possible to start a new session in the foreground or background with a specific running command instead of the default terminal. `zellij attach -c foo -- htop` for foreground `zellij attach -b foo --htop` for background.
5. Some issues fixed with notification parsing specifically regarding OSC9 which overloaded the existing OSC99 notification spec (this manifested for some users as excess notifications when saving a file in nvim for example)
6. Fixed some issues with the kitty image protocol clearing on stacked panes and not working until first resize

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/compare/v0.45.0...v0.45.1

# ZeroClaw v0.8.7

ZeroClaw v0.8.7 is a security and maintenance follow-up to v0.8.6 spanning **81 commits** from **19 contributors**. It moves to patched Wasmtime, Rustls certificate verification, `tokio` and `ctutils` releases for advisories that affect v0.8.6, rebuilds the container images with CA bundles that no longer trust the distrusted emSign chains, and fixes five of v0.8.6's plugin known issues and narrows two more, as well as the daemon's refusal of a group-writable data directory. Precompiled plugin components must be rebuilt for Wasmtime 48.0.7; read [Breaking Changes](#breaking-changes) and [Known issues](#known-issues) before upgrading.

## In brief

Security fixes: Wasmtime 48.0.7 and patched TLS verification. Rebuild precompiled plugins.

Plus five plugin known-issue fixes, Telegram rate-limit handling, ZeroCode cost warnings, and chat that reconnects after a reload.

## Highlights

- **Wasmtime and TLS security advisories are fixed.**
  - The plugin host moves to Wasmtime 48.0.7, with the matching Pulley 48.0.7 and Cranelift 0.135.7 (RUSTSEC-2026-0375 to RUSTSEC-2026-0379).
  - TLS certificate verification uses `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16, `webpki-roots` 1.0.10 and `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.10. Affected versions could accept certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates whose private keys are known (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383).
  - The optional MQTT channel moves from `rumqttc` 0.25 to `rumqttc-v4-next` 0.34, a maintained MQTT 3.1.1 client on the same patched verifier. That removes the last copy of the legacy `rustls-webpki` 0.102.8 and the four audit exceptions it needed.
  - Precompiled `.cwasm` plugin components built for an earlier Wasmtime must be rebuilt for 48.0.7.

  (#11924, closes #11923; includes the original Wasmtime commit from #11906)
  - `ctutils` moves to 0.4.5 for RUSTSEC-2026-0385 (non-constant-time mask generation and `u128` comparisons), a fix from @mov-xound-glitch (#11998), and `tokio` to 1.53.3 for RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (`AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety) (#12010, closes #12009).
  - Container images are rebuilt from refreshed base images and patched CA packages. Their CA bundles, which native tools such as curl, git and OpenSSL-linked programs read, no longer trust the distrusted emSign chains (#11925, closes #11932).
- **Five of v0.8.6's plugin known issues are fixed, and two more are narrowed.**
  - A plugin connection no longer stalls when the first resolved address never answers, typically an IPv6 route that drops packets. The host tries the next address after 250 ms, alternating address families, as browsers do (#11814).
  - Tool packages that connect over WebSocket or raw sockets get their declared egress seeded at install, and `plugin list` reports what their row is missing, as it already did for HTTP tools (#11808).
  - `zeroclaw config set` takes a non-secret plugin setting, such as Discord's `guild_ids`, as given on the command line. Only settings the package marks secret use the masked prompt (#11812).
  - `plugin remove` removes a loaded plugin from the directory it was loaded from, instead of deleting `<plugins_dir>/<name>` (#11809).
  - Peripheral, skill-defined and MCP capability tool names are reserved before plugin tools register, so a plugin tool can no longer take their calls (#11851).
  - Narrowed: new package lock and lease files are created owner-only on Unix (#11807), and `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` report a tool whose retained configuration the runtime refuses as not loading (#11811). [Known issues](#known-issues) says what remains.
- **The daemon starts on a group-writable data directory again.** Under umask `0002`, v0.8.6 created `~/.zeroclaw/data` group-writable and then refused it. v0.8.7 accepts the data directory as it is, as v0.8.5 did, and keeps its config lifecycle lock in an owner-only `data/.lifecycle` directory instead. Read the [Breaking Changes](#breaking-changes) before upgrading a running daemon (#11803).
- **ZeroCode warns before the budget runs out and shows what each session is using.**
  - A `warn_at_percent` cost threshold now reaches ZeroCode as a one-time line in the chat, instead of the first sign being a turn refused at 100%.
  - Overview shows the focused session's agent, model, workspace and whether work is running or queued, next to the other session's.
  - Config explains how to add provider profiles and routing hints, and opens the missing required field.

  (#11692, #11513, #11508)
- **Chat stays connected and responsive.**
  - An open dashboard chat reconnects on its own after a daemon reload, instead of answering every message with an error until the page is refreshed.

### ZeroCode, Dashboard, Desktop and Web

- Surface `[cost] warn_at_percent` warnings in ZeroCode, shown once as a line in the chat; nothing is blocked and no setting changes (#11692).
- Show the focused session's runtime context in Overview. Matching Code and Chat values share a labelled row, different values stay separate, and each context shows whether work is running or queued (#11513).
- Guide Config alias setup:
  - the empty list explains its purpose;
  - the name form says an entry is saved immediately;
  - the editor opens the first missing required field, supplied by the daemon from typed configuration.

  (#11508)
- Desktop app: closing the dashboard window hides it instead of destroying it, so the tray, **Show Dashboard**, **Agent Chat** and relaunching the app bring it back, and tray **Quit** now exits the app (#11802, closes #11087).

- Log what filled the context window when a request cannot fit: request and window sizes, and the shares taken by instructions, tool descriptions and history (#11578).
- Honor `native_tools` for every OpenAI-compatible chat-completions family: `true` selects native tool calling, `false` prompt-guided tools; unset keeps the family default (#11599).
- After `model_switch`, tell the model to carry on and deliver the result in the same reply, instead of announcing the switch and stopping (#11385).
- Report torn or unreadable cost-ledger lines in cost summaries, instead of silently undercounting session, daily and monthly spend (#11557).

### Security and Sandboxing

- Apply a risk profile's `firejail_args` to the Firejail wrapper. Entries that would undo ZeroClaw's own Firejail hardening, or are not single `--option` / `--option=value` flags, are rejected, and the sandbox then refuses every command rather than running without them (#11656, closes #11594).
- Name the cause when a requested bubblewrap backend is rejected: a missing or broken launcher, or a build without `sandbox-bubblewrap` (#11559).
- Correct the sandboxing documentation's description of Linux `auto` backend selection and its fallbacks to match the selector (#11591).
- Narrow the memory threat scanner's credential-URL check to URL user info and credential query or fragment parameters, so text that merely contains a link and an unrelated credential word is no longer flagged (#11144).

### Memory

- Push `since`/`until` time bounds into Qdrant vector search, so out-of-window high-scoring points no longer take the requested result slots (#11143).

### Plugins

- Document the official Discord plugin: install and bind by its registry name, the `discord.com` and `*.discord.gg` egress grant, the masked token prompt, routing to an agent, and a maintainer acceptance runbook (#11329).

### Documentation and Dependencies

- Quickstart help for a provider's `api_key` now says the key is encrypted into `config.toml`, with its encryption key in `.secret_key` beside it, instead of claiming the OS keyring (#11840).
- Bump `js-yaml` to 4.3.2 in the dashboard build, outside advisory GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (#10729).
- The arm64 `dist` container image publishes again: its build now gets 8 GiB of swap and a serial build, as the release workflow's Linux ARM64 build does (#11833, closes #11828).

## Breaking Changes

- **Rebuild precompiled plugin components.** `.cwasm` files compiled for an earlier Wasmtime must be rebuilt for 48.0.7 (#11924).
- **MQTT `keep_alive_secs` must be 0 to 65535.** A larger value now fails listener startup instead of being silently truncated to the protocol's 16-bit field (#11924).
- **MQTT credentials:** when both `username` and `password` are set, empty strings are now sent as explicit empty credentials with their CONNECT flags, instead of being left out. For anonymous access, leave both unset (#11924).
- MQTT broker URLs, `use_tls`, QoS and certificate/hostname verification against the system trust store are unchanged.
- **Plugin connect timeout:** a plugin HTTP request that sets no `connect_timeout` now gets 10 s for the TCP connect instead of 600 s. A timeout the plugin sets is still used as given (#11814).
- **Stop ZeroClaw before upgrading from v0.8.6.** The config lifecycle lock moves from `data/config-lifecycle.lock` to `data/.lifecycle/config-lifecycle.lock`, so v0.8.6 and v0.8.7 processes do not exclude each other. Stop any running `zeroclaw daemon`, `zeroclaw agent` or `zeroclaw acp` before installing v0.8.7, then start it again. The old `data/config-lifecycle.lock` is ignored and can be deleted once no v0.8.6 process is running. The v0.8.6 `chmod go-w` workaround is no longer needed (#11803).
- **SOP runs:** a finished run that an earlier version revived is stored as active, so v0.8.7 restores it and drives its remaining steps. Cancel such runs before upgrading. Upgrade the daemon and any CLI that runs SOPs together: an older binary writing to the same `runs.db` can still reopen a finished run (#11861).
- **Gateway reloads:** a request that reaches a stopped gateway, for example on a connection kept open across a daemon reload, gets `503` with `Retry-After: 1` and `"reason":"gateway_restarting"`. Retry it (#11901).
- **Container images:** pull the v0.8.7 image and recreate containers to get the refreshed CA bundles. An image rebuilt from an earlier release's Dockerfiles keeps the old bundle (#11925).

## Known issues

These issues ship in v0.8.7. None of them weakens a security check; where behaviour is affected, it fails closed.

- **WebSocket routes do not connect over the gateway's built-in TLS listener.** When the gateway serves TLS itself, the server answers a WebSocket upgrade with `101 Switching Protocols` and then closes the connection, so dashboard chat and the other WebSocket routes never connect. This also affects v0.8.6. Terminate TLS in a reverse proxy or tunnel and serve plain HTTP to the gateway instead. The fix is planned for v0.9.0 (#11951). Separately, an upgraded socket outlives a gateway reload on either path (#11709).
- **The host does not record refused WebSocket and socket connections.** A plugin's WebSocket or socket connection to a destination its instance has not been granted is refused, but only HTTP refusals write a `plugin_egress_denied` record with the host and a remedy. For the other two transports only the plugin's own log shows the refusal (#11304).
- **A plugin channel that never reaches its service can stay quiet.** A channel package that cannot reach its server, or whose credential is refused, logs nothing about it at the default level. `/health` reports its component (`channel:plugin.<alias>`) as `starting` with `last_ok: null` for as long as no exchange has succeeded, so treat a component that stays `starting` as unreachable or misconfigured, and check its egress grant and credential.
- **Ten registry channel packages have not run against their live services.** bluesky, gitea, mattermost, mochat, notion, reddit, telegram, twitter, wechat and wecom were checked to install, load, bind, and validate their configuration on a v0.8.6 release-candidate build; none has run against its live service with a real account yet. Discord has (#10999).
- **Package lock files created before v0.8.7 keep their mode.** v0.8.7 creates the package lock and lease files owner-only (`0600`) on Unix but never changes an existing file. A lock created earlier under a permissive umask can still be held by another local account that can read the plugins directory, so install, update and remove fail after 60 seconds. Remove `<plugins_dir>/.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1` while no plugin command is running, and the next one creates it owner-only. A group-shared plugins directory is not supported (#11360).
- **Discovery that overlaps `plugin update` can briefly pair old and new files.** Discovery reads a package's manifest and component separately, so a discovery during an update can pair the old manifest with the new component until the next discovery. Packages whose manifest declares `wasm_sha256` are protected, because admission checks the digest in every signature mode (#11562).
- **An interrupted `plugin install` can leave a hidden stage behind.** If an install is killed after it starts staging the package and before it publishes it, a `.<name>.installing-v1-<id>` directory holding a `lease` file and an empty `package/` stays in the plugins directory, and no command removes it. It does not affect install, update, remove or discovery, and a re-install works. Delete it while no plugin command is running (#11792).
- **A reinstalled package can meet configuration it refuses.** `plugin remove` keeps a package's `[[plugins.entries]]` row and its values, and `plugin install` does not warn when the reinstalled package cannot accept them, so the runtime skips the tool. `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` now report such a tool as "does not load" and name the row to fix; `plugin update` already re-validates retained entries (#11336).
- **Installing over an installed package is refused.** `plugin install` of a package that is already installed refuses and prints the matching `plugin update` command (#10162).
- **Registry packages have no versioned WIT compatibility check yet.** The registry lists only versions built for this release, and the install-time load check refuses an incompatible package, but a package does not yet declare which host versions it supports.
- **Slack no longer shows "is thinking…" in ordinary channel threads.** Since v0.8.5, an agent mentioned in a channel thread shows only the 👀 acknowledgement reaction until it replies; the status line appears only in Slack's AI-assistant pane. With `stream_drafts = true`, progress appears as a draft message that the final answer replaces (#11416).

Skill commands in a chat apply only to the current Agent. - **Skill management**: the original skill is kept when a replacement install fails, and its previous state is restored when enabling or disabling fails; files with a BOM and various metadata formats are supported, and one corrupted config entry no longer affects other skills (Thanks @rudycelekli #3685, #3690, #3695, #3696, #3698, #3711, #3753, #3754, @c020627 #3760). - **Terminal**: fixed commands producing no output and multi-line Python commands being truncated on Windows (Thanks @keeponlight #3795, @rudycelekli #3811, @Nolan527 #3793); the full output is kept after very long lines are truncated (Thanks @rudycelekli #3779); on Windows the full-output log keeps the command's original line breaks, so reading it back at the indicated line numbers lands in the right place (Thanks @tanishqbaweja #3858). - **Syntax checks**: the syntax check before writing accepts files with comments or template syntax, such as `tsconfig.json`, VS Code settings, and Helm templates, while strict JSON files such as `package.json` still reject comments with a hint on how to fix them (Thanks @tanishqbaweja #3853). - **File read/write and search**: fuzzy-match edits no longer add blank lines around the replaced content, and overwriting a file keeps its existing line endings instead of converting them all to CRLF on Windows (Thanks @tanishqbaweja #3854, #3856). Very long lines can be read by offset, CR line endings and the indentation of fuzzy matches are preserved, the original file is not overwritten when the encoding fallback fails, directories and special files are refused for reading and writing, and file read records are scoped to the current conversation; directory filters also apply when ripgrep is not installed (Thanks @rudycelekli #3689, #3715, #3752, #3770, #3772, #3794, #3799, #3810). - **Document parsing**: Word content controls, field results, and merged cells are read in full, and Excel cells outside the declared range are read (Thanks @ningyixi #3786, #3787, @rudycelekli #3773, #3777, #3798). - **Browser**: snapshots can be scoped to a given element, screenshots are saved to the current project, and input fields are filled only when explicit text is provided. Browser profile directories are matched exactly, so similar paths are no longer mistaken as in use, and process detection on Windows has a timeout (Thanks @rudycelekli #3724, #3725, #3727, #3802, @c020627 #3769). - **Vision**: compressed images keep their original orientation, and the next provider is tried when a model returns an empty result (Thanks @rudycelekli #3712, #3726, #3806). - **MCP and scheduled tasks**: MCP connection failures are returned as failed tool calls, and corrupted authorization records are ignored. Scheduled task results map to the exact run, schedule changes made during a run are no longer overwritten, rejected operations are reported as failures, and migration of legacy reminders is more reliable (Thanks @rudycelekli #3713, #3745, #3781, #3782, #3807, #3808). ## 🤝 Multi-Agent Collaboration - **Sub-agents**: delegated only when necessary, such as for in-depth research, and they wrap up and return the results gathered so far as the timeout approaches. Local delegation follows the configured timeout, and invalid arguments or an unreadable template directory no longer abort it (Thanks @rudycelekli #3783, @c020627 #3761). - **Team collaboration**: @mentions are recognized correctly when followed directly by sentence-ending punctuation (Thanks @c020627 #3738). - **Context**: loop-detection hints are removed once the model has seen them instead of lingering in the context (Thanks @NotZhu #3851). New messages after clearing the context are kept, and when saving a channel conversation's execution steps to history fails briefly, it is retried, so tool records are no longer lost (Thanks @rudycelekli #3734, #3804). ## 📡 Channels - **WeChat**: QR code login is more stable, expired QR codes refresh automatically, and an optional `weixin_proxy` can be configured (Thanks @c020627 #3838); sent files keep their original names and types (Thanks @6vision #3817); fixed connections not being released when a media download fails (Thanks @rudycelekli #3750). - **Feishu**: rich-text messages support parsing files and multilingual content. - **Sending files**: Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom Bot, and WeChat Customer Service keep the original file name when sending files. - **DingTalk**: files in group chats are kept separate per sender, and temporary media files are cleaned up promptly (Thanks @rudycelekli #3762, @c020627 #3828). - **WeCom / Official Account**: images saved by WeCom keep their original orientation (Thanks @c020627 #3845); the welcome message on follow is sent on Official Accounts even when no chat prefix is configured (Thanks @rudycelekli #3707). - **Telegram / Discord / Slack**: files can be sent from remote URLs. @mentions of the bot in group chats match the full username, oversized attachments are rejected before downloading, and workspace system notifications no longer get replies (Thanks @rudycelekli #3716, #3764, #3765, #3818, #3819, #3820). - **Plugins**: group admins are matched exactly by ID (Thanks @rudycelekli #3763). ## 🛡 Security Hardening - **Scheduled task permissions**: scheduled Agent tasks keep the permission mode of the session they were created in, so tasks created in a read-only session cannot perform writes (Thanks @EddieMurphy89 #3833). - **Guest request protection**: network requests made on behalf of visitors always block local and private network addresses, and a guest page password cannot be the same as the console password. - **Console password**: newly set passwords must be at least 6 characters, with a strength hint while typing; existing passwords are not affected. - **Resource limits**: the download size of files returned by models is limited (Thanks @c020627 #3832). - **Security policy**: added a security policy and a private channel for reporting vulnerabilities. ## 🛠 UX Improvements & Fixes - **Chat interaction**: you can scroll up freely while a reply is being generated, the scroll-to-bottom button is aligned with the input box, and earlier messages load automatically when you scroll to the top (Thanks @LYLMagui #3785); clicking a blank part of the input area focuses the input box (Thanks @Rofds #3830). - **Smoothness**: fixed UI stutter when replies arrive in bursts. Off-screen messages in long sessions are no longer rendered, so typing and scrolling are smoother (Thanks @zkjqd #3792). - **Wide screens**: the desktop client's chat area adapts to the window width (Thanks @zkjqd #3844, @592774447 #3839). - **Sessions**: the context usage chart is kept after a restart (Thanks @xiao115255 #3767, @jiangch1128 #3619); titles are generated with the fallback model when the main model fails; a failed send shows the specific reason; conversation history is kept when deletion fails (Thanks @rudycelekli #3809); a failure to index artifacts no longer duplicates conversation history. - **File display**: files outside the workspace are copied into it when sent, so they display correctly in the console; images that fail to load show their file name; the desktop client's file preview can reveal the file in its folder. - **Knowledge graph**: fixed unresolved cross-references leaving nodes without titles and dropping every edge. Links relative to the knowledge base root, bare file names, and angle-bracket syntax are supported, as are knowledge base folders under a symlink. - **Console**: the running configuration is kept when saving fails, and concurrent saves of a workspace file report a conflict. Fixed workspace file refresh, editor content validation, preference saving, and the scope of request cancellation; artifacts in registered Agent workspaces are accessible, and replacing knowledge base documents is more reliable (Thanks @rudycelekli #3733, #3746, #3747, #3748, #3749, #3755, #3784, #3801, #3805). - **Agent initialization**: an empty identity file no longer skips onboarding, and concurrent initialization no longer overwrites existing configuration (Thanks @rudycelekli #3722, #3730); trajectory evaluation correctly checks the expected tools and execution status (Thanks @xiong-wei1 #3849, #3848). - **Logs and CLI**: live logs continue after the log file is truncated, and console output is kept when the data directory is not writable. The service detaches from standard input when started in the background, and fixed the process ID being lost without sufficient permissions and a corrupted update status file (Thanks @rudycelekli #3686, #3687, #3709, #3717, #3719, #3780, #3800, #3812, #3814). - **Config and backup**: creating the data directory concurrently no longer fails, remotely pushed configuration is written to the data directory actually in use, and skill scripts keep their executable permission after a backup is restored (Thanks @rudycelekli #3723, #3778, @c020627 #3823). - **Desktop client**: the bundled backend's version matches the client's (Thanks @592774447 #3839); if copying files fails during Windows installation, the files are extracted again automatically; fixed the log file growing until the disk filled up when the client was opened from a terminal or launcher that later exited (Thanks @ClearloveUzi7 #3860). ## 📦 How to Upgrade - **Source deployment**: run `cow update` for a one-click upgrade, update from the version menu in the Web console sidebar, or pull the latest code and restart. See the [upgrade guide](https://docs.cowagent.ai/guide/upgrade). - **Desktop client**: check for updates and update with one click inside the client, or get the latest version from the [download page](https://cowagent.ai/download/). **Release date**: 2026.10.30 | [Full Changelog](https://github.com/zhayujie/CowAgent/compare/2.2.1...2.2.2)

**功能新增**
* 新增任务栏窗口显示在副显示器的功能。#2037 #1974  #1952 #1944 #1875 #1870 #1863 #1734
* 多语言代码重构，多语言字符串在外部ini文件中配置，方便程序本地化。新增德语、意大利语、俄语、波兰语、巴西葡萄牙语、土耳其语、希伯来语等语言的支持。
* 更换皮肤界面皮肤列表控件改为ListBox。
* 选项设置对话框中的控件支持动态调整大小。
* 选项设置对话框调整大小时，垂直滚动条不再复位。
* 任务栏窗口显示项目宽度支持动态调整。
* 新增任务栏资源占用图背景颜色跟随Windows主题颜色的功能。
* 新增每个皮肤的字体、文本颜色、显示文本单独保存的功能。
* 显示文本设置对话框中增加右键菜单，允许为单独的项目恢复默认。
* 崩溃信息窗口新增调用堆栈的显示，新增将崩溃信息写入日志的功能。
* Lite版新增了显卡和硬盘利用率显示。

**问题修正**
* 修正“常规设置”中更新源没有保存的问题 #2020 #1561 #1119
* 修正多显示器DPI不一致时更换皮肤对话框预览图中字体大小不正确的问题。
* 修正当悬浮窗在不同DPI的显示器间移动时DPI可能不正确的问题
* 修正显示了插件项目时任务栏内置项目不能全部去掉，会保留一个上传速度的问题 #1965
* 优化了选项设置中“颜色显示”控件中颜色显示的样式，修正颜色数量大于8个时控件右侧有明显的空白的问题
* 修正主窗口和任务栏窗口设置中，更改“字体大小”文本框中的值后点击“应用”没有生效的问题
* 修正任务栏窗口鼠标提示中的网速单位和设置的不一致的问题
* 修正CPU频率不遵循“数值和单位用空格分隔”选项的问题
* 添加从睡眠状态恢复时重新初始化连接的处理，解决有时从睡眠状态恢复时无法获取到网速的问题。
* 修正皮肤文件中字体名称有Unicode字符时无法获取正确的字体的问题，并修正了皮肤文件解析的一些逻辑问题。
* 其他细节方面的改进。

**New Features**  
- Added the feature to display the taskbar window on secondary monitors. #2037 #1974 #1952 #1944 #1875 #1870 #1863 #1734  
- Refactored multilingual code; multilingual strings are now configured in external INI files for easier localization. Added support for new languages such as German, Italian, Russian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Turkish, Hebrew.  
- Replaced the skin list control in the skin selection interface with a ListBox.  
- Controls in the Options Settings dialog now support dynamic resizing.
- The vertical scrollbar in the Options Settings dialog no longer resets when resizing.  
- The width of items in the taskbar window now supports dynamic adjustment.  
- Added the feature for the taskbar resource usage graph background color to follow the Windows theme color.  
- Added the ability to save fonts, text colors, and display text separately for each skin.  
- Added a right-click menu in the Display Text Settings dialog to restore defaults for individual items.  
- Added the display of call stack in crash information dialog. Add the function of writing the crash information to the log file.
- Added the display of GPU and hard disk utilization for the Lite version.

**Bug Fixes**  
- Fixed the issue where the update source in "General Settings" was not saved. #2020 #1561 #1119  
- Fixed incorrect font size in the preview image of the skin selection dialog when DPI settings differ across multiple monitors.  
- Fixed incorrect DPI when the floating window moves between monitors with different DPI settings.  
- Fixed the issue where built-in items in the taskbar could not be fully removed when plugin items were displayed, leaving an upload speed item. #1965  
- Optimized the style of color display in the "Color Display" control in the Options Settings dialog. Fixed the issue where noticeable blank space appeared on the right side of the control when more than 8 colors were displayed.  
- Fixed the issue where changing the value in the "Font Size" text box in the main window and taskbar window settings did not take effect after clicking "Apply."  
- Fixed the inconsistency between the network speed unit in the taskbar window tooltip and the settings.  
- Fixed the issue where CPU frequency did not follow the "Separate value and unit with a space" option.  
- Added handling to reinitialize connections after resuming from sleep mode, resolving the issue where network speed could not be retrieved after waking from sleep.
- Fixed the issue that the correct font could not be obtained when font name in the skin file contains Unicode characters. Fixed some logical problems when parsing the skin file.
- Improved in other details.
